1 原子里的三种粒子The three particles in an atom Three sub-atomic particles三种亚原子粒子
这一站要你会：说出三种粒子的名字、符号、电荷、相对质量、位置，并能解释「为什么原子是中性的」。Goal: name the three particles with their symbols, charges, relative masses and positions, and explain why an atom is neutral.
把原子想成一个巨大的体育场：正中间的看台风口旁放了一颗小玻璃弹珠，那就是原子核——几乎全部质量都在那儿；而所谓的电子，是几只绕着整个球场乱飞的蚊子。中间全是空的。所以「看上去很硬的桌子」，实际上绝大部分体积是空的。Picture a huge sports stadium: the nucleus is a marble sitting in the middle, holding nearly all the mass; the electrons are a few mosquitoes flying around the whole ground. Everything in between is empty space. So the hard table you are sitting at is almost entirely nothing.
必须记牢的三个角色：The three roles to learn:
粒子Particle符号 · 电荷Symbol · Charge相对质量Relative mass位置Where
质子 protonProton+11核内in nucleus
中子 neutronNeutron01核内in nucleus
电子 electronElectron−11/1840 ≈ 0核外电子层in shells
  • 质子数决定它是哪种元素——11 个质子就一定是钠，改了这个数就是别的元素了。The proton number decides the element — 11 protons is always sodium; change it and you have a different element.
  • 原子是中性的，因为质子数与电子数相等，正负抵掉了。An atom is neutral because proton number equals electron number, so the charges cancel.
  • 质量几乎全在核里——电子太轻，算质量时可以当它不存在。Nearly all the mass is in the nucleus — electrons are so light you ignore them when finding mass.
最容易丢分的地方：题目问「相对质量」和「相对质量数」时写了个单位（比如 g）。相对量是跟 ¹²C 的十二分之一比的，没有单位。The classic lost mark: putting a unit (like g) after a relative mass. Relative masses are comparisons against one-twelfth of carbon-12 — they have no unit.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: The atom has no overall charge because the number of protons equals the number of electrons, so the positive and negative charges cancel out.
例题Example
一个中性原子里有 11 个质子、12 个中子。问：它有几种几种粒子各多少？质量数是多少？它是什么元素？A neutral atom contains 11 protons and 12 neutrons. How many electrons? What is the nucleon number? Which element is it?
① 中性原子 → 质子数 = 电子数 = 11。① neutral atom → electrons = protons = 11. ② 质量数 = 质子 + 中子 = 11 + 12 = 23。② nucleon number = protons + neutrons = 11 + 12 = 23. ③ 质子数 11 → 周期表第 11 号 → 钠 Na。③ proton number 11 → the 11th element → sodium, Na.
练习Practice
同一个套路，换一个原子试试。Same routine, a different atom.

某元素的原子有 26 个质子、30 个中子，并且是中性的。（a）它有多少电子？（b）质量数是多少？（c）它是哪种元素？A neutral atom has 26 protons and 30 neutrons. (a) How many electrons? (b) What is the nucleon number? (c) Which element is it?

点开看答案Show answer
(a) 26 个电子（中性原子电子数 = 质子数）。(b) 质量数 = 26 + 30 = 56。(c) 26 号元素是铁 Fe。注意：这里说的是质量数 56，不是「相对原子质量 55.8」——两者含义不同，下一阶段会分开。 (a) 26 electrons (neutral atom: electrons = protons). (b) nucleon number = 26 + 30 = 56. (c) element 26 is iron, Fe. Note this is the nucleon number 56, not the relative atomic mass 55.8 — those two are different ideas.
— 第 1 站完成 —— Stop 1 done —
2 原子序数、质量数与同位素Proton number, nucleon number, isotopes Isotopes同位素
这一站要你会：看懂 ᴬZX 这个记号，找出质子 / 中子 / 电子数，并解释同位素为什么化学性质几乎一样。Goal: read the A over Z X symbol, work out protons / neutrons / electrons, and explain why isotopes behave almost identically in reactions.
同位素就像同一款车的两个配置：发动机（质子数）一样，所以开起来手感一样（化学性质一样）；多带的备胎和行李（中子）让它更重（质量不同），但不影响它怎么开。Isotopes are like two trims of the same car: the engine (proton number) is the same, so it drives the same way (same chemistry); the extra luggage in the boot (neutrons) makes it heavier, but does not change how it drives.
两个数字:Two numbers:
  • 质子数 Z（原子序数）＝质子个数＝核电荷数＝中性原子的电子数。它决定是谁。Proton (atomic) number Z = number of protons = nuclear charge = number of electrons in a neutral atom. It decides the identity.
  • 质量数 A（核子数）＝质子 + 中子。它决定多重。Nucleon (mass) number A = protons + neutrons. It decides the mass.
  • 中子数 = A − Z（左上减左下）。Neutrons = A − Z.
  • 同位素化学性质几乎相同，因为化学反应只动电子，而同位素的电子排布完全一样；物理性质（密度、沸点）会略有差别。Isotopes have almost identical chemical properties because reactions involve electrons, and isotopes have the same electron arrangement. Physical properties (density, boiling point) differ slightly.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: Isotopes are atoms of the same element with the same number of protons but a different number of neutrons. They have the same electronic configuration, so they have similar chemical properties.
例题Example
已知氯有两种同位素：³⁵Cl 占 75%，³⁷Cl 占 25%。求氯的相对原子质量。Chlorine has two isotopes: ³⁵Cl at 75% and ³⁷Cl at 25%. Calculate the relative atomic mass of chlorine.
把「丰度」当成权重，做加权平均：Use the abundances as weights and take a weighted mean:
Ar = (35 × 75 + 37 × 25) / 100 = (2625 + 925) / 100 = 35.5 （无单位）
所以周期表上氯写的是 35.5，而不是某个整数——它是平均值。That is why the periodic table shows chlorine as 35.5, not a whole number — it is an average.
练习Practice
（a）先数粒子；（b）加权平均的公式照例题套。(a) count particles first; (b) copy the weighted-mean formula from the example.

(a) 写出 ²³₁₁Na 含有的质子、中子、电子数。(b) 硼有 ¹⁰B（20%）和 ¹¹B（80%）两种同位素，求硼的相对原子质量。(a) State the number of protons, neutrons and electrons in ²³₁₁Na. (b) Boron has ¹⁰B (20%) and ¹¹B (80%). Calculate its relative atomic mass.

点开看答案Show answer
(a) 左下角 11 = 质子 11；左上角 23 = 质量数，所以中子 = 23 − 11 = 12；中性原子电子 = 11。
(b) Ar = (10 × 20 + 11 × 80) / 100 = (200 + 880) / 100 = 10.8。周期表上硼就是 10.8，说明算对了。 (a) Z = 11 so 11 protons; A = 23 so neutrons = 23 − 11 = 12; neutral atom → 11 electrons.
(b) Ar = (10 × 20 + 11 × 80) / 100 = (200 + 880)/100 = 10.8. Boron appears as 10.8 in the periodic table, so that checks out.
— 第 2 站完成 —— Stop 2 done —
3 电子住在哪里：电子层、亚层、轨道Where electrons live: shells, sub-shells, orbitals Shells & orbitals电子层与轨道
这一站要你会：分清 electronic shell / sub-shell / orbital 三级，说出 s、p、d 各有几个轨道、最多几个电子。Goal: tell apart shell / sub-shell / orbital, and state how many orbitals and how many electrons s, p, d sub-shells hold.
把整个电子系统想成一栋宿舍楼：电子层（shell）是楼层（1 楼、2 楼、3 楼）；亚层（sub-shell）是楼层里不同户型的房间——单人间叫 s，三人间叫 p，五人间叫 d；而具体的一张床就是轨道（orbital）。规定每张床最多睡 2 个人，还规定两人必须「头朝相反方向」（自旋相反）。Think of it as a hall of residence: the shell is the floor; the sub-shell is the room type on that floor — single rooms are called s, triple rooms p, five-bed rooms d; an actual bed is an orbital. Each bed takes at most 2 students, and the two must lie head-to-toe (opposite spins).
亚层Sub-shell轨道数Orbitals最多电子Max electrons出现在第几层Appears in shell
s12第 1 层起from shell 1
p36第 2 层起from shell 2
d510第 3 层起from shell 3
  • 主电子层 n最多装 2n² 个电子：第 1 层 2 个，第 2 层 8 个，第 3 层 18 个。Shell n holds up to 2n² electrons: 2 in shell 1, 8 in shell 2, 18 in shell 3.
  • 轨道（orbital）是一片区域，不是一条路线——别再画「行星绕圈」了。An orbital is a region of space, not a path — stop drawing planets going round in circles.
  • 同一亚层里的几个轨道能量相同（简并），比如 2p 的三个轨道能量一样。Orbitals in the same sub-shell have equal energy (degenerate) — the three 2p orbitals are identical in energy.
  • 注意 4s 的能量比 3d 低——所以 4s 先被填满（图里 4s 在 3d 下面）。这条决定了下一站的填法。Note 4s is lower in energy than 3d — so 4s fills first (it sits below 3d in the diagram). This decides everything in the next stop.
术语别混：sub-shell（亚层，如 2p）是一个类别；orbital（轨道）是一个具体的格子。说「一个 2p 轨道」是对的，说「一个 2p 亚层里有三个轨道」也是对的，但把两者当成同义词会被扣分。Don't mix the terms: a sub-shell (e.g. 2p) is a category; an orbital is one individual box. "A 2p orbital" is fine, "there are three orbitals in the 2p sub-shell" is fine — treating them as synonyms costs marks.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: An atomic orbital is a region of space around the nucleus which can hold up to two electrons with opposite spins. A p sub-shell contains three p orbitals, so it can hold up to six electrons.
例题Example
写出氯（Z = 17）的完整电子排布，并说出它有多少个已占轨道。Write the full electronic configuration of chlorine (Z = 17) and state how many occupied orbitals it has.
按能量从低到高依次填：1s → 2s → 2p → 3s → 3p。Fill in increasing energy: 1s → 2s → 2p → 3s → 3p.
Cl (Z = 17): 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p5 已占轨道 = 1 + 1 + 3 + 1 + 3 = 9 个轨道
3p⁵ 虽然没填满，但那三个轨道都已经有电子了，所以三个都算「已占」。3p⁵ is not full, yet all three of its orbitals contain electrons, so all three count as occupied.
练习Practice
先把 Asub-shell 的电子数分配好，再数格子。Place the electrons into sub-shells first, then count boxes.

镁 Z = 12。(a) 写出完整电子排布；(b) 它有几个 已占轨道？(c) 它的最外层（第三层）有几个电子？Magnesium, Z = 12. (a) Write the full electronic configuration; (b) how many occupied orbitals? (c) how many electrons in its outer (third) shell?

点开看答案Show answer
(a) 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s²。
(b) 已占轨道 = 1(1s) + 1(2s) + 3(2p) + 1(3s) = 6 个。
(c) 第三层只有 3s²，所以是 2 个最外层电子——这也解释了镁为什么在第 2 族。 (a) 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s².
(b) occupied orbitals = 1(1s) + 1(2s) + 3(2p) + 1(3s) = 6.
(c) the third shell holds only 3s², so 2 outer electrons — which is exactly why magnesium sits in Group 2.
— 第 3 站完成 —— Stop 3 done —
4 电子排布怎么填（三大规则）Writing electronic configurations (three rules) Aufbau · Pauli · Hund三大填充规则
这一站要你会：用三条规则把前 36 号元素的电子排布写出来，并知道 Cr 与 Cu 两个「不讲道理」的例外。Goal: use three rules to write configurations up to Z = 36, and know the two awkward exceptions, Cr and Cu.
填电子就三条规矩：先坐低层的（能量低的先占）——这叫能量最低原理；一张床最多两个人，而且必须一正一反——这叫泡利不相容；同一层里有好几间空房时，大家先一人一间，谁也不跟谁挤，等到每间都有人了才回来配对——这叫洪特规则。三条加起来，你就能算出任何一个原子的电子排布。Only three rules: fill the lowest energy first (Aufbau principle); one box takes at most two electrons and they must spin oppositely (Pauli exclusion principle); when several empty rooms of equal energy are available, everyone takes their own room first before pairing up (Hund's rule). Together they let you work out any configuration.
填充顺序口诀（写到肚子里）：The filling order to learn by heart:
1s 2s 2p 3s 3p 4s 3d 4p 5s 4d 5p ... 容量: 2 2 6 2 6 2 10 6
  • 考试必写的缩写：把前面一段用稀有气体包起来。例如 Fe：1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p⁶3d⁶4s²，写成 [Ar] 3d⁶ 4s²。The exam shorthand: wrap the front part in a noble gas. Iron is 1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p⁶3d⁶4s², written [Ar] 3d⁶ 4s².
  • 写排布时先写 3d 还是 4s？按能量高低写就写 3d 在 4s 前面（失电子时也是先失 4s）。CAIE 两种写法都接受，但要保持一致。3d or 4s first? In order of energy, 3d comes before 4s (and 4s electrons are lost first). CAIE accepts both as long as you are consistent.
  • 两个例外必须背：Cr 是 [Ar] 3d⁵ 4s¹（不是 3d⁴4s²），Cu 是 [Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s¹（不是 3d⁹4s²）——半充满和全充满更稳定。Two exceptions to memorise: Cr is [Ar] 3d⁵ 4s¹ (not 3d⁴4s²) and Cu is [Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s¹ (not 3d⁹4s²) — half-filled and full sub-shells are more stable.
离子怎么办？先写中性原子的排布，再从最外层拿走电子。Fe → Fe²⁺ 要先拿 4s 的两个：[Ar] 3d⁶，而不是 [Ar] 3d⁴4s²。这是选择题里常设的陷阱。Ions? Write the neutral atom first, then remove electrons from the outermost shell. Fe → Fe²⁺ loses both 4s electrons: [Ar] 3d⁶, not [Ar] 3d⁴4s². This is a classic multiple-choice trap.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: Electrons occupy the lowest available energy level (Aufbau principle). Orbitals of the same energy are occupied singly first, with parallel spins, before pairing begins (Hund's rule). Chromium has a half-filled 3d sub-shell, which is more stable.
例题Example
写出 Fe（Z = 26）与 Fe³⁺ 的电子排布。Write the electronic configurations of Fe (Z = 26) and Fe³⁺.
① 中性 Fe：26 个电子 → [Ar] 3d⁶ 4s²。① neutral Fe: 26 electrons → [Ar] 3d⁶ 4s². ② Fe³⁺ 要丢 3 个：先丢 2 个 4s，再丢 1 个 3d。② Fe³⁺ loses three: both 4s first, then one from 3d. ③ 结果：[Ar] 3d⁵。（3d 半充满，所以 Fe³⁺ 特别稳定）③ result: [Ar] 3d⁵. (A half-filled 3d sub-shell, which is why Fe³⁺ is especially stable.)
练习Practice
记得两个例外；做离子时一定先扔 4s。Remember the two exceptions; when forming ions always remove 4s first.

(a) 写出 Cr（Z = 24）的排布；(b) 写出 Cu（Z = 29）的排布；(c) 写出 Cu²⁺ 的排布。(a) Write the configuration of Cr (Z = 24); (b) of Cu (Z = 29); (c) of Cu²⁺.

点开看答案Show answer
(a) [Ar] 3d⁵ 4s¹——把 4s 的一个电子挪去 3d，凑成半满。
(b) [Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s¹——凑成 3d 全满。
(c) [Ar] 3d⁹——先丢 4s 的那个，再从 3d 拿一个。 (a) [Ar] 3d⁵ 4s¹ — one 4s electron is promoted to give a half-filled 3d.
(b) [Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s¹ — giving a full 3d sub-shell.
(c) [Ar] 3d⁹ — lose the 4s electron first, then one from 3d.
— 第 4 站完成 —— Stop 4 done —
5 逐级电离能：怎么看出它在第几族Successive ionisation energies: spotting the group Ionisation energy电离能
这一站要你会：背下电离能的定义与符号方程，并能从一组逐级电离能数据里大跳跃的位置反推电子排布与族序数。Goal: state the definition with its symbol equation, and use the position of the big jump in successive ionisation energies to deduce electron arrangement and group number.
想象你在一层一层地扒洋葱。扒最外面那层很轻松（第一电离能小）；扒完外层，再往里去就要动靠近「核」的那一层，那里被正电荷死死吸住，需要的力气突然大上十倍——这个「突然变大」的位置，就是换层的信号。所以只要盯着数据里落差最大的那一步，就能知道最外层有几个电子。Imagine peeling an onion one layer at a time. The outer layer comes off easily (low first ionisation energy). Once it is gone, you must attack a layer much closer to the positive nucleus, which grips far harder — the effort suddenly multiplies. That sudden jump is the signal that a new shell has started, so counting to the jump tells you how many outer electrons there are.
定义必须一字不差：The definition must be exact:
  • 第一电离能：从一摩尔气态原子中各移走一个电子，形成一摩尔气态 1+ 离子所需的能量。First ionisation energy: the energy required to remove one electron from each atom in one mole of gaseous atoms to form one mole of gaseous 1+ ions.
  • 符号方程必须写气态符号 (g)：The symbol equation must show the state symbol (g):
    Na(g) → Na⁺(g) + e⁻ ΔH = +496 kJ mol⁻¹
  • 永远是吸热（正值）——把电子拽走当然要花力气。Always endothermic (positive) — pulling an electron away always costs energy.
  • 看大跳：钠在第 9→10 次之间暴涨，说明前 9 个还在外面（2+8），换句话说最外层只有 1 个电子 → 第 1 族。Read the jump: sodium's huge leap comes between the 9th and 10th, so nine electrons sit outside (2 + 8) and the outer shell holds just 1 electron → Group 1.
两个高频丢分点：① 忘了写 (g)；② 把第 N 次电离能当成「移走 N 个电子的总能量」——它是移走第 N 个（已经帯 (N−1)+ 的离子再多失一个）。Two frequent lost marks: ① forgetting the (g) state symbol; ② thinking the Nth ionisation energy removes N electrons — it removes the Nth one, from an ion that already carries (N−1)+.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: The large increase between the 9th and 10th ionisation energies shows that the 10th electron is removed from an inner shell, closer to the nucleus and less shielded, so sodium has one electron in its outer shell and is in Group 1.
例题Example
某元素的逐级电离能（kJ mol⁻¹）为：578、1817、2745、11577、14842…… 判断它在第几族，并说明理由。An element has successive ionisation energies (kJ mol⁻¹): 578, 1817, 2745, 11577, 14842… Deduce its group and explain.
看落差：2745 → 11577，是第 3 次到第 4 次之间暴涨（约 4 倍）。Look at the gap: from 2745 to 11577 is the big leap (about 4×), between the 3rd and 4th. 说明前 3 个电子在外层，第 4 个开始深入内层。So the first three electrons are in the outer shell and the 4th comes from an inner shell. 最外层 3 个电子 → 第 3 族（这就是铝 Al，1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p¹）。Three outer electrons → Group 3 (this is aluminium, 1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p¹).
练习Practice
先找最大的那次落差，再数它前面有几个。Find the biggest jump, then count how many come before it.

某元素逐级电离能为：900、1757、14849、21007…… (a) 它在第几族？(b) 写出推断的一句话理由。Successive ionisation energies: 900, 1757, 14849, 21007… (a) Which group? (b) Give a one-sentence reason.

点开看答案Show answer
(a) 大跳在第 2 次与第 3 次之间（1757 → 14849），所以最外层有 2 个电子，是第 2 族（这是铍 Be）。
(b) 「第 3 次电离能远大于第 2 次，说明第 3 个电子来自更靠内的电子层。」 (a) The jump falls between the 2nd and 3rd (1757 → 14849), so there are 2 outer electrons and it is in Group 2 (this is beryllium, Be).
(b) "The third ionisation energy is much larger than the second, so the third electron must be removed from an inner shell closer to the nucleus."
— 第 5 站完成 —— Stop 5 done —
6 质谱仪与相对原子质量Mass spectrometry and relative atomic mass Mass spectrum质谱
这一站要你会：看懂质谱图的横轴 m/z 与纵轴丰度，指出分子离子峰，并用它算相对原子质量 Ar。Goal: read the m/z and abundance axes, identify the molecular ion peak, and use it to calculate relative atomic mass Ar.
质谱仪其实就是一台按体重分拣熔珠的机器：先把原子打成带正电的离子，让它们在电场里起跑，再用磁场把它们甩弯。越重的越难被甩弯，跑偏得越少；于是不同质量的原子落在检测器的不同位置，形成一根根柱子。柱子越高，说明这种「体重」的原子在样品里越多。A mass spectrometer is a machine that sorts marbles by weight: atoms are ionised, accelerated by an electric field, then bent by a magnet. Heavier ions are harder to deflect, so they bend less and land in different places on the detector, giving one bar per mass. Taller bar = more atoms of that mass in the sample.
四个关键词：Four key terms:
  • m/z：质量与电荷之比。离子通常带 1+，所以 m/z 就等于它的质量数。m/z: the mass-to-charge ratio. Ions usually carry 1+, so m/z equals their mass number.
  • 分子离子峰 M⁺：整个分子失去一个电子形成的离子峰。它的 m/z 就是相对分子质量 Mr。Molecular ion peak M⁺: formed when the whole molecule loses one electron. Its m/z gives the relative molecular mass Mr.
  • 碎片峰：分子被打断后剩下的小块。教材里考得少，但看到许多小峰别慌。Fragment peaks: pieces left after the molecule breaks up. Rarely examined at AS, but don't panic when you see small peaks.
  • 计算 Ar：把每个同位素的 m/z 乘它的相对丰度，加起来再除以 100。Calculating Ar: multiply each isotope's m/z by its relative abundance, add them up, divide by 100.
算完要自检：Ar 一定落在最大与最小的同位素之间，而且一定靠近丰度最大的那个。如果算出 21.5 而三个峰是 20/21/22 且 20 占 90%，那肯定算错了。Always sanity-check: Ar must fall between the lowest and highest isotope mass and sit closest to the most abundant one. If your answer for 20/21/22 with 20 at 90% comes out at 21.5, something went wrong.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: The peak with the largest m/z value is the molecular ion peak, and its m/z value gives the relative molecular mass of the compound.
例题Example
氖的质谱给出三个峰：m/z = 20（丰度 90.9%）、21（0.3%）、22（8.8%）。计算氖的相对原子质量。The mass spectrum of neon gives three peaks: m/z = 20 (abundance 90.9%), 21 (0.3%), 22 (8.8%). Calculate the relative atomic mass of neon.
Ar = (20×90.9 + 21×0.3 + 22×8.8) / 100 = (1818 + 6.3 + 193.6) / 100 = 20.2 （1 位小数）
自检：20.2 落在 20 与 22 之间，而且很靠近 20（因为 90.9% 都是 20），合理。Sanity check: 20.2 lies between 20 and 22 and is close to 20 (which holds 90.9% of the atoms), so it is sensible.
练习Practice
丰度加起来要接近 100%，算完记得自检。Check that the abundances add to about 100%, then sanity-check the answer.

某元素的质谱峰为 m/z = 24（79%）、25（10%）、26（11%）。(a) 求它的相对原子质量；(b) 如果该元素的质子数是 12，这三个峰分别代表怎样的原子（各多少中子）？A mass spectrum has peaks at m/z = 24 (79%), 25 (10%), 26 (11%). (a) Calculate its relative atomic mass. (b) If the proton number is 12, describe the three atoms (how many neutrons each).

点开看答案Show answer
(a) Ar = (24×79 + 25×10 + 26×11)/100 = (1896 + 250 + 286)/100 = 24.3。
(b) 三个峰都是镁的同位素：中子数 = 24−12 = 12、25−12 = 13、26−12 = 14。它们质子数都是 12、电子数都是 12，所以化学性质相同。 (a) Ar = (24×79 + 25×10 + 26×11)/100 = (1896 + 250 + 286)/100 = 24.3.
(b) All three are isotopes of magnesium: neutrons = 24−12 = 12, 25−12 = 13, 26−12 = 14. All have 12 protons and 12 electrons, so their chemistry is the same.
— 第 6 站完成 —— Stop 6 done —

单元 1 小结Unit 1 summary

① 质子数决定身份，质量数决定重量；同位素是「同质子不同中子」，所以化学性质几乎一样。
② 电子按 能量最低 → 每格两条相反自旋 → 先一人一格 三条规则排布；别忘了 Cr 与 Cu 两个例外。
③ 逐级电离能的大跳告诉你外层有几个电子；质谱里最高的那个峰告诉你相对质量。① Protons decide identity, neutrons decide weight; isotopes share chemistry because they share electrons.
② Electrons are placed by three rules: lowest energy first → two per box with opposite spins → one per box before pairing; memorise the two exceptions Cr and Cu.
③ The jump in successive ionisation energies reveals the number of outer electrons; the tallest peak in a mass spectrum reveals the relative mass.

下一站最重要的一件事：原子太小了，数不清个数，所以化学家发明了一个「打包单位」——摩尔。这就是单元 2 的主题。Why the next unit matters: atoms are far too small to count, so chemists invented a bulk unit — the mole. That is Unit 2.

单元 2 · 摩尔计算：化学家的「数数单位」Unit 2 · Atoms, molecules and stoichiometry: the chemist's counting unit

CAIE 9701 Topic 2 · 7 站 · 化学的「数数单位」，后面所有计算都得靠它CAIE 9701 Topic 2 · 7 stops · the chemist's counting unit that every later calculation depends on

路线图本单元七站：先发明「数数单位」，再把它接上质量、溶液、气体、式子Seven stops: invent a counting unit, then connect it to mass, solutions, gases and formulae

  1. 为什么要发明「摩尔」：L = 6.02×10²³ mol⁻¹Why the mole exists: L = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹
  2. 相对原子质量 Ar 与相对分子质量 Mr 怎么算Relative atomic mass Ar and relative molecular mass Mr
  3. 摩尔 ↔ 质量的换算：n = m / MConverting between moles and mass: n = m / M
  4. 溶液的浓度 mol dm⁻³ 与配制标准溶液Concentration in mol dm⁻³ and making a standard solution
  5. 气体自带换算：rtp 下 1 mol 占 24 dm³The gas shortcut: 1 mol occupies 24 dm³ at rtp
  6. 实验式与分子式：从百分比到最简整数比Empirical and molecular formulae: percentages to simplest ratio
  7. 配平之后算账：限量反应物、产率与纯度After balancing: limiting reagent, yield and purity

建议：第 1、2、3 站是后面一切的地基，先把 n = m / M 用熟，再去碰溶液和气体。第 7 站是整套功夫的汇演，放在最后做。Tip: stops 1–3 are the foundation for everything else — get comfortable with n = m / M before solutions and gases. Stop 7 is where all of it comes together, so save it for last.

1 为什么要发明「摩尔」Why the mole was invented The mole & Avogadro constant摩尔与阿伏加德罗常数
这一站要你会：说出摩尔与阿伏加德罗常数的定义，用 n = N / L 在「粒子个数」与「摩尔」之间互算，并且每次都说清自己数的是什么粒子。Goal: state the definitions of the mole and the Avogadro constant, convert between particle number and moles using n = N / L, and always say which particles you are counting.
超市不会按「粒」卖米，而是按「袋」卖；铅笔按「打」卖（一打 = 12 支），打印纸按「令」卖（一令 = 500 张）。这些全是打包单位——因为单个东西太小、太便宜、数起来太费劲。
化学家面对的是更极端的情况：一个原子的直径大约只有一亿分之一厘米，一小勺水里就藏着几万亿亿个水分子，一个一个数到宇宙毁灭也数不完。于是他们发明了一个巨大的打包单位：摩尔。一摩尔就是 6.02×10²³ 个粒子，相当于把「一打」放大到天上去。
那为什么偏偏是 6.02×10²³ 这个怪数字？因为它是故意挑的：这么挑之后，一个原子的相对原子质量是几，一摩尔这种原子就刚好是几克。个数和克数，就这样被这一个数接起来了。Shops do not sell rice grain by grain, they sell it by the bag; pencils come by the dozen (12), paper by the ream (500). These are all bulk units — the single item is too small, too cheap and too tedious to count.
Chemists face a far worse version of this: an atom is about one hundred-millionth of a centimetre across, and a single spoonful of water holds trillions of trillions of molecules. Counting them one by one would outlast the universe. So they invented one huge bulk unit: the mole. One mole is 6.02 × 10²³ particles — a dozen blown up beyond imagination.
Why that odd number? Because it was chosen on purpose: chosen so that whatever an atom's relative atomic mass is, one mole of those atoms weighs exactly that many grams. This one number is the bridge between counting and weighing.
四个必须记牢的点：Four points to memorise:
  • 摩尔（mol）是「物质的量」的单位。1 mol 任何东西 = 6.02×10²³ 个该东西。The mole (mol) is the unit of amount of substance. 1 mol of anything = 6.02 × 10²³ of those things.
  • 阿伏加德罗常数 L = 6.02×10²³ mol⁻¹。注意它有单位（每摩尔多少个），写答案时别把单位丢了。The Avogadro constant L = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹. It has a unit (particles per mole) — don't drop it in an answer.
  • 换算公式：n = N / L，反过来 N = n × L。这里的 N 是粒子个数（没有单位）。The conversion: n = N / L, and backwards N = n × L. Here N is the number of particles (no unit).
  • 一定要说清「什么的摩尔」。1 mol H2O 里有 1 mol 水分子，但有 2 mol 氢原子、1 mol 氧原子，加起来 3 mol 原子。Always say "moles of what". 1 mol of H2O holds 1 mol of water molecules, but 2 mol of hydrogen atoms and 1 mol of oxygen atoms — 3 mol of atoms in total.
两个高频丢分点：① 写 L 时忘了 mol⁻¹ 这个单位；② 题目问「多少个原子」，你却只算了分子的个数——记得乘化学式右下角的下标。Two frequent lost marks: ① forgetting the mol⁻¹ unit on L; ② being asked for atoms but only counting molecules — remember to multiply by the subscript in the formula.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: One mole of a substance is the amount of substance that contains 6.02 × 10²³ particles of that substance. The Avogadro constant, L, is 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹. When using the mole, the particles being counted must always be stated.
例题Example
某样品中有 1.204×10²⁴ 个 CO2 分子。(a) 这是多少摩尔二氧化碳？(b) 其中有多少摩尔氧原子？A sample contains 1.204 × 10²⁴ molecules of CO2. (a) How many moles of carbon dioxide is this? (b) How many moles of oxygen atoms does it contain?
① 用 n = N / L 把「个数」换成「摩尔」：① use n = N / L to turn a count into moles:
n = N / L = 1.204×10²⁴ / 6.02×10²³ = 2.00 mol CO₂ （3 位有效数字）
② 每个 CO2 里有 2 个氧原子，所以氧原子是它的 2 倍：② every CO2 holds 2 oxygen atoms, so oxygen is double:
n(O 原子) = 2 × 2.00 = 4.00 mol
③ 顺手自检：原子总共 3 × 2.00 = 6.00 mol（1 mol C + 2 mol O），跟化学式对得上。③ quick check: atoms in total = 3 × 2.00 = 6.00 mol (1 mol C + 2 mol O), which matches the formula.
练习Practice
先算分子的摩尔数，再乘下标拿到原子，最后乘 L 换回个数。Find moles of molecules first, then multiply by the subscript for atoms, then multiply by L to get a count again.

某杯水里有 3.01×10²³ 个 H2O 分子。(a) 是多少摩尔水分子？(b) 含多少摩尔氢原子？(c) 含多少个氢原子？A glass of water contains 3.01 × 10²³ molecules of H2O. (a) How many moles of water molecules? (b) How many moles of hydrogen atoms? (c) How many hydrogen atoms?

点开看答案Show answer
(a) n = 3.01×10²³ / 6.02×10²³ = 0.500 mol 水分子。
(b) 每个 H2O 有 2 个 H，所以 n(H) = 2 × 0.500 = 1.00 mol。
(c) N = n × L = 1.00 × 6.02×10²³ = 6.02×10²³ 个氢原子。看，刚好是原来分子数的两倍——这就是「乘下标」的效果。 (a) n = 3.01 × 10²³ / 6.02 × 10²³ = 0.500 mol of water molecules.
(b) each H2O carries 2 H atoms, so n(H) = 2 × 0.500 = 1.00 mol.
(c) N = n × L = 1.00 × 6.02 × 10²³ = 6.02 × 10²³ hydrogen atoms — exactly twice the original molecule count, which is the "multiply by the subscript" effect.
— 第 1 站完成 —— Stop 1 done —
2 相对原子质量 Ar 与相对分子质量 MrRelative atomic mass Ar and relative molecular mass Mr Relative masses相对质量
这一站要你会：从周期表读出 Ar，把化学式里所有原子的 Ar 加起来得到 Mr（含点乘的结晶水合物也要会），并且记住这些量没有单位。Goal: read Ar from the periodic table, add up every atom in a formula to get Mr (including hydrated salts with the dot), and remember that these quantities have no unit.
把化学式想成一盒乐高：每个积木块上都印着它自己的重量（这就是 Ar，周期表上那个数），而整个盒子的总重量就是 Mr。你要做的只是一件事——数清楚每种积木各有几块，然后全部加起来。
式子中间那个「点」（比如 CuSO4·5H2O）看着唬人，其实意思很生活化：硫酸铜晶体里顺便夹带了 5 个水分子。算总重量时，把这 5 个水分子整个搬进去加就行，一个都不能漏。
还有一条：相对量没有单位。它是「跟碳-12 的十二分之一比出来的倍数」，是个比值，就像「我比你高 1.2 倍」那个 1.2 没有单位一样。Think of a formula as a box of Lego: every brick has its own weight printed on it (that is Ar, the number on the periodic table), and the weight of the whole box is Mr. There is only one job: count how many of each brick, then add them all up.
That dot in the middle (as in CuSO4·5H2O) looks scary but means something homely: the copper sulfate crystal has five water molecules tucked inside it. When you add up the total, just carry those five waters in as well — miss none of them.
And one more rule: relative masses have no unit. They are ratios measured against one-twelfth of carbon-12, like saying "I am 1.2 times your height" — the 1.2 carries no unit.
定义与算法：Definitions and method:
  • Ar（相对原子质量）：一个原子相对于碳-12 质量的十二分之一的质量；无单位，直接从周期表读。Ar (relative atomic mass): the mass of an atom relative to one-twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom; no unit, read it from the periodic table.
  • Mr（相对分子质量 / 相对式量）：把化学式中所有原子的 Ar 加起来；无单位。Mr (relative molecular / formula mass): the sum of the Ar values of every atom in the formula; no unit.
  • 括号右下角的下标，括号里每一个原子都要乘：Ca(OH)2 里有 2 个 O 和 2 个 H。A subscript after a bracket multiplies every atom inside: Ca(OH)2 contains 2 O and 2 H.
  • 点乘「·」表示结晶水：CuSO4·5H2O 要加上 5 份完整的 H2O。The dot means water of crystallisation: CuSO4·5H2O needs five whole H2O added on.
元素ElementHCNONaMgAlSClCaFeCu
Ar（记住它）Ar (learn it)1.012.014.016.023.024.327.032.135.540.155.863.5
最容易错的三处：① 给相对质量写上 g（它们没有单位）；② 括号外的下标只乘了第一个原子；③ 结晶水合物忘记加那几份水。算完可以反向自检：Mr 应该跟化学式里原子个数「感觉对得上」。Three classic slips: ① putting g after a relative mass (they have no unit); ② applying the subscript outside a bracket to only the first atom; ③ forgetting the waters in a hydrated salt. Sanity-check afterwards: the Mr should "feel right" for the size of the formula.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: Relative atomic mass is the mass of one atom of an element relative to one twelfth of the mass of an atom of carbon-12. Relative molecular mass is the sum of the relative atomic masses of all the atoms in the formula; it has no unit.
例题Example
计算 CuSO4·5H2O 的相对式量（Ar：H 1.0，O 16.0，S 32.1，Cu 63.5）。Calculate the relative formula mass of CuSO4·5H2O (Ar: H 1.0, O 16.0, S 32.1, Cu 63.5).
① 先算无水部分 CuSO4：① deal with the anhydrous part CuSO4 first:
CuSO₄ = 63.5 + 32.1 + (4 × 16.0) = 63.5 + 32.1 + 64.0 = 159.6
② 再算 5 份结晶水：② then the five waters of crystallisation:
5H₂O = 5 × (2 × 1.0 + 16.0) = 5 × 18.0 = 90.0
③ 加起来：Mr = 159.6 + 90.0 = 249.6（无单位）。③ add them: Mr = 159.6 + 90.0 = 249.6 (no unit).
练习Practice
(a) 括号里的原子别忘了乘 2；(b) 记得加十份水。(a) don't forget to double everything inside the bracket; (b) remember the ten waters.

求下列两物的相对式量：(a) (NH4)2SO4；(b) Na2CO3·10H2O。（Ar：H 1.0，C 12.0，N 14.0，O 16.0，Na 23.0，S 32.1）Find the relative formula mass of: (a) (NH4)2SO4; (b) Na2CO3·10H2O. (Ar: H 1.0, C 12.0, N 14.0, O 16.0, Na 23.0, S 32.1)

点开看答案Show answer
(a) N：2 × 14.0 = 28.0；H：8 × 1.0 = 8.0；S：32.1；O：4 × 16.0 = 64.0 → Mr = 132.1。
(b) Na2CO3 = 2 × 23.0 + 12.0 + 3 × 16.0 = 106.0；10H2O = 10 × 18.0 = 180.0 → Mr = 286.0。两个答案都不带单位。 (a) N: 2 × 14.0 = 28.0; H: 8 × 1.0 = 8.0; S: 32.1; O: 4 × 16.0 = 64.0 → Mr = 132.1.
(b) Na2CO3 = 2 × 23.0 + 12.0 + 3 × 16.0 = 106.0; 10H2O = 10 × 18.0 = 180.0 → Mr = 286.0. Neither answer carries a unit.
— 第 2 站完成 —— Stop 2 done —
3 摩尔 ↔ 质量的换算Converting between moles and mass n = m / M摩尔与质量
这一站要你会：用 n = m / M 在质量、摩尔、摩尔质量三者之间互算，并且把单位对整齐（g 配 g mol⁻¹）。Goal: convert freely between mass, moles and molar mass using n = m / M, keeping the units consistent (grams with g mol⁻¹).
这其实是买菜的公式：总价 = 单价 × 数量。化学里「总价」是质量 m，「数量」是摩尔 n，而「单价」就是摩尔质量 M——它告诉你一摩尔这种东西值多少克。
妙处在于：M 的数值就等于 Mr，只是加了单位。比如 CaCO3 的 Mr 是 100.1，那么它的摩尔质量就是 100.1 g mol⁻¹——一摩尔碳酸钙正好 100.1 克。上一站你算的「相对式量」，到这儿直接变成「每摩尔多少克」。
唯一要小心的就是单位：公式要求 m 用克。题目给你 0.25 kg，你得先乘 1000 变成 250 g；给你 250 mg，你得先除 1000 变成 0.250 g。单位没换就代公式，是这一站最常见的翻车方式。This is really the shopping formula: total price = price per item × number of items. In chemistry the "total price" is the mass m, the "number of items" is the moles n, and the "price per item" is the molar mass M — it tells you how many grams one mole of this stuff costs.
The beautiful part: the number in M is just Mr with a unit bolted on. CaCO3 has Mr = 100.1, so its molar mass is 100.1 g mol⁻¹ — one mole of calcium carbonate weighs exactly 100.1 g. The relative formula mass you worked out last stop turns straight into grams per mole here.
The one thing to watch is units: the formula wants m in grams. If the question gives 0.25 kg you multiply by 1000 first; if it gives 250 mg you divide by 1000 first. Putting un-converted numbers into the formula is the classic way to crash this stop.
三角里的三个量：The three quantities in the triangle:
  • n = m / M（求摩尔）；m = n × M（求质量）；M = m / n（求摩尔质量）。n = m / M (find moles); m = n × M (find mass); M = m / n (find molar mass).
  • M 的单位是 g mol⁻¹，数值等于上一站算的 Mr。写答案时单位别省。M has the unit g mol⁻¹ and its number equals the Mr from last stop. Never drop the unit in an answer.
  • 换算关系：1 t = 106 g，1 kg = 1000 g，1 g = 1000 mg。题目给什么，先换成 g 再说。Conversions: 1 t = 106 g, 1 kg = 1000 g, 1 g = 1000 mg. Whatever the question gives you, turn it into grams first.
  • 答案的精度：没有特别说明时保留 3 位有效数字，比如 0.200 mol、25.0 g。Precision: unless told otherwise, give 3 significant figures — 0.200 mol, 25.0 g and so on.
三个陷阱：① 把 kg、mg、t 直接代进公式；② 把 M 写成「相对分子质量」而漏掉 g mol⁻¹；③ 计算器给出一长串数字就照抄（0.200 不是 0.1999998）。另外：只有纯净物才能这么算，含杂质的样品要等第 7 站处理。Three traps: ① feeding kg, mg or tonnes straight into the formula; ② calling M a "relative molecular mass" and dropping g mol⁻¹; ③ copying a long decimal from the calculator (0.200, not 0.1999998). Also: this only works for pure substances — impure samples wait until stop 7.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: The amount of substance, n, in moles is found by dividing the mass in grams by the molar mass in g mol⁻¹. The molar mass has the same numerical value as the relative formula mass, but has the unit g mol⁻¹.
例题Example
8.0 g NaOH 是多少摩尔？（Ar：H 1.0，O 16.0，Na 23.0）How many moles are in 8.0 g of NaOH? (Ar: H 1.0, O 16.0, Na 23.0)
① 先算摩尔质量（数值 = Mr，单位是 g mol⁻¹）：① find the molar mass first (number = Mr, unit g mol⁻¹):
M(NaOH) = 23.0 + 16.0 + 1.0 = 40.0 g mol⁻¹
② 代公式（质量已经是 g，单位对齐）：② put it into the formula (the mass is already in g, so the units match):
n = m / M = 8.0 / 40.0 = 0.200 mol
③ 倒推自检：0.200 × 40.0 = 8.0 g，回到原数，说明没算错。③ check backwards: 0.200 × 40.0 = 8.0 g, back where we started, so it is right.
练习Practice
(a) 用 m = n × M；(b) 先把质量单位确认好，再除。(a) use m = n × M; (b) check the mass unit, then divide.

(a) 0.250 mol CaCO3 的质量是多少克？(b) 5.30 g Na2CO3 是多少摩尔？（Ar：C 12.0，O 16.0，Na 23.0，Ca 40.1）(a) What is the mass of 0.250 mol of CaCO3? (b) How many moles are in 5.30 g of Na2CO3? (Ar: C 12.0, O 16.0, Na 23.0, Ca 40.1)

点开看答案Show answer
(a) M(CaCO3) = 40.1 + 12.0 + 3 × 16.0 = 100.1 g mol⁻¹，m = 0.250 × 100.1 = 25.0 g（3 位有效数字）。
(b) M(Na2CO3) = 2 × 23.0 + 12.0 + 3 × 16.0 = 106.0 g mol⁻¹，n = 5.30 / 106.0 = 0.0500 mol。注意末尾的 0 不能省——它代表精度。 (a) M(CaCO3) = 40.1 + 12.0 + 3 × 16.0 = 100.1 g mol⁻¹, so m = 0.250 × 100.1 = 25.0 g (3 s.f.).
(b) M(Na2CO3) = 2 × 23.0 + 12.0 + 3 × 16.0 = 106.0 g mol⁻¹, so n = 5.30 / 106.0 = 0.0500 mol. Keep that trailing zero — it shows the precision.
— 第 3 站完成 —— Stop 3 done —
4 溶液的浓度与配制标准溶液Concentration and making a standard solution Concentration浓度与定容
这一站要你会：用 c = n / V 算浓度（V 必须是 dm³），会把 mol dm⁻³ 换算成 g dm⁻³，并能说出配制标准溶液的完整步骤。Goal: calculate concentration with c = n / V (V must be in dm³), convert mol dm⁻³ into g dm⁻³, and list the full steps for making a standard solution.
浓度就是糖水有多甜：同样一杯水，放一勺糖和放五勺糖，甜度完全不同。化学里我们不用「勺」而用摩尔：浓度告诉你每 1 dm³ 溶液里溶着多少摩尔的溶质。
这里有一个所有人都踩过的坑：公式里的 V 必须是 dm³，而量筒和容量瓶上写的往往是 cm³。1 dm³ = 1000 cm³，所以见到 250 cm³ 就先除以 1000，写成 0.250 dm³ 再代公式。
容量瓶是个很「轴」的仪器：它只有一条刻度线，意思是它只能量出一个固定体积（常见 100 cm³、250 cm³、1000 cm³）。你把液面加到那条线，体积就精确了；多加一滴，整瓶就废了，只能倒掉重配——因为吸出来的同时也会吸走溶质，浓度就不准了。Concentration is just how sweet the sugar water is: one cup of water with one spoon of sugar tastes nothing like one with five spoons. Chemistry counts in moles rather than spoons: concentration tells you how many moles of solute are dissolved in every 1 dm³ of solution.
Here is the pothole everyone falls into: V in the formula must be in dm³, while measuring cylinders and flasks are labelled in cm³. Since 1 dm³ = 1000 cm³, turn 250 cm³ into 0.250 dm³ before you touch the formula.
A volumetric flask is a stubborn instrument: it has only one mark, meaning it measures one fixed volume (commonly 100 cm³, 250 cm³, 1000 cm³). Bring the liquid up to that line and the volume is exact; go one drop past it and the whole flask is ruined — you cannot suck the excess out, because you would remove solute as well and the concentration would be wrong.
公式与步骤：Formula and steps:
  • c = n / V，单位是 mol dm⁻³；反过来 n = c × V（V 用 dm³）。c = n / V in mol dm⁻³; rearranged, n = c × V (V in dm³).
  • 1 dm³ = 1000 cm³ = 1 升。cm³ 换 dm³ 一律 ÷ 1000。1 dm³ = 1000 cm³ = 1 litre. To go from cm³ to dm³, always divide by 1000.
  • 质量浓度（g dm⁻³）= c × M：把「每升多少摩尔」乘上「每摩尔多少克」，每升多少克就出来了。Mass concentration (g dm⁻³) = c × M: moles per litre times grams per mole gives grams per litre.
  • 配制标准溶液五步：称量 → 用少量水溶解 → 全部转入容量瓶（烧杯和玻璃棒要洗，洗液也要倒进去）→ 加水定容到刻度线 → 塞紧反复摇匀。Five steps for a standard solution: weigh → dissolve in a little water → transfer everything into the flask (rinse the beaker and rod, and pour the rinsings in too) → make up to the mark with water → stopper and invert repeatedly to mix.
三个必扣分的地方：① 把 25.0 cm³ 直接当 25.0 代进公式；② 液面超过刻度线后想把多余的水吸出来（只能重配）；③ 把容量瓶拿去加热，或者长期把溶液存在里面（它只负责「配」，不负责「装」）。Three guaranteed lost marks: ① using 25.0 cm³ as 25.0 in the formula; ② trying to pipette the excess away after overshooting the mark (you must start again); ③ heating a volumetric flask or storing solution in it (it is for making solutions, not keeping them).
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: Concentration is the amount of solute, in moles, dissolved in 1 dm³ of solution: c = n / V, where V is measured in dm³. A standard solution is made by weighing the solute, dissolving it, transferring it to a volumetric flask and making up to the graduation mark.
例题Example
把 5.30 g Na2CO3 溶于水，配成 250 cm³ 溶液。(a) 求浓度（mol dm⁻³）；(b) 求质量浓度（g dm⁻³）。5.30 g of Na2CO3 is dissolved and made up to 250 cm³ of solution. (a) Find the concentration in mol dm⁻³. (b) Find the mass concentration in g dm⁻³.
① 先把质量变成摩尔：① turn the mass into moles first:
M(Na₂CO₃) = 2 × 23.0 + 12.0 + 3 × 16.0 = 106.0 g mol⁻¹ n = 5.30 / 106.0 = 0.0500 mol
② 把体积换成 dm³（关键一步）：250 cm³ = 0.250 dm³。② convert the volume into dm³ (the key step): 250 cm³ = 0.250 dm³.
c = n / V = 0.0500 / 0.250 = 0.200 mol dm⁻³
③ 质量浓度 = 浓度 × 摩尔质量：③ mass concentration = concentration × molar mass:
0.200 × 106.0 = 21.2 g dm⁻³
练习Practice
(a) 用 n = c × V，记得先把 500 cm³ 换成 dm³；(b) 再乘摩尔质量。(a) use n = c × V, converting 500 cm³ to dm³ first; (b) then multiply by the molar mass.

一瓶 0.100 mol dm⁻³ 的 NaOH 溶液，取出 500 cm³。(a) 这 500 cm³ 里含多少摩尔 NaOH？(b) 该溶液的质量浓度是多少 g dm⁻³？（Ar：H 1.0，O 16.0，Na 23.0）500 cm³ of a 0.100 mol dm⁻³ NaOH solution is used. (a) How many moles of NaOH does it contain? (b) What is the mass concentration in g dm⁻³? (Ar: H 1.0, O 16.0, Na 23.0)

点开看答案Show answer
(a) V = 500 / 1000 = 0.500 dm³，n = 0.100 × 0.500 = 0.0500 mol。
(b) M(NaOH) = 40.0 g mol⁻¹，质量浓度 = 0.100 × 40.0 = 4.00 g dm⁻³。注意：浓度是溶液整体的性质，取走一半，浓度不变，只有摩尔数变少。 (a) V = 500 / 1000 = 0.500 dm³, so n = 0.100 × 0.500 = 0.0500 mol.
(b) M(NaOH) = 40.0 g mol⁻¹, so mass concentration = 0.100 × 40.0 = 4.00 g dm⁻³. Note: concentration is a property of the whole solution — pour half away and the concentration stays the same, only the number of moles drops.
— 第 4 站完成 —— Stop 4 done —
5 气体自带换算：24 dm³The gas shortcut: 24 dm³ per mole Molar gas volume气体摩尔体积
这一站要你会：说出阿伏加德罗定律，记住 rtp 下气体摩尔体积 24 dm³ mol⁻¹，并用 n = V / 24 或 n = V / 24000 计算。Goal: state Avogadro's law, remember the molar gas volume 24 dm³ mol⁻¹ at rtp, and calculate with n = V / 24 or n = V / 24000.
两个同样大的行李箱，一个装满乒乓球，一个装满篮球——直觉上你以为「球小的那个装得多」。但气体不吃这一套：气体分子之间的距离，比分子本身大得多，所以分子是大是小几乎不影响能装多少。换句话说，只要温度、压强、体积一样，装进去的分子个数就一样——这就是阿伏加德罗定律。
于是化学家干脆把这条定律做成一个「换算按钮」：在室温室压（rtp）下，1 mol 任何气体都占 24 dm³。所以气体题里，你不用先算质量再算摩尔——体积本身就是摩尔，除以 24 就完事。
但别忘了另一头：虽然摩尔数一样，质量可以差很远。24 dm³ 的氢气只有 2.0 g，24 dm³ 的二氧化碳却有 44.0 g。个数相同、体重不同，这就是图上两个盒子想告诉你的事。Two suitcases of the same size, one full of table-tennis balls and one full of basketballs — your instinct says "the one with small balls holds more". Gases do not play by that rule: the gaps between gas molecules are far bigger than the molecules themselves, so molecular size barely matters. In other words, same temperature, same pressure, same volume means same number of molecules — that is Avogadro's law.
Chemists turned that law into a shortcut button: at room temperature and pressure (rtp), 1 mol of any gas occupies 24 dm³. So in gas questions you never need mass first — the volume is already moles, just divide by 24.
Do not forget the other end though: equal moles can mean very unequal masses. 24 dm³ of hydrogen is only 2.0 g, while 24 dm³ of carbon dioxide is 44.0 g. Same count, different weight — exactly what the two boxes in the diagram show.
必须记住的三条：Three things to remember:
  • 阿伏加德罗定律：同温同压下，相同体积的任何气体含有相同数量的分子（摩尔数相同）。Avogadro's law: equal volumes of all gases, at the same temperature and pressure, contain the same number of molecules (the same number of moles).
  • rtp 下气体摩尔体积 Vm = 24 dm³ mol⁻¹；n = V(dm³) / 24，或者 n = V(cm³) / 24000。Molar gas volume at rtp, Vm = 24 dm³ mol⁻¹; n = V(dm³) / 24, or n = V(cm³) / 24000.
  • 只对气体成立。固体、液体的体积由粒子自身大小决定，不能这么算。Gases only. The volume of a solid or liquid is fixed by the size of its particles, so this shortcut does not apply.
  • 单位换算仍是老大难：1 dm³ = 1000 cm³，480 cm³ = 0.480 dm³。Units are still the usual trouble: 1 dm³ = 1000 cm³, so 480 cm³ = 0.480 dm³.
两个常错点：① 把 24 用在固体或液体上；② 用 dm³ 的数去除 24000（应该是：dm³ 除 24，cm³ 除 24000，选一个就行，别混）。另外题目若特别说明「不是 rtp」就不能用 24。Two common errors: ① using 24 for a solid or a liquid; ② dividing a dm³ value by 24000 (dm³ goes with 24, cm³ goes with 24000 — pick one and stay consistent). And if the question states conditions other than rtp, the 24 does not apply.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: Avogadro's law states that equal volumes of gases, at the same temperature and pressure, contain equal numbers of molecules. At room temperature and pressure one mole of any gas occupies 24 dm³, so n = V / 24 when V is in dm³.
例题Example
rtp 下有 120 cm³ 的 CO2 气体。(a) 它的摩尔数是多少？(b) 质量是多少克？A sample of CO2 occupies 120 cm³ at rtp. (a) How many moles is this? (b) What is its mass?
① 体积是 cm³，直接用 24000：① the volume is in cm³, so use 24000 directly:
n = V / 24000 = 120 / 24000 = 5.00 × 10⁻³ mol （即 0.00500 mol）
② 再用 m = n × M，M(CO2) = 12.0 + 2 × 16.0 = 44.0 g mol⁻¹：② then m = n × M with M(CO2) = 12.0 + 2 × 16.0 = 44.0 g mol⁻¹:
m = 5.00 × 10⁻³ × 44.0 = 0.220 g
③ 自检：120 cm³ 只有 24 dm³ 的二百分之一，质量 44.0 g 的二百分之一约 0.22 g，对得上。③ sanity check: 120 cm³ is one two-hundredth of 24 dm³, and one two-hundredth of 44.0 g is about 0.22 g — that matches.
练习Practice
先用 24 算出 dm³，再乘 1000 变 cm³；质量用 m = n × M。Use 24 to get dm³, then × 1000 for cm³; find the mass with m = n × M.

rtp 下有 0.0250 mol 某气体。(a) 它占多大体积（用 cm³ 作答）？(b) 若该气体是 O2，质量是多少？A sample contains 0.0250 mol of gas at rtp. (a) What volume does it occupy, in cm³? (b) If the gas is O2, what is its mass?

点开看答案Show answer
(a) V = n × 24 = 0.0250 × 24 = 0.600 dm³ = 600 cm³。
(b) M(O2) = 2 × 16.0 = 32.0 g mol⁻¹，m = 0.0250 × 32.0 = 0.800 g。注意 (a) 问的是 cm³，多一步 ×1000 别忘了。 (a) V = n × 24 = 0.0250 × 24 = 0.600 dm³ = 600 cm³.
(b) M(O2) = 2 × 16.0 = 32.0 g mol⁻¹, so m = 0.0250 × 32.0 = 0.800 g. Note that (a) asks for cm³ — don't forget that extra × 1000.
— 第 5 站完成 —— Stop 5 done —
6 实验式与分子式Empirical and molecular formulae Empirical formula实验式与分子式
这一站要你会：从质量百分比（或燃烧数据）算出实验式，再由 Mr 反推分子式；并且知道「除完不是整数时要同乘」。Goal: work out an empirical formula from percentage composition (or combustion data), then use Mr to find the molecular formula — including the case where the ratio must be multiplied up.
实验式就是菜谱的最简配比：做蛋糕时面粉:糖:鸡蛋 = 1:2:1，这是配比；但你今天到底用了多少面粉，取决于你做多大的蛋糕。实验式是配比，分子式是实际用量。
怎么从百分比得到配比？试试这个小魔法：既然都是百分比，那就干脆假设样品一共 100 g——于是「40% 的碳」立刻变成「40 g 的碳」，可以直接除 Ar 了。除完拿到的是摩尔比（因为摩尔才代表个数），最后把所有数都除以最小的那个，就得到「最小的一份是多少」。
有时除完会得到 1 : 1.5 这种半截数——这时别慌，也别四舍五入，而是全体同乘 2 变成 2 : 3。看到 .33 或 .67 就同乘 3，看到 .25 或 .75 就同乘 4。An empirical formula is a recipe in its simplest ratio: flour : sugar : egg = 1 : 2 : 1 is the ratio, but how much flour you actually use depends on how big a cake you bake. The empirical formula is the ratio; the molecular formula is the actual amount.
How do you get a ratio from percentages? Here is the trick: since everything is a percentage, just assume the sample weighs exactly 100 g — "40% carbon" instantly becomes "40 g of carbon", ready to divide by Ar. What you get is a ratio of moles (moles mean actual numbers of atoms), and dividing every number by the smallest one tells you how big the smallest portion is.
Sometimes you end up with something like 1 : 1.5. Do not panic and do not round it off — multiply everything by 2 to get 2 : 3. A .33 or .67 means multiply by 3; a .25 or .75 means multiply by 4.
三步走 + 一个反推：Three steps plus one reverse step:
  • ① 假设共 100 g，百分比直接当克数用（或直接拿题目给的质量）。① Assume 100 g, so each percentage becomes a mass in grams (or just use the masses the question gives).
  • ② 各除以 Ar —— 从「质量」跨到「摩尔」，也就是个数之比。② Divide each by Ar — that carries you from mass across to moles, which is a ratio of numbers of atoms.
  • ③ 全部除以最小的那个；如果结果不是整数（出现 .5、.33、.25），就全体同乘 2、3 或 4，凑成整数。③ Divide everything by the smallest; if the result is not whole (a .5, .33 or .25 appears), multiply all of them by 2, 3 or 4 to make them whole.
  • 反推分子式：先算实验式的式量，再用 n = Mr / 式量(实验式)，n 必须是整数；分子式 = (实验式)n。Back to the molecular formula: find the mass of the empirical formula, then n = Mr / empirical-formula mass; n must be a whole number and the molecular formula is (empirical formula)n.
三个高频错误：① 忘记「除以最小的」那一步；② 把 1.99 当成 1.9 而不是 2（摩尔比要宽容地四舍五入）；③ 把实验式直接当成分子式交上去——一定要先用 Mr 检查倍数。Three frequent mistakes: ① skipping the "divide by the smallest" step; ② treating 1.99 as 1.9 rather than 2 (round mole ratios generously); ③ handing in the empirical formula as if it were the molecular formula — always check the multiple using Mr.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: The empirical formula is the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms of each element in a compound. The molecular formula shows the actual number of atoms of each element in one molecule, and is a whole-number multiple of the empirical formula.
例题Example
某化合物含 C 40.0%、H 6.7%、O 53.3%，其 Mr = 60.0。求它的实验式与分子式。A compound contains 40.0% C, 6.7% H and 53.3% O, and has Mr = 60.0. Find its empirical and molecular formulae.
① 假设共 100 g，各除以 Ar：① assume 100 g and divide each by Ar:
C: 40.0 / 12.0 = 3.33 H: 6.7 / 1.0 = 6.70 O: 53.3 / 16.0 = 3.33
② 全部除以最小的 3.33：② divide everything by the smallest, 3.33:
C : H : O = 1 : 2.01 : 1 ≈ 1 : 2 : 1 实验式 = CH₂O
③ 用 Mr 反推倍数：式量(CH2O) = 12.0 + 2.0 + 16.0 = 30.0，n = 60.0 / 30.0 = 2。③ use Mr to find the multiple: formula mass of CH2O = 12.0 + 2.0 + 16.0 = 30.0, so n = 60.0 / 30.0 = 2.
分子式 = (CH₂O)₂ = C₂H₄O₂
练习Practice
除完最小得到 1 : 1.5，记得全体同乘 2。Dividing by the smallest gives 1 : 1.5 — remember to double everything.

某铁的氧化物含 Fe 70.0%、O 30.0%。(a) 求它的实验式；(b) 若它的式量为 159.6，求它的分子式（化学式）。（Ar：O 16.0，Fe 55.8）An oxide of iron contains 70.0% Fe and 30.0% O. (a) Find its empirical formula. (b) If its relative formula mass is 159.6, find its molecular formula. (Ar: O 16.0, Fe 55.8)

点开看答案Show answer
(a) Fe：70.0 / 55.8 = 1.25；O：30.0 / 16.0 = 1.875。除以最小的 1.25 → 1 : 1.5。出现 .5，全体同乘 2 → 2 : 3，所以实验式是 Fe2O3。
(b) 式量(Fe2O3) = 2 × 55.8 + 3 × 16.0 = 111.6 + 48.0 = 159.6，n = 159.6 / 159.6 = 1，所以分子式就是 Fe2O3——倍数可以是 1，这很正常。 (a) Fe: 70.0 / 55.8 = 1.25; O: 30.0 / 16.0 = 1.875. Dividing by the smallest, 1.25, gives 1 : 1.5. A .5 appears, so double everything → 2 : 3, and the empirical formula is Fe2O3.
(b) formula mass of Fe2O3 = 2 × 55.8 + 3 × 16.0 = 111.6 + 48.0 = 159.6, so n = 159.6 / 159.6 = 1 and the molecular formula is simply Fe2O3 — a multiple of 1 is perfectly normal.
— 第 6 站完成 —— Stop 6 done —
7 配平之后算账：限量、产率与纯度After balancing: limiting reagent, yield and purity Reacting masses & yield反应质量与产率
这一站要你会：配平方程式后按「量价比」找出限量反应物，用它算理论产量，再算百分产率与百分纯度，并能解释产率为何低于 100%。Goal: after balancing, use the mole ratio to find the limiting reagent, use it to find the theoretical yield, then calculate percentage yield and percentage purity — and explain why yield falls below 100%.
这一站其实是做三明治的账。配方是：2 片面包 + 1 片奶酪 → 1 个三明治。现在冰箱里有 10 片面包和 3 片奶酪——奶酪先用完，它就是限量原料；不管还剩多少面包，你最多只能做出 3 个三明治。化学里一模一样：先配平方程式拿到配比，再看谁先用完，然后一切都以那个「先用完的」为准。
现实永远比账本差一点：做出来的三明治可能掉在地上、可能被你偷吃一口、可能烤糊了。这就是产率——实际拿到的除以理论上应该拿到的。
还有一种是原料不干净：你买的那袋面粉里掺了别的粉，能做成面包的只有其中一部分。这就是纯度——纯的部分除以样品总质量。两个百分数都很好记：实际 ÷ 理论、纯的 ÷ 总的。This stop is really the accounts for making sandwiches. The recipe: 2 slices of bread + 1 slice of cheese → 1 sandwich. The fridge holds 10 slices of bread and 3 of cheese — the cheese runs out first, so it is the limiting ingredient; however much bread is left, you can make at most 3 sandwiches. Chemistry works exactly the same way: balance the equation to get the ratio, see which reactant runs out first, and everything from then on follows that one.
Reality always falls a little short of the ledger: a sandwich may hit the floor, may get nibbled, may burn. That is the yield — what you actually got divided by what you should have got.
And sometimes the starting material is dirty: the bag of flour has something else mixed in, so only part of it can become bread. That is the purity — pure part divided by total sample. Both percentages are easy to remember: actual ÷ theoretical and pure ÷ total.
主干四步 + 两条支路：Four main steps plus two branches:
  • ① 配平方程式——没配平就没有正确的配比，后面全废。① Balance the equation — no balancing means no correct ratio, and everything after it collapses.
  • ② 把所有已知量都换成摩尔（质量用 n = m / M，溶液用 n = c × V，气体用 n = V / 24）。② Turn every known quantity into moles (mass via n = m / M, solutions via n = c × V, gases via n = V / 24).
  • ③ 找限量反应物：把各自的摩尔数除以方程式里的系数，最小的那个就是限量的；另一个过量。③ Find the limiting reagent: divide each mole value by its coefficient in the equation; the smallest result is the limiting one and the other is in excess.
  • ④ 只用限量的那个算产物（按系数比）。过量物剩余 = 初始 − 已反应。④ Calculate the product from the limiting reagent only (using the coefficient ratio). Excess left over = initial − reacted.
  • 百分产率 = 实际产量 / 理论产量 × 100；百分纯度 = 纯物质质量 / 样品质量 × 100。Percentage yield = actual / theoretical × 100; percentage purity = pure mass / sample mass × 100.
  • 产率为何永远低于 100%：有副反应（原料走了别的路）、反应可逆（没进行到底）、转移与过滤时有损失、产物还没干透或含杂质。Why yield is always below 100%: side reactions (reactant takes a different path), reversible reactions (never go to completion), losses during transfer and filtration, and product that is still wet or impure.
三个致命错误：① 拿过量的那个去算产量（必须用限量的）；② 忘记配平就直接比摩尔数；③ 纯度算完忘了乘 100 变成百分数。反过来，若算出产率大于 100%，通常说明产物没干（里面还有水或杂质）。Three fatal errors: ① calculating the yield from the reagent in excess (it must be the limiting one); ② comparing mole values without balancing first; ③ working out purity and forgetting the × 100. Conversely, a yield above 100% usually means the product was not dry — water or impurity is still in it.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: The limiting reagent is the reactant that is completely used up first, so it determines the maximum amount of product formed. Percentage yield = (actual yield / theoretical yield) × 100, and it is less than 100% because of side reactions, incomplete reaction and losses during transfer.
例题Example
4.86 g Mg 与 0.300 mol 盐酸反应：Mg + 2HCl → MgCl2 + H2。(a) 哪种反应物是限量的？(b) rtp 下理论能收集多少 dm³ 氢气？(c) 若实际只收集到 3.24 dm³，百分产率是多少？4.86 g of Mg reacts with 0.300 mol of hydrochloric acid: Mg + 2HCl → MgCl2 + H2. (a) Which reagent is limiting? (b) What volume of hydrogen, at rtp, should be collected? (c) If only 3.24 dm³ is collected, what is the percentage yield?
① 方程式已配平，把已知量换成摩尔：① the equation is balanced, so convert the known quantities into moles:
n(Mg) = 4.86 / 24.3 = 0.200 mol n(HCl) = 0.300 mol
② 各除以系数：Mg 0.200 / 1 = 0.200；HCl 0.300 / 2 = 0.150 → HCl 更小，是限量的（Mg 过量）。② divide each by its coefficient: Mg 0.200 / 1 = 0.200; HCl 0.300 / 2 = 0.150 → HCl is smaller, so it is limiting (Mg is in excess). ③ 用 HCl 算氢气：系数比 2 HCl : 1 H2，所以 n(H2) = 0.300 / 2 = 0.150 mol。③ use HCl to find hydrogen: the ratio is 2 HCl : 1 H2, so n(H2) = 0.300 / 2 = 0.150 mol.
V = 0.150 × 24 = 3.60 dm³ （理论产量）
④ 产率 = 实际 / 理论：④ yield = actual / theoretical:
% yield = 3.24 / 3.60 × 100 = 90.0%
练习Practice
盐酸过量，所以碳酸钙全反应完；先由气体体积倒推摩尔数，再算质量和纯度。The acid is in excess, so all the calcium carbonate reacts: work backwards from the gas volume to moles, then to mass, then to purity.

一份 5.00 g 的石灰石样品（含 CaCO3 与杂质）与过量盐酸反应，rtp 下收集到 1.08 dm³ CO2：CaCO3 + 2HCl → CaCl2 + H2O + CO2。(a) 样品中 CaCO3 的质量是多少？(b) 样品的百分纯度是多少？（Ar：C 12.0，O 16.0，Ca 40.1）A 5.00 g sample of limestone (CaCO3 plus impurity) reacts with excess hydrochloric acid, giving 1.08 dm³ of CO2 at rtp: CaCO3 + 2HCl → CaCl2 + H2O + CO2. (a) What mass of CaCO3 did it contain? (b) What is the percentage purity? (Ar: C 12.0, O 16.0, Ca 40.1)

点开看答案Show answer
(a) n(CO2) = 1.08 / 24 = 0.0450 mol；系数比 1 : 1，所以 n(CaCO3) = 0.0450 mol；M(CaCO3) = 100.1 g mol⁻¹，m = 0.0450 × 100.1 = 4.50 g。
(b) 纯度 = 4.50 / 5.00 × 100 = 90.0%。
注意思路方向：产率题是「从原料往前算产品」，纯度题是「从产品往回算原料」——方向相反，但每一步用的公式完全一样。 (a) n(CO2) = 1.08 / 24 = 0.0450 mol; the ratio is 1 : 1, so n(CaCO3) = 0.0450 mol; M(CaCO3) = 100.1 g mol⁻¹, so m = 0.0450 × 100.1 = 4.50 g.
(b) purity = 4.50 / 5.00 × 100 = 90.0%.
Note the direction of travel: a yield question runs forwards from reactant to product, while a purity question runs backwards from product to reactant — opposite directions, exactly the same formulas.
— 第 7 站完成 —— Stop 7 done —

单元 2 小结Unit 2 summary

① 摩尔是打包单位：1 mol = 6.02×10²³ 个粒子，n = N / L；说摩尔时一定要说清「什么的摩尔」。
② Mr 是拆积木加总（无单位），M 是每摩尔多少克（g mol⁻¹），二者数值相同 —— 于是 n = m / M 把质量和个数接了起来。
③ 三条「自带换算」的捷径：溶液 n = c × V（V 用 dm³）、气体 n = V / 24（rtp）、实验式 三步走（百分比 → 除 Ar → 除最小）。① The mole is a bulk unit: 1 mol = 6.02 × 10²³ particles, with n = N / L; always state what you are counting.
② Mr is the Lego total (no unit) and M is grams per mole (g mol⁻¹) — the same number, different clothes — so n = m / M links mass to count.
③ Three built-in shortcuts: solutions n = c × V (V in dm³), gases n = V / 24 at rtp, and the three-step empirical formula (percent → divide by Ar → divide by the smallest).

④ 所有计算题共用一个骨架：配平 → 换成摩尔 → 比系数找限量 → 按限量算产物；再分出「产率 = 实际 ÷ 理论」和「纯度 = 纯的 ÷ 总的」两条支路。
⑤ 每次算完都问自己一句：单位换了吗？合理吗？摩尔算错，后面每一个单元都会跟着错。④ Every calculation question shares one skeleton: balance → convert to moles → compare coefficients to find the limiting reagent → work out the product from it; then the two branches, "yield = actual ÷ theoretical" and "purity = pure ÷ total".
⑤ After every calculation ask yourself: did I convert the units, and does the answer make sense? Get the mole wrong and every later unit goes wrong with it.

下一站要去哪里：我们已经会数原子了，但还不知道它们为什么愿意待在一起——这就是单元 3 化学键的主题：离子键、共价键、金属键，以及这些东西怎么决定物质的性质。Where next: we can now count atoms, but we do not yet know why they agree to stay together — that is Unit 3, chemical bonding: ionic, covalent and metallic bonding, and how they decide the properties of a substance.

单元 3 · 化学键与分子形状：原子为什么粘在一起，粘完长什么样Unit 3 · Chemical bonding: why atoms stick together, and what they look like once stuck

CAIE 9701 Topic 3 · 8 站 · 原子为什么粘在一起，粘完之后长什么样CAIE 9701 Topic 3 · 8 stops · why atoms stick together, and what they look like once stuck

路线图本单元八站，先弄懂「为什么成键」，再认识三种键，最后看分子长什么样、有什么脾气Eight stops — first why atoms bond, then the three bond types, and finally the shape and temperament of molecules

  1. 原子为什么要成键：凑满外层、能量更低Why atoms bond: a full outer shell, lower energy
  2. 离子键：彻底的电子交易Ionic bonding: a total electron transfer
  3. 共价键：合伙出电子Covalent bonding: sharing electrons
  4. 配位共价键：一方出双怎么算Dative bonding: one atom donates both electrons
  5. 金属键：一片电子的海Metallic bonding: a sea of electrons
  6. VSEPR：分子长什么形状Shapes of molecules (VSEPR)
  7. 电负性与极性Electronegativity and polarity
  8. 分子间作用力：分子和分子之间的事Intermolecular forces: what holds molecules together

建议：第 1 站先站稳「为什么成键」，再顺着离子键 → 共价键 → 金属键走；最后三站（形状、极性、分子间力）是一条线——先有形状，再谈极性，再谈沸点。Tip: secure "why atoms bond" first, then move through ionic → covalent → metallic. The last three stops form one chain: shape first, then polarity, then boiling point.

1 原子为什么要成键Why atoms bond Why atoms bond原子为什么要成键
这一站要你会：说出稀有气体不活泼的原因，会用「得失电子或共用电子」解释成键，并说明成键会让能量降低、变得更稳定。Goal: explain why noble gases are unreactive, describe bonding in terms of losing, gaining or sharing electrons, and state that bonding lowers energy and increases stability.
把最外层电子想成一张八人桌：稀有气体一家刚好坐满（外层 8 个电子，氦只有 2 个），谁也不缺位，所以懒得跟别人拼桌——这就是它不活泼的原因。别的原子桌上都缺人：有的缺 1 个，有的多 1 个。它们只有两条路：要么把多余的整个送人（得失电子，变离子键），要么跟邻居合坐一把椅子（共用电子，变共价键）。凑满之后，大家都舒服了——舒服的意思就是能量更低、更稳定。Think of the outer shell as a table of eight seats. The noble gases already sit a full table (8 outer electrons; helium just 2), so they never bother sharing — that is why they are unreactive. Other atoms have empty or extra seats. They have two options: give away the extras (lose or gain electrons → ionic bond) or share seats with a neighbour (share electrons → covalent bond). Once the table is full, everyone is comfortable — and comfortable means lower energy, more stable.
三个核心点：Three core points:
  • 稀有气体（第 0/18 族）不活泼，因为它们最外层已经是 8 个电子（氦第一层只有 2 个），是「满」的。Noble gases are unreactive because their outer shell is already full: 8 electrons (helium: only 2 in its first shell).
  • 其他原子不稳定，因为外层没满；它们通过得失电子（离子键）或共用电子（共价键）去凑满外层。Other atoms are unstable because their outer shell is not full; they reach a full shell by transferring (ionic) or sharing (covalent) electrons.
  • 成键会释放能量：单独时能量高，成键后能量低，就像球滚进坑里。能量越低越稳定。Bonding releases energy: separate atoms are high in energy, bonded atoms are low — like a ball rolling into a well. Lower energy = more stable.
别把「满 8 个」当铁律：氢和氦只要 2 个（第一层最多装 2 个）。「八隅体规则」是条经验规律，后面还会遇到例外（比如 BF3、PCl5），现在先记牢常见情况就够。Don't treat "eight" as a hard law: hydrogen and helium only need 2 (the first shell holds at most 2). The octet rule is an empirical guide, and exceptions come later (BF3, PCl5); for now, learn the common cases.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: The noble gases are unreactive because they have a full outer shell of electrons (eight, or two for helium). Other atoms form bonds to achieve a stable full outer shell, and bond formation releases energy, making the atoms more stable.
例题Example
钠的电子排布是 2,8,1，氯是 2,8,7，氖是 2,8。为什么钠和氯都很容易反应，而氖几乎不反应？Sodium has the electron arrangement 2,8,1, chlorine 2,8,7, and neon 2,8. Why do sodium and chlorine react easily, while neon hardly reacts?
① 数外层电子：钠 1 个，氯 7 个，氖 8 个。① Count the outer electrons: sodium 1, chlorine 7, neon 8. ② 氖外层已满（8 个），稳定，所以不反应。② Neon's outer shell is full (8), so it is stable and does not react. ③ 钠外层没满，会失去 1 个电子凑满；氯外层也没满，会得到 1 个电子凑满——所以它们都急着反应。③ Sodium's outer shell is not full, so it loses 1 electron; chlorine's is not full either, so it gains 1 — both react readily.
练习Practice
先数外层电子，再看它「满没满」、离满差几个。Count the outer electrons first, then see whether the shell is full and how far from full it is.

镁的排布是 2,8,2，氧是 2,6。(a) 镁离「满」还差几个电子？它会失还是得？(b) 氧呢？Magnesium has 2,8,2 and oxygen 2,6. (a) How far from full is magnesium, and will it lose or gain electrons? (b) What about oxygen?

点开看答案Show answer
(a) 镁外层 2 个，失去 2 个就能露出底下满的 8 个 → 变成 Mg2+。(b) 氧外层 6 个，得到 2 个就凑满 8 → 变成 O2−。一个失 2 个、一个得 2 个，正好配平——这就是下一站要讲的离子键。 (a) Magnesium has 2 outer electrons; it loses 2 to expose a full 8 underneath → Mg2+. (b) Oxygen has 6 outer electrons; it gains 2 to reach 8 → O2−. One loses two and the other gains two — a perfect match, which is exactly the ionic bonding of the next stop.
— 第 1 站完成 —— Stop 1 done —
2 离子键：彻底的电子交易Ionic bonding: a total electron transfer Ionic bonding离子键
这一站要你会：会读、会画点叉图，写对离子式，并解释离子键是「各向同性的静电吸引」——所以离子化合物里不存在「一个分子」。Goal: read and draw dot-and-cross diagrams, write correct ionic formulae, and explain that ionic bonding is electrostatic attraction in all directions — so there are no separate molecules.
钠最外层就一个「多余的」电子，氯正好缺一个。钠把电子整个过户给氯——一个变阳离子（带 +），一个变阴离子（带 −）。正负一见面就互相吸，像两块磁铁贴在一起。注意：不是「共用一个」，是彻底送出去。而且一个 Na+ 周围会同时吸着好几个 Cl−，一个 Cl− 周围也围着一圈 Na+——四面八方都吸，所以根本没有「一个 NaCl 分子」这回事，只有一大块重复排列的晶格。Sodium has one "spare" outer electron and chlorine is one short. Sodium transfers that electron to chlorine — one becomes a positive ion, the other a negative ion, and they attract like magnets. Note: nothing is shared; the electron is given away outright. And one Na+ attracts several Cl− all around it, while each Cl− is surrounded by Na+. The pull acts in every direction, so there is no such thing as "one NaCl molecule" — only a giant repeating lattice.
必须记牢：Learn these:
  • 金属失电子变阳离子（+），非金属得电子变阴离子（−），正负离子靠静电吸引结合，这就是离子键。Metals lose electrons to form positive ions and non-metals gain electrons to form negative ions; the oppositely charged ions are held by electrostatic attraction — that is the ionic bond.
  • 点叉图只画外层电子，用点（•）表示一种原子的电子、叉（×）表示另一种；离子要加方括号 [ ] 并标电荷。A dot-and-cross diagram shows only outer electrons, with dots (•) for one atom's electrons and crosses (×) for the other's; ions go in square brackets with their charge.
  • 静电吸引是各向同性的——一个离子周围吸着好几个相反电荷的离子，所以不存在「一个离子分子」，只有巨大的离子晶格。The attraction is isotropic — each ion attracts several opposite ions around it, so there are no separate ionic molecules, only a giant lattice.
  • 三个例子：NaCl（Na+Cl−）、MgO（Mg2+O2−）、MgCl2（一个 Mg2+ 配两个 Cl−）。Three examples: NaCl (Na+Cl−), MgO (Mg2+O2−), MgCl2 (one Mg2+ with two Cl−).
写离子式最容易错：镁失 2 个电子是 Mg2+（不是 Mg+），氧得 2 个是 O2−（不是 O−）。一定要让正负电荷总数相等，所以一个 Mg2+ 必须配两个 Cl−，写出来才是 MgCl2。The common mistake with ionic formulae: magnesium loses two electrons to become Mg2+ (not Mg+), and oxygen gains two to become O2− (not O−). The total positive and negative charges must balance, so one Mg2+ needs two Cl− — hence MgCl2.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: In ionic bonding, electrons are transferred from a metal atom to a non-metal atom. The positive and negative ions formed are held together by strong electrostatic attraction, and there are no separate molecules — the ions form a giant lattice.
例题Example
用点叉图表示 MgCl2 的形成，并说明为什么一个镁要配两个氯。Use a dot-and-cross diagram to show the formation of MgCl2, and explain why one magnesium needs two chlorines.
① 镁外层 2 个电子，氯外层 7 个。① Magnesium has 2 outer electrons, chlorine has 7.
Mg → Mg2+ + 2e− Cl + e− → Cl−　（要做两次）
② 镁把 2 个电子分别送给两个氯：Mg 变 Mg2+，两个氯各变一个 Cl−。② Magnesium gives one electron to each of two chlorines: Mg becomes Mg2+, and each chlorine becomes Cl−. ③ 电荷配平：+2 和 2 × (−1) 正好抵消，所以是 MgCl2。点叉图里 Mg2+ 外层空了（只剩内层），每个 Cl− 外层有 8 个电子（7 个自己的点 + 1 个镁给的叉），都加方括号。③ Charges balance: +2 against 2 × (−1). In the diagram, Mg2+ has no outer electrons, and each Cl− has 8 outer electrons (7 of its own dots + 1 cross from magnesium), all in brackets.
练习Practice
镁失几个、氧得几个？各自变成什么离子？How many does magnesium lose and oxygen gain? Which ions form?

用点叉图（或文字描述）表示 MgO 的形成：镁失几个电子、氧得几个？各变成什么离子？Show the formation of MgO (diagram or description): how many electrons does magnesium lose, oxygen gain, and which ions form?

点开看答案Show answer
镁失 2 个电子 → Mg2+（外层清空，露出满的 8 个）；氧得 2 个电子 → O2−（外层从 6 个补到 8 个）。点叉图里 Mg2+ 外层 8 个叉，O2− 外层 6 个自己的点 + 2 个镁给的叉，两者都加方括号、标电荷。+2 和 −2 配平，所以是 MgO。 Magnesium loses 2 electrons → Mg2+ (outer shell emptied, exposing a full 8); oxygen gains 2 → O2− (outer shell fills from 6 to 8). In the diagram Mg2+ shows 8 crosses, and O2− shows 6 of its own dots + 2 crosses from magnesium, both in brackets with charges. +2 and −2 balance, giving MgO.
— 第 2 站完成 —— Stop 2 done —
3 共价键：合伙出电子Covalent bonding: sharing electrons Covalent bonding共价键
这一站要你会：说出共价键是「共用电子对」，分清单键、双键、三键，并能画 H2、Cl2、H2O、CO2、NH3 的点叉图（只画最外层）。Goal: state that a covalent bond is a shared pair of electrons, tell single, double and triple bonds apart, and draw dot-and-cross diagrams for H2, Cl2, H2O, CO2 and NH3 using only outer electrons.
离子键是「整个过户」，共价键是「两人合租」：你我各出一个电子，这一对电子归两个原子共用，谁也别想独占。合租之后，两个原子的外层都凑满了，皆大欢喜。比如水 H2O：氧出 2 个电子，两个氢各出 1 个，凑成两条 O–H 键；氧自己还剩 4 个电子，分成两对「孤对」闲着——后面讲分子形状时，这对孤对还会出来搞事情。Ionic bonding is a full transfer; covalent bonding is two flatmates sharing a room: each atom contributes one electron, and the pair is shared by both. Both outer shells end up full. In water, oxygen contributes two electrons and each hydrogen contributes one, making two O–H bonds; oxygen keeps four electrons as two lone pairs — and those lone pairs will cause trouble when we reach molecular shapes.
几个必须分清的概念：Concepts to keep straight:
  • 共价键 = 两个非金属原子共用一对电子；每共用一对，就是一条键。A covalent bond is a shared pair of electrons between two non-metal atoms; each shared pair is one bond.
  • 单键 = 1 对（H–H、Cl–Cl）；双键 = 2 对（O=C=O）；三键 = 3 对（N≡N）。Single bond = 1 pair (H–H, Cl–Cl); double bond = 2 pairs (O=C=O); triple bond = 3 pairs (N≡N).
  • 点叉图只画最外层电子：共用的电子对画在两个原子之间，没共用的孤对画在原子旁边。Dot-and-cross diagrams show only the outer shell: shared pairs go between the atoms, and unshared lone pairs sit beside an atom.
  • 五个例子：H2（1 条单键）、Cl2（1 条）、H2O（2 条 + 2 孤对）、CO2（2 条双键）、NH3（3 条 + 1 孤对）。Five examples: H2 (one single bond), Cl2 (one), H2O (two bonds + two lone pairs), CO2 (two double bonds), NH3 (three bonds + one lone pair).
别误会「共用」：共价键不是「各出一个电子、还是各归各的」，而是两个电子同时被两个原子核吸引，一起围着两个核转。也不要把原子画得太大、把共用电子的位置画错——那对电子要在两个原子之间。Don't misread "sharing": it does not mean each atom keeps its own electron. The two electrons are attracted to both nuclei at once. Also, draw the shared pair between the two atoms, not off to one side.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: A covalent bond is a shared pair of electrons between two non-metal atoms. A single bond has one shared pair, a double bond two, and a triple bond three. Dot-and-cross diagrams show only the outer-shell electrons.
例题Example
画出 H2O 的电子排布（点叉图），并说明氧为什么能和两个氢成键。Draw the dot-and-cross diagram of H2O and explain why oxygen bonds to two hydrogens.
① 氧外层 6 个电子，还需要再凑 2 个才满 8。① Oxygen has 6 outer electrons and needs 2 more to reach 8. ② 两个氢各出 1 个电子、氧出 2 个，凑成 2 条 O–H 单键。② Two hydrogens each give 1 electron and oxygen gives 2, forming two O–H single bonds. ③ 氧还剩 4 个电子 = 2 对孤对。所以氧周围一共 4 对电子：2 对成键 + 2 对孤对。③ Oxygen keeps 4 electrons = 2 lone pairs. So oxygen has 4 pairs in total: 2 bonding pairs + 2 lone pairs.
练习Practice
先看中心原子外层有几个电子、还缺几个，再数需要几条键。Count the central atom's outer electrons and how many it is short, then work out how many bonds it needs.

CO2 的中心是 C（外层 4 个电子）。(a) C 要和每个 O 共用几对电子？(b) 所以 C 和每个 O 之间是单键还是双键？The central atom of CO2 is C (4 outer electrons). (a) How many pairs does C share with each O? (b) Is each C–O bond single or double?

点开看答案Show answer
(a) C 外层 4 个电子，缺 4 个才满，所以总共要 4 对；两个氧平分，每个氧和 C 共用 2 对。(b) 2 对 = 双键。所以 CO2 的结构是 O=C=O，共 2 条双键（4 对共用电子）。 (a) Carbon has 4 outer electrons and needs 4 more, so it shares 4 pairs in total; shared equally between two oxygens, that is 2 pairs with each O. (b) 2 pairs = a double bond. So CO2 is O=C=O, with two double bonds (4 shared pairs).

4 配位共价键：一方出双怎么算Dative (coordinate) bonding: one atom donates both Dative bonding配位键
这一站要你会：说出配位键是「一对电子都来自同一原子」，认识 NH4+ 和 Al2Cl6 两个必考例子，并知道成键后与普通共价键无法区分。Goal: state that in a dative bond both electrons come from the same atom, know the two exam examples NH4+ and Al2Cl6, and know that the resulting bond is indistinguishable from a normal covalent bond.
普通共价键像「两人合伙做生意，各出一半本钱」；配位键像「一个人出全部本钱，另一个人空手入股」。等公司开起来，账上那笔钱就是两人共有的——没人看得出当初是谁出的。氨 NH3 里的 N 有一对「闲着的」孤对电子，正好 H+ 一个电子都没有（就是个裸质子），N 就把整对拿出来和 H+ 共用，于是有了铵根 NH4+。成键之后，这第四条 N–H 键和另外三条完全相同。An ordinary covalent bond is like two partners each putting in half the capital; a dative bond is like one person putting in everything while the other joins empty-handed. Once the company is running, the money is jointly owned — nobody can tell who originally paid. The N in ammonia NH3 holds a "spare" lone pair, and H+ has no electrons at all (it is a bare proton), so N shares its whole pair with H+, forming the ammonium ion NH4+. Afterwards, that fourth N–H bond is exactly the same as the other three.
三个要点 + 两个必考例子：Three points + two exam examples:
  • 配位（dative / coordinate）键：一对共用电子全部来自同一个原子，另一个原子只提供一个空位置。A dative (coordinate) bond is one in which both electrons of the shared pair come from the same atom; the other atom only provides the space.
  • 一旦形成，它和普通共价键没有任何区别——键长、键能都一样，光看结构分不出来。Once formed, it is identical to an ordinary covalent bond — same length, same strength; you cannot tell them apart from the structure alone.
  • 画法：用箭头从提供孤对的原子指向受体原子。Drawing: use an arrow pointing from the atom that donates the lone pair to the acceptor.
  • 例 1：NH4+。NH3 的 N 有孤对电子，H+ 没有电子；N 把孤对「借」给 H+ → 生成铵根。Example 1: NH4+. The N in NH3 has a lone pair and H+ has none; N donates the lone pair to H+ → the ammonium ion.
  • 例 2：Al2Cl6。AlCl3 里的 Al 外层只有 6 个电子（缺 2 个），于是两个 AlCl3 里 Cl 的孤对电子指过去补位，形成二聚体。Example 2: Al2Cl6. The Al in AlCl3 has only 6 outer electrons (2 short), so a Cl lone pair from the other AlCl3 is donated across to fill the gap, forming the dimer.
怎么判断一条键是不是配位键？看形成过程：如果那对电子原本是「一个人」的，就是配位键。只看最终结构是看不出来的——所以题目总会给你「形成过程」或「电子来源」的线索。How do you tell if a bond is dative? Look at how it formed: if the pair originally belonged to one atom, it is dative. You cannot tell from the final structure alone — which is why questions always give you the formation step or the source of the electrons.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: A dative (coordinate) bond is a covalent bond in which both electrons of the shared pair come from the same atom. Once formed, it is identical to an ordinary covalent bond. In NH₄⁺ the nitrogen atom donates its lone pair to the H⁺ ion.
例题Example
解释 NH3 + H+ → NH4+ 里那个新键是怎么来的，为什么它是配位键。Explain how the new bond in NH3 + H+ → NH4+ forms, and why it is dative.
① NH3 的 N 有一对孤对电子。① The N in NH3 has a lone pair of electrons. ② H+ 是一个没有电子的质子。② H+ is a proton with no electrons. ③ N 把这整对电子拿出来与 H+ 共用。③ N shares that whole pair with H+. ④ 因为这一对电子全部来自 N，所以是配位键；形成后四个 N–H 键完全相同。④ Because both electrons come from N, it is a dative bond; afterwards all four N–H bonds are identical.
练习Practice
Al 外层只有 6 个电子，离满 8 还差几个？Aluminium has only 6 outer electrons; how many is it short of 8?

AlCl3 里的 Al 外层只有 6 个电子。(a) 为什么它还要跟另一个 AlCl3 结合成 Al2Cl6？(b) 这个「补上来」的键是什么类型？The Al in AlCl3 has only 6 outer electrons. (a) Why does it combine with another AlCl3 to form Al2Cl6? (b) What type of bond is this extra one?

点开看答案Show answer
(a) Al 外层只有 6 个电子，缺 2 个才能凑满 8，所以要再补一条键。(b) 两个 AlCl3 里，一个 Cl 的孤对电子整对指给另一个 AlCl3 的 Al → 形成配位键，于是每个 Al 都凑满 8 个，二聚成 Al2Cl6。 (a) Al has only 6 outer electrons, so it is 2 short of a full octet and needs one more bond. (b) A lone pair from a Cl in one AlCl3 is donated whole to the Al of the other → a dative bond, so each Al reaches 8 and the two units dimerise to Al2Cl6.

5 金属键：一片电子的海Metallic bonding: a sea of electrons Metallic bonding金属键
这一站要你会：说出金属键是「阳离子 + 离域电子海」之间的静电吸引，并用它解释金属的导电、延展性和高熔点。Goal: describe metallic bonding as attraction between positive ions and a sea of delocalised electrons, and use it to explain conduction, malleability and high melting points.
把金属想成一堆整整齐齐码放的硬币（阳离子），泡在一大盆会流动的胶水（电子海）里。硬币被胶水粘在一起，所以整块金属很结实；胶水能到处流，所以一通电，电子就能顺着流动——这就是金属能导电的原因。金属被捶打时，硬币层会滑动，但胶水随时跟着补位，硬币不会跟硬币硬撞，所以金属能被拉成丝、捶成片而不碎。Picture a metal as neatly stacked coins (positive ions) sitting in a bath of runny glue (the electron sea). The glue holds the coins together, so the metal is strong; because the glue flows, electrons can drift through when a voltage is applied — that is why metals conduct. When a metal is hammered, the layers of coins slide, but the glue moves with them and the coins never crash into each other — so metals can be drawn into wires and beaten into sheets without shattering.
用金属键解释三件事：Explaining three properties:
  • 金属键＝排列整齐的金属阳离子与离域电子海之间的静电吸引。The metallic bond is the electrostatic attraction between a lattice of positive ions and a sea of delocalised electrons.
  • 导电：加上电压后，离域电子能自由流动 → 形成电流。Conductivity: under a voltage, the delocalised electrons flow freely → an electric current.
  • 延展性（能捶成薄片、拉成丝）：金属层受力滑动时，电子海「跟着调整」，阳离子不会和同号阳离子撞上而断裂，所以金属能被塑形而不碎。Malleability / ductility: when layers slide, the electron sea moves with them, so positive ions never crash into each other — the metal deforms instead of shattering.
  • 高熔点：阳离子和电子海之间的静电吸引很强，要拆散需要大量能量。High melting point: the attraction between ions and the electron sea is strong, so a lot of energy is needed to pull them apart.
经典对比题：离子晶体（如 NaCl）受力会碎——因为离子层一滑动，同号离子就面对面撞上、互相排斥；金属受力却会变形不断。差别就一句话：电子海能不能随时补位。The classic comparison: an ionic crystal like NaCl shatters when stressed — slide the layers and like-charged ions face each other and repel. A metal bends without breaking. The whole difference is one sentence: can the electron sea re-adjust instantly?
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: In a metal, the positive ions are held together by a sea of delocalised electrons. These free electrons allow metals to conduct electricity, and because the layers of ions can slide past each other without breaking, metals are malleable and ductile.
例题Example
为什么金属能导电，而固态 NaCl 不能导电？Why can metals conduct electricity, while solid NaCl cannot?
① 金属里有离域电子，能自由移动 → 导电。① Metals have delocalised electrons free to move → they conduct. ② 固态 NaCl 的离子被牢牢锁在晶格里，动不了 → 不导电。② In solid NaCl the ions are locked into the lattice and cannot move → it does not conduct. ③ NaCl 只有熔化或溶于水、离子能自由移动后，才导电。③ NaCl only conducts once it is molten or dissolved, when its ions are free to move.
练习Practice
两个都从「电子海 / 静电吸引」出发。Start both answers from the electron sea / electrostatic attraction.

用金属键解释：(a) 为什么铜能拉成电线而不容易断？(b) 为什么大多数金属的熔点很高？Use metallic bonding to explain: (a) why copper can be drawn into wires without snapping; (b) why most metals have high melting points.

点开看答案Show answer
(a) 铜的阳离子层受力滑动时，电子海随时跟着移动、继续把阳离子粘住，不会发生同号离子对撞，所以能拉伸不断（延展性好）。(b) 金属阳离子与电子海之间的静电吸引很强，拆散需要大量能量 → 熔点高。 (a) When copper's layers of ions slide, the electron sea moves with them and keeps bonding the ions, so like-charged ions never collide — the wire stretches without breaking (it is ductile). (b) The electrostatic attraction between the ions and the electron sea is strong, so a lot of energy is needed to separate them → a high melting point.
— 第 5 站完成 —— Stop 5 done —
6 VSEPR：分子长什么形状Shapes of molecules (VSEPR) VSEPR分子形状
这一站要你会：数中心原子周围的电子对数，说出 6 种常见形状的名称与键角，并知道孤对排斥比成键对更强。Goal: count the electron pairs around a central atom, name six common shapes with their bond angles, and know that lone pairs repel more strongly than bonding pairs.
电子对都带负电，彼此像互相讨厌的人，挤在中心原子周围时会尽量站得最远。2 对人站成一条直线（180°），3 对人站成等边三角形（120°），4 对人站成正四面体（109.5°）。要是其中有一对是「孤对」——只属于中心原子、不连着别的原子——它更霸道，会把成键对挤得更紧，键角就缩水：NH3 从 109.5° 缩到 107°，H2O 缩到 104.5°。Electron pairs all carry negative charge, so like people who dislike each other they spread out as far as possible around the central atom. Two pairs stand in a line (180°), three in an equilateral triangle (120°), four in a tetrahedron (109.5°). If one pair is a "lone pair" — belonging only to the central atom — it is pushier and squeezes the bonding pairs tighter, shrinking the angle: NH3 drops from 109.5° to 107°, and H2O to 104.5°.
必记的形状表：The shape table to memorise:
中心电子对Pairs成键 : 孤对Bonding : lone形状Shape键角Angle例子Example
22:0直线形linear180°CO2
33:0平面三角形trigonal planar120°BF3
44:0正四面体tetrahedral109.5°CH4
43:1三角锥pyramidal107°NH3
42:2V 形（弯）non-linear104.5°H2O
66:0正八面体octahedral90°SF6
  • 只看中心原子周围的电子对（含孤对），端原子不算。Count only around the central atom, including lone pairs — ignore the outer atoms.
  • 排斥力大小：孤对–孤对 > 孤对–成键对 > 成键对–成键对。Repulsion order: lone–lone > lone–bonding > bonding–bonding.
  • 名字看的是原子排出来的形状，孤对不占名字：NH3 有 4 对电子却叫「三角锥」，因为孤对不显形。The name describes the atoms, not the lone pairs: NH3 has four pairs yet is called "pyramidal", because the lone pair does not show in the shape.
数电子对最容易错：双键、三键只算 1 对。比如 CO2 的 C 周围是 2 个双键 = 2 对电子对，所以是直线形 180°，而不是「4 对」。The common counting error: a double or triple bond counts as one pair. The C in CO2 has two double bonds = 2 pairs, so it is linear, 180° — not "four pairs".
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: Electron pairs around a central atom repel each other and arrange themselves as far apart as possible. Lone pairs repel more than bonding pairs, so they reduce the bond angle. Carbon dioxide has two bonding pairs and is linear, with a bond angle of 180°.
例题Example
判断 H2O 的形状和键角，并解释为什么不是 109.5°。State the shape and bond angle of H2O, and explain why the angle is not 109.5°.
① O 周围 4 对电子：2 对成键（O–H）+ 2 对孤对。① Oxygen has 4 pairs: 2 bonding (O–H) + 2 lone. ② 4 对电子按正四面体排布。② Four pairs arrange tetrahedrally. ③ 但 2 对孤对排斥更强，把 2 条 O–H 挤近。③ The two lone pairs repel more, squeezing the two O–H bonds closer. ④ 所以 H2O 是 V 形（non-linear），键角 104.5°。④ So H2O is non-linear with an angle of 104.5°.
练习Practice
先数电子对（含孤对），再对照表格。Count the pairs (including lone pairs), then match the table.

(a) NH3 中心 N 周围有几对电子、几对孤对？(b) 它的形状和键角是什么？(c) BF3 又是什么形状、多少度？(a) Around the N of NH3, how many electron pairs and how many lone pairs? (b) What are its shape and bond angle? (c) What are the shape and angle of BF3?

点开看答案Show answer
(a) N 周围 4 对电子（3 对成键 + 1 对孤对）。(b) 三角锥（pyramidal），键角 107°（孤对把 3 条 N–H 挤近了 2.5°）。(c) BF3 是 平面三角形（trigonal planar），120°。 (a) Around N there are 4 pairs (3 bonding + 1 lone). (b) Pyramidal, with an angle of 107° (the lone pair squeezes the three N–H bonds in by 2.5°). (c) BF3 is trigonal planar, 120°.

7 电负性与极性Electronegativity and polarity Electronegativity电负性
这一站要你会：用电负性判断键的类型（纯共价 / 极性共价 / 离子键），会用 δ+/δ− 标极性，并知道分子有没有极性还要看结构是否对称。Goal: use electronegativity to classify a bond (pure covalent / polar covalent / ionic), label polarity with δ+/δ−, and know that molecular polarity also depends on symmetry.
电负性就是原子「抢电子的力气」。F 是力气最大的（4.0），抢电子几乎从不失手。两个人共用一对电子，如果力气一样大，电子就平分；如果一大一小，电子就会被拽到力气大的那一边，那头偏负（δ−），另一头偏正（δ+）。抢得足够狠——差值大约到 1.8 以上——就直接把电子整个抢走，变成了离子键。Electronegativity is an atom's "pulling power" over electrons. Fluorine pulls hardest (4.0) and almost never loses a tug-of-war. When two atoms share a pair: equal strength → the electrons are shared evenly; unequal → the pair is dragged to the stronger side, which becomes δ−, leaving the other δ+. Pull hard enough — a difference of roughly 1.8 or more — and the electron is taken outright, becoming an ionic bond.
三件事 + 一个常见陷阱：Three things + one classic trap:
  • 电负性是鲍林标度下的相对值，F 最大 = 4.0；常见还有 O 3.5、N 3.0、Cl 3.0、C 2.5、H 2.1。Electronegativity is a relative Pauling value; F is the largest at 4.0. Common others: O 3.5, N 3.0, Cl 3.0, C 2.5, H 2.1.
  • 差值 ≈ 0 → 纯共价键（H–H、Cl–Cl）；差值中等 → 极性共价键（H–Cl）；差值很大（约 ≥1.8）→ 离子键（NaCl）。Difference ≈ 0 → pure covalent (H–H, Cl–Cl); moderate → polar covalent (H–Cl); large (about ≥1.8) → ionic (NaCl).
  • 标极性用 δ+/δ−：δ+ 在电负性小的一头，δ− 在电负性大的一头。Label polarity with δ+/δ−: δ+ on the less electronegative end, δ− on the more electronegative end.
  • 分子有没有极性，还要看形状：键有极性，但分子若对称、偶极互相抵消，就是非极性分子。Molecular polarity depends on shape: a molecule with polar bonds can still be non-polar if its dipoles cancel by symmetry.
经典陷阱：CO2 的两条 C=O 都是极性键，但 CO2 是非极性分子——因为它是直线形，两个偶极大小相等、方向相反，正好抵消。而 H2O 是 V 形，抵消不掉，所以是极性分子。The classic trap: both C=O bonds in CO2 are polar, yet CO2 is non-polar — because it is linear and the two equal dipoles point in opposite directions and cancel. Water is V-shaped, so its dipoles cannot cancel, making H2O polar.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: Electronegativity is the ability of an atom to attract the bonding electrons towards itself. Fluorine has the highest value, 4.0. If the two atoms have very different electronegativities, the bond is polar; a large difference gives an ionic bond. A molecule is polar only if the bond dipoles do not cancel out.
例题Example
CO2 和 H2O 里，哪个是极性分子？说明理由。Of CO2 and H2O, which is a polar molecule? Explain.
① CO2 里 C=O 是极性键（O 电负性大）。① The C=O bonds in CO2 are polar (O is more electronegative). ② 但 CO2 是直线形，两个偶极大小相等、方向相反 → 互相抵消。② But CO2 is linear, so the two equal dipoles point opposite ways and cancel. ③ 所以 CO2 是非极性分子。③ So CO2 is non-polar. ④ H2O 是 V 形，两个 O–H 偶极不能抵消 → H2O 是极性分子。④ Water is V-shaped, so its two O–H dipoles do not cancel → H2O is polar.
练习Practice
δ− 永远在电负性大的那头；CH₄ 先看形状是否对称。δ− always sits on the more electronegative end; for CH₄, first check whether the shape is symmetric.

(a) H–F 键里哪一头标 δ−？(b) CH4 的四条 C–H 键都是极性键，那 CH4 是极性分子吗？为什么？(a) Which end of the H–F bond is labelled δ−? (b) All four C–H bonds in CH4 are polar, yet is CH4 polar? Why?

点开看答案Show answer
(a) F 电负性大（4.0），标 δ−；H 标 δ+。(b) CH4 是非极性分子——它是正四面体，四条 C–H 偶极方向对称、互相抵消。 (a) Fluorine is more electronegative (4.0), so it carries δ−; H carries δ+. (b) CH4 is non-polar — it is tetrahedral, so the four C–H dipoles point symmetrically and cancel out.
