8 分子间作用力：分子和分子之间的事Intermolecular forces: what holds molecules together Intermolecular forces分子间力
这一站要你会：说出三种分子间力（London、永久偶极–偶极、氢键）分别出现在什么分子里，会按强弱排序，并能解释沸点差异。Goal: name the three intermolecular forces (London, permanent dipole–dipole, hydrogen bonding), say which molecules show each, rank them by strength, and explain boiling-point differences.
分子内部靠共价键「锁住」——那是分子内的强连接；分子和分子之间还有一种弱的「粘性」，叫分子间力。London（色散）力是每个分子都有的：电子临时挤到一边，产生瞬间偶极，再带动邻居；永久偶极–偶极力只出现在极性分子之间，像小磁铁南北极相吸；氢键最特殊——当 H 直接挂在 N、O、F 上时，H 那头变得特别「光」，被邻居的 N/O/F 死死吸住，吸力格外强。记住：真正决定沸点的，不是分子内的共价键，而是分子之间的力。Covalent bonds hold a molecule together from inside — those are strong, intramolecular. Between molecules there is a weaker "stickiness" called intermolecular force. London (dispersion) forces exist in every molecule: electrons momentarily crowd to one side, creating a fleeting dipole that nudges its neighbours. Permanent dipole–dipole forces appear only between polar molecules, like little magnets. Hydrogen bonding is special — when H is directly attached to N, O or F, that H becomes very "exposed" and is gripped tightly by a neighbour's N/O/F. Remember: what decides boiling point is not the covalent bond inside the molecule, but the forces between molecules.
三种力 + 强弱顺序：Three forces + their order:
  • 共价键是「分子内」的力，决定分子的化学性质；分子间力是「分子之间」的力，才决定熔沸点。Covalent bonds are intramolecular and decide chemical behaviour; intermolecular forces act between molecules and decide melting/boiling points.
  • London（色散）力：所有分子都有，由瞬时偶极引起；电子越多、分子越大，力越强。London (dispersion) forces: present in all molecules, caused by instantaneous dipoles; stronger with more electrons / bigger molecules.
  • 永久偶极–偶极力：只出现在极性分子之间。Permanent dipole–dipole forces: only between polar molecules.
  • 氢键：H 直接连到 N / O / F 时才出现，是三种里最强的（但仍远弱于共价键）。注意 C–H 不形成氢键。Hydrogen bonding: only when H is attached to N, O or F; the strongest of the three (yet far weaker than a covalent bond). C–H does not hydrogen-bond.
  • 强弱：London < 偶极–偶极 < 氢键。Order: London < dipole–dipole < hydrogen bonding.
判断氢键只看一个条件：H 是否直接连着 N/O/F。CH4 里 H 连的是 C，所以只有 London 力；HCl 里 H 连的是 Cl（不在 N/O/F），所以是偶极–偶极 + London，没有氢键。H2O、NH3、HF 才有。To spot hydrogen bonding, check one thing: is H directly attached to N/O/F? In CH4 the H is on C, so only London forces. In HCl the H is on Cl (not N/O/F), so dipole–dipole + London, but no hydrogen bond. Only H2O, NH3 and HF have it.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: Intermolecular forces are weak attractions between molecules. The three types are London (dispersion) forces, permanent dipole–dipole forces, and hydrogen bonds. Hydrogen bonds form when hydrogen is bonded to nitrogen, oxygen or fluorine, and they are the strongest of the three. They raise the boiling point of water.
例题Example
解释为什么 H2O 的沸点（100 °C）远高于 CH4（−162 °C）。Explain why H2O boils at 100 °C, far higher than CH4 at −162 °C.
① CH4 是非极性分子，只有 London 力（很弱）。① CH4 is non-polar, with only London forces (very weak). ② H2O 是极性分子，而且 H 直接连 O → 有氢键（三种里最强）。② Water is polar and its H is attached to O → it has hydrogen bonds (the strongest of the three). ③ 打断氢键比打断 London 力需要多得多的能量。③ Breaking hydrogen bonds needs far more energy than breaking London forces. ④ 所以 H2O 沸点远高于 CH4。④ Hence water's boiling point is far higher.
练习Practice
只看 H 是不是直接连在 N/O/F 上。Just check whether H is directly attached to N/O/F.

下列物质中，哪些能形成氢键？(a) HF (b) NH3 (c) CH4 (d) HCl。简单说明判断依据。Which of these can form hydrogen bonds? (a) HF (b) NH3 (c) CH4 (d) HCl. Briefly justify.

点开看答案Show answer
能形成氢键的是 (a) HF 和 (b) NH3——因为 H 直接连着 F 和 N。(c) CH4 不能（H 连的是 C）；(d) HCl 也不能（H 连的是 Cl，Cl 不在 N/O/F 里），HCl 只有偶极–偶极和 London 力。 Hydrogen bonding occurs in (a) HF and (b) NH3 — because H is directly attached to F and N. (c) CH4 cannot (its H is on C); (d) HCl cannot either (its H is on Cl, which is not N/O/F), so HCl has only dipole–dipole and London forces.
— 第 8 站完成 —— Stop 8 done —

单元 3 小结Unit 3 summary

① 成键是为了凑满外层、降低能量：离子键是「整个过户」，共价键是「合伙共用」，配位键是「一方出双」，金属键是「电子海」。
② 形状看 VSEPR：2 对直线形 180°、3 对平面三角 120°、4 对四面体 109.5°，有孤对就缩水（NH3 107°、H2O 104.5°）。
③ 极性看电负性，分子极性还要看对称（CO2 有极性键却是非极性分子）。沸点看分子间力：London < 偶极–偶极 < 氢键。① Atoms bond to fill the outer shell and lower energy: ionic is a full transfer, covalent is sharing, dative is one atom donating both, metallic is a sea of electrons.
② Shape comes from VSEPR: 2 pairs linear 180°, 3 trigonal planar 120°, 4 tetrahedral 109.5°; lone pairs shrink the angle (NH3 107°, H2O 104.5°).
③ Polarity comes from electronegativity, but molecular polarity needs symmetry (CO2 has polar bonds yet is non-polar). Boiling point comes from intermolecular forces: London < dipole–dipole < hydrogen bonding.

下一站最重要的一件事：键只是「一张关系网」，物质还有三种状态——固态、液态、气态怎么互相转变、气体又遵守什么规律，这就是单元 4 的主题。Why the next unit matters: bonding is only the "relationship map". Matter also has three states — how solid, liquid and gas change into each other, and the laws gases follow, is the subject of Unit 4.

Keep 273, 10⁻³ and 10⁻⁶ where you can see them.

1 三态与粒子模型Solids, liquids and gases The particle model粒子模型
这一站要你会：从排列、运动、间距、能量四个角度说出三态的区别；并解释「熔化、沸腾时温度为什么停住不动」。Goal: describe the three states in terms of arrangement, motion, spacing and energy, and explain why the temperature stops rising during melting and boiling.
把一间教室想成三种时刻：上课时每个人坐在固定座位上，只能扭一扭身子——这是固体；课间大家站起来走动，人挨着人，但教室还是那么大——这是液体；放学后人全冲到操场上，隔得老远、各跑各的——这是气体。整栋楼里从来没多出一个人，只是「坐得紧」还是「跑得散」。

那为什么冰化了温度一直是 0 °C？你可以这样想：你交的学费（热量）先被拿去买「拆座位的力气」，还没有变成「涨工资」（升温）。座位没拆完，工资就不涨。等座位全拆完（全化成水），再交的钱才开始涨工资——温度这才往上走。Picture one classroom at three moments: during a lesson everyone sits in a fixed seat and can only wriggle — that is a solid; at break people stand and walk about, still shoulder to shoulder, and the room is still the same size — that is a liquid; after school everyone runs onto the field, far apart, each doing their own thing — that is a gas. Nobody new entered the building; the only difference is how tightly they are packed.

So why does melting ice stay at 0 °C? The heat you pay in is first spent on breaking the seating plan, not on speeding anyone up. Until the seating plan is fully broken (all melted), no extra heat goes into raising the temperature — it only starts to climb once the last seat is gone.
四个角度，一张表看完：Four angles, one table:
状态State排列与运动Arrangement & motion粒子间距Spacing形状 / 体积Shape / volume
固体 solidSolid规则排列，固定在位置上，只能原地振动regular lattice, fixed positions, vibration only最小，几乎挨着smallest, almost touching都有；几乎不可压缩both fixed; almost incompressible
液体 liquidLiquid仍然靠得很近，但能相对滑动still close, but able to slide past each other略大于固体slightly larger than a solid体积固定，形状随容器fixed volume, takes the shape of its container
气体 gasGas无规则，高速乱飞，互相碰撞random, fast, colliding with each other约为粒子直径的十倍about ten particle diameters都没有；可压缩，充满容器neither; compressible, fills the container
  • 能量决定状态。升温 = 粒子平均动能变大；动能大到能挣脱「邻居的拉扯」，固体就变液体，再大就变气体。Energy decides the state. Heating raises the average kinetic energy; once it is enough to escape the pull of neighbours, a solid becomes a liquid, then a gas.
  • 熔化：整齐的格子被拆成「还能互相拉住、但能滑动」的状态。只破坏一部分分子间力。Melting: the neat lattice becomes a state that still holds together but can slide. Only some of the intermolecular forces are broken.
  • 沸腾：粒子要彻底摆脱邻居，跑到很远的地方去。要破坏全部分子间力，所以汽化焓远大于熔化焓。Boiling: particles must escape their neighbours completely and travel far away. All the intermolecular forces are broken, so the enthalpy of vaporisation is far larger than that of fusion.
  • 温度只量「平均动能」，不量「存了多少能量」。所以平台期一直在吸热，温度却不动——热量变成了「位能」，不是「动能」。Temperature measures average kinetic energy, not stored energy. So heat keeps flowing in during the plateau while the temperature sits still: the energy becomes potential energy, not kinetic.
数字感受一下：冰的熔化焓只有 6.01 kJ mol⁻¹，而水的汽化焓是 40.7 kJ mol⁻¹——差了近七倍。为什么？因为熔化只是把座位挪松，沸腾是把人赶出教室。考试问「为什么汽化焓大于熔化焓」，答「沸腾要克服全部分子间力，熔化只需克服一部分」就够。Feel the numbers: ice melts with only 6.01 kJ mol⁻¹, while water boils with 40.7 kJ mol⁻¹ — nearly seven times more. Melting loosens the seating plan; boiling throws everyone out of the room. The exam answer is simply: "boiling overcomes all the intermolecular forces, melting overcomes only some of them."
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: During melting the energy supplied is used to overcome the forces of attraction between the particles, not to increase their kinetic energy, so the temperature remains constant.
例题Example
把 -10 °C 的冰持续加热，一直到 120 °C 的水蒸气。描述温度—时间曲线的形状，并解释其中两段「平台」分别在发生什么。Ice at -10 °C is heated steadily until it becomes steam at 120 °C. Describe the shape of the temperature–time graph and explain what happens during the two plateaus.
① 从 -10 °C 升到 0 °C：冰在升温，粒子振动得更厉害，斜线上升。① From -10 °C to 0 °C the ice warms up: the particles vibrate harder, so the line rises. ② 第一段平台（0 °C）：冰在熔化。温度不动，因为热量全用来破坏晶格里的分子间力。② First plateau (0 °C): the ice melts. The temperature stays flat because the heat is breaking the intermolecular forces in the lattice. ③ 0 °C 到 100 °C：水在升温，粒子跑得更快，斜线再次上升。③ From 0 °C to 100 °C the water warms up, the particles move faster, and the line rises again. ④ 第二段平台（100 °C）：水在沸腾。要彻底把分子拉开，所以这段平台比第一段长得多。④ Second plateau (100 °C): the water boils. Every molecule must be pulled right away from its neighbours, so this plateau is much longer than the first.
熔化 (0 °C): 6.01 kJ mol⁻¹ 汽化 (100 °C): 40.7 kJ mol⁻¹ ≈ 7 倍
⑤ 100 °C 以上：水蒸气继续升温，斜线上升。整条曲线是「斜—平—斜—平—斜」。⑤ Above 100 °C the steam warms up and the line rises again. The whole graph reads: slope, flat, slope, flat, slope.
练习Practice
两问都用粒子模型回答：粒子在哪、动得多快、力有没有被破坏。Answer both with the particle model: where the particles are, how fast they move, and which forces are being broken.

(a) 水在 100 °C 沸腾时，继续加热，温度却一直是 100 °C，为什么？(b) 为什么固体有固定形状，而液体没有？(a) Water boiling at 100 °C stays at 100 °C even though heating continues — why? (b) Why does a solid have a fixed shape while a liquid does not?

点开看答案Show answer
(a) 加热提供的能量被用来克服水分子之间的分子间力，把分子从液体里送到气相，而不是用来加快分子的平均速率。温度只反映平均动能，所以温度不变。
(b) 固体的粒子被固定在规则的位置上，只能在原地振动，所以整体保持确定的形状；液体的粒子虽然也靠得很近，但可以相对滑动，所以能流动、形状随容器改变，体积却基本不变。 (a) The energy supplied is used to overcome the forces of attraction between the water molecules and move them into the gas phase, not to raise their average speed. Temperature reflects average kinetic energy only, so it stays constant.
(b) In a solid the particles are held in fixed, regular positions and can only vibrate, so the whole thing keeps a definite shape. In a liquid the particles are still close but can slide past one another, so it flows and takes the shape of its container while keeping the same volume.
— 第 1 站完成 —— Stop 1 done —
2 理想气体方程 pV = nRTThe ideal gas equation pV = nRT Ideal gas equation理想气体方程
这一站要你会：用 pV = nRT 求 p、V、n、T 中任意一个；并且养成习惯——先把单位换成 Pa、m³、K 再代数字。Goal: use pV = nRT to find any one of p, V, n or T — and always convert to Pa, m³ and K before substituting.
这条式子像一台有三个旋钮的机器：压强、体积、温度。你拧动一个，别的就会跟着动——但前提是你会用正确的刻度。单位就是刻度：拿「厘米」去套「米」的公式，出来的答案一定离谱，而且离谱得很安静（不会报错，只会扣分）。

所以做题时先在草稿纸最上面写三行：p 用 Pa、V 用 m³、T 用 K，再抄公式。这三行写完，这题基本就成功一半了。Think of the equation as a machine with three knobs: pressure, volume, temperature. Turn one and the others move — but only if you use the right scale. Units are the scale: feed centimetres into a formula built for metres and the answer will be wrong, quietly wrong (no error message, just lost marks).

So before anything else, write three lines at the top of your rough work: p in Pa, V in m³, T in K. Half the marks are won right there.
公式本体：The equation itself:
pV = nRT p = 压强 (Pa) V = 体积 (m³) n = 物质的量 (mol) T = 热力学温度 (K) R = 8.31 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ 变形：n = pV / RT V = nRT / p T = pV / nR
量Quantity必须用的单位Unit you must use最常见的错Classic mistake
压强 pPressure pPa直接把 kPa 代进去substituting kPa as it stands
体积 VVolume Vm³直接把 dm³ 或 cm³ 代进去substituting dm³ or cm³ as it stands
温度 TTemperature TK直接把 °C 代进去substituting °C as it stands
  • 温度换算：T(K) = θ(°C) + 273。25 °C = 298 K，0 °C = 273 K，-23 °C = 250 K。注意是 273，不是 273.15（CAIE 用 273 就够）。Temperature: T(K) = θ(°C) + 273. 25 °C = 298 K, 0 °C = 273 K, -23 °C = 250 K. Use 273, not 273.15 — that is what CAIE expects.
  • 体积换算：1 dm³ = 1×10⁻³ m³；1 cm³ = 1×10⁻⁶ m³；1 m³ = 1000 dm³ = 10⁶ cm³。Volume: 1 dm³ = 1 × 10⁻³ m³; 1 cm³ = 1 × 10⁻⁶ m³; 1 m³ = 1000 dm³ = 10⁶ cm³.
  • 压强换算：1 kPa = 1000 Pa；1 MPa = 10⁶ Pa；1 atm ≈ 101 kPa。题目给「100 kPa」就要写成 100 000 Pa。Pressure: 1 kPa = 1000 Pa; 1 MPa = 10⁶ Pa; 1 atm ≈ 101 kPa. A question saying "100 kPa" means 100 000 Pa.
  • R 的单位别丢：8.31 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ 就是 8.31 Pa m³ K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ —— Pa × m³ 正好是焦耳，所以单位能对上。R carries units: 8.31 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ is the same as 8.31 Pa m³ K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ — p × V in Pa m³ is a joule, so everything cancels.
三步自检法（考试时默念）：① 三个量都换成基本单位了吗？② T 是不是加了 273？③ 答案量级合理吗——1 mol 气体在室温常压下大约 24 dm³，也就是 24 个大可乐瓶。算出 0.24 dm³ 或 2400 dm³，立刻回头查单位。Three-step check (say it in the exam): ① are all three quantities in base units? ② did I add 273? ③ is the size sensible — one mole of gas at room conditions is about 24 dm³, roughly 24 large drinks bottles. If you get 0.24 dm³ or 2400 dm³, go back and check the units.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: The pressure must be converted from kPa to Pa, the volume from cm³ to m³, and the temperature from °C to K by adding 273, before these values are substituted into pV = nRT.
例题Example
25 °C、100 kPa 下，0.500 mol 的气体占多大体积？分别用 m³ 和 dm³ 表示。What volume does 0.500 mol of gas occupy at 25 °C and 100 kPa? Give your answer in m³ and in dm³.
① 换温度：T = 25 + 273 = 298 K。① Temperature: T = 25 + 273 = 298 K. ② 换压强：p = 100 kPa = 100 000 Pa。② Pressure: p = 100 kPa = 100 000 Pa. ③ 变形求体积：V = nRT / p。③ Rearrange for volume: V = nRT / p.
V = 0.500 × 8.31 × 298 / 100 000 = 1238 / 100 000 = 1.24 × 10⁻² m³ = 12.4 dm³
④ 自检：0.5 mol 在 rtp 下约 12 dm³，和答案一致——单位没搞错。④ Check: 0.5 mol at room conditions is about 12 dm³, matching the answer — the units are right.
练习Practice
(a) 先换 K 和 Pa；(b) 压强不变时，体积与温度成正比——温度翻倍，体积也翻倍。(a) convert to K and Pa first; (b) at constant pressure, volume is proportional to temperature — double T, double V.

0.250 mol 的气体在 27 °C、120 kPa 下。(a) 它的体积是多少 dm³？(b) 若压强不变，把温度升到 327 °C，体积变成多少 dm³？0.250 mol of gas is at 27 °C and 120 kPa. (a) What is its volume in dm³? (b) If the pressure is unchanged and the temperature rises to 327 °C, what is the new volume?

点开看答案Show answer
(a) T = 27 + 273 = 300 K；p = 120 000 Pa。
V = nRT/p = 0.250 × 8.31 × 300 / 120 000 = 623.25 / 120 000 = 5.19 × 10⁻³ m³ = 5.19 dm³。
(b) 300 K → 600 K，温度变为 2 倍；p、n 不变，所以 V 也变为 2 倍 = 10.4 dm³。（也可用 V2 = V1T2/T1 = 5.19 × 600/300。） (a) T = 27 + 273 = 300 K; p = 120 000 Pa.
V = nRT/p = 0.250 × 8.31 × 300 / 120 000 = 623.25 / 120 000 = 5.19 × 10⁻³ m³ = 5.19 dm³.
(b) 300 K → 600 K, so T doubles; with p and n fixed, V doubles too = 10.4 dm³. (Or V2 = V1T2/T1 = 5.19 × 600/300.)
— 第 2 站完成 —— Stop 2 done —
3 用气体数据反推摩尔质量Finding Mr from gas data Determining Mr测定摩尔质量
这一站要你会：把「质量 + 压强 + 体积 + 温度」这四样数据，变成气体的相对分子质量 Mr，并用它判断这是哪种气体。Goal: turn four measurements — mass, pressure, volume and temperature — into a relative molecular mass Mr, then use it to identify the gas.
这招其实和数糖果一模一样：你称出一整袋糖 500 g，又数出袋里有 100 颗，那么一颗就是 5 g。气体看不见、数不清，但 pV = nRT 能替你「数出有多少颗」——它把体积、压强、温度翻译成摩尔数。

有了「这袋气体是多少 mol」和「这袋有多重」，一除，就得到「每一 mol 多重」。这个数字一旦对上一个分子式，气体就相当于自报家门了。This is exactly the sweet-shop trick: weigh a bag of sweets at 500 g, count 100 sweets, and one sweet must be 5 g. You cannot see or count gas particles, but pV = nRT counts them for you — it translates volume, pressure and temperature into moles.

Once you know how many moles are in the syringe and how much that gas weighs, one division gives the mass of one mole. Match that number to a formula and the gas has introduced itself.
两步公式：Two equations, in order:
第一步（数个数）： n = pV / RT 第二步（称一个）： M = m / n (g mol⁻¹) 最后： Mr 与 M 数值相同，但 Mr 无单位
  • 先 n 后 M，顺序不能反。n 是桥，所有气体数据都要先过这座桥。n first, then M — never the other way round. n is the bridge every gas measurement must cross.
  • m 用克（g），别用 kg。如果题目给 mg，先除以 1000。m in grams, not kilograms. If a question gives mg, divide by 1000 first.
  • V 一定要换成 m³。168 cm³ = 168 × 10⁻⁶ m³ = 1.68 × 10⁻⁴ m³。V must be in m³. 168 cm³ = 168 × 10⁻⁶ m³ = 1.68 × 10⁻⁴ m³.
  • 识别气体：把算出的 M 和候选分子式比。M ≈ 32 → O2；M ≈ 44 → CO2；M ≈ 28 → N2 或 CO；M ≈ 16 → CH4。差 1 以内都算「相符」。Identifying the gas: compare your M with candidate formulae. M ≈ 32 → O2; 44 → CO2; 28 → N2 or CO; 16 → CH4. Within about 1 unit counts as a match.
为什么这题必须「先算 n」？因为气体体积会随温度、压强变，同样 1 mol 在热天占的地方更大。所以不能拿体积直接比，必须先折成 mol。这也是为什么题目一定要给你 T 和 p ——少了任何一个，n 都算不出来。Why must you find n first? Because a gas volume changes with temperature and pressure: one mole takes up more room on a hot day. You cannot compare volumes directly, so convert to moles first. That is exactly why the question must give you T and p — without either one, n is impossible.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: The number of moles is calculated from n = pV/RT, then the molar mass is found from M = m/n; comparing this value with the masses of possible formulae identifies the gas.
例题Example
某气体 0.216 g，在 100 kPa、300 K 下占 168 cm³。求它的摩尔质量，并判断它可能是哪种气体。A gas of mass 0.216 g occupies 168 cm³ at 100 kPa and 300 K. Calculate its molar mass and suggest what the gas could be.
① 换体积：168 cm³ = 168 × 10⁻⁶ = 1.68 × 10⁻⁴ m³。① Volume: 168 cm³ = 168 × 10⁻⁶ = 1.68 × 10⁻⁴ m³. ② 换压强：100 kPa = 100 000 Pa；温度已经是 K，T = 300 K。② Pressure: 100 kPa = 100 000 Pa; the temperature is already in K, T = 300 K. ③ 先求 n：③ Find n first:
n = pV / RT = (100 000 × 1.68 × 10⁻⁴) / (8.31 × 300) = 16.8 / 2493 = 6.74 × 10⁻³ mol
④ 再求 M：④ Then find M:
M = m / n = 0.216 / 6.74 × 10⁻³ = 32.1 g mol⁻¹
⑤ 判断：Mr ≈ 32，最接近 O2（2 × 16.0 = 32.0）。CO 是 28、CO2 是 44，都对不上。⑤ Identify: Mr ≈ 32, closest to O2 (2 × 16.0 = 32.0). CO is 28 and CO2 is 44, so neither fits.
练习Practice
250 cm³ 要先变成 2.50 × 10⁻⁴ m³；算完 M 再和 46 比一比。Turn 250 cm³ into 2.50 × 10⁻⁴ m³ first, then compare your M with 46.

某气体 0.460 g，在 100 kPa、298 K 下占 250 cm³。(a) 求它的摩尔质量。(b) 已知候选气体有 NO2（Mr = 46.0）、N2O（44.0）、SO2（64.1），它是哪一种？A gas of mass 0.460 g occupies 250 cm³ at 100 kPa and 298 K. (a) Calculate its molar mass. (b) Which is it: NO2 (Mr = 46.0), N2O (44.0) or SO2 (64.1)?

点开看答案Show answer
(a) V = 250 × 10⁻⁶ = 2.50 × 10⁻⁴ m³；p = 100 000 Pa；T = 298 K。
n = pV/RT = (100 000 × 2.50 × 10⁻⁴)/(8.31 × 298) = 25.0/2476 = 1.01 × 10⁻² mol。
M = 0.460 / 1.01 × 10⁻² = 45.6 g mol⁻¹。
(b) 45.6 最接近 NO2（46.0）；N2O 的 44.0 差了 1.6，SO2 的 64.1 差得更多。
小提醒：算出的 45.6 与 46.0 差 0.4，属于正常的测量与取整误差，考试里写「与 NO2 相符」就好。 (a) V = 250 × 10⁻⁶ = 2.50 × 10⁻⁴ m³; p = 100 000 Pa; T = 298 K.
n = pV/RT = (100 000 × 2.50 × 10⁻⁴)/(8.31 × 298) = 25.0/2476 = 1.01 × 10⁻² mol.
M = 0.460 / 1.01 × 10⁻² = 45.6 g mol⁻¹.
(b) 45.6 is closest to NO2 (46.0); N2O at 44.0 is 1.6 away and SO2 at 64.1 is far off.
Note: 45.6 against 46.0 is a normal rounding and measurement gap — in the exam just write "consistent with NO2".

4 真实气体为什么不像理想气体Why real gases misbehave Deviation from ideal偏离理想行为
这一站要你会：说出理想气体的两个关键假设，并解释高压与低温各打破哪一个、导致压强偏大还是偏小；最后说出「什么条件下最接近理想」。Goal: state the two key assumptions of an ideal gas, explain which one breaks at high pressure and which at low temperature, and say when a real gas behaves most ideally.
理想气体是一个乌托邦：每个公民都是没有体积的质点，彼此之间毫无感情，撞一下就弹开，从不纠缠。这样的社会算起来特别干净，所以物理学家爱用它。

真实气体不是这样。每个分子都拖着一个行李箱（自身体积），而且彼此之间还有点儿黏（分子间力）。平时箱子小、大家跑得快，这些毛病看不出来；可一旦挤（高压）或者冻（低温），真面目就露出来了。An ideal gas is a utopia: every citizen is a point with no size, feels nothing for its neighbours, bounces off them and never lingers. Such a society is beautifully easy to calculate with, which is why physicists love it.

Real gases are not like that. Every molecule drags a suitcase (its own volume) and is slightly sticky (intermolecular forces). Normally the suitcase is small and everyone moves fast, so nobody notices. Squeeze them (high pressure) or chill them (low temperature) and the truth comes out.
理想气体的三条假设，以及它们怎么倒：The assumptions, and how each one fails:
  • 假设一：分子本身体积可以忽略（把分子当成几何点）。
    高压下失效：分子被挤到一起，自身体积占了容器体积的一部分，真正能自由活动的空间比 V 小；于是分子撞壁更频繁，实测 p 比理想值大。    Assumption 1: the volume of the molecules themselves is negligible (treat them as points).
    It fails at high pressure: squeezed together, the molecules occupy a real share of the container, so the free space is smaller than V; they hit the walls more often and the measured p is larger than ideal.
  • 假设二：分子之间没有作用力（除了碰撞）。
    低温下失效：分子平均速率小，经过邻居身边的时间变长，吸引力有机会起作用；分子快撞到器壁时被「往回拉」一把，实测 p 比理想值小。    Assumption 2: there are no forces between molecules (other than during collisions).
    It fails at low temperature: the molecules move slowly, spend longer near their neighbours, and attraction gets a chance to act; a molecule about to hit the wall is pulled back slightly, so the measured p is smaller than ideal.
  • 假设三：碰撞完全弹性，分子间没有能量交换损失。这一条在普通条件下基本成立，考试很少考。Assumption 3: collisions are perfectly elastic, with no loss of energy. This one holds well under normal conditions and is rarely examined.
  • 结论：低压、高温最接近理想。低压 → 分子隔得远，体积和吸引力都不重要；高温 → 分子跑得快，吸引力来不及拽住它。Conclusion: low pressure and high temperature give the most ideal behaviour. Low p → molecules are far apart, so size and attraction hardly matter; high T → they move so fast that attraction cannot hold them.
Z = pV / (nRT) 压缩因子 Z = 1 理想气体 Z > 1 分子体积占主导（高压） Z < 1 分子间吸引占主导（低温）
两个高频错误，背下来避开：① 写成「高压低温下最接近理想」——正好反了，高压和低温都是最不像理想的条件。② 写成「分子有吸引力，所以压强更大」——吸引力把分子往回拉，只会让压强更小。真正让压强变大的是分子自身体积。Two mistakes to avoid: ① "closest to ideal at high pressure and low temperature" — exactly backwards; both push a gas furthest from ideal. ② "attraction makes the pressure bigger" — attraction pulls molecules back and makes the pressure smaller. It is the volume of the molecules that raises it.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: At high pressure the volume occupied by the gas molecules themselves is no longer negligible, so the pressure is higher than predicted. At low temperature the molecules move slowly and intermolecular forces become significant, so the pressure is lower than predicted.
例题Example
1.00 mol 某气体在 300 K 时被压进 0.100 dm³ 的钢瓶。(a) 用理想气体方程算压强。(b) 实际测得 2.60 × 10⁷ Pa，比理想值大还是小？(c) 用哪一个假设被打破来解释？1.00 mol of a gas at 300 K is compressed into a 0.100 dm³ cylinder. (a) Calculate the pressure using the ideal gas equation. (b) The measured value is 2.60 × 10⁷ Pa — larger or smaller? (c) Which assumption has broken down?
① 换体积：0.100 dm³ = 0.100 × 10⁻³ = 1.00 × 10⁻⁴ m³。① Volume: 0.100 dm³ = 0.100 × 10⁻³ = 1.00 × 10⁻⁴ m³. ② 代公式：② Substitute:
p = nRT / V = (1.00 × 8.31 × 300) / (1.00 × 10⁻⁴) = 2493 / (1.00 × 10⁻⁴) = 2.49 × 10⁷ Pa
③ 比较：实测 2.60 × 10⁷ Pa 大于 2.49 × 10⁷ Pa，约高 4%。③ Compare: the measured 2.60 × 10⁷ Pa is larger than 2.49 × 10⁷ Pa, by about 4%. ④ 解释：这是高压情形，分子被挤得很近，分子自身体积不可忽略，能自由活动的空间小于钢瓶体积，所以撞壁更频繁、压强偏大。此时 Z = pV/nRT ≈ 1.04 > 1。④ Explanation: this is the high-pressure case — the molecules are packed so closely that their own volume is no longer negligible, the free space is less than the cylinder volume, so collisions with the walls are more frequent and the pressure is higher. Here Z = pV/nRT ≈ 1.04 > 1.
练习Practice
低温 → 分子慢 → 吸引力有时间起作用；再想一想哪种气体的分子间力最弱。Low T → slow molecules → attraction has time to act; then ask which gas has the weakest intermolecular forces.

(a) 某气体在低温下测得的压强比理想值小约 8%，用分子运动解释原因。(b) 氦气比二氧化碳更接近理想气体，为什么？(a) At low temperature a gas shows a pressure about 8% below the ideal value. Explain in terms of the particles. (b) Helium behaves more ideally than carbon dioxide — why?

点开看答案Show answer
(a) 低温下分子平均速率小，经过邻居身边的时间更长，分子间吸引力有时间起作用；分子撞向器壁时被邻居往回拉了一点，撞击力变小，所以压强低于理想值（Z < 1）。
(b) 氦原子只有一个电子层、体积很小，而且是非极性单原子，分子间力（色散力）极弱、自身体积也小。两个「假设被打破」的程度都最轻，所以在同样的条件下最接近理想气体。CO2 分子大、电子多，色散力强，偏离更明显。 (a) At low temperature the average speed is small, so a molecule spends longer near its neighbours and intermolecular attraction has time to act. A molecule approaching the wall is pulled back slightly, hits with less force, and the pressure is below the ideal value (Z < 1).
(b) A helium atom has a single shell, is very small and is a non-polar single atom, so its intermolecular (dispersion) forces are extremely weak and it occupies little space. Both assumptions break down least, so it is closest to ideal under the same conditions. CO2 is a larger molecule with more electrons, so its dispersion forces are stronger and the deviation is bigger.

5 四种结构决定四种脾气Four structures, four personalities Structure & properties结构与性质
这一站要你会：看到一种物质，先说它属于四类结构中的哪一类，再由结构推出熔点、导电性、力学性质，而不是死记一个个例子。Goal: classify a substance into one of four structures, then deduce its melting point, conductivity and mechanical behaviour from that structure instead of memorising examples one by one.
把四种结构想成四种社交方式：
离子晶体是「正负相间排排坐」，纪律严明、谁也不许动，所以硬；可一旦有人被推错位，同号的人面对面就吵起来，整块裂开——所以脆。
简单分子是「一对一对的小情侣」，两个人之间黏得很紧（共价键），但情侣和情侣之间几乎不认识，所以很容易被拆散——熔点低、软。
巨型共价是「全城人手拉手」，要拆散一个人得掰开四只手，所以极硬极难熔；石墨是特例，层内手拉手、层间只是叠着，还能滑。
金属是「正离子泡在电子海里」，人可以滑动，海还在，所以能拉成丝、压成片。Think of the four structures as four ways of socialising:
Ionic is "plus and minus seated alternately", strict discipline, nobody moves — hence hard; but push a row out of line and like charges face each other — hence brittle.
Simple molecular is "couples holding hands": each pair is tightly bonded, but couples barely know each other, so the solid falls apart easily — low melting point, soft.
Giant covalent is "the whole city holding hands": to remove one atom you must break four hands — extremely hard and refractory. Graphite is the exception: strong within a layer, only stacked between layers, so the layers slide.
Metallic is "cations floating in a sea of electrons": the layers can slide and the sea still holds them — so metals stretch into wires and flatten into sheets.
一张表对完：The whole comparison in one table:
结构Structure例子Examples熔点Melting point导电Conducts?受力时Under stress
巨型离子Giant ionicNaCl, MgO高（NaCl 801 °C，MgO 2852 °C）high (NaCl 801 °C, MgO 2852 °C)固态不导；熔融或水溶液导电not as a solid; conducts molten or in solution硬而脆，一敲就裂hard but brittle, cracks when hit
简单分子Simple molecularI2, CO2, H2O低（I2 约 114 °C 升华）low (I2 sublimes near 114 °C)不导电does not conduct软、易挥发soft, volatile
巨型共价Giant covalentdiamond, graphite, SiO2极高（金刚石 > 3500 °C）very high (diamond > 3500 °C)金刚石不导；石墨导电diamond no; graphite yes金刚石极硬；石墨层间易滑diamond very hard; graphite layers slide
金属MetallicCu, Fe, Mg中到高（Mg 650 °C，Fe 1538 °C）medium to high (Mg 650 °C, Fe 1538 °C)固态就导电导热conducts as a solid延展，可拉丝、可压片malleable and ductile
  • 熔点是「拆房子」的代价。要熔化的到底是分子间力还是共价键/离子键？前者便宜（简单分子），后者昂贵（巨型结构）。这一句能解释本单元一半的熔点题。Melting point is the price of demolition. Ask what must be broken: intermolecular forces (cheap — simple molecular) or covalent/ionic bonds (expensive — giant structures). That one sentence answers half the melting-point questions in this topic.
  • 导电的判据只有一条：有没有自由移动的带电粒子。离子晶体固态时离子被锁在格子里 → 不导；熔融后离子能跑 → 导。金属有自由电子 → 导。简单分子既无自由离子也无自由电子 → 不导。There is only one test for conduction: are there mobile charged particles? In a solid ionic lattice the ions are locked in place → no conduction; once molten they can move → conduction. Metals have free electrons → conduction. Simple molecules have neither → no conduction.
  • 石墨为什么特殊？每个碳用 3 个共价键连住同一层里的 3 个邻居，第 4 个电子离域在层与层之间，可以自由跑 → 层内导电。层与层之间只有弱作用力 → 容易滑，所以石墨软、能当润滑剂。Why is graphite special? Each carbon uses three covalent bonds to three neighbours in the same layer; the fourth electron is delocalised between the layers and can move freely → conduction along the layer. Only weak forces hold the layers together → they slide, which is why graphite is soft and works as a lubricant.
  • 金属为什么能拉成丝？离子层受力后可以整体滑过去，滑动之后电子海仍然把各层黏在一起，所以只变形、不断裂。Why do metals stretch? The layers of cations slide over one another and the sea of electrons still holds them together afterwards, so the metal changes shape instead of breaking.
解释题的三句式，套上就不会丢分：①「它属于……结构」；②「熔化/变形时需要破坏的是……」（分子间力？离子键？共价键？）；③「所以熔点……/所以能导电……」。只写结论不写「破坏什么」，通常只拿一半分。A three-sentence template for explanation questions: ① "It has a ... structure"; ② "Melting/deforming requires breaking ..." (intermolecular forces? ionic bonds? covalent bonds?); ③ "Therefore the melting point is ... / therefore it conducts." A conclusion without the "what must be broken" step usually earns half marks.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: Sodium chloride has a giant ionic lattice. When molten, the ions are free to move and carry charge, so it conducts electricity; when solid, the ions are held in fixed positions and cannot move.
例题Example
(a) 为什么固态 NaCl 不导电，而熔融的 NaCl 能导电？(b) 为什么金刚石不导电，石墨却能导电？(a) Why does solid NaCl not conduct, while molten NaCl does? (b) Why does diamond not conduct, while graphite does?
① 先定结构：NaCl 是巨型离子晶格；金刚石与石墨都是巨型共价结构。① Name the structures: NaCl is a giant ionic lattice; diamond and graphite are both giant covalent. ② 固态 NaCl：Na+ 与 Cl− 被强大的静电引力固定在格点上，不能移动，所以没有可移动的带电粒子 → 不导电。② Solid NaCl: Na+ and Cl− are locked in the lattice by strong electrostatic attraction and cannot move, so there are no mobile charged particles → no conduction. ③ 熔融 NaCl：晶格被破坏，离子获得自由，离子本身定向移动就能运载电荷 → 导电。（水溶液同理。）③ Molten NaCl: the lattice is broken, the ions become free, and the ions themselves migrate to carry charge → conduction. (Same in aqueous solution.) ④ 金刚石：每个碳的 4 个价电子全部用在 4 个 σ 共价键上，没有自由电子 → 不导电，而且键强、四面体网络坚硬。④ Diamond: all four valence electrons of each carbon are used in four σ bonds, leaving no free electrons → no conduction, and the strong tetrahedral network makes it hard. ⑤ 石墨：每个碳只形成 3 个 σ 键，第 4 个电子离域在层间，能在层内自由移动 → 导电。层间作用力弱 → 软、易滑。⑤ Graphite: each carbon forms only three σ bonds, and the fourth electron is delocalised between the layers and free to move along them → conduction. The weak forces between layers make it soft and slippery.
练习Practice
(a) 比较离子电荷与离子半径，电荷越高、半径越小，静电引力越强；(b) 想一层「滑过去之后」两边是谁对着谁。(a) compare ionic charge and radius — higher charge and smaller radius mean stronger attraction; (b) think about who ends up facing whom after a layer slides.

(a) MgO 的熔点（2852 °C）远高于 NaCl（801 °C），解释原因。(b) 为什么金属能被锤成薄片，而 NaCl 晶体一敲就碎？(a) MgO melts at 2852 °C, far above NaCl at 801 °C — explain. (b) Why can a metal be hammered into a thin sheet while a NaCl crystal shatters?

点开看答案Show answer
(a) 两者都是巨型离子晶格，熔化要破坏离子键。MgO 中离子是 Mg2+ 与 O2−，电荷是 NaCl 中 Na+、Cl− 的两倍；而且 Mg2+、O2− 的半径比 Na+、Cl− 更小，离子间距离更短。静电引力 ∝ 电荷乘积 / 距离²，两个因素都让 MgO 的离子键强得多，所以要高得多的温度才能熔。
(b) 金属是阳离子层泡在电子海里，锤击时层与层整体滑过去，电子海仍然把层黏住，所以只变形不断裂（延展性）。NaCl 晶体被敲时，一层滑动了半个离子位，结果同号离子正对着（Na+ 对 Na+、Cl− 对 Cl−），强烈相斥，裂纹瞬间扩展，整块脆裂。 (a) Both are giant ionic lattices, so melting means breaking ionic bonds. In MgO the ions are Mg2+ and O2−, carrying twice the charge of Na+ and Cl−, and Mg2+/O2− are smaller than Na+/Cl−, so the ions sit closer. Electrostatic attraction goes as charge product over distance squared, so both factors make the bonding in MgO much stronger and a far higher temperature is needed.
(b) A metal is layers of cations in a sea of electrons; hammering makes the layers slide as a whole and the electron sea still holds them together, so the metal deforms rather than breaks (malleable). In NaCl, a knock slides one layer by half a spacing, leaving like charges facing each other (Na+ against Na+, Cl− against Cl−); the strong repulsion propagates a crack and the crystal shatters.

单元 4 小结Unit 4 summary

① 三态的区别只有三件事：粒子隔多远、怎么动、能量够不够。熔化与沸腾时温度不动，是因为热量被拿去破坏分子间力，而不是加快粒子。
② 气体计算的全部难点在单位：p 用 Pa、V 用 m³、T 用 K（+273），R = 8.31。先换算，再代公式，最后用量级自检（1 mol ≈ 24 dm³）。
③ 反推摩尔质量是两步：n = pV/RT 先数出摩尔数，再 M = m/n 得到每摩尔多少克，最后和候选分子式比对。① Three states differ in three things only: how far apart the particles are, how they move, and whether they have enough energy. Temperature stays flat during melting and boiling because the heat goes into breaking intermolecular forces, not into speeding particles up.
② Every gas calculation is really a unit question: p in Pa, V in m³, T in K (+273), R = 8.31. Convert first, substitute second, sanity-check the size last (1 mol ≈ 24 dm³).
③ Finding Mr takes two steps: n = pV/RT counts the moles, then M = m/n gives grams per mole, which you match against candidate formulae.

④ 真实气体在高压下因分子自身体积而 p 偏大，在低温下因分子间吸引而 p 偏小；低压高温最接近理想。
⑤ 结构决定性质：先问「靠什么键连成多大一块」，再问「有没有能自由移动的带电粒子」。离子晶体硬而脆、简单分子软而低熔、巨型共价极硬、金属延展导电——四句话能推出一整章的性质。④ Real gases show a pressure above ideal at high pressure (molecular volume) and below ideal at low temperature (intermolecular attraction); low pressure and high temperature come closest to ideal.
⑤ Structure decides properties: first ask "what bonds hold it together, and how far does the network extend?", then "are there mobile charged particles?". Ionic is hard and brittle, simple molecular is soft with a low melting point, giant covalent is extremely hard, metals are malleable and conduct — four sentences cover a whole chapter of properties.

下一站要去哪里：这一单元我们一直在说「破坏分子间力要花能量」，可到底花了多少、怎么量、能不能算？这就是单元 5 能量学 的主题——焓变、燃烧热、赫斯定律，把「热」变成可以记账的数字。Where next: this unit kept saying that breaking intermolecular forces costs energy — but how much, how do we measure it, and can we calculate it? That is Unit 5, energetics: enthalpy change, enthalpy of combustion and Hess's law, where heat becomes something you can balance like a bank account.

单元 5 · 化学能量学：反应为什么会热、冷、甚至自己烧起来Unit 5 · Chemical energetics: why reactions heat up, cool down or set themselves alight

CAIE 9701 Topic 5 · 6 站 · 反应为什么会热、冷、甚至自己烧起来CAIE 9701 Topic 5 · 6 stops · why reactions give out heat, take it in, or even set themselves alight

路线图本单元六站：先学会给「热」记账，再学怎么画、怎么算、怎么量Six stops: learn to keep an energy account, then draw it, calculate it and measure it

  1. 系统、环境与焓变：先给「热」分个账本System, surroundings and enthalpy change
  2. 反应进程图：能量怎么走（活化能与 ΔH）Reaction profiles: where the energy goes
  3. 三种标准焓变，定义要一字不差Three standard enthalpy changes, definitions word-perfect
  4. 用键焓估算 ΔH：断键花钱，成键回本Estimating ΔH from bond enthalpies
  5. Hess 定律：绕路也一样Hess's law: any route, same answer
  6. 在实验室里量出来：量热计与 q = mcΔTMeasuring enthalpy changes: the calorimeter and q = mcΔT

建议：第 1、2 站是「画面」，一定要先建立直觉；第 3 站是纯背记（定义题按点给分，一个词都不能漏）；第 4、5 站是计算，套路固定，练两题就会；第 6 站把计算和实验接起来，是试卷里最常考的综合题。算完任何一道题都问自己两句：符号对不对、单位是不是 kJ mol⁻¹。Tip: stops 1 and 2 build the picture — get the intuition first. Stop 3 is pure memory (definitions are marked point by point, so not a single word may be dropped). Stops 4 and 5 are calculations with fixed routines. Stop 6 joins calculation to experiment and is the most common exam combination. After every calculation ask yourself two things: is the sign right, and is the unit kJ mol⁻¹?

1 系统、环境与焓变System, surroundings and enthalpy change System & surroundings系统与环境
这一站要你会：区分系统与环境；说出 ΔH 的含义与单位；由温度变化判断放热 / 吸热并写出 ΔH 的正负；并说清「放热」与「自发」不是一回事。Goal: tell the system from the surroundings; state what ΔH means and its unit; decide exothermic or endothermic from a temperature change and give the sign of ΔH; and explain why "exothermic" is not the same as "spontaneous".
把整个宇宙切成两块：你正在研究的那个反应叫系统；剩下的一切叫环境——烧杯里的水、空气、玻璃壁、还有你手里那支温度计，统统算环境。反应放热，就是系统把能量扔给环境，于是环境变热；反应吸热，就是系统从环境借走能量，于是环境变冷。就像冬天屋里生炉子：炉子是系统，屋子是环境，炉子越旺屋子越暖——能量没被创造，也没被销毁，只是从一个口袋换到了另一个口袋。Cut the whole universe into two parts: the reaction you are studying is the system; everything else is the surroundings — the water in the beaker, the air, the glass wall, even the thermometer in your hand. If the reaction gives out heat, the system throws energy out to the surroundings, which get hotter. If it takes heat in, the system borrows energy from the surroundings, which get colder. Like lighting a stove in a cold room: the stove is the system, the room is the surroundings, and the hotter the stove burns the warmer the room gets. Energy is neither created nor destroyed — it just changes pockets.
四条必须记牢：Four things to remember:
  • 系统 system 就是我们盯着看的反应本身；环境 surroundings 是其余的一切（溶剂、容器、空气、温度计）。两者加起来就是整个宇宙。The system is the reaction itself — the chemicals you are watching. The surroundings are everything else: the solvent, the container, the air, the thermometer. Together they make up the universe.
  • 焓变 ΔH：恒压下，系统与环境交换的热量。单位是 kJ mol⁻¹（按方程式进行时每摩尔多少千焦）。Enthalpy change ΔH: the heat exchanged between the system and the surroundings at constant pressure. Unit: kJ mol⁻¹.
  • ΔH 记的是系统的账本：放热时系统少了能量，所以 ΔH 为负；吸热时系统多了能量，所以 ΔH 为正。别跟着环境的感觉走——环境变热，恰恰说明 ΔH 是负的。ΔH is the system's bank account: if it gives out energy its balance falls, so ΔH is negative; if it takes energy in the balance rises, so ΔH is positive. Don't follow your feelings about the surroundings — the surroundings getting hotter is exactly what a negative ΔH looks like.
  • 放热 ≠ 自发。放热只说明能量往哪边流，不说明反应会不会自己发生。冰在 25 °C 的房间里融化是吸热却自发；木头燃烧放热很多，但你得先划一根火柴——那个「起头的力气」叫活化能，第 2 站就讲。Exothermic does not mean spontaneous. "Exothermic" only says which way energy flows, not whether the reaction will happen by itself. Ice melting in a room at 25 °C is endothermic yet spontaneous; wood burning releases plenty of heat, but you still have to strike a match first — that "energy to get going" is the activation energy, the subject of stop 2.
最经典的两个丢分点：① 看到「温度升高」就写 ΔH 为正——温度升高说明环境得了热，也就是系统失了热，ΔH 应该为负。② 把 ΔH 当成环境的账，符号反着写。记一句口诀：热的那个是环境，ΔH 说的是系统。The two classic lost marks: ① seeing "the temperature rises" and writing a positive ΔH — a rising temperature means the surroundings gained heat, so the system lost it and ΔH is negative. ② treating ΔH as the surroundings' account and getting the sign backwards. Remember: the hot thing is the surroundings; ΔH describes the system.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: In an exothermic reaction energy is transferred from the system to the surroundings, so the enthalpy change ΔH is negative and the temperature of the surroundings increases. Exothermic does not mean spontaneous: a reaction can be exothermic and still need a spark to start, because of the activation energy.
例题Example
(a) 生石灰 CaO 加水，水温从 22 °C 升到 58 °C；(b) 硝酸铵 NH4NO3 溶于水，水温从 21 °C 降到 14 °C。分别判断放热还是吸热，写出 ΔH 的符号，并说明判据。(a) Calcium oxide is added to water and the temperature rises from 22 °C to 58 °C. (b) Ammonium nitrate dissolves in water and the temperature falls from 21 °C to 14 °C. Decide whether each is exothermic or endothermic, give the sign of ΔH, and explain the test you used.
① 先认角色：温度计插在水里，水属于环境，所以读数的变化就是环境的变化。① Identify the roles first: the thermometer sits in the water, and the water is part of the surroundings, so the reading tells you what the surroundings did. ② (a) 环境从 22 °C 升到 58 °C → 环境得热 → 能量由系统流向环境 → 放热，ΔH < 0。② (a) the surroundings warm from 22 °C to 58 °C → they gained energy → energy came out of the system → exothermic, ΔH < 0. ③ (b) 环境从 21 °C 降到 14 °C → 环境失热 → 系统从环境吸走能量 → 吸热，ΔH > 0。③ (b) the surroundings cool from 21 °C to 14 °C → they lost energy → the system took it in → endothermic, ΔH > 0. ④ 多想一步：这两个过程都是自发发生的（没人加热，也没人强按着它），可一个放热一个吸热。这说明「会不会自己发生」不能靠 ΔH 的符号来猜。④ One step further: both happen spontaneously (nobody heated them or forced them), yet one is exothermic and one endothermic. So you cannot guess "will it happen by itself?" from the sign of ΔH.
练习Practice
每一步都先问「温度计测的是系统还是环境」，再定符号。Each time, ask first: is the thermometer measuring the system or the surroundings? Then fix the sign.

(a) 镁条放进稀盐酸，试管外壁发烫——判断 ΔH 的符号并说明理由。(b) 柠檬酸与碳酸氢钠混合，杯壁变凉——同样判断并说明。(c) 举一个「吸热但自发」的生活例子。(a) Magnesium ribbon is added to dilute hydrochloric acid and the tube feels hot — give the sign of ΔH and your reason. (b) Citric acid and sodium hydrogencarbonate are mixed and the beaker feels cold — same task. (c) Give an everyday example of something endothermic that still happens by itself.

点开看答案Show answer
(a) 放热，ΔH < 0。试管壁和溶液都是环境，环境变热说明能量由系统（Mg 与酸）流向环境，系统的焓减少，所以 ΔH 为负。
(b) 吸热，ΔH > 0。环境变凉，说明系统从周围「借」走了热量，系统的焓增加，所以 ΔH 为正。
(c) 例子：冰在室温下融化、水在 25 °C 蒸发、急救冷敷袋里的硝酸铵溶于水。它们都吸热，却不需要你加热就自己发生——再一次说明放热与自发是两件事。 (a) Exothermic, ΔH < 0. The tube wall and the solution are the surroundings; if they get hot, energy has flowed out of the system (Mg + acid), so the enthalpy of the system falls and ΔH is negative.
(b) Endothermic, ΔH > 0. The surroundings cool, so the system has taken energy in, its enthalpy rises, and ΔH is positive.
(c) Examples: ice melting at room temperature, water evaporating at 25 °C, a cold pack using ammonium nitrate. All are endothermic yet happen without anyone heating them — once again, exothermic and spontaneous are two different ideas.
— 第 1 站完成 —— Stop 1 done —
2 反应进程图：能量怎么走Reaction profiles: where the energy goes Activation energy活化能
这一站要你会：画出并读懂反应进程图；标出活化能 Ea 与 ΔH；由两条平台的高低判断放热 / 吸热；会算逆反应的活化能。Goal: draw and read a reaction profile; label Ea and ΔH; decide exothermic or endothermic from the two levels; and work out the activation energy of the reverse reaction.
把一次反应想成一次翻山：你站在左边的山谷（反应物），要走到右边的山谷（产物），中间横着一座山。你必须先爬上山顶——那是全程最难熬的一刻，叫过渡态；从山谷到山顶的高度，就是活化能 Ea。翻过顶之后一路下坡，等你落地时比出发时低了还是高了，就是 ΔH。放热反应是终点比起点低（净下坡），吸热反应是终点比起点高（净上坡）。关键的一点是：哪怕终点更低，你也得先爬那座山——这就是木头放热很多却仍要划火柴的原因。Picture a reaction as crossing a mountain: you stand in the valley on the left (reactants), you want to reach the valley on the right (products), and there is a hill in between. You must climb to the top first — the worst moment of the whole trip, called the transition state; the height from your valley to the summit is the activation energy Ea. After the top it is downhill all the way, and whether you end up lower or higher than you began is ΔH. An exothermic reaction ends lower than it started (a net descent); an endothermic one ends higher (a net climb). The key point: even if the end is lower, you still have to climb the hill first — which is why wood releases plenty of heat but still needs a match.
看图五句诀：Five sentences for reading the diagram:
  • 纵轴是焓 H（画得越高代表焓越大），横轴是反应进程（可以理解为「反应进行到多少」）。The y-axis is enthalpy H (higher up = greater enthalpy) and the x-axis is the progress of the reaction.
  • 左右两段平坦的线是反应物平台与产物平台；中间鼓起的包是过渡态（transition state），它不是能分离出来的中间物质。The two flat parts are the reactants level and the products level; the hump in between is the transition state, not a substance you could isolate.
  • ΔH = H(产物) − H(反应物)。产物平台低于反应物 → ΔH 为负（放热）；产物平台高于反应物 → ΔH 为正（吸热）。ΔH = H(products) − H(reactants). Products level below reactants → ΔH negative (exothermic); products level above → ΔH positive (endothermic).
  • Ea 只从反应物平台量到峰顶，与峰的另一侧无关。峰越高，反应越难启动，通常也越慢。Ea is measured only from the reactants level up to the peak; the other side of the hill is irrelevant. A higher peak means a harder start and usually a slower reaction.
  • 逆反应的活化能：Ea(逆) = Ea(正) − ΔH。放热的 ΔH 是负的，减去一个负数等于加，所以逆反应要爬得更高。For the reverse reaction: Ea(reverse) = Ea(forward) − ΔH. Since an exothermic ΔH is negative, subtracting it adds, so the reverse climb is higher.
最容易画错的一笔：把 ΔH 标成「从峰顶量到产物平台」。那一段其实是 Ea(逆)，不是 ΔH。ΔH 只关心两条平台之间的高度差，跟山有多高完全无关——就像你只关心终点海拔减起点海拔，不在乎路上翻过多高的山口。The single most common drawing error: labelling ΔH as the drop from the peak to the products level. That distance is Ea(reverse), not ΔH. ΔH only cares about the gap between the two flat levels — just as a hike's net change in altitude ignores how high the pass in between was.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: The activation energy, Ea, is the minimum energy needed for a reaction to occur; it is measured from the enthalpy of the reactants to the top of the curve. ΔH is the difference between the enthalpy of the products and the enthalpy of the reactants. For an exothermic reaction the products are at a lower enthalpy than the reactants, so ΔH is negative.
例题Example
某反应的正反应活化能 Ea(正) = 120 kJ mol⁻¹，ΔH = −80 kJ mol⁻¹。求逆反应的活化能，并说明这个反应是放热还是吸热。A reaction has Ea(forward) = 120 kJ mol⁻¹ and ΔH = −80 kJ mol⁻¹. Calculate the activation energy of the reverse reaction, and say whether the forward reaction is exothermic or endothermic.
① ΔH = −80 < 0，说明产物平台比反应物平台低 80 → 正反应放热。① ΔH = −80 < 0, so the products level is 80 lower than the reactants → the forward reaction is exothermic. ② 逆反应从产物出发，要先爬回那 80 的落差，再爬正反应那段 120 的山。② The reverse reaction starts from the products, so it must first climb back up the 80 drop and then climb the 120 hill the forward reaction faced.
Ea(逆) = Ea(正) − ΔH = 120 − (−80) = 200 kJ mol⁻¹
③ 自检：逆反应必然比正反应更难（200 > 120），因为要把刚放出去的 80 再补回来，合理。③ Sanity check: the reverse must be harder than the forward (200 > 120), because it has to pay back the 80 that was given out — that makes sense.
练习Practice
先把 ΔH 的符号翻成「终点比起点高还是低」，再套 Ea(逆) = Ea(正) − ΔH。First turn the sign of ΔH into "does the end sit higher or lower than the start?", then use Ea(reverse) = Ea(forward) − ΔH.

某反应 Ea(正) = 95 kJ mol⁻¹，ΔH = +45 kJ mol⁻¹。(a) 它是放热还是吸热？在图上产物平台应该画在反应物平台的上面还是下面？(b) 逆反应的活化能是多少？A reaction has Ea(forward) = 95 kJ mol⁻¹ and ΔH = +45 kJ mol⁻¹. (a) Is it exothermic or endothermic, and should the products level be drawn above or below the reactants level? (b) What is the activation energy of the reverse reaction?

点开看答案Show answer
(a) ΔH = +45 > 0 → 吸热，产物平台要画在反应物平台的上面（高 45）。
(b) Ea(逆) = Ea(正) − ΔH = 95 − 45 = 50 kJ mol⁻¹。吸热反应的逆反应更容易启动（50 < 95），因为下坡方向本来就能把那 45 还回来。 (a) ΔH = +45 > 0 → endothermic, and the products level is drawn above the reactants level (45 higher).
(b) Ea(reverse) = Ea(forward) − ΔH = 95 − 45 = 50 kJ mol⁻¹. The reverse of an endothermic reaction is easier to start (50 < 95), because going downhill hands back that 45.
— 第 2 站完成 —— Stop 2 done —
3 三种标准焓变，定义要一字不差Three standard enthalpy changes Standard conditions标准条件
这一站要你会：背下标准条件的四条；把燃烧焓、生成焓、中和焓的定义一字不差写出来；并为每种焓变写出配平的方程式（允许 ½ 系数）。Goal: learn the four standard conditions; write the definitions of the enthalpy of combustion, formation and neutralisation word for word; and write a balanced equation for each.
为什么非得加「标准」两个字？就像买菜要论斤、量身高要脱鞋——口径不统一，数字就没法比。你说甲烷燃烧放出 890，我说放出 800，差在哪？可能一个产物写的是液态水，一个写的是水蒸气。于是化学家统一了四把尺子：298 K（25 °C）、100 kPa、各物质处在标准态、数量按 1 mol。在这套口径下量出来的焓变，就加一个上标 ⊖，写成 ΔH⊖。至于元素的生成焓为什么是 0——那是人为规定的零点，就像海拔以海平面为 0：不是因为那里真的「没有高度」，而是大家都同意从那儿开始数。Why the word "standard"? It is like weighing vegetables in jin, or taking off your shoes before measuring height — without one agreed convention, the numbers cannot be compared. You say methane releases 890, I say 800; maybe one of us wrote liquid water as the product and the other wrote steam. So chemists agreed on four rulers: 298 K (25 °C), 100 kPa, every substance in its standard state, and amounts counted per 1 mol. Measured that way, the symbol gains a superscript ⊖: ΔH⊖. And why is the enthalpy of formation of an element zero? Because it is a zero point we agreed on by definition — like measuring altitude from sea level. Not because there is "no height" there, but because everyone counts from the same place.
名称Name定义（一句话）Definition (one sentence)方程式示例Example equation
燃烧焓combustion一摩尔物质在过量氧气中完全燃烧时的焓变the enthalpy change when one mole of a substance is completely burned in excess oxygenCH4(g) + 2O2(g) → CO2(g) + 2H2O(l)
生成焓formation由其组成元素（标准态）生成一摩尔该化合物时的焓变the enthalpy change when one mole is formed from its elements in their standard statesC(s) + O2(g) → CO2(g)
中和焓neutralisation酸与碱反应生成一摩尔水时的焓变the enthalpy change when an acid and a base form one mole of waterH+(aq) + OH−(aq) → H2O(l)
  • 标准条件四条：298 K、100 kPa、各物质处于标准态（该条件下最稳定的形态，如碳是石墨 graphite）、数量按方程式所写的 1 mol 计。Four standard conditions: 298 K, 100 kPa, every substance in its standard state (the most stable form under those conditions — carbon is graphite), and amounts read as 1 mol as written in the equation.
  • 元素的 ΔHf⊖ = 0，这是定义出来的零点。所以「C(s) + O2(g) → CO2(g)」既是碳的燃烧焓，也是 CO2 的生成焓——两个身份，同一个数（−394 kJ mol⁻¹）。ΔHf⊖ of an element in its standard state is 0, by definition. That is why "C(s) + O2(g) → CO2(g)" is both the enthalpy of combustion of carbon and the enthalpy of formation of CO2 — two names, one number (−394 kJ mol⁻¹).
  • 状态符号必须写。H2O(l) 与 H2O(g) 的焓差了约 44 kJ mol⁻¹，写错状态，整个答案就错了。State symbols are compulsory. H2O(l) and H2O(g) differ by about 44 kJ mol⁻¹, so the wrong state symbol ruins the whole answer.
  • 热化学方程式允许分数系数：为了凑出「1 mol」，写 ½O2、3½O2 完全正常，不算没配平。Fractional coefficients are allowed in thermochemical equations: to make exactly one mole you may write ½O2 or 3½O2 — that is not "unbalanced".
  • 强酸与强碱的中和焓约 −57 kJ mol⁻¹；若用的是弱酸或弱碱，数值会明显小一些（绝对值更小），因为还要扣掉弱电解质电离吸的那点热。A strong acid plus a strong base gives about −57 kJ mol⁻¹. With a weak acid or a weak base the value is noticeably smaller in magnitude, because some heat is spent ionising the weak electrolyte.
定义题是「按点给分」的默写题。考官手里四个得分点：① 1 mol；② 关键动作（完全燃烧 / 由元素生成 / 生成 1 mol 水）；③ 标准条件（298 K、100 kPa）；④ 各物质处于标准态。漏一个扣一分。写方程式时同样按点：化学式、配平、状态符号，缺一不可。Definition questions are marked point by point. The examiner holds four marks: ① one mole; ② the key action (complete combustion / formed from elements / one mole of water formed); ③ standard conditions (298 K, 100 kPa); ④ substances in their standard states. Miss one, lose one. Equations are marked the same way: formulae, balancing, state symbols — all three needed.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: The standard enthalpy change of combustion is the enthalpy change when one mole of a substance is completely burned in excess oxygen under standard conditions (298 K, 100 kPa), with all substances in their standard states. The standard enthalpy change of formation is the enthalpy change when one mole of a compound is formed from its elements in their standard states; the enthalpy of formation of an element in its standard state is zero.
例题Example
(a) 下面哪个方程式表示的是 MgO 的标准生成焓？(A) Mg(s) + ½O2(g) → MgO(s)；(B) 2Mg(s) + O2(g) → 2MgO(s)。(b) 若 (B) 式的 ΔH = −1204 kJ mol⁻¹，求 MgO 的标准生成焓。(a) Which equation represents the standard enthalpy of formation of MgO? (A) Mg(s) + ½O2(g) → MgO(s); (B) 2Mg(s) + O2(g) → 2MgO(s). (b) If equation (B) has ΔH = −1204 kJ mol⁻¹, calculate the standard enthalpy of formation of MgO.
① 生成焓的第一条是「一摩尔产物」。(A) 生成 1 mol MgO，(B) 生成 2 mol → 选 (A)。① The first requirement is one mole of product. (A) makes 1 mol of MgO, (B) makes 2 mol → the answer is (A). ② 两个式子的反应物都是标准态下的元素（Mg 固体、O2 气体），都满足「由元素生成」这一条，差别只在数量。② Both start from elements in their standard states (solid Mg, gaseous O2), so both satisfy "formed from its elements"; they differ only in amount.
ΔHf⊖(MgO) = −1204 / 2 = −602 kJ mol⁻¹
③ 一句话记住：焓变跟着方程式的系数走。系数乘 2，ΔH 也乘 2；反过来除以 2 就回到「每摩尔」。③ Remember it in one line: ΔH scales with the coefficients. Double the equation, double the ΔH; halve it again to get back to "per mole".
练习Practice
三个方程式都先想「1 mol 什么」，再配平，最后补状态符号。For all three equations, decide "one mole of what?" first, then balance, then add state symbols.

写出表示下列过程的方程式（含状态符号）：(a) 乙烷 C2H6 的标准燃烧焓；(b) 液态水 H2O(l) 的标准生成焓；(c) 硝酸与氢氧化钾反应的标准中和焓。Write equations, with state symbols, for: (a) the standard enthalpy of combustion of ethane, C2H6; (b) the standard enthalpy of formation of liquid water; (c) the standard enthalpy of neutralisation between nitric acid and potassium hydroxide.

点开看答案Show answer
(a) C2H6(g) + 3½O2(g) → 2CO2(g) + 3H2O(l)——乙烷系数为 1（1 mol 燃料），氧原子左边 7 个、右边 4+3 = 7 个，配平了；水必须是 液态。
(b) H2(g) + ½O2(g) → H2O(l)——由元素生成 1 mol 水，允许 ½ 系数。
(c) HNO3(aq) + KOH(aq) → KNO3(aq) + H2O(l)，水的系数是 1；也可写离子式 H+(aq) + OH−(aq) → H2O(l)。若题目给的是硫酸这类二元酸，记得把系数折半，保证只生成 1 mol 水。 (a) C2H6(g) + 3½O2(g) → 2CO2(g) + 3H2O(l) — ethane has coefficient 1 (one mole of fuel) and the oxygen balances: 7 on the left, 4 + 3 = 7 on the right. The water must be liquid.
(b) H2(g) + ½O2(g) → H2O(l) — one mole of water from its elements, and a ½ coefficient is fine.
(c) HNO3(aq) + KOH(aq) → KNO3(aq) + H2O(l) with water coefficient 1, or the ionic form H+(aq) + OH−(aq) → H2O(l). With a dibasic acid such as sulfuric acid, halve the coefficients so that exactly one mole of water forms.
— 第 3 站完成 —— Stop 3 done —
4 用键焓估算 ΔHEstimating ΔH from bond enthalpies Bond enthalpy键焓
这一站要你会：说出键焓的定义；用 ΔH ≈ Σ(断键) − Σ(成键) 估算反应焓变；并解释为什么算出来的只是估算值。Goal: define bond enthalpy; estimate an enthalpy change from ΔH ≈ Σ(bonds broken) − Σ(bonds formed); and explain why the result is only an estimate.
把分子想成乐高模型。要改成一个新造型，得先把旧模型拆开——拆的时候你得用力掰，这部分力气是花出去的成本；然后把积木拼成新的，每拼好一块都会「咔哒」一声松口气，这部分能量是收回来的回款。成键一定是放热的（两个原子终于牵上手，能量降下来了），断键一定是吸热的。最后这笔买卖是赚还是赔，就看两边谁大：收回来的比花出去的多，就是放热。Think of a molecule as a Lego model. To rebuild it into a new shape you must first pull the old model apart — and pulling costs effort, the money going out. Then you click the bricks into the new shape, and every click releases a little relief — the money coming back. Making a bond always releases energy (two atoms finally hold hands and settle to a lower energy); breaking a bond always costs energy. Whether the deal ends in profit or loss depends on which side is bigger: if you get back more than you paid, the reaction is exothermic.
公式与四条提醒：The formula and four reminders:
ΔH ≈ Σ(断开的键的键焓) − Σ(形成的键的键焓)
  • 键焓的定义：在气态下断开 1 mol 某种共价键所需要的能量。它永远是正值（断键总得花力气）。Definition: the energy needed to break one mole of a covalent bond, with everything in the gaseous state. It is always positive — breaking always costs.
  • 数清楚个数！2 mol HCl 里有 2 个 H–Cl 键；1 mol CH4 里有 4 个 C–H 键。漏乘个数是最常见的错误。Count them! 2 mol of HCl contains two H–Cl bonds; 1 mol of CH4 contains four C–H bonds. Forgetting to multiply is the single most common error.
  • 为什么只是估算：数据手册给的是平均键焓——同一个 C–H 键在甲烷里和乙醇里其实略有差别，表里取的是平均值。Why it is only an estimate: data books list mean (average) bond enthalpies. A C–H bond in methane is not quite the same as one in ethanol; the table gives an average of many compounds.
  • 只适用于气体。键焓是气相数据，若反应里有液体或固体，分子间作用力（单元 4 讲过）没被算进去，误差会更大。Gases only. Bond enthalpies are gas-phase values. If liquids or solids appear, the intermolecular forces (Unit 4) are left out of the account and the error grows.
两个高频失分点：① 把公式记反，写成「成键 − 断键」，符号正好反过来；② 题目给的是「2 mol 产物」，却只按 1 mol 数键。解法是先在草稿纸上把每个分子的结构式画出来，一根一根数，再套公式。Two frequent lost marks: ① learning the formula back to front ("bonds formed − bonds broken"), which flips the sign; ② being told "2 mol of product" and counting the bonds in only one mole. The cure: draw the displayed formula of every molecule on scrap paper, count bond by bond, then substitute.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: The bond enthalpy is the energy required to break one mole of a covalent bond in the gaseous state. ΔH is estimated from the total energy absorbed to break bonds minus the total energy released when bonds form. The answer is only an estimate because mean bond enthalpies are averages and intermolecular forces are not included.
例题Example
用下列键焓估算 H2(g) + Cl2(g) → 2HCl(g) 的 ΔH：H–H = 436，Cl–Cl = 243，H–Cl = 431 kJ mol⁻¹。Estimate ΔH for H2(g) + Cl2(g) → 2HCl(g) using H–H = 436, Cl–Cl = 243, H–Cl = 431 kJ mol⁻¹.
① 先列清单：断开的键是 1 个 H–H 和 1 个 Cl–Cl；形成的键是 2 个 H–Cl（因为生成 2 mol HCl）。① Make the list: bonds broken are one H–H and one Cl–Cl; bonds formed are two H–Cl (because 2 mol of HCl are made).
断键吸热 = 436 + 243 = 679 kJ mol⁻¹ 成键放热 = 2 × 431 = 862 kJ mol⁻¹ ΔH = 679 − 862 = −183 kJ mol⁻¹
② 判断符号：收回来的 862 比付出去的 679 多，净放热，所以 ΔH 为负，与算出的 −183 一致。② Check the sign: 862 comes back against 679 paid out, so there is a net release and ΔH is negative, matching the −183 you obtained. ③ 自检：实验值约 −184 kJ mol⁻¹，估算值 −183 非常接近——因为这里反应物和产物全是气体，键焓法最拿手。③ Sanity check: the experimental value is about −184 kJ mol⁻¹, very close to the estimate of −183 — no surprise, since everything here is gaseous, which is where this method works best.
练习Practice
先把 N2 画成 N≡N、H2 画成 H–H、NH3 画成三个 N–H，再一根一根数。Draw N2 as N≡N, H2 as H–H and NH3 with three N–H bonds, then count bond by bond.

用键焓估算合成氨反应 N2(g) + 3H2(g) → 2NH3(g) 的 ΔH：N≡N = 945，H–H = 436，N–H = 391 kJ mol⁻¹。Estimate ΔH for the Haber process, N2(g) + 3H2(g) → 2NH3(g), using N≡N = 945, H–H = 436, N–H = 391 kJ mol⁻¹.

点开看答案Show answer
断键：1 个 N≡N（945）+ 3 个 H–H（3 × 436 = 1308）＝ 2253 kJ mol⁻¹。
成键：2 mol NH3 每个有 3 个 N–H，共 6 个（6 × 391 = 2346）。
ΔH = 2253 − 2346 = −93 kJ mol⁻¹。
符号自检：成键收回来的更多 → 放热 → 负号，与工业上合成氨要不断移走热量完全吻合。 Broken: one N≡N (945) plus three H–H (3 × 436 = 1308) = 2253 kJ mol⁻¹.
Formed: each NH3 has three N–H bonds, so 2 mol contain six (6 × 391 = 2346).
ΔH = 2253 − 2346 = −93 kJ mol⁻¹.
Sign check: more energy comes back than goes in → exothermic → negative, which matches the fact that an ammonia plant must keep removing heat.
— 第 4 站完成 —— Stop 4 done —
5 Hess 定律：绕路也一样Hess's law: any route, same answer Hess's law赫斯定律
这一站要你会：表述赫斯定律；画（或读）燃烧路线与生成路线两种循环图；用 ΔH₁ = ΔH₂ − ΔH₃ 与生成焓公式求出无法直接测量的焓变。Goal: state Hess's law; draw (or read) both a combustion cycle and a formation cycle; and use ΔH₁ = ΔH₂ − ΔH₃ plus the formation formula to find an enthalpy change you cannot measure directly.
赫斯定律说的是一件特别生活化的事：焓就像海拔，只看起点和终点。你家在山脚、学校在半山腰，无论你走大路、抄小巷还是先爬到山顶再下来，海拔的变化都是同一个数。反应也一样——有些反应（比如把碳只烧到一氧化碳）你根本没法在实验室里让它「只停在一半」，量不出它的热量；那就绕路：先让它彻底烧成 CO2（这一步能测），再把多走的那一段减掉。绕路的账，等于直达的账。Hess's law says something very ordinary: enthalpy is like altitude — only the start and the finish matter. Your house is at the foot of the hill and school is halfway up; whether you take the main road, a shortcut, or climb to the summit and come back down, the change in altitude is the same number. Reactions work the same way. Some reactions — burning carbon only as far as carbon monoxide — simply refuse to stop halfway, so you cannot measure their heat directly. So you go the long way round: burn it completely to CO2 (which you can measure), then subtract the step you did not need. The long way round adds up to the direct route.
定律与两条常用套路：The law and the two standard routes:
  • 赫斯定律：一个反应的焓变只由始态与终态决定，与实际走的路径无关（前提是始末状态完全相同）。Hess's law: the enthalpy change of a reaction depends only on the initial and final states, not on the route taken between them (provided the start and finish are exactly the same).
  • 燃烧路线（图里那条）：把反应物和产物分别烧掉，两条下坡路之差就是答案：ΔH₁ = ΔH₂ − ΔH₃。The combustion route (the one in the diagram): burn the reactants and the products separately; the difference between the two downhill paths is the answer: ΔH₁ = ΔH₂ − ΔH₃.
  • 生成路线（更快的写法）：有了生成焓数据表，直接套 ΔH = ΣΔHf(产物) − ΣΔHf(反应物)。元素的 ΔHf 是 0，别忘乘系数。The formation route (the quicker way): with a table of formation enthalpies, just use ΔH = ΣΔHf(products) − ΣΔHf(reactants). Elements contribute 0, and do not forget the coefficients.
  • 箭头方向决定符号：如果循环里某一步必须逆着数据给的方向走，就把那个数变号（正变负、负变正）。这是整章最容易出错的一笔。The arrow direction fixes the sign: if a step in your cycle has to run against the direction the data gives, flip the sign of that number. This is the easiest thing in the whole chapter to get wrong.
  • 单位始终是 kJ mol⁻¹，且「每摩尔」指的是按你所写的方程式进行一次。The unit is always kJ mol⁻¹, where "per mole" means one run of the equation exactly as you have written it.
解题三件套：① 把目标方程式写在最上面，作为循环的上边；② 把已知的两条「下坡路」写在下面，箭头一律指向共同的中间物（通常是燃烧产物）；③ 顺着箭头走：同向取原值，逆向取相反数。做完用一句话自检——「放热越多，数字越负」。The three-step routine: ① write the target equation along the top as the upper edge of the cycle; ② write the two known "downhill" paths below, with arrows all pointing at the shared intermediate (usually the combustion products); ③ walk the arrows: with an arrow take the value as given, against an arrow take its negative. Finish with one sentence of self-check — "the more heat given out, the more negative the number".
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: Hess's law states that the enthalpy change of a reaction is independent of the route taken, provided the initial and final states are the same. The direct conversion cannot be measured because carbon monoxide is always formed together with some carbon dioxide, so an indirect route using enthalpies of combustion is used instead.
例题Example
已知 C(s) 的燃烧焓 = −394 kJ mol⁻¹，CO(g) 的燃烧焓 = −283 kJ mol⁻¹。求 C(s) + ½O2(g) → CO(g) 的 ΔH。The enthalpy of combustion of C(s) is −394 kJ mol⁻¹ and that of CO(g) is −283 kJ mol⁻¹. Calculate ΔH for C(s) + ½O2(g) → CO(g).
① 目标反应是「烧一半」，实验里做不到——碳一烧就混着 CO2，量不准。所以绕道。① The target is "half-burning", which you cannot do cleanly in the lab — carbon always gives some CO2 as well. So take the long way. ② 画循环：上面 C + ½O2 → CO（ΔH₁ 待求）；下面两条都指向 CO2：C 完全燃烧 ΔH₂ = −394，CO 完全燃烧 ΔH₃ = −283。② Draw the cycle: on top, C + ½O2 → CO (ΔH₁, unknown); below, two arrows both pointing to CO2: C burnt completely, ΔH₂ = −394, and CO burnt completely, ΔH₃ = −283. ③ 从 CO2 回到 CO 要逆着 ΔH₃ 走，所以取 +283：③ Getting from CO2 back to CO means going against ΔH₃, so take +283:
ΔH₁ = ΔH₂ − ΔH₃ = −394 − (−283) = −394 + 283 = −111 kJ mol⁻¹
④ 自检：这个数就是 CO 的标准生成焓（−111 ≈ 课本值 −110.5），而 CO 确实还能继续燃烧放热，所以「生成 CO 只放出 111，比生成 CO2 的 394 少」完全合理。④ Sanity check: this is the standard enthalpy of formation of CO (−111 against the textbook −110.5), and CO really can burn further, so "forming CO releases only 111 while forming CO2 releases 394" makes perfect sense.
练习Practice
把 CH4 的燃烧当成第三段路：C 与 H2 各自烧到产物，也可以经 CH4 再烧到同样的产物，两条总账必须相等。Treat the combustion of CH4 as a third path: C and H2 can burn to the products directly, or go via CH4 and then burn; the two totals must be equal.

已知燃烧焓：C(s) = −394，H2(g) = −286，CH4(g) = −890 kJ mol⁻¹。用赫斯定律求 CH4(g) 的标准生成焓，即 C(s) + 2H2(g) → CH4(g) 的 ΔH。Enthalpies of combustion: C(s) = −394, H2(g) = −286, CH4(g) = −890 kJ mol⁻¹. Use Hess's law to find the standard enthalpy of formation of CH4(g), i.e. ΔH for C(s) + 2H2(g) → CH4(g).

点开看答案Show answer
设生成焓为 ΔHf。走「先合成再烧」这条路：ΔHf + (−890)；走「分别烧」这条路：(−394) + 2 × (−286) = −966。
两条路终点相同（都是 CO2 + 2H2O），所以 ΔHf − 890 = −966 → ΔHf = −966 + 890 = −76 kJ mol⁻¹。
说明：课本值是 −74.8 kJ mol⁻¹，这里的差别来自题目把燃烧焓取整成了 −890 等整数——这也提醒你，赫斯定律算出来的精度取决于原始数据的精度。 Let the formation enthalpy be ΔHf. Route "make it, then burn it": ΔHf + (−890). Route "burn the elements separately": (−394) + 2 × (−286) = −966.
Both finish at the same place (CO2 + 2H2O), so ΔHf − 890 = −966, giving ΔHf = −966 + 890 = −76 kJ mol⁻¹.
Note: the textbook value is −74.8 kJ mol⁻¹; the difference comes from rounding the combustion enthalpies to whole numbers here — a reminder that a Hess calculation is only as precise as the data you start from.
— 第 5 站完成 —— Stop 5 done —
6 在实验室里量出来Measuring enthalpy changes in the lab Calorimetry量热法
这一站要你会：用 q = mcΔT 算热量；用 ΔH = −q/n 换算成每摩尔的焓变；说出中和热与燃烧热两套装置，并列出主要误差来源。Goal: use q = mcΔT; convert to an enthalpy change with ΔH = −q/n; describe the two experiments (neutralisation and combustion) and list the main sources of error.
量热的思路朴素得可爱：反应放出的热，都被周围的水接住了，水升温多少就说明接了多少热。所以只要知道「这杯水有多重」「水升高一度要吃多少热」（4.18 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹），再量出温度升高多少，三者相乘就是热量 q。接着把它摊到「每摩尔反应」头上：ΔH = −q/n。那个负号别忘——q 是水（环境）得到的热，是正数；而 ΔH 记的是系统的账，系统失去热，所以要添个负号。The idea behind calorimetry is charmingly simple: the heat the reaction gives out is caught by the surrounding water, and how far the water warms tells you how much it caught. So if you know how heavy the water is, how much heat one gram of water swallows per degree (4.18 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹), and how far the temperature rose, multiplying the three gives the energy q. Then spread it over one mole of reaction: ΔH = −q/n. Do not drop that minus sign — q is the heat gained by the water (the surroundings), so it is positive, while ΔH keeps the system's books, and the system lost that heat.
公式里每个字母都要认得：Know every letter in the formula:
q = m c ΔT ΔH = −q / n m = 溶液（或水）的质量，单位 g c = 4.18 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹（把溶液当成水） ΔT = 温度升高值，单位 K（与 °C 的差值相同）
  • m 是溶液的质量，不是某一种反应物的质量。两份各 25 cm³ 的溶液混在一起，m = 50 g（稀溶液密度按 1 g cm⁻³ 算）。m is the mass of the solution, not of one reagent. Mixing 25 cm³ with 25 cm³ gives m = 50 g (taking the density of a dilute solution as 1 g cm⁻³).
  • n 是「限量」那一个的物质的量，中和实验里通常就是生成的水的摩尔数：n = c × V（V 必须换成 dm³）。n is the amount, in moles, of the limiting reagent — in a neutralisation, the moles of water formed: n = c × V, with V in dm³.
  • 别忘了把 J 换成 kJ（除以 1000），因为 ΔH 的单位是 kJ mol⁻¹。Convert J to kJ (divide by 1000), because ΔH is quoted in kJ mol⁻¹.
  • 中和热实验：泡沫塑料杯 + 盖子 + 温度计 + 搅拌棒，两只溶液先各自恒温，混合后读到最高温度。Neutralisation experiment: polystyrene cup with a lid, thermometer and stirrer; both solutions are left to reach the same temperature, then mixed and the highest temperature recorded.
  • 燃烧热实验：铜量热器（导热快）装已知质量的水，下面烧酒精灯；量水温升，同时称酒精灯前后质量算出烧掉了几摩尔。Combustion experiment: a copper calorimeter (a good conductor) holds a known mass of water above a spirit burner; you measure the temperature rise and weigh the burner before and after to find how many moles burnt.
  • 误差来源（都要会写）：热量散失到空气（最大头）、燃烧不完全（生成 CO 或碳烟）、液体蒸发带走热、搅拌不均、温度计精度、把溶液的比热容当成水、非标准状态。它们几乎都让测出的 |ΔH| 偏小。Sources of error (learn them all): heat lost to the air (the biggest one), incomplete combustion (giving CO or soot), evaporation carrying energy away, uneven stirring, thermometer precision, assuming the solution has the same specific heat capacity as water, and non-standard conditions. Nearly all of them make the measured |ΔH| too small.
两个必死的坑：① 单位：q 算出来是 J，答案要 kJ，一定要除 1000；② 符号：q 是环境得到的热（正），ΔH 是系统失去的热（负），一定要加负号。写出来之前先问一句「这是谁的账」。Two fatal traps: ① units — q comes out in J but the answer is in kJ, so divide by 1000; ② the sign — q is heat gained by the surroundings (positive) while ΔH is heat lost by the system (negative), so add the minus sign. Before writing either, ask "whose account is this?"
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: The heat energy change is calculated from q = mcΔT, where m is the mass of the solution, c is 4.18 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹ and ΔT is the temperature rise. The enthalpy change is ΔH = −q/n in kJ mol⁻¹. The main source of error is heat loss to the surroundings, which makes the value less negative than the data-book value; this can be reduced by using a lid, an insulated cup and a polystyrene jacket.
例题Example
25.0 cm³ 的 1.00 mol dm⁻³ HCl 与 25.0 cm³ 的 1.00 mol dm⁻³ NaOH 混合，温度从 21.0 °C 升到 27.0 °C。求中和焓（c = 4.18 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹，溶液密度 1 g cm⁻³）。25.0 cm³ of 1.00 mol dm⁻³ HCl is mixed with 25.0 cm³ of 1.00 mol dm⁻³ NaOH and the temperature rises from 21.0 °C to 27.0 °C. Calculate the enthalpy of neutralisation (c = 4.18 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹, density 1 g cm⁻³).
① 先数摩尔：n = c × V = 1.00 × 0.0250 = 0.0250 mol 的 HCl，也就是生成 0.0250 mol 水。① Count the moles first: n = c × V = 1.00 × 0.0250 = 0.0250 mol of HCl, so 0.0250 mol of water forms. ② 溶液总质量 m = 25.0 + 25.0 = 50.0 g；ΔT = 27.0 − 21.0 = 6.0 K。② Total mass m = 25.0 + 25.0 = 50.0 g; ΔT = 27.0 − 21.0 = 6.0 K.
q = m c ΔT = 50.0 × 4.18 × 6.0 = 1254 J ΔH = −q / n = −1254 / 0.0250 = −50 160 J mol⁻¹ = −50.2 kJ mol⁻¹
③ 判断：答案为负（放热），数量级几十 kJ mol⁻¹，合理。它比课本值 −57 的绝对值小，正是热量散失造成的——这也是为什么实验题总要你答「加盖、用保温杯」。③ Judge it: the answer is negative (exothermic) and of the order of tens of kJ mol⁻¹, so it is sensible. It is smaller in magnitude than the data-book −57 exactly because heat escaped — which is why experiment questions always ask you to suggest "use a lid and an insulated cup".
练习Practice
先算 n（V 要换 dm³），再算 q（m 是两份溶液之和），最后除、换单位、加负号。Find n first (V in dm³), then q (m is the two solutions together), then divide, convert the unit and add the sign.

50.0 cm³ 的 1.00 mol dm⁻³ HNO3 与 50.0 cm³ 的 1.00 mol dm⁻³ KOH 混合，温度从 20.5 °C 升到 27.0 °C。(a) 计算中和焓；(b) 说出两个误差来源，并各说明它让结果偏大还是偏小。50.0 cm³ of 1.00 mol dm⁻³ HNO3 is mixed with 50.0 cm³ of 1.00 mol dm⁻³ KOH and the temperature rises from 20.5 °C to 27.0 °C. (a) Calculate the enthalpy of neutralisation. (b) State two sources of error and say whether each makes the result larger or smaller.

点开看答案Show answer
(a) n = 1.00 × 0.0500 = 0.0500 mol；m = 100 g；ΔT = 6.5 K。
q = 100 × 4.18 × 6.5 = 2717 J；ΔH = −2717 / 0.0500 = −54 340 J mol⁻¹ = −54.3 kJ mol⁻¹。
(b) 例：① 热量散失到空气——一部分热没被水接住，ΔT 偏小，算出的 |ΔH| 偏小（如 −54.3 比 −57 小）；② 溶液蒸发带走热量，同样让 ΔT 偏小、|ΔH| 偏小；③ 若把比热容当成 4.18 而实际溶液略有不同，也会带来误差。（答出任意两个并说清方向即可） (a) n = 1.00 × 0.0500 = 0.0500 mol; m = 100 g; ΔT = 6.5 K.
q = 100 × 4.18 × 6.5 = 2717 J; ΔH = −2717 / 0.0500 = −54 340 J mol⁻¹ = −54.3 kJ mol⁻¹.
(b) For example: ① heat lost to the air — some energy never reaches the water, ΔT is too small and |ΔH| comes out too small (−54.3 instead of −57); ② evaporation carries energy away, again making ΔT and |ΔH| too small; ③ assuming c = 4.18 when the solution is not pure water also introduces error. (Any two, with the direction stated, will do.)
— 第 6 站完成 —— Stop 6 done —

单元 5 小结Unit 5 summary

① 先分账本：系统是反应本身，环境是其余一切；ΔH 记的是系统的账，放热为负、吸热为正；放热不等于自发。
② 会看图：反应进程图里，从反应物平台到峰顶是活化能 Ea，两条平台的高度差是 ΔH；产物更低即放热。
③ 定义要一字不差：标准条件是 298 K、100 kPa、标准态、1 mol；燃烧焓、生成焓、中和焓三种，元素的生成焓为 0。① Sort out the accounts: the system is the reaction, the surroundings are everything else; ΔH keeps the system's books, negative when exothermic and positive when endothermic; and exothermic is not the same as spontaneous.
② Read the diagram: on a reaction profile, the climb from the reactants level to the peak is Ea and the gap between the two levels is ΔH; products lower means exothermic.
③ Definitions word-perfect: standard conditions are 298 K, 100 kPa, standard states, one mole; combustion, formation and neutralisation, with the formation enthalpy of an element equal to zero.

④ 两种算法：键焓法 ΔH ≈ Σ断键 − Σ成键，只适用于气体且只是估算；赫斯定律 ΔH 只看始末，燃烧循环用 ΔH₁ = ΔH₂ − ΔH₃，生成数据用 ΣΔHf(产物) − ΣΔHf(反应物)。
⑤ 一种量法：q = mcΔT 算出环境得的热，ΔH = −q/n 换回系统的账，记得除以 1000 变 kJ、加上负号；误差几乎都让结果偏小。④ Two ways to calculate: bond enthalpies, ΔH ≈ Σ broken − Σ formed, work for gases only and give only an estimate; Hess's law says ΔH depends only on the start and finish — use ΔH₁ = ΔH₂ − ΔH₃ for a combustion cycle, or ΣΔHf(products) − ΣΔHf(reactants) with formation data.
⑤ One way to measure: q = mcΔT gives the heat the surroundings gained, and ΔH = −q/n puts it back on the system's account; remember to divide by 1000 for kJ and add the minus sign. Errors almost always make the answer too small in magnitude.

下一站要去哪里：这一单元我们只问了「能量往哪边流、流了多少」，却没问「为什么这个反应能发生」、也没问那些失去的电子去了哪里。把电子的得与失单独拎出来看，就是单元 6 氧化还原——它和能量学共用同一枚硬币的两面。Where next: this unit asked only which way energy flows and how much of it, never why the reaction happens at all, nor where the electrons went. Pulling out the gain and loss of electrons on its own is Unit 6, redox — the other face of the same coin as energetics.
