1 氧化数怎么数How to count oxidation numbers Oxidation number rules氧化数规则
这一站要你会：背下那套氧化数规则，并且能算出任何化合物或离子里某个元素的氧化数。Goal: learn the oxidation-number rules and work out the oxidation number of any element in a compound or ion.
把氧化数想成一本电子账本。两个原子共用电子时，规定把电子全部「判」给电负性更大（更贪心）的那一方：判到电子的记负号，交出电子的记正号。单质里谁也没贪谁的，所以记 0。整本账必须平——中性分子加起来是 0，离子加起来就是它的电荷。先把这套规则背熟，后面所有判断都靠它。Think of an oxidation number as a bookkeeping entry for electrons. When atoms share electrons, we pretend the electrons belong entirely to the greedier (more electronegative) atom: the one that gains them is marked negative, the one that gives them up is marked positive. In an element nobody has taken from anybody, so it scores 0. The book must always balance — a neutral molecule sums to 0, an ion sums to its charge. Learn these rules first; every later judgement leans on them.
一套规则，背到条件反射：The rules to learn by heart:
  • 单质为 0：O2、Cl2、Na、Fe 里的元素氧化数都是 0。Elements are 0: every atom in O2, Cl2, Na or Fe has oxidation number 0.
  • 简单离子 = 它的电荷：Na+ 是 +1，Cl− 是 −1，Fe3+ 是 +3。Simple ions equal their charge: Na+ is +1, Cl− is −1, Fe3+ is +3.
  • 氢 H 通常 +1（跟金属结合成氢化物时才是 −1）。Hydrogen is usually +1 (only −1 in metal hydrides).
  • 氧 O 通常 −2；过氧化物里是 −1（如 H2O2、Na2O2）。Oxygen is usually −2; in peroxides it is −1 (e.g. H2O2, Na2O2).
  • 氟 F 永远 −1——它最贪心，从不松手。Fluorine is always −1 — it is the greediest and never lets go.
  • 总和守恒：化合物里所有氧化数之和 = 0；多原子离子里 = 离子所带电荷。The sum is fixed: in a compound it is 0; in a polyatomic ion it equals the ion's charge.
最容易栽的坑：H2O2 里 O 不是 −2，是 −1——因为它是过氧化物。题目只要出现「过氧化物」三个字，先把 O 记成 −1。The classic trap: in H2O2 oxygen is −1, not −2, because it is a peroxide. The moment you see "peroxide", set O to −1 first.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: The oxidation number of an element is the charge it would have if all the shared electrons were given to the more electronegative atom. It is 0 in elements, equal to the charge in a simple ion; hydrogen is usually +1, oxygen is usually −2 but −1 in peroxides, and fluorine is always −1.
例题Example
求 MnO4− 里 Mn 和 SO42− 里 S 的氧化数。Find the oxidation numbers of Mn in MnO4− and of S in SO42−.
① 设未知数，把已知的 O 写成 −2（共 4 个）。① Let the unknown be x; write each O as −2 (four of them).
MnO₄⁻：Mn + 4×(−2) = −1 → Mn = +7 SO₄²⁻：S + 4×(−2) = −2 → S = +6
② 自检：+7 和 +6 都是这两个离子里常见的「高价态」，结果合理。② Sanity check: +7 and +6 are the familiar high states in these two ions, so the answers make sense.
练习Practice
先写每个 O 的 −2，再设未知数；看到 H2O2 记得 O 是 −1。Write each O as −2 first, then set up the unknown; for H2O2 remember O is −1.

求 (a) Cr2O72− 里 Cr、(b) H2O2 里 O、(c) H2S 里 S 的氧化数。Find the oxidation number of (a) Cr in Cr2O72−, (b) O in H2O2, (c) S in H2S.

点开看答案Show answer
(a) 2Cr + 7×(−2) = −2 → Cr = +6。
(b) H2O2 是过氧化物，O = −1（不是 −2！）。
(c) H 是 +1，两个 H 共 +2，所以 S = −2。 (a) 2Cr + 7×(−2) = −2 → Cr = +6.
(b) H2O2 is a peroxide, so O = −1 (not −2!).
(c) each H is +1, two of them give +2, so S = −2.
— 第 1 站完成 —— Stop 1 done —
2 氧化还原的三个说法Three ways to say redox OIL RIGOIL RIG 口诀
这一站要你会：说出氧化、还原各自三种等价定义，并用 OIL RIG 判断某个元素是被氧化还是被还原。Goal: state three equivalent definitions of oxidation and of reduction, and use OIL RIG to decide whether an element is oxidised or reduced.
氧化和还原是同一件事的两面，像跷跷板：一个人失电子，另一个人必然得电子，谁也离不开谁。所以别把「氧化」理解成「跟氧气有关」——那只是最早的一种说法。真正的主角是电子：失电子就是氧化，得电子就是还原。Oxidation and reduction are two sides of the same coin, like a seesaw: when one atom loses electrons, another must gain them — you never get one without the other. So don't reduce "oxidation" to "something with oxygen"; that is only the oldest definition. The real star is the electron: lose them and you are oxidised, gain them and you are reduced.
三个说法，说哪个都对：Three definitions — any of them is correct:
  • 氧化 oxidation＝得氧 / 失电子 / 氧化数升高。Oxidation = gain of oxygen / loss of electrons / increase in oxidation number.
  • 还原 reduction＝失氧 / 得电子 / 氧化数降低。Reduction = loss of oxygen / gain of electrons / decrease in oxidation number.
  • OIL RIG 口诀：Oxidation Is Loss（氧化＝失），Reduction Is Gain（还原＝得）——都是指电子。OIL RIG: Oxidation Is Loss, Reduction Is Gain — of electrons.
  • 一定同时发生：有氧化必有还原，电子不会凭空消失。They always occur together: no oxidation without reduction — electrons don't vanish.
小心「得氧/失氧」的局限：它只对有氧气参与的反应好用。碰到 Zn + Cu2+ 这种没氧的，就得改用「失电子/氧化数」来判断。Mind the limits of "oxygen": it only works when oxygen is actually involved. For something like Zn + Cu2+ with no oxygen, switch to "electrons / oxidation number".
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: Oxidation is the loss of electrons (or an increase in oxidation number), and reduction is the gain of electrons (or a decrease in oxidation number). Oxidation and reduction always occur together in a redox reaction.
例题Example
在 Zn + Cu2+ → Zn2+ + Cu 中，谁被氧化？谁被还原？氧化数各怎么变？In Zn + Cu2+ → Zn2+ + Cu, which species is oxidised and which is reduced? How do the oxidation numbers change?
① Zn：0 → +2，氧化数升高，失去 2 个电子 → 被氧化。① Zn goes 0 → +2, the oxidation number rises, it loses two electrons → oxidised. ② Cu：+2 → 0，氧化数降低，得到 2 个电子 → 被还原。② Cu goes +2 → 0, the oxidation number falls, it gains two electrons → reduced. ③ 一失一得，电子数正好相等——这就是方程电荷守恒的由来。③ One loses exactly what the other gains — that is why the equation is charge-balanced.
练习Practice
先标氧化数，再看谁升谁降。Label the oxidation numbers first, then see who rises and who falls.

在 Mg + 2H+ → Mg2+ + H2 中，(a) 谁被氧化？(b) 谁被还原？(c) 各用一句话说明理由。In Mg + 2H+ → Mg2+ + H2, (a) which species is oxidised? (b) which is reduced? (c) give one reason for each.

点开看答案Show answer
(a) Mg 被氧化：0 → +2，氧化数升高、失电子。
(b) H 被还原：+1 → 0，氧化数降低、得电子。
(c) 一句话：Mg 失去电子所以被氧化，H+ 得到电子所以被还原。 (a) Mg is oxidised: 0 → +2, oxidation number rises, it loses electrons.
(b) H is reduced: +1 → 0, oxidation number falls, it gains electrons.
(c) In one sentence: Mg loses electrons so it is oxidised; H+ gains electrons so it is reduced.
— 第 2 站完成 —— Stop 2 done —
3 谁氧化谁：氧化剂与还原剂Who oxidises whom: oxidising and reducing agents Oxidising & reducing agents氧化剂与还原剂
这一站要你会：分清氧化剂、还原剂两个角色，尤其记住「氧化剂是接受电子、自己被还原的一方」。Goal: tell the oxidising agent from the reducing agent, and above all remember that the oxidising agent is the one that accepts electrons and is itself reduced.
氧化剂是抢电子的强盗：它从别人那儿抢来电子，所以把别人氧化了，自己却因为多得了电子而被还原（氧化数降低）。还原剂是送电子的老实人：它把电子送出去，把别人还原了，自己反而被氧化。一句话记住——氧化剂「抢」、还原剂「送」，而自己永远落到相反的那一头。The oxidising agent is the electron robber: it snatches electrons from the other species, oxidising it, while itself is reduced (oxidation number falls). The reducing agent is the electron donor: it hands electrons over, reducing the other species, while itself is oxidised. Remember it in one line — the oxidiser "grabs", the reducer "gives", and each ends up on the opposite side.
两个角色，别记反：Two roles — don't get them backwards:
  • 氧化剂 oxidising agent：把别人氧化，自己接受电子、被还原，氧化数降低。Oxidising agent: oxidises the other species while it accepts electrons and is itself reduced; its oxidation number falls.
  • 还原剂 reducing agent：把别人还原，自己给出电子、被氧化，氧化数升高。Reducing agent: reduces the other species while it donates electrons and is itself oxidised; its oxidation number rises.
  • 最易搞混的一句：「氧化剂是接受电子的一方」——不是它被氧化，而是它把别人氧化。The easiest mix-up: "the oxidising agent accepts electrons" — it is not oxidised; it oxidises the other species.
  • 记忆钩子：氧化剂 = 抢（electron acceptor），还原剂 = 送（electron donor）。Memory hook: oxidiser = grabber (electron acceptor), reducer = giver (electron donor).
别被中文绕晕：「氧化剂」三个字里带「氧化」，但它自己并不被氧化；「还原剂」自己也不被还原。名字说的是它对别人做的事，结果落到自己身上恰恰相反。Don't let the names confuse you: an oxidising agent is not itself oxidised, and a reducing agent is not itself reduced. The name says what it does to the other species; what happens to itself is the opposite.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: An oxidising agent is a substance that oxidises another substance and is itself reduced (it gains electrons). A reducing agent reduces another substance and is itself oxidised (it loses electrons).
例题Example
在 Cl2 + 2I− → I2 + 2Cl− 中，指出氧化剂与还原剂，并说明理由。In Cl2 + 2I− → I2 + 2Cl−, identify the oxidising and reducing agents and justify your answer.
① I：−1 → 0，氧化数升高，失电子、被氧化 → I− 是还原剂。① I goes −1 → 0, oxidation number rises, loses electrons, is oxidised → I− is the reducing agent. ② Cl：0 → −1，氧化数降低，得电子、被还原 → Cl2 是氧化剂。② Cl goes 0 → −1, oxidation number falls, gains electrons, is reduced → Cl2 is the oxidising agent.
练习Practice
先标氧化数：Fe 和 I 各往哪边变，谁升谁降。Label the oxidation numbers first: which way do Fe and I move, who rises, who falls.

在 2Fe3+ + 2I− → 2Fe2+ + I2 中，(a) 谁是氧化剂？(b) 谁是还原剂？In 2Fe3+ + 2I− → 2Fe2+ + I2, (a) which is the oxidising agent? (b) which is the reducing agent?

点开看答案Show answer
(a) 氧化剂是 Fe3+：+3 → +2，氧化数降低、得电子、自己被还原。
(b) 还原剂是 I−：−1 → 0，氧化数升高、失电子、自己被氧化。 (a) The oxidising agent is Fe3+: +3 → +2, oxidation number falls, it gains electrons and is reduced.
(b) The reducing agent is I−: −1 → 0, oxidation number rises, it loses electrons and is oxidised.
— 第 3 站完成 —— Stop 3 done —
4 配平氧化还原方程式（半反应法）Balancing redox equations (half-reaction method) Half-reaction method半反应法
这一站要你会：用半反应法在酸性条件下配平氧化还原离子方程式，并会自检电荷与原子都守恒。Goal: use the half-reaction method to balance redox ionic equations in acidic conditions, and check that both charge and atoms balance.
配平就像把两本流水账合成一笔总账：先把「失电子」和「得电子」分开各写一条（半反应），各自把电荷和质量配平，然后让两条里电子的数目对上号，最后加起来、把两边相同的电子划掉。酸性条件下缺什么就补什么——缺氧加水，缺氢加 H⁺。Balancing is like merging two small ledgers into one big entry: write the "electron-losing" and "electron-gaining" as two separate half-reactions, balance the charge and mass of each, then make the number of electrons match, add them up and cancel the electrons. In acid, fill whatever is missing — add water for missing oxygen, add H⁺ for missing hydrogen.
半反应法四步（酸性条件）：The four steps (acidic conditions):
  • ① 拆两半：写一条氧化半反应、一条还原半反应，只写发生变化的粒子。① Split into two: write one oxidation and one reduction half-reaction, using only the species that change.
  • ② 配电荷：在缺电子的一边加 e⁻，让两边电荷相等。② Balance charge: add e⁻ to the electron-poor side so both sides have equal charge.
  • ③ 配质量：酸性条件下缺氧加 H₂O、缺氢加 H⁺。③ Balance mass: in acid, add H₂O for oxygen and H⁺ for hydrogen.
  • ④ 等电子相加：把两条半反应乘上合适系数让 e⁻ 数相等，相加后约掉 e⁻。④ Equalise and add: multiply each half-reaction so the e⁻ counts match, add them, then cancel the e⁻.
先配「主角」再配 H/O：多数题里 Mn、Cr、Fe 这些元素只出现一次，先配它们，再回头补 H₂O 和 H⁺，最后点电子数。顺序一乱就容易漏项。Balance the main element before H and O: elements like Mn, Cr and Fe usually appear only once — balance them first, then top up H₂O and H⁺, and finally count electrons. A messy order is how items get dropped.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: Write the two half-reactions, balance atoms by adding H₂O and H⁺ (in acid), balance charge by adding electrons, then multiply so the electrons cancel before adding the half-reactions together.
例题Example
酸性条件下，MnO4− 把 Fe2+ 氧化成 Fe3+，自身被还原成 Mn2+。写出配平后的离子方程式。In acidic conditions, MnO4− oxidises Fe2+ to Fe3+ and is itself reduced to Mn2+. Write the balanced ionic equation.
① 写出两条半反应（先配 O/H，再配电荷）：① Write the two half-reactions (balance O/H first, then charge):
还原：MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5e⁻ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O 氧化：Fe²⁺ → Fe³⁺ + e⁻
② 电子数不同（5 和 1），把氧化半反应 ×5。② The electron counts differ (5 vs 1), so multiply the oxidation half-reaction by 5.
5Fe²⁺ → 5Fe³⁺ + 5e⁻
③ 相加、约掉两边各 5 个电子：③ Add the two and cancel the five electrons on each side:
MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5Fe²⁺ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O + 5Fe³⁺
④ 自检：原子（Mn 1、O 4、H 8、Fe 5）都守恒；电荷左边 −1+8+10 = +17，右边 +2+15 = +17，也守恒。④ Check: atoms balance (Mn 1, O 4, H 8, Fe 5); charge on the left is −1+8+10 = +17 and on the right +2+15 = +17, so it balances too.
练习Practice
还原半反应已给，氧化半反应照 Fe²⁺ 那条套。The reduction half-reaction is given; adapt the Fe²⁺ oxidation half-reaction.

酸性条件下 Cr2O72− 氧化 Fe2+ 成 Fe3+，自身还原成 Cr3+。已知还原半反应：Cr2O72− + 14H+ + 6e⁻ → 2Cr3+ + 7H2O。写出配平后的总离子方程式。In acidic conditions Cr2O72− oxidises Fe2+ to Fe3+ and is reduced to Cr3+. Given the reduction half-reaction Cr2O72− + 14H+ + 6e⁻ → 2Cr3+ + 7H2O, write the balanced overall ionic equation.

点开看答案Show answer
氧化半反应 ×6：6Fe2+ → 6Fe3+ + 6e⁻。
相加约掉电子：Cr2O72− + 14H+ + 6Fe2+ → 2Cr3+ + 7H2O + 6Fe3+。自检：Cr 2、O 7、H 14、Fe 6 都守恒，电荷左 +24、右 +24。 Oxidation half-reaction ×6: 6Fe2+ → 6Fe3+ + 6e⁻.
Add and cancel the electrons: Cr2O72− + 14H+ + 6Fe2+ → 2Cr3+ + 7H2O + 6Fe3+. Check: Cr 2, O 7, H 14, Fe 6 balance; charge +24 on each side.

5 歧化反应：自己人打自己人Disproportionation: one element, two fates Disproportionation歧化反应
这一站要你会：认得歧化反应，并能用氧化数判断「同一元素一边升、一边降」。Goal: recognise a disproportionation reaction and use oxidation numbers to see "one element goes up and down at the same time".
歧化就是自己人打自己人：同一个元素，在反应里一部分升价（被氧化）、一部分降价（被还原），一个人把「氧化剂」和「还原剂」两个角色全包了。氯气最典型——它既想抢别人的电子，又能被抢，于是自己跟自己「掰手腕」。Disproportionation is one element fighting itself: part of it is oxidised (oxidation number up) while another part is reduced (oxidation number down), so the single element plays both oxidising and reducing agent at once. Chlorine is the classic example — it can both grab electrons and be robbed of them, so it arm-wrestles itself.
判断方法与两个经典例子：How to spot it, and two classic examples:
  • 定义：同一元素的氧化数同时升高和降低的反应。Definition: a reaction in which the same element is simultaneously oxidised and reduced.
  • 判断法：看同一元素在产物里是否出现两种氧化数，一个比反应物高、一个比反应物低。How to tell: check whether the element appears with two oxidation numbers in the products, one higher and one lower than in the reactant.
  • Cl₂ 与水：Cl2 + H2O → HCl + HClO（Cl：0 → −1 和 +1）。Cl₂ with water: Cl2 + H2O → HCl + HClO (Cl: 0 → −1 and +1).
  • Cl₂ 与冷、稀 NaOH：Cl2 + 2NaOH → NaCl + NaClO + H2O。Cl₂ with cold, dilute NaOH: Cl2 + 2NaOH → NaCl + NaClO + H2O.
别和普通氧化还原搞混：普通反应是两个不同元素一升一降；歧化是同一个元素自己一升一降。看准「同一种原子」是不是出现在两个不同的产物里。Don't mix it up with ordinary redox: an ordinary reaction has two different elements, one up and one down; disproportionation has one element going both ways. Look for the same atom appearing in two different products.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: In a disproportionation reaction the same element is both oxidised and reduced, so its oxidation number increases in one product and decreases in the other. Chlorine undergoes disproportionation with cold, dilute aqueous sodium hydroxide.
例题Example
用氧化数判断 Cl2 + 2NaOH → NaCl + NaClO + H2O 是不是歧化反应，并说明理由。Use oxidation numbers to decide whether Cl2 + 2NaOH → NaCl + NaClO + H2O is a disproportionation reaction, and explain.
① 反应物 Cl2 里 Cl 的氧化数是 0。① In the reactant Cl2, chlorine has oxidation number 0. ② 产物 NaCl 里 Cl 是 −1（降低，被还原）；NaClO 里 Cl 是 +1（升高，被氧化）。② In NaCl, Cl is −1 (lowered, reduced); in NaClO, Cl is +1 (raised, oxidised). ③ 同一个元素 Cl 一边升、一边降 → 是歧化反应；Cl2 既作氧化剂又作还原剂。③ The same element Cl goes both up and down → it is a disproportionation; Cl2 is both the oxidising and the reducing agent.
练习Practice
先算 H₂O₂ 里 O 的氧化数（过氧化物），再看它落到哪两种产物里。First find O's oxidation number in H₂O₂ (a peroxide), then see which two products it lands in.

判断 2H2O2 → 2H2O + O2 是不是歧化反应，并说明理由。Decide whether 2H2O2 → 2H2O + O2 is a disproportionation reaction, and explain.

点开看答案Show answer
H2O2 里 O = −1；产物 H2O 里 O = −2（降低，被还原），O2 里 O = 0（升高，被氧化）。同一元素 O 一边升一边降 → 是歧化反应。 In H2O2, O = −1; in H2O it is −2 (lowered, reduced) and in O2 it is 0 (raised, oxidised). The same element O goes both up and down → it is a disproportionation.
— 第 5 站完成 —— Stop 5 done —
6 氧化还原滴定：紫色到无色的魔法Redox titration: the purple-to-colourless magic Redox titration氧化还原滴定
这一站要你会：说出 KMnO₄ 与 I₂/Na₂S₂O₃ 两套滴定的指示剂与颜色变化，并能按配平方程式的计量比计算浓度或体积。Goal: state the indicator and colour changes for the KMnO₄ and I₂/Na₂S₂O₃ titrations, and calculate concentrations or volumes using the stoichiometric ratio.
滴定就是让颜色当裁判。KMnO₄ 自己就是指示剂——它紫得发亮，一被还原就变成几乎无色的 Mn²⁺；等瓶子里的还原剂用光了，下一滴没人接，紫色赖着不走，溶液就泛起淡淡的粉，这就是终点。另一套用碘：碘遇淀粉变蓝，滴到蓝刚好褪成无色就是终点。Titration lets colour act as the referee. KMnO₄ is its own indicator — it is bright purple, and turns almost colourless Mn²⁺ once reduced; when the reducing agent in the flask is used up, the next drop has nothing to react with, so the solution takes on a faint pink: that is the endpoint. The other system uses iodine: iodine turns starch blue, and the endpoint is when the blue just disappears.
两套滴定 + 计量比怎么用：Two titrations, and how to use the ratio:
  • KMnO₄：酸性条件下紫色 MnO4− → 无色 Mn2+；自身作指示剂，终点显淡粉。用于滴定 Fe2+、H2O2、C2O42−。KMnO₄: in acid, purple MnO4− → colourless Mn2+; it is its own indicator, endpoint pale pink. Used to titrate Fe2+, H2O2, C2O42−.
  • I₂ / Na₂S₂O₃：2S2O32− + I2 → S4O62− + 2I−；淀粉指示剂，蓝 → 无色。I₂ / Na₂S₂O₃: 2S2O32− + I2 → S4O62− + 2I−; starch indicator, blue → colourless.
  • 计量比用法：先写配平方程式，再用 n = cV 算物质的量，最后按摩尔比换算到目标物质。Using the ratio: write the balanced equation, find moles with n = cV, then convert using the mole ratio to the target species.
  • 记一个关键比例：MnO4− : C2O42− = 2 : 5（来自 2MnO4− + 5C2O42− + 16H+ → 2Mn2+ + 10CO2 + 8H2O）。Memorise one key ratio: MnO4− : C2O42− = 2 : 5 (from 2MnO4− + 5C2O42− + 16H+ → 2Mn2+ + 10CO2 + 8H2O).
终点 vs 等当点：「终点」是颜色刚好变了那一刻，「等当点」是两种物质恰好按比例完全反应的理论时刻。它们几乎重合但不完全是一回事——答题时别把两个词当同义词乱写。Endpoint vs equivalence point: the endpoint is the moment the colour just changes; the equivalence point is the theoretical moment the two substances have reacted in exactly the right ratio. They nearly coincide but are not identical — don't treat the two words as synonyms.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: Potassium manganate(VII) acts as its own indicator: its purple colour disappears as it is reduced to colourless Mn²⁺, and the endpoint is shown by the first permanent pale-pink colour. In iodine–thiosulfate titrations, starch is added and the endpoint is the disappearance of the blue colour.
例题Example
用 0.0200 mol dm⁻³ 的酸性 KMnO₄ 溶液滴定 25.0 cm³ 的草酸钠（Na2C2O4）溶液，恰好用去 25.0 cm³。已知 2MnO4− + 5C2O42− + 16H+ → 2Mn2+ + 10CO2 + 8H2O，求草酸钠溶液的浓度。A 0.0200 mol dm⁻³ acidic KMnO₄ solution is used to titrate 25.0 cm³ of sodium oxalate (Na2C2O4) solution, and exactly 25.0 cm³ is used. Given 2MnO4− + 5C2O42− + 16H+ → 2Mn2+ + 10CO2 + 8H2O, calculate the concentration of the oxalate solution.
① n(MnO4−) = cV = 0.0200 × 25.0/1000 = 5.00 × 10⁻⁴ mol。① n(MnO4−) = cV = 0.0200 × 25.0/1000 = 5.00 × 10⁻⁴ mol. ② 摩尔比 MnO4− : C2O42− = 2 : 5，所以 n(C2O42−) = 5.00×10⁻⁴ × 5/2 = 1.25 × 10⁻³ mol。② The mole ratio MnO4− : C2O42− = 2 : 5, so n(C2O42−) = 5.00×10⁻⁴ × 5/2 = 1.25 × 10⁻³ mol. ③ c = n/V = 1.25×10⁻³ / (25.0/1000) = 0.0500 mol dm⁻³。③ c = n/V = 1.25×10⁻³ / (25.0/1000) = 0.0500 mol dm⁻³. ④ 自检：体积相同，浓度比应等于摩尔比的反比，5/2 × 0.0200 = 0.0500，对上了。④ Check: with equal volumes, the concentration ratio is the inverse of the mole ratio, 5/2 × 0.0200 = 0.0500, which matches.
练习Practice
MnO₄⁻ : Fe²⁺ = 1 : 5（方程式是 MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5Fe²⁺ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O + 5Fe³⁺）。MnO₄⁻ : Fe²⁺ = 1 : 5 (from MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5Fe²⁺ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O + 5Fe³⁺).

用 0.0100 mol dm⁻³ 的 KMnO₄ 溶液滴定 20.0 cm³ 的未知浓度 Fe²⁺ 溶液，用去 16.0 cm³。求 Fe²⁺ 溶液的浓度。A 0.0100 mol dm⁻³ KMnO₄ solution titrates 20.0 cm³ of an Fe²⁺ solution of unknown concentration, using 16.0 cm³. Find the concentration of the Fe²⁺ solution.

点开看答案Show answer
n(MnO₄⁻) = 0.0100 × 16.0/1000 = 1.60×10⁻⁴ mol。
n(Fe²⁺) = 1.60×10⁻⁴ × 5 = 8.00×10⁻⁴ mol。
c(Fe²⁺) = 8.00×10⁻⁴ / (20.0/1000) = 0.0400 mol dm⁻³。 n(MnO₄⁻) = 0.0100 × 16.0/1000 = 1.60×10⁻⁴ mol.
n(Fe²⁺) = 1.60×10⁻⁴ × 5 = 8.00×10⁻⁴ mol.
c(Fe²⁺) = 8.00×10⁻⁴ / (20.0/1000) = 0.0400 mol dm⁻³.

单元 6 小结Unit 6 summary

① 氧化数是一本账：单质 0、简单离子看电荷、H 通常 +1、O 通常 −2（过氧化物 −1）、F 恒 −1，总和 = 0 或离子电荷。
② 氧化＝失电子＝氧化数升高，还原＝得电子＝氧化数降低（OIL RIG）；氧化剂抢电子、自己被还原，还原剂送电子、自己被氧化。
③ 配平用半反应法：拆两半 → 配电荷加 e⁻ → 配质量加 H₂O/H⁺ → 等电子相加。
④ 歧化＝同一元素一边升一边降；滴定＝颜色当裁判，KMnO₄ 紫→无色（终点淡粉），碘+淀粉蓝→无色。① Oxidation number is bookkeeping: 0 in elements, the charge for simple ions, H usually +1, O usually −2 (−1 in peroxides), F always −1, and the sum is 0 or the ion's charge.
② Oxidation = loss of electrons = oxidation number up; reduction = gain = oxidation number down (OIL RIG). The oxidiser grabs electrons and is reduced; the reducer gives electrons and is oxidised.
③ Balance by the half-reaction method: split in two → balance charge with e⁻ → balance mass with H₂O/H⁺ → equalise electrons and add.
④ Disproportionation = one element going up and down; titration = colour as referee — KMnO₄ purple→colourless (pale-pink endpoint), iodine+starch blue→colourless.

1 可逆反应与动态平衡Reversible reactions and dynamic equilibrium Dynamic equilibrium动态平衡
这一站要你会：说出「动态平衡」到底是什么意思，写对可逆箭头 ⇌，并解释为什么平衡时浓度不变、反应却还在进行。Goal: say what "dynamic equilibrium" really means, write the reversible arrow ⇌ correctly, and explain why concentrations stay constant even though the reaction is still going.
把可逆反应想成食堂门口：进去的人和出来的人都有。当进的速度 = 出的速度时，食堂里的人数就稳定下来了——但门并没有关，人还在不停地进出。化学平衡就是这样：正反应和逆反应都还在跑，只是速度相等，所以从外面看浓度不再变了。它不是「停下来了」，而是「两边跑得一样快」。Think of a canteen doorway: people go in and people come out. When the rate in equals the rate out, the number of people inside stays steady — yet the door never closes, people keep moving. Equilibrium is the same: forward and reverse reactions keep running, just at equal speed, so from outside the concentrations look unchanged. It hasn't stopped — it's running both ways at the same pace.
两个特征，缺一不可：Two features — you need both:
  • 可逆反应用 ⇌ 表示：正反应（A → B）和逆反应（B → A）都能发生。A reversible reaction is shown with ⇌: the forward (A → B) and reverse (B → A) reactions both happen.
  • 特征一 · 速率相等：平衡时正反应速率 = 逆反应速率，而且都不等于零。Feature 1 · equal rates: at equilibrium the forward and reverse rates are equal, and neither is zero.
  • 特征二 · 浓度恒定：所有物质的浓度不再变化（必须在封闭体系、温度不变时才算数）。Feature 2 · constant concentrations: the concentrations of everything stop changing (this needs a closed system at constant temperature).
  • 「动态」指的是微观上正逆反应一直没停；「平衡」指的是宏观上浓度不再变。两个词不能拆开理解。"Dynamic" means both reactions keep going at the particle level; "equilibrium" means the bulk concentrations no longer change. Don't separate the two words.
最经典的一句错话：「达到平衡后反应就停止了。」——错。平衡只是两股速度相等，反应仍然在双向进行。写这句话会被直接扣分。The classic wrong sentence: "once equilibrium is reached the reaction stops." Wrong — the rates are just equal, and both directions still run. Writing that will cost you marks.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: At equilibrium, the rate of the forward reaction equals the rate of the reverse reaction, so the concentrations of the reactants and products remain constant. The reaction has not stopped — it is a dynamic equilibrium.
例题Example
氮气和氢气合成氨：N2 + 3H2 ⇌ 2NH3。反应进行到某时刻后，各组分浓度不再改变。问：(1) 反应停止了吗？(2) 用一句话说明现在发生了什么。Nitrogen and hydrogen form ammonia: N2 + 3H2 ⇌ 2NH3. After a while the concentrations stop changing. (1) Has the reaction stopped? (2) In one sentence, what is happening now?
① 没有停止——正反应（合成氨）和逆反应（氨分解）都还在进行。① No — both the forward reaction (making NH3) and the reverse (breaking NH3) still run. ② 已经到达动态平衡：正逆反应速率相等，所以浓度保持不变。② It has reached dynamic equilibrium: the forward and reverse rates are equal, so the concentrations stay constant.
练习Practice
把两句错话揪出来，再改成对的说法。Spot the two wrong statements, then correct them.

密闭容器里 2SO2 + O2 ⇌ 2SO3 达到平衡。判断下面两句对不对，错了就改正：(a) 平衡时 SO2 不再转化成 SO3；(b) 平衡时正逆两个反应都停止了。In a closed container 2SO2 + O2 ⇌ 2SO3 reaches equilibrium. Are these true or false? Correct any that are wrong. (a) At equilibrium SO2 no longer turns into SO3. (b) At equilibrium both the forward and reverse reactions have stopped.

点开看答案Show answer
(a) 错：SO2 仍在转化成 SO3，只是同时 SO3 也在以相同速率变回 SO2，所以浓度不变。
(b) 错：两个方向都在进行，只是速率相等——这叫动态平衡，不是静止。 (a) False: SO2 still turns into SO3, but SO3 turns back into SO2 at the same rate, so concentrations stay the same.
(b) False: both directions still run, just at equal rates — that's what makes it a dynamic equilibrium, not a static one.
— 第 1 站完成 —— Stop 1 done —
2 勒夏特列原理Le Chatelier's principle Le Chatelier's principle勒夏特列原理
这一站要你会：用一句话说清勒夏特列原理，并能判断浓度、压强、温度变化时平衡往哪边移动。Goal: state Le Chatelier's principle in one sentence, and predict which way equilibrium shifts when concentration, pressure or temperature changes.
平衡像一个倔脾气的系统：你从外面推它，它就往反方向使劲，尽量把你的动作抵消掉。你加反应物，它就赶紧把多余的反应物用掉、往产物那边跑；你加压，它就往「占地方小」（分子数少）的那边缩；你升温，它就往「吸热」那边走，好把多余的热量吸走。催化剂是唯一不倔的：它帮两边同时加速，谁也不偏袒，所以平衡位置原地不动。Equilibrium is a stubborn system: push it from outside and it pushes back, trying to cancel what you did. Add reactant and it rushes to use it up, shifting toward products; raise the pressure and it squeezes toward the side with fewer gas molecules; heat it up and it moves toward the endothermic side to absorb the extra heat. A catalyst is the only one that doesn't fight back — it speeds up both sides equally, taking no sides, so the position stays put.
原理一句话 + 三条具体规则：The principle plus three concrete rules:
  • 勒夏特列原理：如果一个处于平衡的系统被改变了条件，平衡会向抵消这个改变的方向移动。Le Chatelier's principle: if a system at equilibrium is subjected to a change, the position of equilibrium shifts to oppose that change.
  • 浓度：加反应物 → 向右；加产物 → 向左。Concentration: add reactant → shifts right; add product → shifts left.
  • 压强：只数气态分子。增大压强 → 往气态分子数少的一侧；两边气态分子数相同则不动。Pressure: count gas molecules only. Increase pressure → shift to the side with fewer gas molecules; equal numbers → no shift.
  • 温度：升温 → 往吸热（endothermic）方向；降温 → 往放热方向。Temperature: heat it up → shift in the endothermic direction; cool it down → shift in the exothermic direction.
  • 催化剂：加快到达平衡的速度，但不改变平衡位置（正逆都加速，Kc 不变）。Catalyst: speeds up reaching equilibrium but does not move its position (it accelerates both directions; Kc is unchanged).
压强那条最容易漏字：一定说「气态分子数」。像 H2 + I2 ⇌ 2HI，两边气态分子都是 2 个，改变压强不移动平衡。只写「分子数」而不限定气态，可能被扣分。The word people drop: always say "gas molecules". For H2 + I2 ⇌ 2HI both sides have 2 gas molecules, so changing pressure does not shift the equilibrium. Saying "molecules" without "gas" can lose you the mark.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: If a system at equilibrium is subjected to a change in concentration, pressure or temperature, the position of equilibrium shifts in the direction that opposes the change.
例题Example
合成氨 N2(g) + 3H2(g) ⇌ 2NH3(g)，正向放热。分别判断下面三种变化时，平衡往哪边移动：(1) 增大压强；(2) 升高温度；(3) 再加入更多 N2。Ammonia is made by N2(g) + 3H2(g) ⇌ 2NH3(g), which is exothermic in the forward direction. Predict the shift for: (1) increasing pressure; (2) raising the temperature; (3) adding more N2.
① 压强：左边 1 + 3 = 4 个气态分子，右边 2 个 → 增压向右（往分子少的一侧，多产氨）。① Pressure: left has 1 + 3 = 4 gas molecules, right has 2 → increasing pressure shifts right (fewer molecules, more ammonia). ② 温度：正向放热、逆向吸热 → 升温向左（往吸热方向，抵消升温）。② Temperature: forward is exothermic, reverse is endothermic → heating shifts left (toward the endothermic side). ③ 浓度：加 N2 → 向右（消耗掉多加的反应物）。③ Concentration: add N2 → shifts right (uses up the extra reactant).
练习Practice
先数两边的气态分子数，再想「抵消」的方向。Count gas molecules on each side first, then think about "opposing".

反应 2SO2(g) + O2(g) ⇌ 2SO3(g) 正向放热。判断平衡往哪边移动：(a) 加入更多 O2；(b) 减小压强；(c) 降低温度。For 2SO2(g) + O2(g) ⇌ 2SO3(g), exothermic in the forward direction, predict the shift when: (a) more O2 is added; (b) pressure is decreased; (c) the temperature is lowered.

点开看答案Show answer
(a) 加 O2 → 向右（消耗掉多余的 O2）。
(b) 减小压强 → 向左（左边 3 个气态分子、右边 2 个，减压往分子多的一侧）。
(c) 降温 → 向右（正向放热，降温时往放热方向走，多放热来抵消降温）。 (a) add O2 → right (uses up the extra O2).
(b) decrease pressure → left (3 gas molecules on the left vs 2 on the right; lower pressure shifts toward more molecules).
(c) cool it down → right (forward is exothermic; cooling shifts toward the exothermic side, releasing heat to oppose the cooling).

3 平衡常数 KcThe equilibrium constant Kc Kc expression平衡常数表达式
这一站要你会：写出任意反应的 Kc 表达式（知道固体和纯液体不写进去），并用平衡浓度算出 Kc——包括它的单位。Goal: write the Kc expression for any reaction (knowing solids and pure liquids are omitted), and calculate Kc from equilibrium concentrations — including its units.
Kc 就像平衡时刻的一张成绩单：它记录下产物和反应物的浓度比。只要温度不变，同一个反应的 Kc 就固定不变，跟一开始放了多少原料没关系。记法很简单：分子放产物、分母放反应物，幂就是方程里的系数。Kc is like a report card at the moment of equilibrium: it records the ratio of product to reactant concentrations. As long as the temperature is fixed, Kc is constant for a given reaction — it doesn't matter how much you started with. The memory trick: products on top, reactants on the bottom, powers equal to the coefficients.
写表达式 + 三个注意：Writing the expression + three cautions:
对于 aA + bB ⇌ cC + dD： Kc = [C]c[D]d / [A]a[B]b
  • 用平衡时的浓度（mol dm−3），不是摩尔数；用方括号 [X] 表示浓度。Use equilibrium concentrations (mol dm−3), not moles; square brackets [X] mean concentration.
  • 固体 (s) 和纯液体 (l) 不写进表达式——它们的浓度恒定，已经折进常数里了。Solids (s) and pure liquids (l) are left out — their concentration is constant and folded into the constant.
  • Kc 只随温度变；浓度、压强、催化剂都改不了它。Kc only changes with temperature; concentration, pressure and catalyst leave it alone.
  • Kc 常有单位：单位 = (mol dm−3) 的「分子幂和 − 分母幂和」次方。若上下幂相等，Kc 无单位。Kc usually has units: units = (mol dm−3) raised to (sum of product powers − sum of reactant powers). If those sums are equal, Kc has no unit.
大小怎么看：Kc 很大（如 106）→ 平衡偏向产物，反应几乎走完；Kc 很小（如 10−6）→ 平衡偏向反应物，几乎不反应。Reading the size: a large Kc (e.g. 106) → the equilibrium lies far toward products, the reaction nearly goes to completion; a tiny Kc (e.g. 10−6) → it lies toward reactants, almost nothing reacts.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: Kc is the ratio of the product concentrations to the reactant concentrations, each raised to the power of its coefficient in the equation, measured at equilibrium. Solids and pure liquids are not included.
例题Example
反应 H2(g) + I2(g) ⇌ 2HI(g) 在某温度达到平衡，[H2] = 0.10、[I2] = 0.10、[HI] = 0.20（单位 mol dm−3）。计算 Kc，并说明它的单位。For H2(g) + I2(g) ⇌ 2HI(g) at equilibrium: [H2] = 0.10, [I2] = 0.10, [HI] = 0.20 (mol dm−3). Calculate Kc and state its units.
① 写表达式：① write the expression:
Kc = [HI]2 / ([H2][I2])
② 代入浓度：② substitute:
Kc = (0.20)2 / (0.10 × 0.10) = 0.040 / 0.010 = 4.0
③ 单位：分子幂 = 2，分母幂 = 1 + 1 = 2，相等 → 无单位。所以 Kc = 4.0。③ units: product power = 2, reactant power = 1 + 1 = 2, they cancel → no unit. So Kc = 4.0.
练习Practice
先写表达式、再代入、最后单独算单位，别一次全混在一起。Write the expression, substitute, then work out the units separately — don't do it all at once.

反应 N2(g) + 3H2(g) ⇌ 2NH3(g) 达到平衡时 [N2] = 0.20、[H2] = 0.30、[NH3] = 0.60（mol dm−3）。计算 Kc 并写出它的单位。For N2(g) + 3H2(g) ⇌ 2NH3(g) at equilibrium: [N2] = 0.20, [H2] = 0.30, [NH3] = 0.60 (mol dm−3). Calculate Kc and give its units.

点开看答案Show answer
表达式：Kc = [NH3]2 / ([N2][H2]3)。
代入：Kc = (0.60)2 / (0.20 × 0.303) = 0.36 / (0.20 × 0.027) = 0.36 / 0.0054 = 66.7。
单位：分子幂 2、分母幂 1 + 3 = 4，差 = −2 → mol−2 dm6。所以 Kc ≈ 66.7 mol−2 dm6。 Expression: Kc = [NH3]2 / ([N2][H2]3).
Substitute: Kc = (0.60)2 / (0.20 × 0.303) = 0.36 / (0.20 × 0.027) = 0.36 / 0.0054 = 66.7.
Units: product power 2, reactant power 1 + 3 = 4, difference = −2 → mol−2 dm6. So Kc ≈ 66.7 mol−2 dm6.

4 酸与碱的定义Brønsted–Lowry acids and bases Brønsted–Lowry酸碱质子理论
这一站要你会：用「质子给体 / 受体」定义酸碱，找出反应里的两对共轭酸碱对，并解释水为什么是「两性」的。Goal: define acids and bases as proton donors / acceptors, pick out the two conjugate pairs in a reaction, and explain why water is amphoteric.
把 H⁺（质子）想成一颗烫手的小球：酸是愿意把球扔出去的人（给体），碱是伸手去接的人（受体）。扔出去之后，酸自己少了一个 H⁺、变成了「碱」；接住的那个多了一个 H⁺、变成了「酸」——这一前一后差一个 H⁺ 的搭档，就叫共轭酸碱对。水最特别：它既能当酸扔球，也能当碱接球，这叫「两性（amphoteric）」。Picture H⁺ (a proton) as a hot potato: an acid is the person willing to toss it away (donor), a base is the one who catches it (acceptor). After the throw, the acid has lost one H⁺ and become a base; the catcher has gained one H⁺ and become an acid — that pair differing by one H⁺ is a conjugate acid–base pair. Water is special: it can toss the potato (act as acid) or catch it (act as base), which is called amphoteric.
定义 + 三个要点：The definitions + three points:
  • 酸 = 质子（H⁺）给体；碱 = 质子受体——这是 Brønsted–Lowry 定义，考试只认这一套。An acid is a proton (H⁺) donor; a base is a proton acceptor — this is the Brønsted–Lowry definition, the only one the exam uses.
  • 共轭酸碱对：只差一个 H⁺ 的一对（HCl / Cl⁻，NH₄⁺ / NH₃）。酸永远比它的共轭碱多一个 H⁺。Conjugate pair: two species differing by one H⁺ (HCl / Cl⁻, NH₄⁺ / NH₃). The acid always has one more H⁺ than its conjugate base.
  • 水是两性的：能给出 H⁺ 变成 OH⁻（当酸），也能接受 H⁺ 变成 H₃O⁺（当碱）。Water is amphoteric: it can donate H⁺ to form OH⁻ (acting as acid) or accept H⁺ to form H₃O⁺ (acting as base).
  • 范例：HCl + H₂O → H₃O⁺ + Cl⁻。HCl 给质子（酸），水接质子（碱）。The example: HCl + H₂O → H₃O⁺ + Cl⁻. HCl donates the proton (acid), water accepts it (base).
判断共轭对只看一件事：谁比谁多一个 H⁺。酸去掉一个 H⁺ 就是它的共轭碱；碱加上一个 H⁺ 就是它的共轭酸。别再背整张表。Judge a conjugate pair by one thing only: who has one more H⁺. An acid minus one H⁺ is its conjugate base; a base plus one H⁺ is its conjugate acid. Stop memorising tables.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: A Brønsted–Lowry acid is a proton donor and a base is a proton acceptor. In HCl + H₂O → H₃O⁺ + Cl⁻, HCl donates a proton to water and forms its conjugate base, Cl⁻.
例题Example
反应 NH₃ + H₂O ⇌ NH₄⁺ + OH⁻ 中，谁是酸、谁是碱？写出两对共轭酸碱对。In NH₃ + H₂O ⇌ NH₄⁺ + OH⁻, which is the acid and which the base? Write down the two conjugate pairs.
① NH₃ 接受了一个 H⁺ → 是碱；H₂O 给出了一个 H⁺ → 是酸。① NH₃ accepts an H⁺ → it is the base; H₂O donates an H⁺ → it is the acid. ② 共轭对 1：NH₃ / NH₄⁺（碱 + 它的共轭酸）；共轭对 2：H₂O / OH⁻（酸 + 它的共轭碱）。② Pair 1: NH₃ / NH₄⁺ (base and its conjugate acid); pair 2: H₂O / OH⁻ (acid and its conjugate base).
练习Practice
先看谁给了 H⁺、谁接了 H⁺，再配对。Find who gives and who takes the H⁺ first, then pair them up.

反应 CH₃COOH + H₂O ⇌ CH₃COO⁻ + H₃O⁺ 中，指出酸和碱，并写出两对共轭酸碱对。In CH₃COOH + H₂O ⇌ CH₃COO⁻ + H₃O⁺, identify the acid and base, and write the two conjugate pairs.

点开看答案Show answer
CH₃COOH 给出 H⁺ → 酸；H₂O 接受 H⁺ → 碱。
共轭对 1：CH₃COOH / CH₃COO⁻（酸 + 共轭碱）；共轭对 2：H₃O⁺ / H₂O（酸 + 共轭碱）。注意 H₂O 这次当的是碱，它的共轭酸就是 H₃O⁺。 CH₃COOH donates H⁺ → acid; H₂O accepts H⁺ → base.
Pair 1: CH₃COOH / CH₃COO⁻ (acid and conjugate base); pair 2: H₃O⁺ / H₂O (acid and conjugate base). Note H₂O acts as the base here, and its conjugate acid is H₃O⁺.

5 强酸弱酸与 pHpH and strong & weak acids pH scalepH 值
这一站要你会：用 pH = −log₁₀[H⁺] 算强酸的 pH，说清强酸和弱酸的区别（电离程度不同），并比较同浓度下的 pH 与导电性。Goal: use pH = −log₁₀[H⁺] to find the pH of a strong acid, explain the difference between strong and weak acids (how fully they ionise), and compare pH and conductivity at equal concentration.
把酸放进水，它就要「拆家」释放 H⁺。强酸是「全拆」——每个分子都电离出 H⁺；弱酸是「拆一半」——大部分分子还抱团不动，只有一点点 H⁺ 跑出来。所以同样浓度下，强酸的 H⁺ 多得多，pH 更低、导电也更好。记住：强酸强的是「电离的决心」，不是「浓度的大小」。Drop an acid into water and it "breaks house" to release H⁺. A strong acid breaks completely — every molecule ionises; a weak acid breaks only a little — most molecules stay together and only a few H⁺ escape. So at the same concentration a strong acid has far more H⁺, a lower pH and better conductivity. Remember: "strong" is about how fully it ionises, not how concentrated it is.
一条公式 + 两类酸：One formula + two kinds of acid:
pH = −log10[H+]
  • 强酸完全电离（单向箭头）：HCl、H₂SO₄、HNO₃。1 个分子放出全部 H⁺，所以 [H⁺] = 酸的浓度。Strong acids ionise completely (single arrow): HCl, H₂SO₄, HNO₃. Each molecule releases its H⁺, so [H⁺] = the acid concentration.
  • 弱酸部分电离（可逆箭头）：CH₃COOH ⇌ H⁺ + CH₃COO⁻。只有很小一部分拆开，[H⁺] 远小于酸的浓度。Weak acids ionise partially (reversible arrow): CH₃COOH ⇌ H⁺ + CH₃COO⁻. Only a small fraction breaks up, so [H⁺] is far below the acid concentration.
  • 同浓度对比：强酸 pH 更低、导电性更强、和金属反应更快；弱酸各项都更「温和」。At equal concentration: the strong acid has a lower pH, higher conductivity and faster reaction with metals; the weak acid is milder on every count.
  • pH 每降 1，[H⁺] 变成 10 倍（对数刻度）。pH = 2 的溶液，H⁺ 是 pH = 3 的 10 倍。Each pH step of 1 changes [H⁺] by 10× (a log scale). A solution at pH 2 has 10 times the H⁺ of one at pH 3.
两个别混：「强 / 弱」说的是电离程度（性质），「浓 / 稀」说的是浓度（多少水）。一瓶稀盐酸虽然「稀」，但 HCl 依然 100% 电离——它照样是强酸。Don't mix two words: "strong/weak" is about how fully it ionises (a property); "concentrated/dilute" is about how much water (amount). Dilute hydrochloric acid is "dilute", yet HCl still ionises 100% — it is still a strong acid.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: A strong acid fully dissociates in water, so [H⁺] equals the acid concentration. A weak acid only partially dissociates, so [H⁺] is much smaller, giving a higher pH.
例题Example
计算 0.0100 mol dm⁻³ 盐酸（HCl，强酸）的 pH。Calculate the pH of 0.0100 mol dm⁻³ hydrochloric acid (HCl, a strong acid).
① 强酸完全电离：HCl → H⁺ + Cl⁻，所以 [H⁺] = 0.0100 mol dm⁻³。① a strong acid ionises fully: HCl → H⁺ + Cl⁻, so [H⁺] = 0.0100 mol dm⁻³.
pH = −log10(0.0100) = −log10(10−2) = 2.00
② 两位小数照题目精度写：pH = 2.00。② keep two decimal places to match the data: pH = 2.00.
练习Practice
先判断是不是强酸，再让 [H⁺] = 酸的浓度。Check it's a strong acid, then set [H⁺] equal to the acid concentration.

计算 0.100 mol dm⁻³ 硝酸（HNO₃，强酸）的 pH。Calculate the pH of 0.100 mol dm⁻³ nitric acid (HNO₃, a strong acid).

点开看答案Show answer
HNO₃ 是强酸，完全电离 → [H⁺] = 0.100 mol dm⁻³。
pH = −log₁₀(0.100) = −log₁₀(10⁻¹) = 1.00。 HNO₃ is a strong acid and ionises fully → [H⁺] = 0.100 mol dm⁻³.
pH = −log₁₀(0.100) = −log₁₀(10⁻¹) = 1.00.
— 第 5 站完成 —— Stop 5 done —
6 Ka 与 pKaKa and pKa Ka expression酸电离常数
这一站要你会：写出弱酸的 Ka 表达式，用 Ka / pKa 比较酸性强弱，并用近似式 [H⁺] = √(Ka×c) 估算弱酸的 pH。Goal: write the Ka expression for a weak acid, compare acid strength using Ka / pKa, and estimate a weak acid's pH with [H⁺] = √(Ka×c).
强酸「全拆」，我们直接数 H⁺ 就行；弱酸「拆一半」，就得拿一把尺子量它到底拆了多少——这把尺子就是 Ka。Ka 越大，拆得越彻底，酸越强。但 Ka 的数值常常小得离谱（10⁻⁵ 这种），化学家就取个负对数，把它变成好读的 pKa：pKa 越小，酸越强，跟 Ka 正好反过来。A strong acid breaks fully, so we just count H⁺; a weak acid breaks only a little, so we need a ruler to measure how much — that ruler is Ka. The bigger Ka is, the more it breaks and the stronger the acid. Since Ka is often awkwardly tiny (like 10⁻⁵), chemists take its negative logarithm to get a friendlier pKa: the smaller pKa is, the stronger the acid — the opposite of Ka.
表达式 + 近似式：The expression + the approximation:
弱酸 HA ⇌ H⁺ + A⁻： Ka = [H⁺][A⁻] / [HA]
  • Ka 越大 → 酸越强（[H⁺] 越多）。Bigger Ka → stronger acid (more H⁺).
  • pKa = −log₁₀ Ka；反过来 pKa 越小 → 酸越强。pKa = −log₁₀ Ka; the reverse holds: smaller pKa → stronger acid.
  • 弱酸近似：因为电离得很少，[HA] ≈ c（起始浓度），且 [H⁺] = [A⁻]，于是：The weak-acid approximation: since very little ionises, [HA] ≈ c (initial concentration) and [H⁺] = [A⁻], giving:
    [H⁺] = √(Ka × c)
  • 算出 [H⁺] 后再套 pH = −log₁₀[H⁺]。Once you have [H⁺], use pH = −log₁₀[H⁺].
近似式有前提：只对「电离度很小」的弱酸成立。强酸完全电离，[H⁺] = c，绝不能套 √(Ka×c)。看到题目给 Ka，就默认是弱酸。The approximation has a condition: it only works for a weak acid that ionises very little. A strong acid has [H⁺] = c — never apply √(Ka×c). If a question gives Ka, assume a weak acid.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: For a weak acid HA, Ka = [H⁺][A⁻]/[HA]. A larger Ka (or a smaller pKa) means a stronger acid, because more of the acid is ionised.
例题Example
某弱酸的 Ka = 1.0 × 10⁻⁴，浓度为 0.10 mol dm⁻³。估算 [H⁺] 和 pH。A weak acid has Ka = 1.0 × 10⁻⁴ and concentration 0.10 mol dm⁻³. Estimate [H⁺] and the pH.
① 套近似式：① apply the approximation:
[H⁺] = √(Ka × c) = √(1.0×10⁻⁴ × 0.10) = √(1.0×10⁻⁵) = 3.16×10⁻³ mol dm⁻³
② 算 pH：② find the pH:
pH = −log10(3.16×10⁻³) ≈ 2.50
③ 对照：同浓度强酸 pH 会是 1.00，弱酸 2.50 明显更高——说明 H⁺ 少了很多。③ Compare: a strong acid at this concentration would be pH 1.00, so 2.50 is clearly higher — far fewer H⁺.
练习Practice
先乘起来再开根号，最后取负对数。Multiply first, take the square root, then the negative log.

某弱酸的 Ka = 4.0 × 10⁻⁶，浓度为 0.010 mol dm⁻³。估算它的 pH。A weak acid has Ka = 4.0 × 10⁻⁶ and concentration 0.010 mol dm⁻³. Estimate its pH.

点开看答案Show answer
[H⁺] = √(4.0×10⁻⁶ × 0.010) = √(4.0×10⁻⁸) = 2.0×10⁻⁴ mol dm⁻³。
pH = −log₁₀(2.0×10⁻⁴) ≈ 3.70。自检：弱酸浓度 0.010，pH 3.70 比同浓度强酸的 2.00 高不少，合理。 [H⁺] = √(4.0×10⁻⁶ × 0.010) = √(4.0×10⁻⁸) = 2.0×10⁻⁴ mol dm⁻³.
pH = −log₁₀(2.0×10⁻⁴) ≈ 3.70. Sanity check: a weak acid at 0.010 mol dm⁻³ giving pH 3.70 is well above the strong-acid value of 2.00 — sensible.
— 第 6 站完成 —— Stop 6 done —
7 缓冲溶液与指示剂Buffers and indicators Buffers & indicators缓冲与指示剂
这一站要你会：说清缓冲溶液是什么、怎么「接住」外加的酸 / 碱，并解释指示剂为什么能随 pH 变色。Goal: say what a buffer is, how it "catches" added acid or base, and explain why an indicator changes colour with pH.
缓冲溶液像一块吸质子的海绵：你往里滴几滴酸，它把多余的 H⁺ 吸走；滴几滴碱，它又吐出 H⁺ 去中和。所以 pH 几乎纹丝不动。它通常是「弱酸 + 它的共轭碱」搭伙（比如醋酸 + 醋酸根），一个负责「吸 H⁺」，一个负责「吐 H⁺」。指示剂则是一种弱酸，它自己的分子和离子颜色不同——pH 一变，哪种形态占多数就跟着变，于是我们看到颜色翻了个身。A buffer is a proton-soaking sponge: add a few drops of acid and it mops up the extra H⁺; add a few drops of base and it releases H⁺ to neutralise them. The pH barely moves. It is usually a weak acid plus its conjugate base (like ethanoic acid and ethanoate), one partner to soak up H⁺ and the other to hand it back. An indicator is a weak acid whose molecule and ion have different colours — when the pH shifts, whichever form dominates changes, and we see the colour flip.
缓冲怎么工作 + 指示剂怎么变色：How buffers work + how indicators change colour:
  • 缓冲溶液：能抵抗少量酸或碱的加入，保持 pH 基本不变。A buffer solution resists small additions of acid or base and keeps the pH nearly constant.
  • 组成：弱酸 + 它的共轭碱（如 CH₃COOH / CH₃COO⁻）。What's in it: a weak acid plus its conjugate base (e.g. CH₃COOH / CH₃COO⁻).
  • 加酸时：CH₃COO⁻ + H⁺ → CH₃COOH，醋酸根把 H⁺ 接住，[H⁺] 几乎不变。Adding acid: CH₃COO⁻ + H⁺ → CH₃COOH; the ethanoate grabs the H⁺, so [H⁺] barely changes.
  • 加碱时：CH₃COOH + OH⁻ → CH₃COO⁻ + H₂O，醋酸给出 H⁺ 去中和 OH⁻。Adding base: CH₃COOH + OH⁻ → CH₃COO⁻ + H₂O; the acid hands out H⁺ to neutralise the OH⁻.
  • 指示剂是弱酸：HIn ⇌ H⁺ + In⁻，两种形态颜色不同，pH 决定哪种占多数。An indicator is a weak acid: HIn ⇌ H⁺ + In⁻, its two forms have different colours and pH decides which dominates.
  • 变色范围：甲基橙约 3.1–4.4（红→黄）；酚酞约 8.2–10.0（无色→粉红）。Ranges: methyl orange ≈ 3.1–4.4 (red→yellow); phenolphthalein ≈ 8.2–10.0 (colourless→pink).
选指示剂看滴定：强酸滴定强碱，突跃大，甲基橙或酚酞都行；强酸滴定弱碱（终点偏酸）用甲基橙，弱酸滴定强碱（终点偏碱）用酚酞。原则只有一句：变色范围要罩住 pH 突跃。Pick the indicator for the titration: strong acid + strong base has a big jump, so either indicator works; strong acid + weak base (acidic end point) needs methyl orange, weak acid + strong base (basic end point) needs phenolphthalein. One rule: the colour-change range must cover the steep pH jump.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: A buffer resists changes in pH when small amounts of acid or base are added. It is a mixture of a weak acid and its conjugate base. An indicator is a weak acid whose two forms have different colours.
例题Example
解释：向醋酸 / 醋酸钠（CH₃COOH / CH₃COO⁻）缓冲溶液里加入少量盐酸后，pH 为什么几乎不变。Explain why the pH of an ethanoic acid / ethanoate (CH₃COOH / CH₃COO⁻) buffer stays almost unchanged when a little hydrochloric acid is added.
① 加入的 HCl 提供额外的 H⁺。① the added HCl supplies extra H⁺. ② 缓冲里的醋酸根把 H⁺ 接住：CH₃COO⁻ + H⁺ → CH₃COOH。② the ethanoate in the buffer grabs the H⁺: CH₃COO⁻ + H⁺ → CH₃COOH. ③ H⁺ 被消耗，溶液中 [H⁺] 几乎没变 → pH 几乎不变。③ the H⁺ is removed, so [H⁺] barely changes → the pH barely changes.
练习Practice
这回是碱来捣乱，想想谁负责「吐 H⁺」去中和。This time base is the intruder — think about who hands out H⁺ to neutralise it.

解释：向醋酸 / 醋酸钠缓冲溶液里加入少量氢氧化钠溶液后，pH 为什么几乎不变。Explain why the pH of an ethanoic acid / ethanoate buffer stays almost unchanged when a little sodium hydroxide solution is added.

点开看答案Show answer
加入的 NaOH 提供 OH⁻；缓冲里的醋酸给出 H⁺ 去中和：CH₃COOH + OH⁻ → CH₃COO⁻ + H₂O。OH⁻ 被消耗，[H⁺] 几乎不变 → pH 几乎不变。 The added NaOH supplies OH⁻; the ethanoic acid in the buffer hands out H⁺ to neutralise it: CH₃COOH + OH⁻ → CH₃COO⁻ + H₂O. The OH⁻ is removed, so [H⁺] barely changes → the pH barely changes.
— 第 7 站完成 —— Stop 7 done —

单元 7 小结Unit 7 summary

① 可逆反应达到动态平衡：正逆速率相等、浓度不变（不是停止）；勒夏特列原理告诉你条件一变，平衡往「抵消」的方向动。
② Kc = 产物浓度（带系数幂）除以反应物浓度；固体和纯液体不写进去，单位要单独对。
③ 酸给 H⁺、碱接 H⁺；强酸全电离、弱酸部分电离；pH = −log[H⁺]，Ka 越大（pKa 越小）酸越强；缓冲靠「弱酸 + 共轭碱」稳住 pH。① Reversible reactions reach dynamic equilibrium: equal rates, constant concentrations (never stopped); Le Chatelier's principle says any change makes it shift to oppose it.
② Kc = product concentrations (raised to their powers) over reactant concentrations; omit solids and pure liquids, and work out the units separately.
③ Acids donate H⁺, bases accept H⁺; strong acids ionise fully, weak ones partially; pH = −log[H⁺], bigger Ka (smaller pKa) = stronger acid; buffers hold pH steady with a weak acid plus its conjugate base.

下一站最重要的一件事：平衡只回答「能走到哪」，动力学（单元 8）才回答「走得有多快」——两者分开记，别混。Why the next unit matters: equilibrium only tells you how far a reaction goes — kinetics (Unit 8) tells you how fast. Keep the two ideas separate.

单元 8 · 反应动力学：为什么有的反应瞬间完成，有的要等一万年Unit 8 · Reaction kinetics: why some reactions finish in a flash and others take forever

CAIE 9701 Topic 8 · 5 站 · 为什么有的反应瞬间完成，有的要等一万年CAIE 9701 Topic 8 · 5 stops · why some reactions finish in an instant and others would wait ten thousand years

路线图本单元五站，先学会「怎么测快慢」，再弄懂「为什么有快慢」Five stops, in order — first how we measure speed, then why speed differs at all

  1. 反应速率怎么定义和测量Defining and measuring rate of reaction
  2. 碰撞理论：不碰不上Collision theory: no collision, no reaction
  3. 温度为什么这么关键Why temperature matters so much
  4. 催化剂：抄近路Catalysts: the shortcut
  5. 把概念串起来Putting it all together

建议：先把第 2 站「碰撞理论」吃透，后面温度、催化剂、表面积全是它的「应用题」。Tip: get stop 2 (collision theory) clear first — temperature, catalysts and surface area are all just applications of it.

1 反应速率怎么定义和测量Defining and measuring rate of reaction Rate of reaction反应速率
这一站要你会：给出速率的定义与单位，并说出四种常用测量方法（气体体积、质量减少、比色、pH）各适用什么情况。Goal: state the definition and units of rate, and name four ways to measure it (gas volume, mass loss, colorimetry, pH) and when each works.
想象你在数一场演唱会散场：门口站着个人，每秒钟数一次场内还剩多少人。反应速率就是这个「计数器」——它只关心浓度每秒钟变化了多少。你不用等反应全部走完，只要盯住曲线上的一小段，就知道它此刻跑得有多快。Picture counting the crowd leaving a concert: someone at the door checks every second how many people remain inside. The rate of reaction is that counter — it only cares how much the concentration changes each second. You never wait for the whole thing to finish; you watch one small stretch of the curve and you know how fast it is going right now.
定义与单位：Definition and units:
rate = −Δ[reactant] / Δt = +Δ[product] / Δt 单位 = mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹
  • 速率 = 反应物（或产物）浓度的变化 ÷ 时间。方括号 [ ] 表示浓度，单位是 mol dm⁻³。Rate = change in concentration of a reactant (or product) ÷ time. Square brackets [ ] mean concentration, in mol dm⁻³.
  • 反应物在减少，所以 Δ[reactant] 是负数，前面加负号让速率是正数；产物在增多，用正号即可。A reactant decreases, so Δ[reactant] is negative — the minus sign makes rate positive; a product increases, so it takes a plus sign.
  • 平均速率看一整段，瞬时速率看某一刻（曲线切线的斜率）。图里切线越陡，那一刻越快。Average rate covers a whole stretch; instantaneous rate is at one moment (the gradient of the tangent). The steeper the tangent, the faster that moment.
四种测量方法：Four ways to measure it:
  • 测气体体积：反应放出气体，用注射器或倒扣量筒收集，看体积随时间怎么涨（如大理石 + 盐酸）。Gas volume: if a gas is produced, collect it in a syringe or inverted measuring cylinder and watch the volume grow over time (e.g. marble + acid).
  • 测质量减少：生成的气体跑掉了，天平读数变轻，看质量随时间怎么掉。Mass loss: the gas escapes, so the balance reading falls — watch the mass drop over time.
  • 比色法：反应物或产物有颜色，用比色计测透光率（或吸光度）随时间的变化，颜色越深吸光越多。Colorimetry: if something is coloured, measure how much light is transmitted (or absorbed) over time — the darker the colour, the more light absorbed.
  • 测 pH：反应消耗或生成酸/碱，用 pH 计盯着读数随时间的变化。pH: if the reaction uses up or makes an acid or base, follow the pH reading over time.
选方法的诀窍：先看反应里有没有「看得见、称得着、量得出」的东西在变——有气体就量气体或称质量，有颜色就比色，有酸碱性就测 pH。四种方法本质上都是「换个办法测浓度在不在变」。How to pick a method: find whatever is visible, weighable or measurable and changing — gas → volume or mass; colour → colorimetry; acid/base → pH. All four are really just "another way to watch the concentration change".
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: Rate of reaction is the change in concentration of a reactant or product per unit time, and it is measured in mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹.
例题Example
某反应中，产物 B 的浓度在 20 秒内从 0 升到 0.60 mol dm⁻³。求这段时间的平均反应速率。In a reaction, the concentration of product B rises from 0 to 0.60 mol dm⁻³ in 20 s. Calculate the average rate of reaction.
① 产物在增多，用正号：rate = Δ[B] / Δt。① the product is increasing, so use a plus sign: rate = Δ[B] / Δt. ② = (0.60 − 0) / 20 = 0.030 mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹。② = (0.60 − 0) / 20 = 0.030 mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹.
练习Practice
反应物在减少，别忘了那个负号。The reactant is decreasing — don't forget the minus sign.

反应物 A 的浓度在 40 s 内从 1.00 mol dm⁻³ 降到 0.20 mol dm⁻³。求这段时间内「对 A 而言」的平均速率。The concentration of reactant A falls from 1.00 mol dm⁻³ to 0.20 mol dm⁻³ in 40 s. Calculate the average rate with respect to A.

点开看答案Show answer
rate = −Δ[A]/Δt = −(0.20 − 1.00)/40 = 0.80/40 = 0.020 mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹。对反应物加负号，让速率是正数；对产物则直接用正号。 rate = −Δ[A]/Δt = −(0.20 − 1.00)/40 = 0.80/40 = 0.020 mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹. The minus sign makes the rate positive for a reactant; a product takes a plus sign.
— 第 1 站完成 —— Stop 1 done —
2 碰撞理论：不碰不上Collision theory: no collision, no reaction Collision theory碰撞理论
这一站要你会：用碰撞理论说出反应必须满足的三个条件，并解释「提高浓度为什么能加快反应」。Goal: state the three conditions a reaction needs, and explain why raising the concentration speeds a reaction up.
化学反应不是「把两个东西放一起就自动变」。它像投篮：球（粒子）必须砸到篮筐（发生碰撞），出手角度还得对（方向正确），力气更要够大才进得去（能量够）。三项缺一，球就弹出去白搭。凡是能凑成又准又狠那一投的碰撞，就叫有效碰撞。A reaction is not "put two things together and it just happens". It is like shooting a basket: the ball (particle) must reach the hoop (collide), come in at the right angle (correct orientation), and be thrown hard enough (enough energy). Miss any one and the ball bounces away. A collision that lands both accurate and hard is called an effective collision.
三个条件，缺一不可：Three conditions, all required:
  • ① 必须碰撞——不碰就根本没机会反应。① They must collide — no contact, no chance of reacting.
  • ② 方向要对（正确取向）——撞歪了，旧键也断不了、新键也成不了。② Correct orientation — hit at the wrong angle and old bonds won't break or new bonds won't form.
  • ③ 能量要够——至少要达到活化能 Ea，这是反应发生所需的最低能量。③ Enough energy — at least the activation energy, Ea, the minimum energy needed for reaction.
  • 有效碰撞＝同时满足「方向对 + 能量够」的碰撞，只有它能导致反应。An effective collision = one with correct orientation and enough energy; only it leads to reaction.
  • 提高浓度 → 更快：单位体积里粒子变多 → 碰撞频率升高 → 有效碰撞也按比例变多 → 速率加快。Higher concentration → faster: more particles per unit volume → more frequent collisions → more effective collisions → faster rate.
最常漏的一条是「方向」。解释题里三个条件要写全，尤其是问「为什么有些碰撞没反应」时——答案是「方向不对，或能量不够」。"Orientation" is the one people forget. In explain questions, write all three conditions — especially when asked "why do some collisions not react": because the orientation is wrong or the energy is too low.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: For a reaction to occur, particles must collide with energy at least equal to the activation energy and with the correct orientation. Increasing the concentration increases the frequency of effective collisions, so the rate increases.
例题Example
解释：为什么把盐酸的浓度加倍，锌与盐酸的反应会明显变快？Explain why doubling the concentration of hydrochloric acid makes its reaction with zinc noticeably faster.
① 浓度加倍 → 单位体积里的 H⁺ 粒子变多。① doubled concentration → more H⁺ particles per unit volume. ② 碰撞频率升高。② the frequency of collisions rises. ③ 有效碰撞的频率升高 → 反应速率加快。③ the frequency of effective collisions rises → the rate increases.
练习Practice
照例题的「三步」：粒子数 → 碰撞 → 有效碰撞。Follow the example's three steps: particles → collisions → effective collisions.

气体反应中，把压强增大（相当于浓度变大）为什么能加快反应？用碰撞理论解释。For a gaseous reaction, why does increasing the pressure (which raises the concentration) speed it up? Explain using collision theory.

点开看答案Show answer
增大压强把气体粒子挤得更密，单位体积内粒子变多 → 碰撞频率升高 → 有效碰撞频率升高 → 反应速率加快。 Higher pressure squeezes the gas particles closer together, so there are more particles per unit volume → more frequent collisions → more effective collisions → a faster rate.
— 第 2 站完成 —— Stop 2 done —
3 温度为什么这么关键Why temperature matters so much Maxwell–Boltzmann麦克斯韦–玻尔兹曼分布
这一站要你会：用 Maxwell–Boltzmann 分布解释「为什么升温一点点，速率却快很多」。Goal: use the Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution to explain why a small rise in temperature speeds a reaction up so much.
升温为什么这么猛？不只是因为粒子跑得快、撞得勤，更关键的是「越过门槛的人」变多了。想象一场及格线很高的考试，活化能 Ea 就是那条及格线；温度一升，等于给所有学生补了一轮课，能过线的人数暴增——这就是曲线尾巴那一小块阴影迅速变大的意思。门槛没变，但够格的人多了。Why is heating so powerful? Not only do particles move faster and collide more — what really matters is that more of them clear the bar. Picture an exam with a very high pass mark: the activation energy Ea is that pass line. Raising the temperature is like giving every student a revision class, and the number who pass shoots up — that is exactly the shaded tail growing fast. The bar never moves; the number who qualify does.
升温的两个效果（第二个才是主角）：Two effects of heating (the second is the star):
  • ① 平均动能变大 → 粒子跑得更快、碰撞更频繁。① Higher average kinetic energy → particles move faster and collide more often.
  • ② 更重要的是：能量 ≥ Ea 的粒子比例大幅上升 → 有效碰撞急剧增多。这才是升温提速的主因。② More importantly: the fraction with energy ≥ Ea rises sharply → effective collisions shoot up. This is the main reason heating works.
  • 分布的形状：从原点起、先升到峰、再拖着一条长尾趋近 x 轴；曲线下总面积 = 粒子总数，升温不会改变总数，所以面积不变。The curve's shape: it starts at the origin, rises to a peak, then has a long tail approaching the x-axis; the total area equals the number of particles, so heating changes the shape but not the area.
  • 高温曲线：峰变矮、右移、尾部更肥 → Ea 右侧的面积（能反应的粒子）更大。At higher T: the peak is lower, shifted right, with a fatter tail → a bigger area to the right of Ea (particles able to react).
别只说「碰撞更多」。升温对速率的主要贡献是「越过 Ea 的比例增大」。考试里写对这条才有分，只写碰撞更多往往只得一半。Don't just say "more collisions". The main effect of heating is "a larger fraction exceed Ea". Writing that earns the mark; "more collisions" alone often gets only half.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: At a higher temperature the Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution flattens and shifts to the right, so a much larger fraction of particles have energy greater than the activation energy. This greatly increases the rate of reaction.
例题Example
解释：为什么升高温度对速率的提升，远大于「只是碰撞更频繁」所能解释的程度？Explain why raising the temperature boosts the rate far more than "just more frequent collisions" can account for.
① 升温使粒子的动能普遍增大。① heating raises the kinetic energy of the particles overall. ② Maxwell–Boltzmann 分布曲线右移、变宽。② the Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution shifts right and broadens. ③ 能量超过 Ea 的粒子比例大幅上升 → 有效碰撞急剧增多 → 速率大增。③ the fraction with energy above Ea rises sharply → effective collisions increase greatly → the rate jumps.
练习Practice
从「峰的位置、高度、尾部」三个角度描述变化。Describe the change in terms of peak position, height and tail.

描述升温后 Maxwell–Boltzmann 曲线相对低温曲线的两处变化，并指出哪块面积代表「能反应的粒子」。Describe two changes the Maxwell–Boltzmann curve shows on heating, and state which area represents the particles that can react.

点开看答案Show answer
① 峰变得更矮、更靠右；② 尾部更肥，向高能方向延伸得更远。曲线下总面积不变（= 粒子总数）。Ea 右侧、曲线与 x 轴之间的面积代表「能量足够、能反应的粒子」。 ① the peak becomes lower and shifts right; ② the tail is fatter and extends further to high energy. The total area is unchanged (= total particles). The area to the right of Ea, between the curve and the x-axis, represents the particles with enough energy to react.
— 第 3 站完成 —— Stop 3 done —
4 催化剂：抄近路Catalysts: the shortcut Catalysts催化剂
这一站要你会：说出催化剂的定义与作用方式，区分均相与多相催化，并举酶作生物催化剂的例子。Goal: state what a catalyst is and how it works, tell homogeneous from heterogeneous catalysis, and give enzymes as biological catalysts.
催化剂就像一条「高速公路抄近路」：目的地不变（产物和 ΔH 都不变），但它带你走一条坡度更小的坡（活化能更低），所以更多人能爬过去。最妙的是它自己全程不用消耗——把反应送过山之后，它原封不动地等在原地，准备带下一批。A catalyst is a shortcut on the motorway: the destination never changes (the products and ΔH stay the same), but it leads you up a gentler slope (lower activation energy), so far more people make it over. Best of all, it is not used up — after shepherding the reaction over, it sits there untouched, ready for the next batch.
催化剂的三件事：Three things about catalysts:
  • 作用方式：提供一条活化能更低的替代路径，从而加快反应。How it works: it provides an alternative pathway with a lower activation energy, so the reaction speeds up.
  • 反应前后不变：质量不变、化学性质不变（只是物理形态可能变）。Unchanged after: its mass and chemical properties are the same at the end (its physical form may change).
  • 均相催化：催化剂与反应物同相（都在溶液里，或都是气体）。Homogeneous: the catalyst is in the same phase as the reactants (all in solution, or all gases).
  • 多相（异相）催化：催化剂与反应物不同相，通常是固体催化剂 + 气体/液体反应物。例：Haber 法合成氨用的铁、加氢反应用的镍。Heterogeneous: the catalyst is in a different phase, usually a solid catalyst with gaseous or liquid reactants — e.g. iron in the Haber process, nickel in hydrogenation.
  • 酶 = 生物催化剂（本质是蛋白质），高度专一，只在合适的温度与 pH 下工作。Enzymes are biological catalysts (proteins), highly specific, and only work at suitable temperature and pH.
催化剂不改变 ΔH，也不移动平衡位置。它只是让反应「更快到达」那个平衡，正逆两个方向被同等加速。选择题常考这条。A catalyst changes neither ΔH nor the position of equilibrium. It only makes the reaction reach equilibrium sooner, speeding up the forward and reverse directions equally. A classic multiple-choice point.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: A catalyst increases the rate of a reaction by providing an alternative pathway with a lower activation energy. It remains chemically unchanged at the end of the reaction. Enzymes are biological catalysts.
例题Example
说明铁在 Haber 法（合成氨 N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃）中的作用，并说出它属于哪一种催化。State the role of iron in the Haber process (N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃) and say which type of catalysis it is.
① 铁提供一条活化能更低的路径，加快 N₂ 与 H₂ 的反应。① iron provides a lower-activation-energy pathway, speeding up the reaction of N₂ and H₂. ② 铁是固体、反应物是气体，两者不同相 → 多相（异相）催化剂。② iron is solid and the reactants are gases, different phases → a heterogeneous catalyst. ③ 反应前后铁的量与化学性质都不变。③ the mass and chemical nature of the iron are unchanged after the reaction.
练习Practice
看催化剂与反应物「是不是同一相」来区分两类。Decide the type by whether the catalyst is in the same phase as the reactants.

(a) 什么叫均相催化剂、什么叫多相催化剂，各举一例。(b) 酶属于哪一类催化剂？为什么说它「高度专一」？(a) What is a homogeneous and a heterogeneous catalyst? Give one example of each. (b) Which type are enzymes, and why are they called "highly specific"?

点开看答案Show answer
(a) 均相：催化剂与反应物同相（例：酯化反应里的浓 H₂SO₄ 与反应物同在液相）；多相：不同相（例：Haber 法里固体铁 + 气体反应物）。
(b) 酶是生物催化剂（蛋白质）。「高度专一」指一种酶通常只催化一种（或一类）反应，只认特定的底物。 (a) Homogeneous: catalyst and reactants in the same phase (e.g. concentrated H₂SO₄ in an esterification, all in the liquid phase). Heterogeneous: different phases (e.g. solid iron with gaseous reactants in the Haber process).
(b) Enzymes are biological catalysts (proteins). "Highly specific" means one enzyme usually catalyses only one (or one type of) reaction and recognises only its particular substrate.
— 第 4 站完成 —— Stop 4 done —
5 把概念串起来Putting it all together Review综合小结
这一站要你会：面对「反应为什么变快」，能从浓度、温度、催化剂、表面积四个角度，各用一句碰撞理论的话解释。Goal: given "why did the reaction get faster?", explain it from four angles — concentration, temperature, catalyst, surface area — each in one collision-theory sentence.
现在把所有线索织成一张网。有人问你「这个反应怎么变快了」，你脑子里要有四把钥匙：是不是更浓了？是不是更热了？是不是加了催化剂？是不是把固体磨得更碎了？四把钥匙长得不一样，却都能打开同一扇门——「有效碰撞更多了」。能把它们串到这一句上，这一单元才算真的过关。Now weave every thread into one net. When someone asks "why did the reaction speed up?", keep four keys in your head: is it more concentrated? Is it hotter? Was a catalyst added? Was the solid ground finer? The four keys look different, yet all open the same door — more effective collisions. If you can trace everything back to that one sentence, you have truly passed this unit.
四句标准解释：Four standard explanations:
  • 浓度 ↑：单位体积粒子变多 → 碰撞更频繁 → 有效碰撞更多。Concentration ↑: more particles per unit volume → more collisions → more effective collisions.
  • 温度 ↑：动能变大 → 越过 Ea 的粒子比例大增 → 有效碰撞更多。Temperature ↑: higher kinetic energy → far more particles exceed Ea → more effective collisions.
  • 催化剂：降低 Ea → 更多粒子够格反应 → 有效碰撞更多。Catalyst: lowers Ea → more particles qualify → more effective collisions.
  • 表面积 ↑：固体更碎 → 接触面更大 → 粒子能碰到的位置更多 → 碰撞更多。这条只对固体反应物有意义。Surface area ↑: finer solid → larger contact surface → more sites for particles to hit → more collisions. This one only matters for solid reactants.
气体和溶液不用谈表面积——它们已经是「完全暴露」的状态。表面积这条，专门留给「块状固体 vs 粉末」的对比。Gases and solutions have no surface-area story — they are already fully exposed. That factor is reserved for comparing lump solids against powders.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: Any factor that increases the frequency of effective collisions — higher concentration, higher temperature, a catalyst, or a larger surface area — increases the rate of reaction.
例题Example
锌粒与稀盐酸反应较慢；若改用锌粉并微热，速率大增。从至少两个角度用碰撞理论解释。Zinc granules react slowly with dilute acid; using zinc powder and gentle heating makes the reaction far faster. Explain using collision theory from at least two angles.
① 表面积：锌粉比锌粒接触面大得多 → 粒子能碰撞的位置更多 → 有效碰撞更多。① surface area: the powder has a far larger contact surface than granules → more collision sites → more effective collisions. ② 温度：微热使动能增大、越过 Ea 的比例上升 → 有效碰撞更多。② temperature: heating raises kinetic energy and the fraction exceeding Ea → more effective collisions. ③ 两个因素叠加，速率自然大增。③ the two factors add together, so the rate jumps.
练习Practice
三选三：浓度、温度、催化剂各来一句。Pick three: one sentence each for concentration, temperature and catalyst.

某反应在室温下进行得很慢。给出三种不同原理的方法让它变快（分别基于浓度、温度、催化剂），并各用一句碰撞理论的话解释。A reaction is very slow at room temperature. Give three methods based on different principles (concentration, temperature, catalyst) to speed it up, each with a one-sentence collision-theory explanation.

点开看答案Show answer
① 浓度：增大某反应物浓度 → 单位体积粒子更多 → 碰撞更频繁 → 有效碰撞更多。
② 温度：升高温度 → 动能增大、越过 Ea 的比例上升 → 有效碰撞更多。
③ 催化剂：加入合适催化剂 → 提供活化能更低的路径 → 更多粒子够格 → 有效碰撞更多。三种方法都归结为「有效碰撞频率升高」。 ① concentration: raise the concentration of a reactant → more particles per unit volume → more collisions → more effective collisions.
② temperature: increase the temperature → higher kinetic energy and a larger fraction exceed Ea → more effective collisions.
③ catalyst: add a suitable catalyst → a lower-activation-energy pathway → more particles qualify → more effective collisions. All three boil down to "a higher frequency of effective collisions".
— 第 5 站完成 —— Stop 5 done —

单元 8 小结Unit 8 summary

① 速率＝浓度变化 ÷ 时间，单位 mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹；测量靠「气体体积、质量减少、比色、pH」四种办法。
② 碰撞理论：要反应必须①碰撞、②方向对、③能量 ≥ 活化能 Ea；凡是能让「有效碰撞」变多的因素，都能加快反应。
③ 温度通过让「越过 Ea 的比例」大幅上升来提速（Maxwell–Boltzmann 曲线右移、尾巴变肥，总面积不变）；催化剂靠降低 Ea 抄近路，本身不消耗、不改变 ΔH；表面积越大，固体接触面越大、碰撞越多。① Rate = change in concentration ÷ time, in mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹; measure it by gas volume, mass loss, colorimetry or pH.
② Collision theory: a reaction needs ① a collision, ② correct orientation and ③ energy ≥ the activation energy Ea; anything that raises the number of effective collisions speeds the reaction up.
③ Temperature speeds things up by sharply raising the fraction that exceeds Ea (the Maxwell–Boltzmann curve shifts right with a fatter tail, its area unchanged); a catalyst takes a lower-Ea shortcut without being used up or changing ΔH; a larger surface area gives solids more contact, hence more collisions.

下一站最重要的一件事：化学不是只问「会不会反应」，还要问「多久能到平衡」。接下来进入无机化学的世界（第 9–12 单元），你会看到这些规律在周期表里一圈一圈地重演。Why the next unit matters: chemistry asks not only "does it react?" but "how fast does it reach equilibrium?". Next come the inorganic units (9–12), where you will see these rules play out again and again across the periodic table.

单元 9 · 周期性与第 3 周期：从左到右有规律Unit 9 · Periodicity and Period 3: patterns left to right

CAIE 9701 Topic 9 · 6 站 · 周期表不是乱排的，从左到右有规律CAIE 9701 Topic 9 · 6 stops · the periodic table is not random — trends run left to right

路线图本单元六站，把「规律」两个字刻进脑子里Six stops that drill the word "trend" into your head

  2. 原子半径与电离能的趋势Atomic radius and ionisation energy trends
  3. 第 3 周期元素与水、氧、氯Period 3 reactions with water, oxygen and chlorine
  4. 第 3 周期氯化物的水解Hydrolysis of period 3 chlorides
  5. 熔点趋势：先升到 Si 再骤降Melting-point trend: rise to Si, then crash

建议：把第 2 站和第 6 站当「双子站」一起记——半径、电离能、电负性背后其实是同一个原因。Tip: treat stops 2 and 6 as twins — radius, ionisation energy and electronegativity all share one cause.

1 周期表的结构：周期、族与分区Structure of the table: periods, groups, blocks Period & group周期与族
这一站要你会：分清 period 与 group，说出「同周期」和「同族」各有什么共同点，并能指出 s 区 / p 区 / d 区。Goal: tell period from group, state what elements in the same period or group share, and point out the s, p and d blocks.
把周期表想成一座宿舍楼：横着看，同一排（周期）的同学住在同一层楼——他们最外层电子所在的层数一样；竖着看，同一列（族）的同学家里有一样多的「外窗」——最外层电子数一样。化学性质主要看最外层电子，所以同一族的人脾气特别像。Think of it as a hall of residence: read across and everyone in the same row (period) lives on the same floor — the shell holding their outer electrons is the same. Read down and everyone in a column (group) has the same number of "outer windows" — the same number of outer electrons. Chemistry is decided by the outer electrons, which is why elements in the same group behave alike.
必须记牢的四件事：Four things to learn:
  • 周期 period＝横排：最外层电子层数相同，周期数＝电子层数。A period is a row: the number of electron shells is the same, and the period number equals the number of shells.
  • 族 group＝竖列：最外层电子数相同（对主族而言，族数＝最外层电子数）。A group is a column: the number of outer electrons is the same (for main groups, the group number equals the outer-electron count).
  • 三个区：s 区（第 1、2 族 + He）、p 区（第 13–18 族）、d 区（过渡金属，从第 4 周期起）。Three blocks: s block (groups 1–2 plus He), p block (groups 13–18), d block (transition metals, from period 4).
  • 金属 / 非金属分界：左下方是金属，右上方是非金属，中间斜线（B、Si、Ge、As、Sb、Te）是半金属。The metal–non-metal divide: metals sit lower-left, non-metals upper-right, and a diagonal of metalloids (B, Si, Ge, As, Sb, Te) runs between them.
最快的判断题：主族元素的族数＝最外层电子数。Na 最外层 1 个 → 第 1 族；Cl 最外层 7 个 → 第 17 族。但这条不适用于 d 区的过渡金属。The fastest check: for main-group elements, group number = number of outer electrons. Na has 1 → Group 1; Cl has 7 → Group 17. But this does not work for the d-block transition metals.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: Elements in the same period have the same number of electron shells. Elements in the same group have the same number of outer electrons, so they have similar chemical properties.
例题Example
某元素原子有 3 个电子层，最外层有 5 个电子。(a) 它位于第几周期、第几族？(b) 它是什么元素？(c) 它在哪个区？An atom has 3 electron shells and 5 outer electrons. (a) Which period and group is it in? (b) Which element? (c) Which block?
① 3 个电子层 → 第 3 周期（周期数＝电子层数）。① 3 shells → period 3 (period number = number of shells). ② 最外层 5 个电子 → 第 15 族（VA 族）。② 5 outer electrons → Group 15. ③ 第 3 周期第 15 族 → 磷 P，位于 p 区。③ period 3, group 15 → phosphorus, P, in the p block.
练习Practice
先看电子层数，再看最外层电子数。Count the shells first, then the outer electrons.

某元素在周期表第 2 周期、第 16 族。(a) 它的电子层数和最外层电子数各是多少？(b) 它是什么元素？(c) 它在哪个区？An element is in period 2, group 16. (a) How many shells and outer electrons? (b) Which element? (c) Which block?

点开看答案Show answer
(a) 第 2 周期 → 2 个电子层；第 16 族 → 6 个最外层电子。
(b) 氧 O（1s²2s²2p⁴）。
(c) 第 16 族 → p 区。 (a) period 2 → 2 shells; group 16 → 6 outer electrons.
(b) oxygen, O (1s²2s²2p⁴).
(c) group 16 → p block.
— 第 1 站完成 —— Stop 1 done —
2 原子半径与电离能的趋势Atomic radius and ionisation energy trends Atomic radius原子半径
这一站要你会：解释同周期半径为何从左到右减小、同族为何从上到下增大，并说出电离能随半径的变化方向。Goal: explain why radius falls across a period and rises down a group, and state how ionisation energy changes with radius.
把原子核想成一块磁铁，最外层电子是被吸住的小铁屑。同一周期从左到右，磁铁（核电荷）越来越强，可外层那批电子还是同一层，中间挡着的（屏蔽）也差不多——于是吸力越来越大，原子被「攥」得越来越小。吸得越紧，想把最外层电子拽走就越费劲，所以电离能越来越大。Think of the nucleus as a magnet and the outer electrons as iron filings. Across a period the magnet (nuclear charge) grows stronger, yet the outer electrons stay in the same shell with about the same shielding — so the pull grows and the atom is squeezed smaller. The tighter the grip, the harder it is to tear an outer electron away, so the ionisation energy rises.
趋势背后的四个词：Four words behind the trend:
  • 同周期半径↓：核电荷↑、屏蔽相近 → 有效核电荷↑ → 吸引力↑ → 半径↓。Radius falls across a period: nuclear charge ↑, shielding similar → effective nuclear charge ↑ → attraction ↑ → radius ↓.
  • 同族半径↑：从上到下电子层数增多，最外层离核更远。Radius rises down a group: more shells, so the outer electrons sit further from the nucleus.
  • 电离能：半径越小、吸引力越强，越难失电子 → 电离能↑（同周期总体上升）。Ionisation energy: a smaller radius means a stronger grip, so losing an electron is harder → ionisation energy rises across a period.
  • 电负性：同周期从左到右↑，同族从上到下↓（吸引成键电子的能力）。Electronegativity: rises across a period, falls down a group (the power to attract bonding electrons).
解释题必须踩中两个词：「核电荷增大」+「屏蔽相近」。只写「原子变小了」不给分，得说出为什么变小。Explanation questions need two phrases: "nuclear charge increases" and "shielding stays similar". Writing "the atom gets smaller" alone earns nothing — you must say why.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: Across a period, the atomic radius decreases because the nuclear charge increases while shielding stays about the same, so the outer electrons are pulled in more strongly.
例题Example
解释为什么 Mg 的第一电离能比 Na 大。Explain why the first ionisation energy of magnesium is greater than that of sodium.
① Mg 的核电荷（12）比 Na（11）大。① Mg has a higher nuclear charge (12) than Na (11). ② 两者最外层电子受的屏蔽相近。② Their outer electrons experience similar shielding. ③ 所以 Mg 对最外层电子的吸引力更强、半径更小 → 更难失电子 → 电离能更大。③ So Mg pulls its outer electrons harder and is smaller → harder to ionise → higher ionisation energy.
练习Practice
Na 和 K 在同一族，先想「层数」的差别。Na and K are in the same group — think about the number of shells first.

比较 Na 与 K：谁的原子半径更大？谁的第一电离能更大？各给一句话理由。Compare Na and K: which has the larger radius? Which has the larger first ionisation energy? Give a reason for each.

点开看答案Show answer
K 半径更大：它比 Na 多一个电子层，最外层离核更远。
Na 电离能更大：Na 的最外层离核更近、被吸得更紧，更不容易失去。 K is larger: it has one more shell than Na, so its outer electrons are further from the nucleus.
Na has the higher ionisation energy: its outer electron is closer to the nucleus and held more tightly.
— 第 2 站完成 —— Stop 2 done —
3 第 3 周期元素与水、氧、氯Period 3 reactions with water, oxygen and chlorine Period 3 reactions第 3 周期反应
这一站要你会：写出 Na、Mg 与水、Mg、Al 与盐酸的反应，并按「碱性→两性→酸性」给六种氧化物排好队。Goal: write the reactions of Na and Mg with water and Mg and Al with acid, and sort the six oxides from basic to acidic.
这一站是第 3 周期的「现场实验」：左边两个金属（Na、Mg）跟水较劲——Na 是暴脾气，一沾冷水就剧烈反应；Mg 是慢热型，冷水不理你，得用热水或蒸汽才肯反应。跟酸打交道时，Mg 和 Al 都放氢气，但 Al 表面有层氧化膜，得先磨掉才开始。至于它们烧出来的氧化物，口味从左到右一路从「碱性」变到「酸性」。This stop is period 3 "in the lab": the two left-hand metals take on water — Na is hot-tempered and reacts violently with cold water, while Mg is slow to warm up, ignoring cold water and needing hot water or steam. With acid, both Mg and Al release hydrogen, but Al wears an oxide coat that must be removed first. And their oxides change taste from basic to acidic as you move right.
先记反应，再记规律：Learn the reactions, then the pattern:
2Na(s) + 2H2O(l) → 2NaOH(aq) + H2(g) Mg(s) + 2H2O(g) → MgO(s) + H2(g) Mg(s) + 2HCl(aq) → MgCl2(aq) + H2(g) 2Al(s) + 6HCl(aq) → 2AlCl3(aq) + 3H2(g)
  • Na 与水剧烈反应，浮在水面游动、冒氢气；Mg 与水要热水或蒸汽才反应。Na + water reacts violently, fizzing on the surface with hydrogen; Mg + water needs hot water or steam.
  • Mg 与 Al 都跟盐酸放出 H2，但 Mg 更快——Al 表面的氧化膜先要跟酸反应掉。Both Mg and Al release H2 with dilute acid, but Mg is faster — Al's oxide layer must dissolve first.
  • 氧化物递变：Na₂O、MgO 碱性 → Al₂O₃ 两性 → SiO₂、P₄O₁₀、SO₃ 酸性。Oxide trend: Na₂O and MgO basic → Al₂O₃ amphoteric → SiO₂, P₄O₁₀ and SO₃ acidic.
  • 两性 Al₂O₃：既能跟酸、也能跟碱反应。Amphoteric Al₂O₃ reacts with both acids and alkalis.
别把「两性」当成「中性」：两性＝既能跟酸又能跟碱反应；中性＝既不是酸也不是碱（比如 NaCl 溶液）。这两个是两码事。Don't confuse "amphoteric" with "neutral": amphoteric means it reacts with both acid and alkali; neutral means neither acidic nor basic (like NaCl solution). They are different ideas.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: Sodium reacts vigorously with cold water, forming sodium hydroxide and hydrogen. Across period 3, the oxides change from basic (Na₂O, MgO) through amphoteric (Al₂O₃) to acidic (SiO₂, P₄O₁₀, SO₃).
例题Example
判断 MgO 与 SO₃ 的酸碱性，并分别写出它们与水反应的方程式。State the acid–base nature of MgO and SO₃, and write the equation of each with water.
① MgO 是碱性氧化物，与水反应生成碱：① MgO is a basic oxide; with water it forms an alkali:
MgO(s) + H2O(l) → Mg(OH)2(s)
② SO₃ 是酸性氧化物，与水反应生成强酸：② SO₃ is an acidic oxide; with water it forms a strong acid:
SO3(g) + H2O(l) → H2SO4(aq)
练习Practice
Al₂O₃ 要写两个方程式：一个跟酸、一个跟碱。Al₂O₃ needs two equations: one with acid, one with alkali.

把 Na₂O、Al₂O₃、P₄O₁₀ 按「碱性→两性→酸性」分类，并写出 Al₂O₃ 表现两性时的两个方程式（分别与盐酸、与 NaOH 溶液）。Classify Na₂O, Al₂O₃ and P₄O₁₀ as basic, amphoteric or acidic, and write the two equations showing Al₂O₃ is amphoteric (with HCl and with NaOH).

点开看答案Show answer
分类：Na₂O 碱性、Al₂O₃ 两性、P₄O₁₀ 酸性。
与酸：Al₂O₃ + 6HCl → 2AlCl₃ + 3H₂O。
与碱：Al₂O₃ + 2NaOH + 3H₂O → 2NaAl(OH)₄。 Classification: Na₂O basic, Al₂O₃ amphoteric, P₄O₁₀ acidic.
With acid: Al₂O₃ + 6HCl → 2AlCl₃ + 3H₂O.
With alkali: Al₂O₃ + 2NaOH + 3H₂O → 2NaAl(OH)₄.
— 第 3 站完成 —— Stop 3 done —
4 第 3 周期氯化物的水解Hydrolysis of period 3 chlorides Chloride hydrolysis氯化物水解
这一站要你会：判断第 3 周期氯化物遇水后溶液显酸性还是中性，并写出 SiCl₄、PCl₅ 的水解方程式。Goal: predict whether a period 3 chloride gives an acidic or neutral solution, and write the hydrolysis equations for SiCl₄ and PCl₅.
把氯化物想成性格不同的几个人掉进水里：NaCl、MgCl₂ 是老实人，溶进去就安静待着，水还是中性；AlCl₃ 有点「酸」，一沾水就和水反应，把水搅酸了；而 SiCl₄、PCl₅ 是暴脾气，一碰水就剧烈反应，呛出一股 HCl 白雾。Picture the chlorides as people with different tempers jumping into water: NaCl and MgCl₂ are quiet, dissolve and leave the water neutral; AlCl₃ is a bit "sour" and reacts with water, turning it acidic; SiCl₄ and PCl₅ have a short fuse, react violently and puff out white HCl fumes.
按「遇水的脾气」分成三档：Three grades, by how they behave in water:
  • NaCl、MgCl₂：溶解但不水解，溶液中性。NaCl and MgCl₂: dissolve without hydrolysing — neutral solution.
  • AlCl₃：水解显酸性（Al³⁺ 夺走了水里的 OH⁻）。AlCl₃: hydrolyses to an acidic solution (Al³⁺ grabs OH⁻ from water).
  • SiCl₄、PCl₅：遇水剧烈水解，产生 HCl 白雾：SiCl₄ and PCl₅: violent hydrolysis, giving HCl fumes:
SiCl4(l) + 2H2O(l) → SiO2(s) + 4HCl(g) PCl5(s) + 4H2O(l) → H3PO4(aq) + 5HCl(g)
「白雾」不是「烟」：它是 HCl 气体遇到空气中的水汽，凝成的小液滴。描述现象时写「white fumes」才给分，写「smoke」会丢分。"Fumes" are not "smoke": they are tiny droplets formed when HCl gas meets moisture in the air. Write "white fumes", not "smoke", to earn the mark.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: SiCl₄ and PCl₅ react violently with water, forming white fumes of hydrogen chloride gas. AlCl₃ dissolves to give an acidic solution, while NaCl and MgCl₂ simply dissolve to give neutral solutions.
例题Example
写出 SiCl₄ 与水反应的方程式，并描述观察到的现象。Write the equation for the reaction of SiCl₄ with water and describe what you observe.
① 方程式：① Equation:
SiCl4(l) + 2H2O(l) → SiO2(s) + 4HCl(g)
② 现象：剧烈反应，产生 HCl 白雾——因为 HCl 气体与空气里的水汽结合成小液滴。② Observation: a violent reaction producing white fumes of HCl, because the HCl gas condenses with moisture into tiny droplets.
练习Practice
PCl₅ 里磷的化合价是 +5，水解产物是磷酸。In PCl₅, phosphorus is +5, so the product is phosphoric acid.

写出 PCl₅ 与水反应的方程式，并说明 PCl₅ 的水解与 NaCl 溶于水有什么不同。Write the equation for the reaction of PCl₅ with water, and explain how this differs from NaCl dissolving in water.

点开看答案Show answer
PCl₅ + 4H₂O → H₃PO₄ + 5HCl。
不同：PCl₅ 遇水发生化学变化（水解），放出 HCl 白雾并生成磷酸；NaCl 只是物理溶解，不水解，溶液中性。 PCl₅ + 4H₂O → H₃PO₄ + 5HCl.
Difference: PCl₅ undergoes a chemical change (hydrolysis), releasing HCl fumes and forming phosphoric acid; NaCl only dissolves physically without hydrolysing, so its solution is neutral.
— 第 4 站完成 —— Stop 4 done —
5 熔点趋势：先升到 Si 再骤降Melting-point trend: rise to Si, then crash Melting point trend熔点趋势
这一站要你会：解释第 3 周期熔点「先升到 Si 再骤降」的原因，并能比较任意两个相邻元素的熔点。Goal: explain why period 3 melting points rise to Si then crash, and compare any two neighbouring elements.
把第 3 周期想成一条街：左边几家（Na、Mg、Al）是「大金属」，越靠右价电子越多、金属键越结实，熔点一路走高；走到 Si，变成一座整块金刚石式的大厦（巨型共价），熔点冲到最高；再往右 P、S、Cl，变成一个个独立的小分子家庭，彼此只靠弱弱的分子间力拉着，熔点一落千丈。Think of period 3 as a street: the left-hand houses (Na, Mg, Al) are "big metals" — as you move right, more valence electrons make the metallic bonding stronger and melting points climb. At Si you hit a diamond-like tower (giant covalent) and the melting point peaks. Beyond it, P, S and Cl are separate little molecular households held only by weak intermolecular forces, so melting points crash.
分三段看这条折线：Read the line in three sections:
  • Na → Al 上升：金属键越来越强（价电子↑、离子电荷↑、半径↓）。Na → Al rises: metallic bonding strengthens (more valence electrons, higher ionic charge, smaller radius).
  • Si 是顶峰：巨型共价结构，Si–Si 共价键非常强（熔点 1414 °C）。Si is the peak: a giant covalent structure with very strong Si–Si bonds (melting point 1414 °C).
  • P、S、Cl 骤降：简单分子，只靠弱的范德华力 → 熔点很低。P, S, Cl crash: simple molecules held only by weak van der Waals forces → low melting points.
  • 比较熔点的套路：先问「它是什么晶体类型」，再比键的强弱。The routine: first ask "what structure type is it?", then compare bond strength.
别用「金属键强」去解释 P/S/Cl——它们根本没有金属键。先把晶体类型分对，再解释。Don't explain P, S or Cl with "strong metallic bonding" — they have no metallic bonding at all. Sort out the structure type first, then explain.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: The melting point rises from sodium to silicon because the metallic bonding strengthens, and silicon has a giant covalent structure. It then drops sharply for phosphorus, sulfur and chlorine, which are simple molecular substances held only by weak intermolecular forces.
例题Example
解释为什么 Si 的熔点远高于 Al，而 P 的熔点远低于 Al。Explain why silicon melts far higher than aluminium, yet phosphorus melts far lower.
① Si 是巨型共价结构，熔化要打断大量强共价键 → 熔点极高。① Si is giant covalent; melting means breaking many strong covalent bonds → very high melting point. ② Al 是金属，金属键虽强，但仍弱于 Si 的共价键。② Al is a metal; its metallic bonds are strong but still weaker than Si's covalent bonds. ③ P 是简单分子（P₄），分子间只有弱的范德华力 → 熔点很低。③ P is simple molecular (P₄), with only weak van der Waals forces between molecules → very low melting point.
练习Practice
S 和 Mg 的晶体类型完全不同。S and Mg have completely different structure types.

第 3 周期元素 Na、Mg、Al、Si、P、S 中：(a) 熔点最高的是谁？(b) 解释 S 的熔点为什么比 Mg 低。Among Na, Mg, Al, Si, P and S: (a) which has the highest melting point? (b) explain why sulfur melts lower than magnesium.

点开看答案Show answer
(a) Si（巨型共价，熔点 1414 °C）。
(b) S 是简单分子（S₈），靠弱的范德华力；Mg 是金属，靠金属键。金属键远强于范德华力，所以 Mg 熔点更高。 (a) Si (giant covalent, 1414 °C).
(b) S is simple molecular (S₈), held by weak van der Waals forces; Mg is a metal held by metallic bonds. Metallic bonding is far stronger, so Mg melts higher.
