6 半径、电离能、电负性一起复习Radius, ionisation energy and electronegativity together Trend review趋势复习
这一站要你会：从「核电荷增大 + 屏蔽相近」这一个原因出发，一口气解释半径、电离能、电负性三条趋势。Goal: start from one cause — higher nuclear charge with similar shielding — and explain all three trends at once.
这三条趋势其实是同一个故事的三张照片。故事就一句话：从左到右，原子核的「正电荷」越来越大，而最外层那层电子受到的「遮挡」（屏蔽）几乎不变——于是核把外层电子越吸越紧。吸得紧 → 半径变小；吸得紧 → 更难拽走 → 电离能变大；吸得紧 → 更容易抢别人的电子 → 电负性变大。记住这一句，三道解释题都不用背。These three trends are three photos of one story. The story is one sentence: left to right, the positive charge on the nucleus grows while the shielding felt by the outer electrons barely changes — so the nucleus grips the outer electrons ever tighter. Tighter grip → smaller radius; tighter grip → harder to pull away → higher ionisation energy; tighter grip → better at grabbing shared electrons → higher electronegativity. Remember the sentence and three explanation questions answer themselves.
一个原因，三条结论：One cause, three conclusions:
  • 共同原因：同周期核电荷↑、屏蔽相近 → 有效核电荷↑。The shared cause: across a period, nuclear charge ↑ with similar shielding → effective nuclear charge ↑.
  • 半径↓：电子被拉得更近。Radius ↓: electrons are pulled closer in.
  • 电离能总体↑：越难失去电子（Mg→Al、P→S 两处因亚层排布有轻微回落的小坑）。Ionisation energy generally ↑: electrons are harder to remove (with small dips at Mg→Al and P→S from sub-shell arrangement).
  • 电负性↑：吸引成键电子的能力变强（稀有气体除外）。Electronegativity ↑: stronger pull on bonding electrons (noble gases excepted).
两个「小坑」要能说一句：Mg→Al 是 Al 的电子进到能量略高的 3p；P→S 是 S 的 3p 有电子配对，配对电子互相排斥、更容易失去。所以电离能不是一路直线向上。The two "dips" in one line each: Mg→Al because Al's new electron enters the slightly higher-energy 3p; P→S because S has a paired electron in 3p, and paired electrons repel, making one easier to remove. So ionisation energy does not rise in a straight line.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: Across a period, the nuclear charge increases while shielding stays similar, so the effective nuclear charge rises. This makes the atoms smaller, harder to ionise and more electronegative.
例题Example
用「有效核电荷」解释：为什么同周期从左到右电负性增大。Using effective nuclear charge, explain why electronegativity increases across a period.
① 核电荷↑、屏蔽相近 → 有效核电荷↑。① nuclear charge ↑, shielding similar → effective nuclear charge ↑. ② 核对电子的吸引力↑ → 吸引成键电子的能力（电负性）↑。② The nucleus attracts electrons more strongly → its pull on bonding electrons (electronegativity) ↑.
练习Practice
Ar 是最外层已满的稀有气体。Ar is a noble gas with a full outer shell.

(a) 第 3 周期中，为什么 Ar 一般没有电负性数值？(b) 为什么 Cl 的电负性比 Na 大？(a) Why is argon usually given no electronegativity value? (b) Why is chlorine more electronegative than sodium?

点开看答案Show answer
(a) Ar 是稀有气体，最外层已满、几乎不形成化合物，所以一般不给电负性数值。
(b) Cl 核电荷比 Na 大、屏蔽相近，有效核电荷更大，吸引电子能力更强 → 电负性更大。 (a) Argon is a noble gas with a full outer shell and forms almost no compounds, so it is usually given no value.
(b) Chlorine has a higher nuclear charge than sodium with similar shielding, so its effective nuclear charge and electron-attracting power are greater → higher electronegativity.
— 第 6 站完成 —— Stop 6 done —

单元 9 小结Unit 9 summary

① 周期表有章法：横排周期（电子层相同）、竖列族（最外层电子数相同），主族族数＝最外层电子数。
② 一个原因贯穿全局：同周期核电荷↑、屏蔽相近 → 半径↓、电离能总体↑、电负性↑。
③ 第 3 周期的具体表现：氧化物碱性→两性→酸性；氯化物从「不水解」到「水解显酸」再到「剧烈水解冒 HCl 白雾」；熔点先升到 Si 再骤降。① The table has rules: periods are rows (same shell), groups are columns (same outer-electron count), and for main groups the group number equals the outer electrons.
② One cause runs through everything: across a period, nuclear charge ↑ with similar shielding → radius ↓, ionisation energy generally ↑, electronegativity ↑.
③ Period 3 in action: oxides run basic → amphoteric → acidic; chlorides go from "no hydrolysis" to "acidic hydrolysis" to "violent hydrolysis with HCl fumes"; melting point rises to Si then crashes.

下一站往哪走：既然同一族「脾气像」，那就挑两族重点看——第 2 族的碱土金属，以及第 17 族的卤素，就是单元 10 和单元 11 的主题。Where next: since elements in the same group behave alike, we zoom into two of them — the Group 2 alkaline earth metals and the Group 17 halogens, which are Units 10 and 11.

单元 10 · 第 2 族（碱土金属）：越往下越好欺负Unit 10 · Group 2 (alkaline earth metals): the lower, the more reactive

CAIE 9701 Topic 10 · 5 站 · 一群越来越爱交电子的「软柿子」CAIE 9701 Topic 10 · 5 stops · a family that gives electrons away more and more easily

路线图本单元五站，把第 2 族这五个金属从头到尾摸一遍Five stops, in order — together they cover everything about Group 2

  1. 第 2 族是谁：五个「软柿子」金属Meet Group 2: five reactive metals
  2. 与水和氧气反应：越往下越热闹Reactions with water and oxygen
  3. 氧化物与氢氧化物：碱性往下变强Oxides and hydroxides: more basic down the group
  4. 碳酸盐与硝酸盐：往下越难分解Thermal stability of carbonates and nitrates
  5. 为什么越往下越活泼：三件事串起来Explaining the trends: three ideas joined up

建议：前四站是现象，第五站是「总开关」——弄懂最后一站，前面四站都不用死背。Tip: the first four stops are the observations, the fifth is the master switch — once the last stop clicks, you can stop memorising the first four.

1 第 2 族是谁：五个爱送电子的金属Meet Group 2: the metals that give electrons away Group 2 overview第 2 族总览
这一站要你会：认出 Be、Mg、Ca、Sr、Ba 五个成员，背下「最外层都是 ns²」，并说出 Mg→Ba 的三个趋势（半径↑、第一电离能↓、反应性↑）。Goal: name the five members Be, Mg, Ca, Sr, Ba, state that their outer shell is ns², and give the three trends down the group (radius ↑, first ionisation energy ↓, reactivity ↑).
第 2 族像一家五个兄弟：口袋里都只装两块钱（两个最外层电子），天生就想把钱花出去（变成 2+ 离子）。老大 Be 最小，把钱捂得紧；越往下的兄弟个子越大、手臂越长，那两块钱离身体核心越远，谁都能轻松抢走——所以越往下，他们越「好欺负」、越容易反应。Group 2 is like five brothers: each carries exactly two coins (two outer electrons) and is itching to give them away (becoming a 2+ ion). The smallest, Be, holds his coins tight; going down the family each brother is bigger with longer arms, so the two coins sit further from the core of his body and are easy to snatch — that is why they get more "bulliable" and more reactive going down.
先把成员记熟：Learn the members first:
  • 五个成员：铍 Be、镁 Mg、钙 Ca、锶 Sr、钡 Ba——名字和符号要能对上。The five members: beryllium Be, magnesium Mg, calcium Ca, strontium Sr, barium Ba — match each name to its symbol.
  • 最外层都是 ns²：n 就是周期数。Be 2s²、Mg 3s²、Ca 4s²、Sr 5s²、Ba 6s²。The outer shell is always ns², where n is the period: Be 2s², Mg 3s², Ca 4s², Sr 5s², Ba 6s².
  • 半径 Mg→Ba 增大：电子层一层层叠上去，球自然越来越大。Radius increases from Mg to Ba: each new shell makes the ball bigger.
  • 第一电离能减小：最外层电子离核越来越远、越来越「松」。First ionisation energy decreases: the outer electrons sit further out and are held more loosely.
  • 反应性增强：越容易失去那两个电子，反应就越活泼。Reactivity increases: the easier the two electrons are lost, the more reactive the metal.
小心铍这个「异类」：Be 太小、电荷密度大，氧化物偏共价，很多性质跟其他兄弟不一样。AS 考题最爱单独拎 Be 出来问「为什么它不一样」——先记住「Be 特殊」这个印象，后面遇到不慌。Watch out for beryllium, the odd one out: it is small with high charge density, its oxide is more covalent, and much of its behaviour differs from the rest. Exams love to single out Be — just carry the idea "Be is special" and you won't panic when it appears.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: Group 2 elements each have two electrons in their outermost shell (ns²). Going down the group, atomic radius increases and first ionisation energy decreases, so the elements lose their two outer electrons more easily and become more reactive.
例题Example
写出 Mg 与 Ba 的最外层电子排布，并解释为什么 Ba 的第一电离能比 Mg 低。Write the outer-shell electronic configurations of Mg and Ba, and explain why Ba has a lower first ionisation energy than Mg.
① Mg 是第 3 周期，最外层 3s²；Ba 是第 6 周期，最外层 6s²。① Mg is in period 3, so its outer shell is 3s²; Ba is in period 6, so 6s². ② Ba 的外层电子在第 6 层，离核远得多，中间还隔着更多层电子在「屏蔽」。② Ba's outer electrons sit in the sixth shell, much further from the nucleus, with more inner shells shielding them. ③ 核对最外层电子的吸引力变弱，所以 Ba 更容易失去电子，第一电离能更低。③ The nucleus pulls less strongly on the outer electrons, so Ba loses them more easily and its first ionisation energy is lower.
练习Practice
先看周期数写 ns²，再顺着「半径 → 电离能」的思路推。Use the period to write ns², then argue along radius → ionisation energy.

(a) 写出 Ca（原子序 20）的最外层电子排布。(b) 把 Mg、Ca、Sr 按第一电离能从高到低排序。(c) 预测它们三个里谁与水反应最剧烈。(a) Write the outer-shell configuration of Ca (atomic number 20). (b) Order Mg, Ca, Sr from highest to lowest first ionisation energy. (c) Predict which of the three reacts most vigorously with water.

点开看答案Show answer
(a) Ca 是第 4 周期 → 最外层 4s²（完整写 [Ar] 4s²）。
(b) 半径越大电离能越低：Mg > Ca > Sr。
(c) Sr 最剧烈——它最大，外层电子最容易失去。 (a) Ca is in period 4, so its outer shell is 4s² (in full, [Ar] 4s²).
(b) Bigger radius means lower ionisation energy: Mg > Ca > Sr.
(c) Sr is the most vigorous — it is the biggest, so it loses its outer electrons most easily.
— 第 1 站完成 —— Stop 1 done —
2 与水和氧气反应：越往下越热闹Reactions with water and oxygen Water & oxygen水与氧气
这一站要你会：写出 Mg 与冷水/蒸汽、Ca/Sr/Ba 与冷水的反应方程式，说出「越往下越剧烈」的趋势，并记住它们与氧气都生成氧化物。Goal: write equations for Mg with cold water/steam and Ca/Sr/Ba with cold water, state that the reaction grows more vigorous down the group, and remember they all form oxides with oxygen.
把「与水反应」想成往水里丢一块金属。镁像温水煮青蛙：丢进冷水半天冒几个泡，可一遇到滚烫的蒸汽就「噌」地反应起来；钙、锶、钡则是急性子，一沾冷水就咕嘟咕嘟猛冒氢气，钡甚至热到能点燃自己刚冒出来的氢气。越往下，这锅水被搅得越热闹。Think of it as dropping metal into water. Magnesium is a slow boil: a few bubbles in cold water, but hit it with hot steam and it reacts at once. Calcium, strontium and barium are hotheads: the moment they touch cold water they fizz and pour out hydrogen — barium even gets hot enough to ignite the hydrogen it just made. The lower you go, the wilder the pot gets.
要背的几条反应：The reactions to learn:
  • Ca/Sr/Ba 与冷水（剧烈）：Ca/Sr/Ba with cold water (vigorous):
    X(s) + 2H2O(l) → X(OH)2(aq) + H2(g)
  • Mg 与冷水（很慢）：Mg with cold water (very slow):
    Mg(s) + 2H2O(l) → Mg(OH)2(aq) + H2(g)
  • Mg 与蒸汽（很快）——生成的是氧化物，不是氢氧化物：Mg with steam (fast) — this gives the oxide, not the hydroxide:
    Mg(s) + H2O(g) → MgO(s) + H2(g)
  • 与氧气都生成氧化物；Ba 在充足氧气下还能生成过氧化物 BaO₂：With oxygen they all form oxides; with plenty of oxygen barium can form the peroxide BaO₂:
    2Mg(s) + O2(g) → 2MgO(s) Ba(s) + O2(g) → BaO2(s)
别把 Mg 的两条反应搞混：冷水 → Mg(OH)2，蒸汽 → MgO。记法：蒸汽条件更「狠」、更干，直接把氢氧根里的水也「烤」掉了，所以只剩下 MgO。Don't mix up magnesium's two reactions: cold water → Mg(OH)2, steam → MgO. Memory hook: steam is the harsher, drier condition, so it bakes the water right out of the hydroxide and leaves only MgO.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: Going down Group 2, the metals react more vigorously with water. Calcium, strontium and barium react with cold water to form the metal hydroxide and hydrogen gas: X + 2H₂O → X(OH)₂ + H₂.
例题Example
写出钙与冷水反应的配平方程式，并描述能观察到的现象。Write a balanced equation for calcium with cold water, and describe what you would observe.
① 钙是第 2 族，丢两个电子，跟水里的两个 H⁺ 交换，生成氢氧化物和氢气。① Calcium is in Group 2, so it loses two electrons and swaps them for two H⁺ from water, giving a hydroxide and hydrogen.
Ca(s) + 2H2O(l) → Ca(OH)2(aq) + H2(g)
② 现象：金属变小、溶解，冒出无色气泡（氢气）；因为 Ca(OH)2 微溶，溶液会变浑浊、显碱性。② Observations: the metal shrinks and dissolves, colourless bubbles form (hydrogen); since Ca(OH)2 is only slightly soluble, the solution turns cloudy and is alkaline.
练习Practice
第 2 族都丢 2 个电子；配平时先数氢氧根，再数氢。Group 2 metals all lose 2 electrons; balance the hydroxide first, then the hydrogens.

(a) 写出镁与蒸汽反应的方程式。(b) 写出钡与冷水反应的方程式。(c) 为什么钡的反应比镁剧烈得多？(a) Write the equation for magnesium with steam. (b) Write the equation for barium with cold water. (c) Why is barium's reaction much more vigorous than magnesium's?

点开看答案Show answer
(a) Mg + H₂O(g) → MgO + H₂。
(b) Ba + 2H₂O → Ba(OH)₂ + H₂。
(c) 钡的原子半径大得多，外层电子离核远、屏蔽多、更容易失去，所以反应更快更剧烈。 (a) Mg + H₂O(g) → MgO + H₂.
(b) Ba + 2H₂O → Ba(OH)₂ + H₂.
(c) Barium has a much larger radius, so its outer electrons are further from the nucleus, more shielded and easier to lose — the reaction is faster and more vigorous.
— 第 2 站完成 —— Stop 2 done —
3 氧化物与氢氧化物：碱性往下变强Oxides and hydroxides: more basic down the group Oxides & hydroxides氧化物与氢氧化物
这一站要你会：说出第 2 族氧化物都是碱性氧化物，写出 CaO 与水变成 Ca(OH)2 的转化，并用「溶解度」解释为什么越往下氢氧化物碱性越强。Goal: state that Group 2 oxides are all basic, write the CaO + water → Ca(OH)2 conversion, and use "solubility" to explain why the hydroxides get more basic down the group.
这些氧化物都是碱性氧化物，遇水就变成对应的碱。CaO 俗称生石灰，往上一浇水，「哗」地放热，变成熟石灰 Ca(OH)2——工地的石灰墙、腌皮蛋的石灰水都是它。关键是溶解度：Mg(OH)2 几乎不溶，碱性很弱；Ba(OH)2 溶解度高得多，水里 OH⁻ 更多，碱性自然更强。These oxides are all basic oxides — add water and they turn into the matching alkali. CaO is quicklime; splash water on it and it heats up into slaked lime Ca(OH)2, used in mortar and limewater. The key is solubility: Mg(OH)2 barely dissolves, so it is only weakly alkaline; Ba(OH)2 dissolves far better, so there are more OH⁻ ions and it is much more basic.
三句话记牢：Three points to learn:
  • 都是碱性氧化物：跟酸反应生成盐和水（碱的通性）。All are basic oxides: they react with acids to give a salt and water.
  • CaO 遇水放热，变成熟石灰：CaO reacts with water, releasing heat, to give slaked lime:
    CaO(s) + H2O(l) → Ca(OH)2(aq)
  • 碱性往下增强：Mg(OH)2 几乎不溶 → Ca(OH)2 微溶（石灰水）→ Ba(OH)2 溶解度高得多，所以碱性更强。Basicity increases down the group: Mg(OH)2 is almost insoluble → Ca(OH)2 is slightly soluble (limewater) → Ba(OH)2 dissolves far better, so it is more basic.
  • 农业用途：撒 Ca(OH)2（熟石灰）或 CaCO3（石灰石）来中和酸性土壤。Use in farming: spread Ca(OH)2 (slaked lime) or CaCO3 (limestone) to neutralise acidic soil.
「碱性更强」不是「氢氧根更多」：是溶解得更多。同样一勺，Ba(OH)2 能溶进水的比 Ca(OH)2 多，水里 OH⁻ 浓度更高，所以碱性强。别写成「Ba(OH)2 本身氢氧根更多」。"More basic" is not "more hydroxide groups": it means more dissolves. The same spoonful of Ba(OH)2 dissolves further than Ca(OH)2, giving a higher OH⁻ concentration, hence a stronger alkali. Don't write "Ba(OH)2 has more hydroxide groups".
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: Group 2 oxides and hydroxides become more basic going down the group because the hydroxides become more soluble, so they release more OH⁻ ions into solution.
例题Example
为什么 Ca(OH)2 的碱性比 Mg(OH)2 强？Why is Ca(OH)2 a stronger alkali than Mg(OH)2?
① 两者都是第 2 族氢氧化物，碱性来自溶进水里的 OH⁻。① Both are Group 2 hydroxides; their alkalinity comes from the OH⁻ that dissolves. ② Ca(OH)2 的溶解度比 Mg(OH)2 大，能放出更多 OH⁻。② Ca(OH)2 is more soluble than Mg(OH)2, so it releases more OH⁻. ③ 溶液里 OH⁻ 浓度更高 → 碱性更强。③ A higher OH⁻ concentration → a stronger alkali.
练习Practice
抓「溶解度」这个词；农业题记得两种料（熟石灰和石灰石）。Grab the word "solubility"; for the farming question remember both materials (slaked lime and limestone).

(a) 写出生石灰与水反应的方程式。(b) 农民用哪种第 2 族化合物来中和酸性土壤？(c) 为什么 Ba(OH)2 的碱性比 Ca(OH)2 强？(a) Write the equation for quicklime with water. (b) Which Group 2 compound do farmers use to neutralise acidic soil? (c) Why is Ba(OH)2 a stronger alkali than Ca(OH)2?

点开看答案Show answer
(a) CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂。
(b) Ca(OH)₂（熟石灰）或 CaCO₃（石灰石）都可以，最常见的是撒熟石灰或石灰石粉。
(c) Ba(OH)₂ 溶解度更大，溶出更多 OH⁻，所以碱性更强。 (a) CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂.
(b) Ca(OH)₂ (slaked lime) or CaCO₃ (limestone); slaked lime or powdered limestone is most common.
(c) Ba(OH)₂ is more soluble, so it releases more OH⁻ and is a stronger alkali.
— 第 3 站完成 —— Stop 3 done —
4 碳酸盐与硝酸盐：往下越难分解Thermal stability of carbonates and nitrates Thermal decomposition热分解
这一站要你会：说出「越往下热稳定性越高」的趋势，用「电荷密度 / 极化」解释原因，并写出碳酸盐、硝酸盐的分解方程式。Goal: state that thermal stability increases down the group, explain it using charge density / polarisation, and write the decomposition equations for carbonates and nitrates.
把碳酸盐想成一个硬壳，里面裹着 CO₂。小个子阳离子（Be²⁺、Mg²⁺）电荷密度大，像一个又小又凶的拳头，狠狠把旁边的碳酸根「拽歪」（这就是极化），让 CO₂ 很容易被挤出来，所以一加热就分解；大个子（Ba²⁺）拳头软、还离得远，碳酸根稳稳当当，得用猛火猛烤才肯交出 CO₂。Think of a carbonate as a shell wrapped around some CO₂. A small cation (Be²⁺, Mg²⁺) has high charge density — a small, fierce fist — that yanks the carbonate ion out of shape (polarises it), so the CO₂ pops out easily on gentle heating. A big cation (Ba²⁺) has a soft fist held far away, so the carbonate stays comfortable and needs a serious roast before it gives up its CO₂.
两条分解 + 一条趋势：Two decompositions + one trend:
  • 碳酸盐分解（越往下温度越高）：Carbonates decompose (higher temperature going down):
    XCO3(s) → XO(s) + CO2(g)
  • CaCO₃ 煅烧就是工业上制生石灰的办法：Heating CaCO₃ is how industry makes quicklime:
    CaCO3(s) → CaO(s) + CO2(g)
  • 硝酸盐分解，一定放出红棕色 NO₂ 和助燃的 O₂：Nitrates decompose, always giving brown NO₂ and O₂:
    2X(NO3)2(s) → 2XO(s) + 4NO2(g) + O2(g)
  • 趋势：BeCO₃ 易分解 < MgCO₃ < CaCO₃ < SrCO₃ < BaCO₃（最难）。原因：阳离子电荷密度↓ → 极化能力↓ → 化合物更稳定。Trend: BeCO₃ decomposes easily < MgCO₃ < CaCO₃ < SrCO₃ < BaCO₃ (hardest). Reason: charge density of the cation ↓ → polarising power ↓ → the compound is more stable.
硝酸盐分解必出两个气体：红棕色的 NO₂ 和让带火星木条复燃的 O₂。别漏配平——2 份硝酸盐给 4 份 NO₂ + 1 份 O₂，这个「2 : 4 : 1」要背下来。Nitrate decomposition always gives two gases: brown NO₂ and O₂, which relights a glowing splint. Don't mess up the balancing — two nitrates give four NO₂ plus one O₂; learn this "2 : 4 : 1" ratio.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: Thermal stability of the carbonates increases down the group because the cation gets larger, so its charge density and polarising power decrease; it distorts the carbonate ion less, and the compound is harder to decompose.
例题Example
写出 CaCO₃ 受热分解的方程式，并比较 MgCO₃ 和 BaCO₃ 哪个更容易分解、为什么。Write the equation for the thermal decomposition of CaCO₃, and state which of MgCO₃ and BaCO₃ decomposes more easily, with a reason.
① 碳酸钙分解：① Calcium carbonate decomposes:
CaCO3(s) → CaO(s) + CO2(g)
② MgCO₃ 更容易分解：Mg²⁺ 比 Ba²⁺ 小得多，电荷密度大。② MgCO₃ decomposes more easily: Mg²⁺ is much smaller than Ba²⁺, so its charge density is higher. ③ 极化能力更强，把碳酸根拽得更歪，CO₂ 更容易出来；BaCO₃ 需要高得多的能量。③ Its polarising power is stronger, so it distorts the carbonate ion more and CO₂ escapes more easily; BaCO₃ needs far more energy.
练习Practice
配平硝酸盐记住「2 : 4 : 1」；比较题答「电荷密度 + 极化」两个词。Balance the nitrate with "2 : 4 : 1"; for the comparison, use the words "charge density" and "polarisation".

(a) 写出硝酸钙热分解的方程式。(b) 把 BeCO₃、CaCO₃、BaCO₃ 按「最容易分解到最难」排序。(c) 一句话解释为什么 BaCO₃ 最难分解。(a) Write the equation for the thermal decomposition of calcium nitrate. (b) Order BeCO₃, CaCO₃ and BaCO₃ from easiest to hardest to decompose. (c) In one sentence, explain why BaCO₃ is the hardest to decompose.

点开看答案Show answer
(a) 2Ca(NO₃)₂ → 2CaO + 4NO₂ + O₂。
(b) 易 → 难：BeCO₃ > CaCO₃ > BaCO₃。
(c) Ba²⁺ 半径大、电荷密度低，极化能力弱，碳酸根稳定，所以需要最高的温度才分解。 (a) 2Ca(NO₃)₂ → 2CaO + 4NO₂ + O₂.
(b) Easiest → hardest: BeCO₃ > CaCO₃ > BaCO₃.
(c) Ba²⁺ is large with low charge density, so its polarising power is weak and the carbonate stays stable — it needs the highest temperature to decompose.
— 第 4 站完成 —— Stop 4 done —
5 为什么越往下越活泼：三件事串起来Explaining the trends: three ideas joined up Explaining trends趋势总解
这一站要你会：用「电荷密度、屏蔽效应、晶格能」三个词，把半径、电离能、反应性、氢氧化物碱度、碳酸盐稳定性这几条趋势连成一个完整解释。Goal: use "charge density, shielding, lattice energy" to connect radius, ionisation energy, reactivity, hydroxide basicity and carbonate stability into one coherent explanation.
这一站是「收网」——前面四站讲了五个现象，其实都源于同一件事：原子越往下越大。球大了，外层电子离核远、还被中间层挡着（屏蔽），所以容易丢（电离能低、反应活泼）；丢出来的 2+ 离子也大，电荷密度低、极化弱，所以氢氧化物更容易「泡开」（碱性强）、碳酸盐更结实（难分解）。一条线穿到底，根本不用死背。This stop pulls the net together — the last four stops described five observations, but they all come from one fact: atoms get bigger going down. A bigger ball means the outer electrons are further from the nucleus and shielded by the inner layers, so they are lost easily (low ionisation energy, high reactivity). The 2+ ion it forms is also big, so its charge density is low and it polarises little — the hydroxide dissolves more easily (more basic) and the carbonate stays intact (harder to decompose). One thread runs through it all, so there is nothing to memorise.
把因果链条背下来：Learn the causal chain:
  • 往下：电子层变多 → 半径增大。Going down: more shells → radius increases.
  • 屏蔽增强 + 距离变远 → 外层电子吸引力↓ → 第一电离能↓ → 反应性↑。More shielding + greater distance → weaker pull on outer electrons → first ionisation energy ↓ → reactivity ↑.
  • 2+ 离子越大 → 电荷密度↓ → 极化能力↓。The bigger the 2+ ion → lower charge density → weaker polarising power.
  • 极化弱 → 氢氧化物更易溶（碱性↑）、碳酸盐更稳定（难分解）。Weaker polarisation → the hydroxide dissolves more easily (more basic) and the carbonate is more stable (harder to decompose).
  • 晶格能：离子越大，晶格能越小，越容易溶——这解释了「氢氧化物越往下越溶」。Lattice energy: bigger ions give a smaller lattice energy, so the compound dissolves more easily — this explains why the hydroxides become more soluble down the group.
解释题的三段式：① 半径（谁大谁小）→ ② 电荷密度 / 极化（谁强谁弱）→ ③ 结果（碱度 / 稳定性）。按这个顺序写，踩分点一个不落。The three-step answer for "explain" questions: ① radius (which is bigger) → ② charge density / polarisation (which is stronger) → ③ the result (basicity or stability). Write in this order and you will hit every mark.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: Down Group 2, atomic radius increases and shielding increases, so the outer electrons are less strongly attracted and the elements become more reactive. The larger 2+ ions have lower charge density, so they polarise anions less; this makes the hydroxides more soluble (more basic) and the carbonates more thermally stable.
例题Example
解释为什么 Ba(OH)2 的碱性比 Mg(OH)2 强，而 BaCO₃ 又比 MgCO₃ 更难分解。Explain why Ba(OH)2 is a stronger alkali than Mg(OH)2, yet BaCO₃ is harder to decompose than MgCO₃.
① Ba²⁺ 比 Mg²⁺ 大得多，电荷密度低、极化能力弱。① Ba²⁺ is much larger than Mg²⁺, so its charge density and polarising power are lower. ② 对 OH⁻：Ba(OH)2 更容易在水中解离（溶解度大），OH⁻ 更多 → 碱性强。② For OH⁻: Ba(OH)2 dissolves more readily (higher solubility), giving more OH⁻ → a stronger alkali. ③ 对 CO₃²⁻：Ba²⁺ 把碳酸根拽得不够歪，CO₂ 难逸出 → 热稳定性高、难分解。③ For CO₃²⁻: Ba²⁺ distorts the carbonate ion too little, so CO₂ is hard to release → high thermal stability.
练习Practice
两个问都用「电荷密度 / 极化」当桥梁。Use "charge density / polarisation" as the bridge in both parts.

(a) 解释为什么 Sr 的第一电离能低于 Ca。(b) 解释为什么 Mg(OH)2 碱性比 Sr(OH)2 弱。(c) 预测 MgCO₃ 和 SrCO₃ 哪个热稳定性更高。(a) Explain why Sr has a lower first ionisation energy than Ca. (b) Explain why Mg(OH)2 is a weaker alkali than Sr(OH)2. (c) Predict which of MgCO₃ and SrCO₃ is more thermally stable.

点开看答案Show answer
(a) Sr 半径更大、屏蔽更多，外层电子吸引力弱，更容易失去 → 电离能更低。
(b) Mg²⁺ 小、电荷密度大、极化强，Mg(OH)₂ 更难溶解，OH⁻ 少 → 碱性弱。
(c) SrCO₃ 更稳定（更难分解），因为 Sr²⁺ 更大、极化更弱。 (a) Sr has a larger radius and more shielding, so its outer electrons are held more weakly and lost more easily → lower ionisation energy.
(b) Mg²⁺ is small with high charge density and strong polarising power, so Mg(OH)₂ dissolves less and releases fewer OH⁻ → weaker alkali.
(c) SrCO₃ is more stable (harder to decompose), because Sr²⁺ is larger and polarises less.
— 第 5 站完成 —— Stop 5 done —

单元 10 小结Unit 10 summary

① 第 2 族五个兄弟，最外层都是 ns²：越往下半径越大、电离能越小、反应越活泼。
② 与水反应越往下越剧烈，都放出氢气（Mg 与蒸汽生成 MgO）；与氧气都生成氧化物。
③ 氢氧化物碱性往下增强（溶解度是关键）；碳酸盐 / 硝酸盐热稳定性往下增强（电荷密度 / 极化是关键）。
④ 一切趋势都能用「半径 → 电荷密度 / 极化」一条线串起来，死背不如想明白。① All five Group 2 brothers have an ns² outer shell: going down, radius rises, ionisation energy falls and reactivity rises.
② Reaction with water gets more vigorous going down, always releasing hydrogen (Mg + steam gives MgO); with oxygen they all form oxides.
③ Hydroxide basicity increases down the group (solubility is the key); carbonate / nitrate thermal stability increases down the group (charge density / polarisation is the key).
④ Every trend hangs on one thread — radius → charge density / polarisation. Understand it and you can stop memorising.

下一站最重要的一件事：第 2 族是「送电子」，而第 7 族卤素正好相反——它们是一群抢电子的「狠角色」，这就是单元 11 的主题。Why the next unit matters: Group 2 gives electrons away, while Group 7, the halogens, do the opposite — they are the electron-grabbing tough guys. That is Unit 11.

单元 11 · 第 17 族（卤素）：一群抢电子的「强盗」Unit 11 · Group 17 (the halogens): the electron-grabbing robbers

路线图本单元五站，先认识这群「强盗」的长相，再学它们怎么抢、怎么被抓、怎么用来消毒Five stops — meet the gang, then learn how they steal, how they get caught, and how we use them to disinfect

建议：前两站先把「是谁」和「氧化性顺序」弄熟，后面的检验和用途都会用到。Tip: get stops 1 and 2 solid first — the tests and uses later all lean on them.

1 卤素是谁、物理性质The halogens: who they are and physical properties Group 17 · physical properties第 17 族 · 物理性质
这一站要你会：说出四种卤素的名称、符号、状态与颜色，并解释「为什么越往下沸点越高」。Goal: name the four halogens with their symbols, states and colours, and explain why boiling points rise down the group.
第 17 族是周期表里出了名的抢电子强盗——它们只差一个电子就凑满最外层，所以见谁都想去抢一个。这一家有四个兄弟：氟 F2、氯 Cl2、溴 Br2、碘 I2。从氟到碘，分子一个比一个「块头大」（电子多），彼此之间的色散力也越来越强，像几个人越抱越紧，想把它拆开（沸腾）就要费更大的劲——所以沸点一路往上升。Group 17 is the famous electron-robbing gang of the periodic table — one electron short of a full outer shell, so they grab one from anyone. Four brothers: fluorine F2, chlorine Cl2, bromine Br2, iodine I2. From fluorine to iodine the molecules get bigger (more electrons), so the dispersion forces between them grow stronger — like people holding on tighter and tighter, needing more effort to pull apart (to boil). So the boiling points climb all the way up.
必须记牢的四兄弟：The four brothers to learn:
卤素Halogen符号Formula常温状态State颜色Colour
氟 fluorinefluorineF2气体gas浅黄pale yellow
氯 chlorinechlorineCl2气体gas黄绿yellow-green
溴 brominebromineBr2液体liquid红棕red-brown
碘 iodineiodineI2固体solid紫黑violet-black
  • 沸点：F₂ < Cl₂ < Br₂ < I₂，越往下越高。Boiling point: F₂ < Cl₂ < Br₂ < I₂ — it rises down the group.
  • 原因：分子越大，分子间色散力（dispersion forces）越强，拆开越费劲。Why: bigger molecules have stronger dispersion forces between them, so more energy is needed to pull them apart.
  • 卤素单质都是双原子分子（X2），不是单个原子。Halogen elements are all diatomic molecules (X2), not single atoms.
一个小考点：I2 受热会直接从固体变成紫色蒸气（升华），这个现象后面检验碘时会再见到。A small exam point: I2 turns straight from solid to purple vapour on heating (sublimation) — you will meet this again when testing for iodine.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: Down Group 17 the boiling points increase because the halogen molecules get larger, so the dispersion forces (instantaneous dipole–induced dipole forces) between them become stronger and more energy is needed to overcome them.
例题Example
为什么溴在常温下是液体，而氯是气体？Why is bromine a liquid at room temperature while chlorine is a gas?
① 两者都是双原子分子，但 Br2 比 Cl2 分子更大、电子更多。① both are diatomic, but Br2 is larger with more electrons than Cl2. ② 电子越多，分子间的色散力越强。② more electrons → stronger dispersion forces between molecules. ③ 所以 Br2 需要更高温度才能沸腾 → 常温下是液体，Cl2 是气体。③ so Br2 needs a higher temperature to boil → it is liquid at room temperature, Cl2 is a gas.
练习Practice
先按分子大小排，再用色散力一句话解释。Order by molecule size, then explain in one line with dispersion forces.

把 F2、Cl2、Br2、I2 按沸点从低到高排列，并说明理由。Arrange F2, Cl2, Br2 and I2 in order of increasing boiling point, and give a reason.

点开看答案Show answer
F2 < Cl2 < Br2 < I2。分子越大，分子间色散力越强，克服它所需的能量越多，沸点越高。 F2 < Cl2 < Br2 < I2. Larger molecules have stronger dispersion forces, so more energy is needed to overcome them and the boiling point is higher.
— 第 1 站完成 —— Stop 1 done —
2 氧化性与置换反应Oxidising power and displacement Oxidising power & displacement氧化性与置换
这一站要你会：背出氧化性顺序 F2 > Cl2 > Br2 > I2，会写置换反应方程式，并能根据颜色变化判断生成了什么。Goal: learn the oxidising-power order F2 > Cl2 > Br2 > I2, write displacement equations, and read the colour change to tell what has formed.
氧化性就是抢电子的本事。排在上面的更霸道，能把排在下面的卤离子从它们的盐里「赶走」，自己抢到电子变成卤离子。比如把氯气通进无色的溴化钾溶液，氯把溴离子手里的电子抢过来，溴离子就变成橙色的溴单质——溶液从无色变橙色。Oxidising power is the skill of grabbing electrons. The one higher up is more aggressive and can kick out a lower halide ion from its salt, taking the electron to become a halide itself. Bubble chlorine into colourless potassium bromide solution: chlorine steals the electrons from bromide, which turns into orange bromine — the solution goes from colourless to orange.
三条必须背的：Three things to memorise:
  • 氧化性（得电子能力）：F₂ > Cl₂ > Br₂ > I₂。Oxidising power (ability to gain electrons): F₂ > Cl₂ > Br₂ > I₂.
  • 上层卤素能置换下层卤离子：Cl2 + 2Br− → Br2 + 2Cl−。A higher halogen displaces a lower halide ion: Cl2 + 2Br− → Br2 + 2Cl−.
  • 颜色：Br2 橙色；I2 棕色（水溶液）；卤离子本身无色。Colours: Br2 orange; I2 brown (in aqueous solution); the halide ions themselves are colourless.
答题要点：置换的实质是「抢电子」——Cl2 被还原成 Cl−，Br− 被氧化成 Br2。说清谁被氧化、谁被还原才拿全分。For full marks: displacement is really electron-grabbing — Cl2 is reduced to Cl− while Br− is oxidised to Br2. State clearly which is oxidised and which is reduced.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: Chlorine displaces bromine from potassium bromide because chlorine is a stronger oxidising agent. Chlorine oxidises the bromide ions to bromine, and is itself reduced to chloride ions.
例题Example
把 Cl2 通入 KBr 溶液。(a) 写化学方程式；(b) 观察到的颜色变化；(c) 谁是氧化剂？Chlorine gas is bubbled into KBr solution. (a) Write the equation; (b) describe the colour change; (c) which is the oxidising agent?
① 方程式（离子式）：① equation (ionic):
Cl₂ + 2KBr → 2KCl + Br₂ 离子式：Cl₂ + 2Br⁻ → Br₂ + 2Cl⁻
② 颜色：无色 → 橙色。② colour: colourless → orange. ③ 氧化剂是 Cl2（它得电子，自己被还原）。③ the oxidising agent is Cl2 (it gains electrons and is itself reduced).
练习Practice
套路和 KBr 完全一样，只是卤离子换成 I⁻。Same routine as KBr, just swap the halide for I⁻.

把 Cl2 通入 KI 溶液。(a) 写离子方程式；(b) 颜色变化；(c) 谁是氧化剂？Chlorine gas is bubbled into KI solution. (a) Write the ionic equation; (b) the colour change; (c) which is the oxidising agent?

点开看答案Show answer
(a) Cl2 + 2I− → I2 + 2Cl−。(b) 无色 → 棕色。(c) Cl2。 (a) Cl2 + 2I− → I2 + 2Cl−. (b) colourless → brown. (c) Cl2.
— 第 2 站完成 —— Stop 2 done —
3 卤化氢 HX 的性质与稳定性Hydrogen halides: properties and stability Hydrogen halides HX卤化氢 HX
这一站要你会：知道 HF/HCl/HBr/HI 都是酸性气体，能排出它们的热稳定性顺序并解释原因，说出 HI 受热的现象。Goal: know that HF/HCl/HBr/HI are all acidic gases, rank their thermal stability and explain why, and describe what happens when HI is heated.
HX 就是「氢 + 卤素」搭成的小分子。往下走，卤素原子越来越大，H—X 这根绳子就越来越长——绳子越长越细，越容易剪断。所以热稳定性（受热容不容易分解）是 HI < HBr < HCl < HF。最弱的 HI 一受热就断，分解出的碘蒸气是紫色的，一眼就能认出来。HX is a little molecule made of hydrogen + halogen. Going down, the halogen atom gets bigger, so the H—X rope gets longer — and a longer, thinner rope snaps more easily. So thermal stability (how easily it breaks on heating) goes HI < HBr < HCl < HF. The weakest, HI, breaks apart on heating, and the iodine vapour it makes is purple — you can't miss it.
四句话记住：Remember four points:
  • HX 都是无色、有刺鼻气味的酸性气体，溶于水成酸（HF 是弱酸，其余是强酸）。The HX are all colourless acidic gases with a sharp smell; they dissolve in water to form acids (HF is weak, the rest are strong).
  • 热稳定性：HI < HBr < HCl < HF。Thermal stability: HI < HBr < HCl < HF.
  • 原因：从 F 到 I 原子半径增大，H—X 键长变长，键能变小，越易断。Why: from F to I the atoms get bigger, so the H–X bond lengthens, its bond energy drops, and it breaks more easily.
  • HI 受热：2HI → H2 + I2，出现紫色碘蒸气。Heating HI: 2HI → H2 + I2, giving purple iodine vapour.
别混：「热稳定性」说的是受热分解难易，跟「酸性强弱」是两码事——酸性上 HCl 一挂更强，稳定性上却是 HF 最强。Don't mix them up: thermal stability is about breaking on heating, not acidity — HCl is the stronger acid family, while HF is the most thermally stable.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: Hydrogen iodide is the least thermally stable because the H–I bond is the longest and weakest, so it decomposes on heating to give hydrogen and purple iodine vapour.
例题Example
为什么热稳定性 HF > HCl > HBr > HI？Why is the thermal stability HF > HCl > HBr > HI?
① 从 F 到 I 原子半径增大，H—X 键长变长。① from F to I the atomic radius increases, so the H–X bond lengthens. ② 键长越长，键能越小，键越容易断裂。② a longer bond has a smaller bond energy, so it breaks more easily. ③ 因此受热越容易分解，稳定性越差。③ so it decomposes more readily on heating and is less stable.
练习Practice
套「键长 → 键能 → 稳定性」的链条。Use the chain: bond length → bond energy → stability.

把 HF、HCl、HBr、HI 按热稳定性从强到弱排列，并说明理由。Arrange HF, HCl, HBr and HI in order of decreasing thermal stability, and give a reason.

点开看答案Show answer
HF > HCl > HBr > HI。从 F 到 I 键长变长、键能变小，键越容易断裂，所以受热越容易分解、稳定性越差。 HF > HCl > HBr > HI. From F to I the bond lengthens and its energy drops, so it breaks more easily and the molecule decomposes more readily on heating.
— 第 3 站完成 —— Stop 3 done —
4 卤离子的检验Testing for halide ions AgNO₃ + NH₃ test硝酸银与氨水检验
这一站要你会：会用 AgNO3 + 稀 HNO3 检验卤离子，记住 AgCl/AgBr/AgI 的沉淀颜色，并能用 NH3 进一步区分。Goal: test for halide ions with AgNO3 + dilute HNO3, recall the precipitate colours of AgCl/AgBr/AgI, and use NH3 to tell them apart.
三种卤离子平时都无色，混在一起根本分不出来。给它加「照妖镜」——硝酸银加稀硝酸：氯离子变白色沉淀，溴离子变奶油色，碘离子变黄色。可白和奶油色有时候还是像，再加氨水区分：氯化银一加稀氨水就溶，溴化银要用浓氨水才溶，碘化银怎么都不溶。All three halide ions are colourless in solution, impossible to tell apart. Add the "mirror" — silver nitrate with dilute nitric acid: chloride gives a white precipitate, bromide a cream one, iodide a yellow one. White and cream can still look alike, so add ammonia: silver chloride dissolves in dilute ammonia, silver bromide needs concentrated ammonia, and silver iodide won't dissolve at all.
检验三步：The three-step test:
  • 试剂：AgNO3(aq) + 稀 HNO3（加酸是为了除去碳酸根的干扰）。Reagents: AgNO3(aq) + dilute HNO3 (the acid removes carbonate interference).
  • 颜色：AgCl 白色、AgBr 奶油色、AgI 黄色。Colours: AgCl white, AgBr cream, AgI yellow.
  • 加 NH3：AgCl 溶于稀 NH3；AgBr 仅溶于浓 NH3；AgI 不溶。With NH3: AgCl dissolves in dilute NH3; AgBr only in concentrated NH3; AgI is insoluble.
  • 离子方程：Ag+ + Cl− → AgCl。Ionic equation: Ag+ + Cl− → AgCl.
稀硝酸的用处：除掉 CO32−——不然 Ag2CO3 也是白色沉淀，会跑来捣乱。Why the acid: it removes CO32−, otherwise Ag2CO3 would also give a white precipitate and confuse the test.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: Silver nitrate solution acidified with dilute nitric acid gives a white precipitate with chloride ions, a cream precipitate with bromide ions and a yellow precipitate with iodide ions. Silver chloride dissolves in dilute ammonia, silver bromide only in concentrated ammonia, and silver iodide is insoluble.
例题Example
一种未知溶液加 AgNO3 + 稀 HNO3 后出现奶油色沉淀，再加稀氨水不溶、加浓氨水才溶。它含什么离子？An unknown solution gives a cream precipitate with acidified AgNO3, which does not dissolve in dilute ammonia but dissolves in concentrated ammonia. Which ion is present?
① 奶油色沉淀 → 是 AgBr。① cream precipitate → it is AgBr. ② 稀氨水不溶、浓氨水才溶 → 正好是 AgBr 的特征。② insoluble in dilute NH3 but soluble in concentrated NH3 — the signature of AgBr. ③ 所以溶液里含 Br−。③ so the solution contains Br−.
练习Practice
先靠颜色区分，再靠氨水溶解度收尾。Separate by colour first, then confirm with ammonia solubility.

简述如何区分三瓶分别含 Cl−、Br−、I− 的无色溶液。Describe how to distinguish three colourless solutions containing Cl−, Br− and I−.

点开看答案Show answer
各加 AgNO3 + 稀 HNO3：白色沉淀是 Cl−、奶油色是 Br−、黄色是 I−。若白与奶油色难分，再各加稀氨水：溶的是 AgCl（Cl−），不溶的再加浓氨水才溶的是 AgBr（Br−）。 Add acidified AgNO3 to each: a white precipitate shows Cl−, cream shows Br−, yellow shows I−. If white and cream are hard to tell apart, add dilute ammonia: AgCl (Cl−) dissolves; the one that needs concentrated ammonia to dissolve is AgBr (Br−).
— 第 4 站完成 —— Stop 4 done —
5 氯水、漂白与自来水Chlorine, bleach and tap water Cl₂ + H₂O · bleach氯气与水 · 漂白
这一站要你会：写出 Cl2 与水的歧化反应、与 NaOH 的反应，说明 HClO 是杀菌有效成分，并知道氯气的毒性。Goal: write the disproportionation of Cl2 with water and the reaction with NaOH, explain that HClO is the active disinfectant, and know chlorine's toxicity.
氯气像一位带刺的保镖：它钻进水里，先把自己拆成两半——一半变 Cl−（降了价），一半变 HClO（升了价），这种同一个元素又升又降的反应叫歧化。升价出的次氯酸 HClO 才是真正杀菌的那把刀；游泳池、自来水里那股淡淡的「消毒水味」就是它。但这位保镖本身有毒，浓度高了会伤人，所以要用得恰到好处。Chlorine is a bodyguard with a sting: it slips into water and splits itself in two — one half becomes Cl− (going down in oxidation state), the other becomes HClO (going up). This same-element-up-and-down reaction is called disproportionation. The hypochlorous acid HClO it produces is the real germ-killing blade — that faint "pool smell" in tap and swimming-pool water is it. But the bodyguard is itself toxic at high levels, so it must be dosed just right.
三件事记牢：Three things to remember:
  • 与水歧化：Disproportionation with water:
    Cl₂ + H₂O ⇌ HCl + HClO （Cl 从 0 → −1 和 +1）
  • HClO 是杀菌 / 漂白的有效成分。HClO is the active disinfecting / bleaching agent.
  • 与 NaOH 制漂白剂：Cl2 + 2NaOH → NaCl + NaClO + H2O。With NaOH it makes bleach: Cl2 + 2NaOH → NaCl + NaClO + H2O.
  • 氯气有毒（曾用作化学武器），用于自来水、泳池消毒时要控制用量。Chlorine is toxic (once used as a chemical weapon), so it must be dosed carefully when disinfecting tap or pool water.
写「歧化」的要点：一定要体现同一元素的化合价既升高又降低，两个产物都要写出来。Writing "disproportionation": show the same element going both up and down in oxidation state — write out both products.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: Chlorine reacts with water in a disproportionation reaction to form hydrochloric acid and hypochlorous acid: Cl₂ + H₂O ⇌ HCl + HClO. The hypochlorous acid is the active agent that kills bacteria in treated water.
例题Example
写出 Cl2 与水反应的方程式，标出 Cl 的氧化态变化，并说明为什么这是歧化反应。Write the equation for Cl2 with water, state the oxidation-state changes of chlorine, and explain why it is disproportionation.
① 方程式：Cl2 + H2O ⇌ HCl + HClO。① equation: Cl2 + H2O ⇌ HCl + HClO. ② Cl 的氧化态：0 → −1（HCl 里）和 0 → +1（HClO 里）。② oxidation states: Cl goes 0 → −1 (in HCl) and 0 → +1 (in HClO). ③ 同一元素既升又降 → 歧化。③ the same element is both oxidised and reduced → disproportionation.
练习Practice
NaOH 的反应同样看 Cl 的氧化态 0 → −1 和 +1。For the NaOH reaction, again Cl goes 0 → −1 and +1.

Cl2 与冷的 NaOH 溶液反应。(a) 写方程式；(b) 标出 Cl 的氧化态变化；(c) 产物有什么用途？Cl2 reacts with cold NaOH solution. (a) Write the equation; (b) state the oxidation-state changes of Cl; (c) what is the product used for?

点开看答案Show answer
(a) Cl2 + 2NaOH → NaCl + NaClO + H2O。(b) Cl 从 0 → −1（NaCl）和 0 → +1（NaClO），也是歧化。(c) NaClO 可作消毒剂 / 漂白剂。 (a) Cl2 + 2NaOH → NaCl + NaClO + H2O. (b) Cl goes 0 → −1 (in NaCl) and 0 → +1 (in NaClO) — another disproportionation. (c) NaClO is used as a disinfectant / bleach.
— 第 5 站完成 —— Stop 5 done —

单元 11 小结Unit 11 summary

① 卤素 F2/Cl2/Br2/I2 状态「气气液固」、颜色由浅到深，沸点越往下越高（色散力增强）。
② 氧化性 F2 > Cl2 > Br2 > I2，上层卤素能置换下层卤离子（Cl2 + 2Br− → Br2 + 2Cl−）。
③ HX 热稳定性 HI < HBr < HCl < HF（键长越长越易断），HI 受热出紫色碘。
④ 检验：AgNO3 + 稀 HNO3 出 AgCl 白 / AgBr 奶油 / AgI 黄，再用 NH3 区分。
⑤ 氯气与水歧化生成 HCl + HClO，HClO 杀菌，与 NaOH 制漂白剂。① The halogens F2/Cl2/Br2/I2 go gas, gas, liquid, solid with colours darkening down the group; boiling points rise as the dispersion forces strengthen.
② Oxidising power: F2 > Cl2 > Br2 > I2; a higher halogen displaces a lower halide (Cl2 + 2Br− → Br2 + 2Cl−).
③ Thermal stability: HI < HBr < HCl < HF (longer bonds break more easily); HI gives purple iodine on heating.
④ Test: acidified AgNO3 gives white AgCl, cream AgBr, yellow AgI; NH3 then tells them apart.
⑤ Chlorine disproportionates with water to give HCl + HClO; HClO disinfects, and NaOH makes bleach.

下一站最重要的一件事：卤素只差一个电子就满壳，所以特别爱「抢」；而单元 12 的氮和硫，靠的是氧化态多、反应复杂，套路完全不同。Why the next unit matters: the halogens are one electron short of a full shell, so they love to grab. Unit 12's nitrogen and sulfur play a different game — many oxidation states and more complicated reactions.

单元 12 · 氮与硫：从「懒洋洋的氮气」到化肥和硫酸Unit 12 · Nitrogen and sulfur: from lazy nitrogen to fertiliser and sulfuric acid

路线图本单元五站，先搞懂氮气为什么「懒」，再顺着它去看化肥、酸雨和硫酸是怎么来的Five stops — first understand why nitrogen is so lazy, then follow it to fertiliser, acid rain and sulfuric acid

  1. 氮气为什么那么「懒」Why nitrogen is so lazy
  2. Haber 法造氨The Haber process for ammonia
  3. 氨与铵盐化肥Ammonia and ammonium fertilisers
  4. 氮氧化物与酸雨Oxides of nitrogen and acid rain
  5. 硫、SO₂ 与接触法硫酸Sulfur, sulfur dioxide and sulfuric acid

建议：第 1 站是关键——「氮气为什么难反应」想通了，后面 Haber 法的折中条件、酸雨的成因就都好懂了。Tip: stop 1 is the key — once you see why nitrogen is hard to react, the Haber compromise and the causes of acid rain all make sense.

1 氮气为什么那么「懒」Why nitrogen is so "lazy" N≡N triple bond氮氮三键
这一站要你会：说出氮气为什么常温极不活泼，知道它约占空气 78%，并理解「固氮」为什么是件大事。Goal: explain why nitrogen is so unreactive at room temperature, know it makes up about 78% of the air, and understand why nitrogen fixation matters so much.
把氮分子想成两个手拉手的伙伴：别人只勾一根手指，它俩却三根手指死死扣在一起。想拆散这一对，得用上惊人的力气——所以常温下，你把它放在氧气、水、金属旁边，它都懒得搭理。空气里约五分之四都是氮气，可偏偏绝大多数生物「看得见摸不着」：植物要的是能溶进水里、能被吸收的氮（比如硝酸根、铵根），而不是飘在头顶的气态氮。把这种「用不了」的气态氮，变成「用得动」的含氮化合物，就叫做固氮——闪电能劈出一点点，豆科植物根上的根瘤菌能办到，而人类靠的是下一站的 Haber 法。Picture a nitrogen molecule as two friends holding hands: most molecules link by one finger, but these two grip with all three. Breaking them apart takes enormous force — so at room temperature, nitrogen just ignores oxygen, water and metals. About four-fifths of the air is nitrogen, yet most living things "can see it but can't use it": plants need nitrogen that dissolves and can be absorbed (like nitrate or ammonium ions), not the gas floating overhead. Turning that useless gas into usable nitrogen compounds is called nitrogen fixation — lightning makes a little, bacteria on the roots of legumes do it, and humans do it with the Haber process, next stop.
必须记牢的三点：Three points to learn:
  • N₂ 里是 N≡N 三键，键能约 944 kJ mol⁻¹，非常强 → 所以常温下氮气极不活泼。N₂ contains a triple bond N≡N with a bond energy around 944 kJ mol⁻¹, so it is very unreactive at room temperature.
  • 氮气占空气约 78%，但气态 N₂ 不能被大多数生物直接利用。Nitrogen makes up about 78% of the air, but N₂ gas cannot be used directly by most organisms.
  • 固氮（nitrogen fixation）＝把 N₂ 变成含氮化合物。自然界靠闪电和固氮细菌，工业靠 Haber 法。Nitrogen fixation = turning N₂ into nitrogen compounds. In nature it is done by lightning and nitrogen-fixing bacteria; in industry, by the Haber process.
  • 氮不活泼也有好处：可以当保护气，食品包装里充氮气防氧化变质。Being unreactive is useful: nitrogen acts as an inert blanket gas, and food packs are filled with it to stop oxidation.
别把话说死：氮气是「常温下不活泼」，不是永远不反应。高温或放电时它照样会跟氧气反应（下一站和第 4 站会用到）。考试写「氮气不活泼」一定要带上「常温」这个前提。Don't overstate it: nitrogen is unreactive at room temperature, not forever. At high temperature or in a spark it does react with oxygen (used in stops 2 and 4). Always add "at room temperature" in the exam.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: Nitrogen is very unreactive because its molecule contains a very strong triple bond, N≡N, which requires a large amount of energy to break.
例题Example
为什么常温下氮气几乎不参与化学反应？请从化学键的角度回答。Why does nitrogen barely react at room temperature? Answer in terms of chemical bonding.
① 氮分子由两个氮原子通过三键（N≡N）相连。① two nitrogen atoms are joined by a triple bond (N≡N). ② 三键的键能非常大，拆开它需要大量能量。② the triple bond has a very high bond energy, so breaking it needs a lot of energy. ③ 常温下没有足够的能量，所以反应极慢，几乎不反应。③ at room temperature there is not enough energy, so it barely reacts.
练习Practice
从「含量」和「键」两处入手。Think about both its amount and its bond.

空气中含量最多的气体是什么？为什么它占这么多，却能一直稳定地待在那里？Which gas is most abundant in the air? Why can it stay there, so abundant and so stable?

点开看答案Show answer
是氮气，约占空气的 78%。因为氮分子里是极强的 N≡N 三键，常温下几乎不跟其他物质反应，所以它能一直稳定存在、越积越多。 Nitrogen, about 78% of the air. Its molecules contain a very strong N≡N triple bond, so it barely reacts at room temperature and just keeps building up.
— 第 1 站完成 —— Stop 1 done —
2 Haber 法造氨The Haber process for ammonia N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃合成氨
这一站要你会：写出合成氨的方程式与条件（450 °C、200 atm、铁催化剂），并解释为什么温度要「折中」。Goal: write the equation with its conditions (450 °C, 200 atm, iron catalyst), and explain why the temperature is a compromise.
想让懒洋洋的氮气动起来，人类想了个狠招：把它和氢气一起塞进又热又高压的反应器，再请「铁」当红娘，撮合它俩结婚生子——孩子就是氨。可这桩婚事有点别扭：温度一高，见面快（反应快），可这对夫妻又容易闹离婚（平衡往逆向跑，产率掉）；温度一低，婚姻稳定，可它俩又害羞得不肯牵手（反应太慢）。于是选了 450 °C 这个「折中温度」，两边各退一步，再靠催化剂在后面推一把，总算把产率保住。To make lazy nitrogen get to work, humans used a strong trick: shove it and hydrogen into a hot, high-pressure reactor and let iron play matchmaker — the baby is ammonia. But the marriage is awkward: heat it up and they meet fast (fast reaction), yet the couple also splits up easily (equilibrium shifts backwards, yield drops); cool it down and the marriage is stable, but they are too shy to join hands (reaction too slow). So 450 °C was chosen as a compromise, with a catalyst pushing things along.
方程式与条件：The equation and conditions:
N2(g) + 3H2(g) ⇌ 2NH3(g) 条件：约 450 °C · 200 atm · 铁（Fe）催化剂conditions: ≈ 450 °C · 200 atm · iron (Fe) catalyst
  • 温度是折中：低温产率高但反应太慢；高温反应快，但平衡朝吸热的逆反应移动、产率低。所以取 450 °C 并靠催化剂补速率。The temperature is a compromise: low temperature gives a high yield but is too slow; high temperature is fast but shifts the equilibrium towards the endothermic reverse reaction, lowering yield. So 450 °C plus a catalyst.
  • 高压有利：正向是「4 个气体分子变 2 个」，加压把平衡推向氨；但设备成本高，所以取 200 atm 平衡。High pressure helps: the forward reaction turns 4 gas molecules into 2, so pressure pushes equilibrium towards ammonia; but plant cost rises, so 200 atm is the balance.
  • 原料来源：N₂ 来自空气（液态空气分馏），H₂ 来自天然气（甲烷）与水蒸气反应。Raw materials: N₂ from air (fractional distillation of liquid air), H₂ from natural gas (methane) reacting with steam.
  • 催化剂只改速率，不改平衡位置——它让反应更快到达平衡，但不会多「造」一点氨。A catalyst changes only the rate, not the position of equilibrium — it reaches equilibrium faster but makes no extra ammonia.
两个容易混的地方：① 正向是放热，升温使平衡向吸热方向（逆向）移动——别和「升温加快速率」混为一谈；② 催化剂的作用是「同等加快正逆反应」，不是「提高产率」。Two easy mix-ups: ① the forward reaction is exothermic, so heating shifts equilibrium towards the endothermic (reverse) side — don't confuse this with "heating speeds it up"; ② a catalyst speeds up both directions equally, it does not increase yield.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: The Haber process makes ammonia from nitrogen and hydrogen at about 450 °C and 200 atm using an iron catalyst. A higher temperature would speed up the reaction but shift the equilibrium to the left because the forward reaction is exothermic, so a compromise temperature is used.
例题Example
为什么 Haber 法不干脆用更高的温度来加快反应？Why doesn't the Haber process simply use a higher temperature to speed up the reaction?
① 合成氨的正向反应是放热的。① the forward reaction is exothermic. ② 升温会使平衡向吸热方向（逆反应）移动。② heating shifts the equilibrium towards the endothermic (reverse) reaction. ③ 结果氨的产率下降，所以用 450 °C 折中，再靠铁催化剂补偿速率。③ so the yield of ammonia falls; hence 450 °C as a compromise, with the iron catalyst making up the speed.
练习Practice
催化剂、温度、压强各说一遍，再解释温度。State the catalyst, temperature and pressure, then explain the temperature.

写出合成氨的方程式，并说出（a）催化剂（b）温度（c）压强，以及为什么温度选 450 °C 而不是更高。Write the equation for making ammonia, state (a) the catalyst, (b) the temperature, (c) the pressure, and explain why 450 °C is used rather than a higher temperature.

点开看答案Show answer
方程式：N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃。催化剂是铁，温度约 450 °C，压强约 200 atm。温度选 450 °C：更高虽然反应更快，但正向放热，升温使平衡逆向移动、氨产率降低；450 °C 是速率与产率之间的折中。 Equation: N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃. Catalyst iron, about 450 °C and 200 atm. 450 °C is used because a higher temperature, though faster, shifts the exothermic equilibrium backwards and lowers the yield — 450 °C is the compromise between rate and yield.
— 第 2 站完成 —— Stop 2 done —
3 氨与铵盐化肥Ammonia and ammonium fertilisers NH₄NO₃铵盐
这一站要你会：说出氨溶于水显碱性、与酸生成铵盐，会用「加碱加热放出氨气」检验铵盐，并知道硝酸铵是常见氮肥。Goal: state that ammonia is alkaline in water and forms ammonium salts with acids, test for ammonium salts by heating with alkali, and know ammonium nitrate as a common fertiliser.
氨是个特别爱「认碱」的气体：一进水就抢走水的氢离子，留下氢氧根，所以氨水显碱性，闻起来还一股冲鼻子的味儿。它又很好客，遇到酸立刻结成一对——氨气和硝酸一碰，就得到硝酸铵，一种白花花的氮肥。化肥为什么非得含氮？因为植物造蛋白质、长叶子全靠氮，而土里的氮常常不够，农民就撒这些铵盐下去补。检验铵盐有个小妙招：加点碱、热一热，氨气就会被赶出来，拿湿润的红色石蕊试纸一凑，变蓝就是它。Ammonia is a gas that loves being alkaline: in water it grabs a hydrogen ion, leaving hydroxide behind — so ammonia solution is alkaline and smells sharp. It is also sociable: meet an acid and it pairs up at once. Ammonia plus nitric acid gives ammonium nitrate, a white nitrogen fertiliser. Why must fertiliser contain nitrogen? Because plants need it to build proteins and leaves, and soil often runs short — so farmers sprinkle on these ammonium salts. Testing an ammonium salt is neat: add alkali and warm it, ammonia is driven off, and a damp red litmus paper turns blue.
三个反应要会写：Three reactions to write:
  • 氨溶于水显碱性（可逆，生成铵离子和氢氧根）：Ammonia is alkaline in water (reversible, forming ammonium and hydroxide ions):
    NH3(g) + H2O(l) ⇌ NH4+(aq) + OH−(aq)
  • 氨与酸生成铵盐（例：与硝酸）：Ammonia plus an acid gives an ammonium salt (e.g. nitric acid):
    NH3 + HNO3 → NH4NO3
  • 检验铵盐：加碱 + 加热 → 放出 NH₃，使湿润的红色石蕊试纸变蓝。Test for ammonium salts: add alkali and warm → NH₃ is released and turns damp red litmus blue.
  • 常见氮肥：硝酸铵 NH₄NO₃（含氮量高）、硫酸铵 (NH₄)₂SO₄。Common fertilisers: ammonium nitrate NH₄NO₃ (high nitrogen content) and ammonium sulfate (NH₄)₂SO₄.
检验题的条件要说全：「加碱」和「加热」两个条件一起说才给全分；试纸必须是「湿润的红色石蕊试纸」。少说一个词，这题的分就悄悄溜走了。State the test fully: say both "add alkali" and "warm" for full marks, and the paper must be "damp" and "red". Miss one word and the mark slips away.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: Ammonia is alkaline in water because it accepts H⁺ to form NH₄⁺, leaving OH⁻ in solution. An ammonium salt is tested by heating it with alkali: ammonia gas is released, which turns damp red litmus paper blue.
例题Example
写出氨气与硝酸反应生成化肥的方程式，并说出产物的名称。Write the equation for ammonia reacting with nitric acid to make a fertiliser, and name the product.
① 氨是碱性的，酸是硝酸，两者生成盐和水里的「盐」。① ammonia is basic and nitric acid is an acid — they form the salt directly.
NH3 + HNO3 → NH4NO3
② 产物叫硝酸铵，是一种常见的氮肥。② the product is ammonium nitrate, a common nitrogen fertiliser.
练习Practice
试剂、加热、试纸的颜色变化，一个都不能少。Reagent, heating, and the colour change — none may be missed.

怎样检验一种白色固体是不是铵盐？写出操作步骤和观察到的现象。How would you test whether a white solid is an ammonium salt? Give the steps and the observation.

点开看答案Show answer
取样，加入氢氧化钠（碱）并微热；若放出有刺激性气味的气体，且该气体使湿润的红色石蕊试纸变蓝，则证明是铵盐（放出的是氨气）。 Add sodium hydroxide (alkali) to a sample and warm it. If a pungent gas is given off that turns damp red litmus paper blue, the solid is an ammonium salt (the gas is ammonia).
— 第 3 站完成 —— Stop 3 done —
4 氮氧化物与酸雨Oxides of nitrogen and acid rain NO → NO₂ → HNO₃氮氧化物
这一站要你会：写出高温下 N₂ 与 O₂ 生成 NO、NO 被氧化成 NO₂、NO₂ 溶于水生成硝酸的反应，并解释酸雨的成因与催化转换器的作用。Goal: write the formation of NO from N₂ and O₂ at high temperature, its oxidation to NO₂, and NO₂ dissolving to give nitric acid, then explain acid rain and the catalytic converter.
氮气平时懒，可一碰到高温就「上头」了——汽车发动机里、雷暴的闪电里，温度高得吓人，氮气和氧气被强行撮合，生出一氧化氮。一氧化氮不甘心，很快又被氧气氧化成二氧化氮。二氧化氮溶进雨水，就成了硝酸，于是天上下的雨成了「酸雨」。好在汽车排气管里装了个「净化器」——催化转换器，用铂、铑当催化剂，把有毒的一氧化碳氧化成二氧化碳，把一氧化氮还原回氮气，一道工序同时救了两样。Nitrogen is usually lazy, but give it heat and it "loses its temper" — in car engines and lightning the temperature is extreme, so nitrogen and oxygen are forced together to make nitrogen monoxide, NO. NO is soon oxidised further to nitrogen dioxide, NO₂. When NO₂ dissolves in rain it becomes nitric acid — and the rain turns into acid rain. Luckily cars carry a "purifier" — the catalytic converter — which uses platinum and rhodium to oxidise toxic carbon monoxide to carbon dioxide and reduce nitrogen monoxide back to nitrogen, fixing two problems in one step.
一路走来的三个反应：The three reactions along the way:
  • 高温（发动机 / 闪电）下生成 NO：NO forms at high temperature (engines / lightning):
    N2 + O2 → 2NO
  • NO 再被氧化成 NO₂：NO is oxidised further to NO₂:
    2NO + O2 → 2NO2
  • NO₂ 溶于水生成硝酸和亚硝酸（酸雨成因之一）：NO₂ dissolves in water to give nitric and nitrous acids (a cause of acid rain):
    2NO2 + H2O → HNO3 + HNO2
  • 催化转换器：把 NO 还原回 N₂、把 CO 氧化成 CO₂（合并写）：Catalytic converter: reduces NO back to N₂ and oxidises CO to CO₂ (combined):
    2CO + 2NO → 2CO2 + N2
别把两种酸雨混了：氮氧化物来自高温燃烧（汽车、闪电），SO₂ 来自含硫燃料燃烧（下一站）。两者都能让雨水变酸，但「出身」不同，题目问「汽车尾气」时答氮氧化物，问「烧煤」时答 SO₂。Don't mix up the two acid-rain sources: oxides of nitrogen come from high-temperature burning (cars, lightning), while SO₂ comes from burning sulfur-containing fuels (next stop). Both acidify rain, but their origins differ — answer "nitrogen oxides" for car exhaust and "SO₂" for coal.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: In a car engine the high temperature makes nitrogen and oxygen react to form nitrogen monoxide, NO, which is oxidised to nitrogen dioxide, NO₂. NO₂ dissolves in rainwater to form nitric acid, contributing to acid rain. The catalytic converter reduces NO back to N₂ and oxidises CO to CO₂.
例题Example
写出汽车发动机高温下氮气与氧气反应，以及 NO 进一步被氧化的两个方程式。Write two equations: nitrogen reacting with oxygen at the high temperature of a car engine, and NO being oxidised further.
① 高温下氮气与氧气直接化合，生成一氧化氮。① at high temperature nitrogen and oxygen combine directly to give nitrogen monoxide.
N2 + O2 → 2NO
② 一氧化氮很快被空气里的氧气继续氧化成二氧化氮。② nitrogen monoxide is quickly oxidised by air to nitrogen dioxide.
2NO + O2 → 2NO2
练习Practice
一个被氧化、一个被还原，别写反了。One is oxidised, one is reduced — don't swap them.

催化转换器把哪些有害气体转化成了什么？分别写出对应的两个变化。Which harmful gases does the catalytic converter turn into what? Write the two changes.

点开看答案Show answer
把一氧化碳 CO 氧化成二氧化碳 CO₂：2CO + O₂ → 2CO₂；把一氧化氮 NO 还原成氮气 N₂：2NO → N₂ + O₂。也可合并写：2CO + 2NO → 2CO₂ + N₂。 It oxidises carbon monoxide CO to carbon dioxide CO₂: 2CO + O₂ → 2CO₂, and reduces nitrogen monoxide NO to nitrogen N₂: 2NO → N₂ + O₂. Combined: 2CO + 2NO → 2CO₂ + N₂.
— 第 4 站完成 —— Stop 4 done —
5 硫、SO₂ 与接触法硫酸Sulfur, sulfur dioxide and sulfuric acid Contact process接触法
这一站要你会：写出硫燃烧生成 SO₂、SO₂ 催化氧化成 SO₃、SO₃ 被浓硫酸吸收成发烟硫酸的反应，并解释为什么不让 SO₃ 直接加水。Goal: write sulfur burning to SO₂, SO₂ oxidised to SO₃, and SO₃ absorbed in concentrated acid to oleum, and explain why SO₃ is not added directly to water.
硫是黄色固体，点着后冒蓝色火焰，生成呛人的二氧化硫——这也是烧煤、烧石油时酸雨的另一个来源。想用二氧化硫造硫酸，工业上走一条叫「接触法」的路：先让硫在空气里烧成 SO₂，再用五氧化二钒当催化剂、把 SO₂ 氧化成 SO₃。最后一步最妙——不是直接加水，而是先让 SO₃ 溶进浓硫酸里，变成「发烟硫酸」，再慢慢稀释。为什么不直接加水？因为 SO₃ 碰到水会剧烈放热、喷出酸雾白烟，又危险又浪费，根本控制不住，所以用浓硫酸「接住」它，再把水一点一点加进去。Sulfur is a yellow solid; light it and it burns with a blue flame, giving choking sulfur dioxide — the other source of acid rain when coal or oil is burned. To turn SO₂ into sulfuric acid, industry uses the Contact process: burn sulfur in air to SO₂, then use a vanadium(V) oxide catalyst to oxidise SO₂ into SO₃. The last step is the clever bit — not adding water directly, but first dissolving SO₃ in concentrated sulfuric acid to make "oleum", then diluting slowly. Why not just add water? Because SO₃ hits water with violent heat and sprays an acid mist — dangerous and wasteful, impossible to control — so concentrated acid "catches" it first, then water is added gradually.
接触法四步方程式：The four equations of the Contact process:
  • 硫燃烧：Sulfur burns:
    S + O2 → SO2
  • SO₂ 催化氧化（可逆，V₂O₅ 催化）：SO₂ oxidised (reversible, V₂O₅ catalyst):
    2SO2 + O2 ⇌ 2SO3
  • SO₃ 被浓硫酸吸收 → 发烟硫酸：SO₃ absorbed in concentrated acid → oleum:
    SO3 + H2SO4 → H2S2O7
  • 发烟硫酸加水 → 硫酸：Oleum plus water → sulfuric acid:
    H2S2O7 + H2O → 2H2SO4
  • SO₂ 也是酸雨的另一成因：它溶进雨水生成酸性溶液。SO₂ is the other acid-rain cause: it dissolves in rainwater to make an acidic solution.
两处常被扣分：① 第二步要写可逆号 ⇌ 和 V₂O₅ 催化剂，漏了就没全分；② 第三步是「浓硫酸吸收」，不是加水——H₂S₂O₇ 叫发烟硫酸（oleum），这个词在考试里经常露脸。Two places marks are lost: ① step 2 needs the reversible arrow ⇌ and the V₂O₅ catalyst; ② step 3 is "absorb in concentrated acid", not water — H₂S₂O₇ is called oleum, a word that appears often in exams.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: Sulfur burns in air to form sulfur dioxide. In the Contact process, SO₂ is oxidised to SO₃ using a V₂O₅ catalyst, then the SO₃ is absorbed in concentrated sulfuric acid to form oleum, which is diluted to give sulfuric acid. SO₃ is not added directly to water because the reaction is violent, very exothermic and produces an uncontrollable acid mist.
例题Example
写出接触法中 SO₂ 转成 SO₃ 的方程式，说明催化剂和条件，并解释为什么最后一步不把 SO₃ 直接加进水里。Write the equation for SO₂ becoming SO₃ in the Contact process, state the catalyst and conditions, and explain why SO₃ is not added directly to water.
① SO₂ 在催化剂作用下被氧气氧化成 SO₃，反应可逆。① SO₂ is oxidised by oxygen over a catalyst; the reaction is reversible.
2SO2 + O2 ⇌ 2SO3 （V₂O₅ 催化）
② 不直接加水：因为 SO₃ 与水反应剧烈放热、形成酸雾，难以收集又危险，还会降低收率。② not added to water directly: SO₃ reacts violently and exothermically, forming an acid mist that is hard to collect and dangerous, lowering the yield. ③ 所以先让浓硫酸吸收成发烟硫酸，再稀释成硫酸。③ so it is first absorbed in concentrated acid to oleum, then diluted to sulfuric acid.
练习Practice
第一个直接化合，第二个记得写可逆号。The first is direct combination; remember the reversible arrow for the second.

写出（a）硫在空气中燃烧，以及（b）SO₂ 在催化剂作用下继续被氧化的两个方程式。Write equations for (a) sulfur burning in air and (b) SO₂ being oxidised further over a catalyst.

点开看答案Show answer
(a) S + O₂ → SO₂。
(b) 2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃，用五氧化二钒（V₂O₅）作催化剂。 (a) S + O₂ → SO₂.
(b) 2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃, using vanadium(V) oxide (V₂O₅) as the catalyst.
— 第 5 站完成 —— Stop 5 done —

单元 12 小结Unit 12 summary

① 氮气懒，是因为 N≡N 三键极强——所以固氮（闪电、固氮菌、Haber 法）是件大事。
② Haber 法用 450 °C、200 atm、铁催化剂把氮气和氢气做成氨；温度是「速率 vs 产率」的折中。
③ 氨显碱性，与酸生成铵盐（如硝酸铵化肥）；检验铵盐靠「加碱 + 加热 → 石蕊变蓝」。
④ 酸雨有两大来源：高温燃烧产生的氮氧化物（NO → NO₂ → 硝酸），和含硫燃料燃烧产生的 SO₂。
⑤ 接触法三步造硫酸：烧硫得 SO₂ → 催化氧化得 SO₃ → 浓硫酸吸收成发烟硫酸再稀释。① Nitrogen is lazy because the N≡N triple bond is so strong — that is why nitrogen fixation (lightning, bacteria, the Haber process) matters.
② The Haber process makes ammonia from nitrogen and hydrogen at 450 °C, 200 atm with an iron catalyst; the temperature balances rate against yield.
③ Ammonia is alkaline and forms ammonium salts with acids (e.g. ammonium nitrate fertiliser); test them by "alkali + heat → litmus turns blue".
④ Acid rain has two sources: nitrogen oxides from hot burning (NO → NO₂ → nitric acid), and SO₂ from sulfur-containing fuels.
⑤ The Contact process makes sulfuric acid in three steps: burn sulfur to SO₂ → catalytic oxidation to SO₃ → absorb in concentrated acid to oleum, then dilute.

下一站最重要的一件事：从碳开始，化学换了个世界——有机化学里，碳原子能自己跟自己手拉手连成链、成环，这就是单元 13 的开场。Why the next unit matters: starting from carbon, chemistry enters a new world — in organic chemistry carbon atoms join hands with each other to build chains and rings. That is the opening of Unit 13.

单元 13 · 有机化学入门：碳的乐高世界Unit 13 · An introduction to organic chemistry: carbon's building blocks

CAIE 9701 Topic 13 · 7 站 · 碳的乐高：为什么有机分子能拼出几百万种CAIE 9701 Topic 13 · 7 stops · carbon LEGO: why organic molecules come in millions

路线图本单元七站：先看懂碳为什么是主角，再认官能团、学命名，最后分清键与异构、反应分类Seven stops: why carbon is the star, then functional groups and naming, then bonds, isomerism and reaction types

  1. 碳凭什么当主角：4 只手、自己接自己Why carbon is the star: four hands, bonds to itself
  2. 官能团：分子的身份证Functional groups and homologous series
  3. 命名四步走：主链、编号、取代基、后缀Naming organic compounds in four steps
  4. σ 键与 π 键：握手与贴肩Sigma and pi bonds: handshake and side-hug
  5. 结构异构：同样的配方不同的搭法Structural isomerism: same formula, different build
  6. 立体异构：明明连着一样却不一样Stereoisomerism: same connections, different space

建议：先把第 1、2 站看明白（碳为什么能搭 + 官能团长什么样），再学命名——命名其实就是「照着图报地址」。Tip: get stops 1 and 2 clear (why carbon builds, and what the groups look like) before naming — naming is just reading an address off a diagram.

1 碳凭什么当主角Why carbon is the star Why carbon碳为何是主角
这一站要你会：说出碳为什么能形成 4 根键、为什么能「自己接自己」，并知道 diamond 与 graphite 是同一种元素的两种形态（同素异形体）。Goal: explain why carbon forms four bonds and can bond to itself, and know that diamond and graphite are two forms of the same element (allotropes).
把碳想成一块乐高积木：它身上正好有 4 个凸点（4 个价电子），所以能同时接 4 块别的积木；更厉害的是，碳的凸点还能互相对接，于是碳能接碳、再接碳……一节节连成链、围成环，拼出几百万种形状。地球上没有第二种元素这么「爱搭积木」，所以整个有机化学，本质就是碳的乐高说明书。Picture carbon as a LEGO brick: it has exactly 4 studs (4 valence electrons), so it can snap onto 4 other bricks. Even better, those studs can join to each other, so carbon links to carbon, then carbon again — building chains and rings into millions of shapes. No other element is so keen on building, which is why all of organic chemistry is really carbon's building manual.
四个必须记住的点：Four points to learn:
  • 碳的电子排布是 1s² 2s² 2p²——最外层 4 个电子，所以形成 4 个共价键。Carbon is 1s² 2s² 2p² — four electrons in the outer shell, so it forms 4 covalent bonds.
  • 4 根键都是共价键（分享电子），又强又稳，所以有机分子很「耐造」。All four bonds are covalent (shared electrons), strong and stable, so organic molecules are tough.
  • 碳能接碳：成链（chain）、成环（ring）、生支链——「几百万种」的秘密全在这里。Carbon bonds to carbon: chains, rings and branches — the whole secret behind "millions of compounds".
  • 同素异形体（allotropes）：diamond（每个碳接 4 个碳，自然界最硬）和 graphite（层状、能导电、做铅笔芯）——同样的碳原子，不同搭法，性质天差地别。Allotropes: diamond (each carbon bonded to 4 carbons, the hardest natural substance) and graphite (layered, conducts electricity, pencil lead) — same carbon atoms, different build, totally different properties.
别把两个词搞混：「同素异形体」是同一种元素的不同结构（碳的两种搭法）；「同位素」是同一种元素的不同原子核（中子数不同）。一个是拼法，一个是体重。Don't mix the two words: "allotropes" are different structures of the same element; "isotopes" are different nuclei of the same element (different neutrons). One is about shape, the other about weight.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: Carbon has four electrons in its outer shell, so it forms four covalent bonds. It can also form bonds with other carbon atoms to make chains and rings, which is why there are so many different carbon compounds.
例题Example
碳的原子序数是 6。写出它的电子排布，并解释为什么碳通常形成 4 个共价键。Carbon has proton number 6. Write its electronic configuration and explain why carbon usually forms four covalent bonds.
① 6 个电子 → 1s² 2s² 2p²。① 6 electrons → 1s² 2s² 2p². ② 最外层（第 2 层）有 4 个电子；要像氖那样凑到 8 电子的稳定结构，还差 4 个。② Its outer shell (shell 2) holds 4 electrons; to reach the stable 8-electron arrangement of neon it needs 4 more. ③ 于是碳再分享 4 个电子，形成 4 根共价键，凑满 8 个。③ So carbon shares 4 more electrons, forming 4 covalent bonds to reach eight.
练习Practice
硅就在碳正下方，同族，套路完全一样。Silicon sits directly below carbon, same group, same routine.

硅（Z = 14）与碳同族。写出硅的电子排布，并解释为什么硅通常也形成 4 个共价键。Silicon (Z = 14) is in the same group as carbon. Write its electronic configuration and explain why silicon usually forms four covalent bonds.

点开看答案Show answer
硅的排布是 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p²，最外层（第 3 层）也是 4 个电子，所以和碳一样分享 4 个电子、形成 4 根共价键（比如 SiCl₄、SiO₂）。这就是同族元素「脾气相近」的原因——最外层电子数一样。 Silicon is 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p², with 4 electrons in its outer shell (shell 3), so like carbon it shares 4 electrons to form four covalent bonds (e.g. SiCl₄, SiO₂). This is why elements in the same group behave alike — they have the same number of outer electrons.
— 第 1 站完成 —— Stop 1 done —
2 官能团：分子的身份证Functional groups and homologous series Functional groups官能团
这一站要你会：认出 10 个常见官能团并说出所属系列，理解同系物「差一个 CH₂、通式相同、化学性质相似」。Goal: recognise ten common functional groups, name their series, and understand that homologous series differ by CH₂, share a general formula, and have similar chemistry.
官能团就是分子的身份证：名字后缀一样（比如都叫「某醇」），化学行为就一样，因为决定脾气的是那一小撮原子——–OH 让它变醇，C=C 让它活泼。旁边碳链是长是短，只是「个头」不同，不影响「脾气」。同一系列里的兄弟一个接一个，只差一个 CH₂，就像排队的人，前后只差一个「肩膀宽度」。A functional group is a molecule's identity card: same suffix (all "something-ol") means same chemistry, because the character comes from that small bunch of atoms — –OH makes it an alcohol, C=C makes it reactive. A longer or shorter carbon chain just changes the "size", not the "personality". Members of a series line up one after another, each differing by a single CH₂ — like people in a queue, each one "shoulder-width" apart.
必记官能团表：The functional groups to memorise:
系列Series官能团Group例子Example后缀Suffix
烷烃 alkaneAlkaneC–CCH₄-ane
烯烃 alkeneAlkeneC=CCH₂=CH₂-ene
卤代烃 halogenoalkaneHalogenoalkane–XCH₃CH₂Clchloro- 等前缀
醇 alcoholAlcohol–OHCH₃CH₂OH-ol
醛 aldehydeAldehyde–CHOCH₃CHO-al
酮 ketoneKetone>C=OCH₃COCH₃-one
羧酸 carboxylic acidCarboxylic acid–COOHCH₃COOH-oic acid
酯 esterEster–COO–CH₃COOCH₂CH₃-yl -oate
腈 nitrileNitrile–C≡NCH₃CN-nitrile
胺 amineAmine–NH₂CH₃NH₂-amine
  • 同系物（homologous series）：同一系列里的成员，一个个只差 CH₂，通式相同，化学性质相似。A homologous series is a family whose members each differ by CH₂, share a general formula, and have similar chemical properties.
  • 物理性质随链长渐变（碳越多沸点越高），化学性质由官能团决定。Physical properties change gradually with chain length (more carbons, higher boiling point); chemistry is set by the functional group.
  • 通式举例：烷烃 CnH2n+2、烯烃 CnH2n、醇 CnH2n+1OH。General formulas: alkanes CnH2n+2, alkenes CnH2n, alcohols CnH2n+1OH.
名字一起记：–OH 叫羟基（不是「氢氧根」，那是离子 OH⁻），–COOH 叫羧基，–CHO 叫醛基。把官能团当「词根」，命名和反应都靠它。Learn the names together: –OH is the hydroxyl group (not "hydroxide", which is the ion OH⁻), –COOH is the carboxyl group, –CHO is the carbonyl/aldehyde group. Treat the group as the "root" of the word — naming and reactions both depend on it.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: A homologous series is a family of compounds with the same functional group and the same general formula, in which each member differs from the next by a CH₂ group.
例题Example
CH₃CH₂OH 属于哪一类有机化合物？它的官能团是什么？写出这一类的通式。To which class does CH₃CH₂OH belong? What is its functional group? Write the general formula of the series.
① 找特征基团 → 有 –OH（羟基）。① Find the characteristic group → there is –OH (hydroxyl). ② 含羟基 → 醇（alcohol）。② Contains hydroxyl → alcohol. ③ 醇的同系通式：CnH2n+1OH。③ General formula of alcohols: CnH2n+1OH.
练习Practice
先圈出特征基团，再对表。Circle the characteristic group first, then match the table.

判断下列物质的类别和官能团：(a) CH₃CHO　(b) CH₃COCH₃　(c) CH₃COOH。State the class and functional group of: (a) CH₃CHO (b) CH₃COCH₃ (c) CH₃COOH.

点开看答案Show answer
(a) 醛，官能团 –CHO；(b) 酮，官能团 >C=O；(c) 羧酸，官能团 –COOH。
注意 (a) 和 (b) 都含 C=O，但醛的羰基在链端、酮的羰基在链中间——位置不同，系列就不同。 (a) aldehyde, group –CHO; (b) ketone, group >C=O; (c) carboxylic acid, group –COOH.
Note (a) and (b) both contain C=O, but an aldehyde's carbonyl is at the end of the chain while a ketone's is in the middle — different position, different series.
— 第 2 站完成 —— Stop 2 done —
3 命名四步走Naming organic compounds Naming命名法
这一站要你会：用「最长链 → 编号 → 取代基 → 后缀」四步，正确命名简单的烷烃、烯烃、醇。Goal: name simple alkanes, alkenes and alcohols using the four steps: longest chain → numbering → substituents → suffix.
命名其实就是报家庭住址：先说住哪条街（主链，几个碳），再说门牌号（官能团/取代基在第几号碳），最后说这家人姓什么（后缀）。顺序对了，别人一听就知道分子长什么样。所以命名不是背名词，是照着地图报地址。Naming is really just reading out an address: first the street (the main chain, how many carbons), then the house number (which carbon carries the group), then the family name (the suffix). Get the order right and anyone can picture the molecule. So naming isn't memorising words — it's reading an address off a map.
四步走：The four steps:
  • ① 找主链：选含官能团（或双键）的最长碳链，数碳数 → 词干 meth-(1) / eth-(2) / prop-(3) / but-(4) / pent-(5)。① Longest chain: choose the longest carbon chain containing the group (or double bond), count the carbons → stem meth-(1) / eth-(2) / prop-(3) / but-(4) / pent-(5).
  • ② 编号：从离官能团/双键/取代基最近的一端开始，让它们的编号尽量小。② Number: start from the end closest to the functional group / double bond / substituent, so it gets the lowest number.
  • ③ 写取代基：支链（如 methyl）按字母顺序写在前面，前面标位置号。③ Substituents: name the branches (e.g. methyl) in alphabetical order, each with its position number.
  • ④ 定后缀：烷 -ane、烯 -ene、醇 -ol、醛 -al、酮 -one、酸 -oic acid。④ Suffix: alkane -ane, alkene -ene, alcohol -ol, aldehyde -al, ketone -one, acid -oic acid.
编号时「官能团优先」：给醇、醛、烯命名时，要让官能团/双键的编号最小，而不是先照顾支链。这是最常见的扣分点。The group wins the numbering: when naming alcohols, aldehydes and alkenes, give the functional group / double bond the lowest number — not the branch. This is the most common place marks are lost.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: To name an organic compound, find the longest carbon chain, number it so that the functional group or double bond gets the lowest number, name any substituents, and add the correct suffix.
例题Example
给 CH₃–CH(CH₃)–CH₂–CH₃ 命名。Name CH₃–CH(CH₃)–CH₂–CH₃.
① 最长碳链有 4 个碳 → 主链叫 butane。① The longest chain has 4 carbons → the parent is butane. ② 编号：这个分子对称，无论从哪端数，甲基都在 2 号。② Numbering: the molecule is symmetric, so the methyl is on carbon 2 from either end. ③ 有一个甲基取代基 → 2-methyl。③ One methyl substituent → 2-methyl. ④ 拼起来：2-methylbutane。④ Put it together: 2-methylbutane.
练习Practice
先找主链，再决定从哪端编号（让 OH 编号最小）。Find the main chain, then number from the end that gives the OH the lowest number.

命名：(a) CH₃–CH(OH)–CH₃　(b) CH₃–CH(OH)–CH₂–CH₃。Name: (a) CH₃–CH(OH)–CH₃ (b) CH₃–CH(OH)–CH₂–CH₃.

点开看答案Show answer
(a) 3 个碳的主链 + –OH 在 2 号 → propan-2-ol。
(b) 4 个碳的主链 + –OH 在 2 号 → butan-2-ol。
注意：要从靠近 OH 的一端开始编号，让 OH 的号码尽量小。 (a) 3-carbon chain + –OH on carbon 2 → propan-2-ol.
(b) 4-carbon chain + –OH on carbon 2 → butan-2-ol.
Note: number from the end closest to the OH so the OH gets the smallest number.
— 第 3 站完成 —— Stop 3 done —
4 σ 键与 π 键：握手与贴肩Sigma and pi bonds σ & π bondsσ 与 π 键
这一站要你会：说出单键 = 1σ、双键 = 1σ + 1π、三键 = 1σ + 2π，对应杂化 sp³ / sp² / sp，并知道 π 键更活泼。Goal: state that single = 1σ, double = 1σ + 1π, triple = 1σ + 2π, match them to sp³ / sp² / sp, and know π bonds are more reactive.
把两个原子的轨道想象成两只手：单键是两人面对面握手（头对头），握得又紧又稳，这就是 σ 键；双键除了握手，还肩膀靠肩膀贴一下（侧面重叠），这个「贴肩」就是 π 键——它没握手牢，所以「手一松」就能被别的反应物插进来，这就是双键更活泼的原因。Think of two atoms' orbitals as two hands: a single bond is a firm face-to-face handshake (head-to-head) — that's a σ bond. A double bond adds a shoulder-to-shoulder touch (sideways overlap) — that extra "side-hug" is the π bond. It is not as strong as the handshake, so the moment it slips, another reactant can slip in. That is why double bonds are more reactive.
四个要点：Four points:
  • σ 键：头对头重叠，重叠区在键轴线上，最牢。σ bond: head-to-head overlap along the bond axis; the strongest.
  • π 键：两个 p 轨道侧面平行重叠，分布在键轴上下两侧，比 σ 弱、易断。π bond: sideways overlap of two p orbitals, above and below the bond axis; weaker than σ, breaks easily.
  • 键的组成：单键 = 1σ；双键 = 1σ + 1π；三键 = 1σ + 2π。Bond composition: single = 1σ; double = 1σ + 1π; triple = 1σ + 2π.
  • 杂化对应：单键碳 sp³（四面体 109.5°）、双键碳 sp²（平面 120°）、三键碳 sp（直线 180°）。Hybridisation: single-bonded C is sp³ (tetrahedral, 109.5°), double-bonded C is sp² (trigonal planar, 120°), triple-bonded C is sp (linear, 180°).
双键不是「两根一样的键」，而是「一根 σ + 一根 π」，强度不同。题目常问「双键里哪部分先断」——答案是 π。A double bond is not "two identical bonds" — it is one σ plus one π, of different strength. If asked "which part of the double bond breaks first", answer π.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: A double bond consists of one sigma bond (formed by head-on overlap of orbitals) and one pi bond (formed by sideways overlap of p orbitals). The pi bond is weaker and breaks first in reactions.
例题Example
乙烷（CH₃CH₃）、乙烯（CH₂=CH₂）、乙炔（HC≡CH）里各有多少个 σ 键、多少个 π 键？How many σ bonds and π bonds are there in ethane (CH₃CH₃), ethene (CH₂=CH₂) and ethyne (HC≡CH)?
① 乙烷：全是单键。C–C 是 1σ，另有 6 个 C–H σ → 7σ、0π。① Ethane: all single bonds. C–C is 1σ, plus 6 C–H σ → 7σ, 0π. ② 乙烯：C=C 是 1σ + 1π，另有 4 个 C–H σ → 5σ、1π。② Ethene: C=C is 1σ + 1π, plus 4 C–H σ → 5σ, 1π. ③ 乙炔：C≡C 是 1σ + 2π，另有 2 个 C–H σ → 3σ、2π。③ Ethyne: C≡C is 1σ + 2π, plus 2 C–H σ → 3σ, 2π.
练习Practice
先数 C–H，再处理 C 与 C 之间的键。Count the C–H bonds first, then handle the C–C bonds.

丙烯 CH₃–CH=CH₂ 里有多少个 σ 键、多少个 π 键？How many σ and π bonds are in propene, CH₃–CH=CH₂?

点开看答案Show answer
C–H 有 6 个 σ；C–C 单键 1 个 σ；C=C 是 1σ + 1π。
所以 σ = 6 + 1 + 1 = 8，π = 1。总共 8σ + 1π。 6 C–H σ bonds; the C–C single bond is 1σ; the C=C is 1σ + 1π.
So σ = 6 + 1 + 1 = 8 and π = 1. In total 8σ + 1π.
— 第 4 站完成 —— Stop 4 done —
5 结构异构：同样的配方不同的搭法Structural isomerism Isomers异构体
这一站要你会：分清链异构、位置异构、官能团异构，并能说明「分子式相同、结构不同、性质不同」。Goal: tell apart chain, position and functional group isomerism, and explain "same molecular formula, different structure, different properties".
结构异构就像同一盒乐高拼出两种东西：砖块一样（分子式相同），但搭法不同（结构不同），一个是车一个是飞机，玩起来当然不一样（性质不同）。链异构是「直链 vs 带叉」，位置异构是「同一个东西放的位置不同」，官能团异构是「连积木的『头』都不一样」。Structural isomerism is like building two things from the same box of LEGO: same bricks (same molecular formula), different build (different structure) — one becomes a car, the other a plane, and they behave differently. Chain isomerism is "straight vs branched", position isomerism is "the same part in a different spot", and functional group isomerism is "even the connecting head is different".
三种结构异构：Three kinds of structural isomerism:
  • 定义：分子式相同、结构不同、物理和化学性质都不同 → 互为结构异构体。Definition: same molecular formula, different structure, different physical and chemical properties → structural isomers.
  • 链异构 chain：碳骨架不同（直链 vs 支链），如 C₄H₁₀ 的正丁烷和异丁烷。Chain isomerism: different carbon skeleton (straight vs branched), e.g. n-butane and isobutane, both C₄H₁₀.
  • 位置异构 position：官能团/双键位置不同，如 propan-1-ol 和 propan-2-ol。Position isomerism: the group / double bond sits in a different place, e.g. propan-1-ol and propan-2-ol.
  • 官能团异构 functional：官能团不同，如丙醛 CH₃CH₂CHO（醛）和丙酮 CH₃COCH₃（酮），都是 C₃H₆O。Functional group isomerism: different functional group, e.g. propanal CH₃CH₂CHO (aldehyde) and propanone CH₃COCH₃ (ketone), both C₃H₆O.
数异构体要按顺序：先骨架（链），再位置，再看官能团——养成这个顺序就不会漏。Count isomers in order: skeleton (chain) first, then position, then functional group — keep that order and you won't miss any.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: Structural isomers have the same molecular formula but different structural formulae, so they have different physical and chemical properties.
例题Example
写出 C₄H₁₀ 的所有结构异构体并命名。Draw and name all the structural isomers of C₄H₁₀.
① 先画直链：CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₃ → butane（正丁烷）。① First the straight chain: CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₃ → butane. ② 再画支链：把一个端头碳拆下来挂到中间 → 2-methylpropane（异丁烷）。② Then the branch: move an end carbon to the middle → 2-methylpropane. ③ 数一遍碳和氢：都是 C₄H₁₀。就这两种。③ Count the carbons and hydrogens: both are C₄H₁₀. Just these two.
练习Practice
先直链，再逐级「拆端头碳往中间挂」。Start with the straight chain, then move end carbons inward step by step.

戊烷 C₅H₁₂ 有几个链异构体？写出并命名。How many chain isomers does pentane, C₅H₁₂, have? Draw and name them.

点开看答案Show answer
3 个：正戊烷 pentane（直链）、2-甲基丁烷 2-methylbutane、2,2-二甲基丙烷 2,2-dimethylpropane。
注意：「2-甲基丁烷」和「3-甲基丁烷」不是两种——只是把链反过来看，其实是同一种。 Three: pentane (straight), 2-methylbutane, and 2,2-dimethylpropane.
Note: "2-methylbutane" and "3-methylbutane" are not two different compounds — read the chain the other way and they are the same thing.
— 第 5 站完成 —— Stop 5 done —
6 立体异构：明明连着一样却不一样Stereoisomerism cis–trans顺反异构
这一站要你会：说清顺反（E–Z）异构出现的条件（双键两端各连两个不同基团），并会画、会认 cis 和 trans。Goal: state the condition for cis–trans (E–Z) isomerism — each double-bond carbon must carry two different groups — and draw or recognise cis and trans.
顺反异构就像同款双开门，一个门把手都在左、另一个一左一右：连的东西一模一样，只是空间朝向不同，而双键不能自由旋转，转不回去，于是成了两种不同的物质。cis 是「同侧」，trans 是「对侧」。Cis–trans is like two identical double doors, one with both handles on the left, the other with one on each side: the parts are the same, only their orientation in space differs, and since the double bond cannot rotate, they cannot turn into each other. cis means "same side", trans means "opposite sides".
三个要点：Three points:
  • 出现条件：双键两端，每一端都连着两个不同的基团，才可能出现 cis–trans。The condition: cis–trans needs each end of the C=C to carry two different groups.
  • 为什么是两种：双键不能旋转，所以「同侧/对侧」被固定成两种结构，无法互相转换。Why there are two: the double bond cannot rotate, so "same side / opposite side" are locked as two distinct structures.
  • 例子：cis-1,2-dichloroethene（两 Cl 同侧）和 trans-1,2-dichloroethene（两 Cl 异侧）。Examples: cis-1,2-dichloroethene (both Cl same side) and trans-1,2-dichloroethene (Cl on opposite sides).
记一个反例：1,1-dichloroethene（CCl₂=CH₂）两个 Cl 在同一个碳上，那一端两个基团相同，所以没有 cis–trans。题目就爱拿它当「陷阱」。Learn the counter-example: 1,1-dichloroethene (CCl₂=CH₂) has both Cl on the same carbon, so that end has two identical groups and it has no cis–trans. Questions love using it as a trap.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: Cis–trans isomerism occurs when each carbon of a C=C double bond is attached to two different groups, because the double bond cannot rotate.
例题Example
1,2-dichloroethene 有顺反异构，画出 cis 和 trans 两种结构；而 1,1-dichloroethene 没有，为什么？1,2-dichloroethene shows cis–trans isomerism — draw both; 1,1-dichloroethene does not. Why?
① 1,2-：每个双键碳都连一个 H 和一个 Cl（两个不同基团）→ 有 cis/trans。① 1,2-: each double-bond carbon carries one H and one Cl (two different groups) → cis/trans exist. ② cis 是两 Cl 同侧，trans 是两 Cl 异侧（见上图）。② cis has both Cl on the same side, trans on opposite sides (see the diagram). ③ 1,1-：同一个碳上连了两个 Cl，这一端两个基团相同 → 不具备顺反条件。③ 1,1-: the same carbon carries two Cl, so that end has two identical groups → no cis–trans possible.
练习Practice
先看每个双键碳上连的两个基团是否都不同。First check whether each double-bond carbon carries two different groups.

判断下列物质是否有顺反异构：(a) CHBr=CHBr　(b) CH₂=CHBr　(c) CH₃CH=CHCH₃。Decide whether these show cis–trans isomerism: (a) CHBr=CHBr (b) CH₂=CHBr (c) CH₃CH=CHCH₃.

点开看答案Show answer
(a) 有：每个碳连 H 和 Br，两个基团不同。(b) 无：左边碳连两个 H，相同。(c) 有：每个碳连 CH₃ 和 H，不同（but-2-ene 有 cis/trans）。
口诀：同一端两个基团相同 → 没有顺反异构。 (a) yes: each carbon carries H and Br, two different groups. (b) no: the left carbon carries two H atoms, identical. (c) yes: each carbon carries CH₃ and H (but-2-ene has cis/trans).
Rule of thumb: same two groups on one end → no cis–trans.
— 第 6 站完成 —— Stop 6 done —
7 有机反应怎么分类Types of organic reactions Reaction types反应类型
这一站要你会：分清自由基取代、亲电加成、亲核取代、氧化/还原这几大类，能看试剂判断反应类型，并会用弯箭头表示电子移动。Goal: tell apart radical substitution, electrophilic addition, nucleophilic substitution and oxidation/reduction, judge the type from the reagent, and use curly arrows to show electron movement.
有机反应看起来千变万化，其实就四种「打架」方式：有的派一个缺电子的「正电猎手」（亲电试剂）去攻双键——亲电加成；有的派一个带负电、有孤对电子的「负电刺客」（亲核试剂）去顶替——亲核取代；有的让光把氯拆成两个「野人」去抢氢——自由基取代；剩下的氧化还原、水解、酯化，本质都是「换人 / 加氧去氢」。弯箭头（curly arrow）就是在图上标出电子往哪跑的那支笔。Organic reactions look endless, but they are really just four ways of "fighting": one sends an electron-poor "positive hunter" (an electrophile) to attack a double bond — electrophilic addition; another sends a negative, lone-pair-carrying "assassin" (a nucleophile) to push something out — nucleophilic substitution; a third lets light split chlorine into two "wild men" that grab hydrogens — radical substitution. The rest (oxidation, reduction, hydrolysis, esterification) are all "swapping people / adding oxygen or removing hydrogen". A curly arrow is just the pen that marks where the electrons run.
分类总览：The big picture:
  • 自由基取代 radical substitution：烷烃 + 卤素（光照）→ 卤代烃。Radical substitution: alkane + halogen (in light) → halogenoalkane.
  • 亲电加成 electrophilic addition：烯烃 + Br₂ / HBr / H₂O → 双键打开。Electrophilic addition: alkene + Br₂ / HBr / H₂O → the double bond opens.
  • 亲核取代 nucleophilic substitution：卤代烃 + OH⁻ / CN⁻ → 卤素被顶掉。Nucleophilic substitution: halogenoalkane + OH⁻ / CN⁻ → the halogen is displaced.
  • 氧化/还原：醇 → 醛/酮/酸（加氧是氧化；去氧加氢是还原）。另有水解（酯 + 水 → 酸 + 醇）和酯化（酸 + 醇 → 酯 + 水）。Oxidation/reduction: alcohol → aldehyde/ketone/acid (adding oxygen is oxidation; removing oxygen or adding hydrogen is reduction). Also hydrolysis (ester + water → acid + alcohol) and esterification (acid + alcohol → ester + water).
  • 弯箭头：尾巴在电子多的地方，箭头指向电子少的地方，表示一对电子的流动方向。Curly arrow: the tail sits where the electrons are, the head points to where they go — it shows the movement of an electron pair.
先看试剂「爱正还是爱负」：「亲电」攻的是电子多的地方（双键、苯环）；「亲核」攻的是电子少、带 δ⁺的地方（如 C–X 里的碳）。判断完试剂性格，再对号入座。First ask what the reagent loves: electrophiles attack electron-rich sites (double bonds, benzene rings); nucleophiles attack electron-poor, δ⁺ sites (like the carbon in C–X). Work out the reagent's character, then slot it in.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：How to say it in the exam: Organic reactions are classified by how electrons move: radical substitution (alkanes + halogens), electrophilic addition (alkenes + halogens), and nucleophilic substitution (halogenoalkanes + nucleophiles). Curly arrows show the movement of a pair of electrons.
例题Example
给反应 CH₃CH₂Br + NaOH → CH₃CH₂OH + NaBr 分类，并说明理由。Classify the reaction CH₃CH₂Br + NaOH → CH₃CH₂OH + NaBr, and explain.
① 反应物是卤代烃，试剂 NaOH 提供 OH⁻。① The reactant is a halogenoalkane; NaOH supplies OH⁻. ② OH⁻ 带负电、有孤对电子 → 亲核试剂。② OH⁻ is negative with a lone pair → a nucleophile. ③ 它把 Br 顶替下来、自己接上去 → 亲核取代（nucleophilic substitution）。③ It displaces Br and takes its place → nucleophilic substitution.
练习Practice
看反应物身上是哪个官能团，再看试剂是什么性格。Look at the functional group on the reactant, then at the reagent's character.

判断反应类型：(a) CH₂=CH₂ + Br₂ → CH₂BrCH₂Br　(b) CH₄ + Cl₂（光照）→ CH₃Cl + HCl　(c) CH₃CH₂OH 在 K₂Cr₂O₇/H⁺ 下 → CH₃COOH。Classify: (a) CH₂=CH₂ + Br₂ → CH₂BrCH₂Br (b) CH₄ + Cl₂ (light) → CH₃Cl + HCl (c) CH₃CH₂OH with K₂Cr₂O₇/H⁺ → CH₃COOH.

点开看答案Show answer
(a) 亲电加成（烯烃 + 卤素，双键打开）；(b) 自由基取代（烷烃 + 卤素，光照）；(c) 氧化（醇被氧化成酸）。
看到「烯烃」想加成、「烷烃 + 光照」想自由基、「醇 + K₂Cr₂O₇」想氧化。 (a) electrophilic addition (alkene + halogen, double bond opens); (b) radical substitution (alkane + halogen, in light); (c) oxidation (alcohol oxidised to acid).
See "alkene" → addition; "alkane + light" → radical; "alcohol + K₂Cr₂O₇" → oxidation.
— 第 7 站完成 —— Stop 7 done —

单元 13 小结Unit 13 summary

① 碳靠 4 个价电子和「自己接自己」搭出几百万种分子，diamond 与 graphite 是它的两种同素异形体。
② 官能团是分子的「身份证」，同系物只差一个 CH₂，通式相同、化学性质相似。
③ 命名四步：最长链 → 编号 → 取代基（按字母序）→ 后缀。
④ 单键 σ、双键 1σ+1π、三键 1σ+2π，对应 sp³ / sp² / sp。
⑤ 异构分两类：结构异构（链 / 位置 / 官能团）和立体异构（cis–trans）。
⑥ 反应四类：自由基取代、亲电加成、亲核取代、氧化还原，弯箭头标电子去向。① Carbon's 4 valence electrons and its ability to bond to itself build millions of molecules; diamond and graphite are its two allotropes.
② The functional group is the molecule's identity card; members of a homologous series differ by CH₂, with the same general formula and similar chemistry.
③ Naming in four steps: longest chain → numbering → substituents (alphabetical) → suffix.
④ Single = σ, double = 1σ+1π, triple = 1σ+2π, matching sp³ / sp² / sp.
⑤ Two kinds of isomerism: structural (chain / position / functional group) and stereo (cis–trans).
⑥ Four reaction families: radical substitution, electrophilic addition, nucleophilic substitution, oxidation/reduction, with curly arrows tracking the electrons.

下一站最重要的一件事：开始「挨个点名」——先认识烷烃和烯烃这两个「碳氢化合物」家族。它们的结构、反应和燃烧，是后面所有有机反应的底子。Why the next unit matters: we start meeting them one by one — first the two "hydrocarbon" families, alkanes and alkenes. Their structures, reactions and combustion are the foundation for everything that follows.

单元 14 · 烷烃与烯烃：只由碳和氢搭出来的分子Unit 14 · Hydrocarbons: molecules built from carbon and hydrogen

CAIE 9701 Topic 14 · 6 站 · 只由碳氢组成的分子，一"饱和"一"不饱和"CAIE 9701 Topic 14 · 6 stops · molecules made of only carbon and hydrogen — one "saturated", one "unsaturated"
